knowledge_statements.statement_title: Demyanov difference of convex compact sets
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines the gradient-based difference of two convex compact sets and records its well-definedness and compactness.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(U,V\subset\mathbb R^n\) be nonempty convex compact sets with support functions \(p_U,p_V\). If \(T\) is any full-measure set on which both support functions are differentiable, define
\[
U\doteq V:=\operatorname{cl}\operatorname{co}\{\nabla p_U(x)-\nabla p_V(x):x\in T\}.
\]
This set is independent of the choice of \(T\), is convex and compact, and satisfies \(U\doteq V\subseteq U-V\), where the right-hand side is the Minkowski difference.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For convex compact sets U and V, their Demyanov difference is the closed convex hull of differences of support-function gradients taken in common differentiability directions. It does not depend on the chosen full-measure set of directions, is convex compact, and is contained in the Minkowski difference.
assumptions_latex: U,V\subset\mathbb R^n\text{ are nonempty convex compact sets}
T\subseteq\{x:\nabla p_U(x)\text{ and }\nabla p_V(x)\text{ exist}\}\text{ has full measure}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: U\doteq V=\operatorname{cl}\operatorname{co}\{\nabla p_U(x)-\nabla p_V(x):x\in T\}\text{ is well-defined and convex compact, with }U\doteq V\subseteq U-V.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Quasidifferentials of finite maxima and minima
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Preserves the source formulas in terms of active maximum and minimum index sets.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f_i:X\to\mathbb R\), \(i=1,\ldots,m\), be quasidifferentiable at \(x\in X\), where \(X\subset\mathbb R^n\) is open. Define \(\varphi_1=\max_i f_i\), \(\varphi_2=\min_i f_i\), \(R(x)=\{i:f_i(x)=\varphi_1(x)\}\), and \(Q(x)=\{i:f_i(x)=\varphi_2(x)\}\). Then both extrema are quasidifferentiable at \(x\), with \[\underline\partial\varphi_1(x)=\operatorname{conv}\!\bigcup_{k\in R(x)}\left(\underline\partial f_k(x)-\sum_{\substack{i\in R(x)\\i\ne k}}\bar\partial f_i(x)\right),\qquad \bar\partial\varphi_1(x)=\bigcup_{k\in R(x)}\bar\partial f_k(x),\] \[\underline\partial\varphi_2(x)=\bigcup_{k\in Q(x)}\underline\partial f_k(x),\qquad \bar\partial\varphi_2(x)=\operatorname{conv}\!\bigcup_{k\in Q(x)}\left(\bar\partial f_k(x)-\sum_{\substack{i\in Q(x)\\i\ne k}}\underline\partial f_i(x)\right).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A finite pointwise maximum or minimum of functions quasidifferentiable at a point is quasidifferentiable there. Its quasidifferential is determined by the functions active at the maximum or minimum through the stated convex-hull, union, and Minkowski-sum formulas.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \varphi_1=\max_{1\le i\le m}f_i\text{ and }\varphi_2=\min_{1\le i\le m}f_i\text{ are quasidifferentiable at }x\text{ with the displayed active-index formulas}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Quasidifferentiability, quasidifferentials, and the Hadamard variant
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Includes the defining representation, terminology, nonuniqueness, and Hadamard quasidifferentiability.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A function \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) is quasidifferentiable at \(x\) if there exist compact convex sets \(\underline\partial f(x),\bar\partial f(x)\subset\mathbb R^n\) such that, for every \(d\in\mathbb R^n\), \[f'(x;d)=\max_{\xi\in\underline\partial f(x)}\xi^Td+\min_{\nu\in\bar\partial f(x)}\nu^Td.\] The pair \(\mathcal Df(x)=[\underline\partial f(x),\bar\partial f(x)]\) is a quasidifferential, with its components called the subdifferential and superdifferential. It is nonunique: for every compact convex \(A\subset\mathbb R^n\), \([\underline\partial f(x)+A,\bar\partial f(x)-A]\) is another quasidifferential. Replacing \(f'(x;d)\) by the Hadamard derivative \(\lim_{\alpha\downarrow0,\,d'\to d}[f(x+\alpha d')-f(x)]/\alpha\) defines Hadamard quasidifferentiability.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A function is quasidifferentiable at a point when every directional derivative is the sum of the support function of one compact convex set and the negative support function of another. The representing pair is its quasidifferential and is nonunique under opposite translations by any compact convex set. Using the Hadamard directional derivative gives Hadamard quasidifferentiability.
assumptions_latex: \underline\partial f(x),\bar\partial f(x)\subset\mathbb R^n\text{ are compact and convex}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: f'(x;d)=\max_{\xi\in\underline\partial f(x)}\xi^Td+\min_{\nu\in\bar\partial f(x)}\nu^Td\quad\forall d\in\mathbb R^n

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Face-based quasidifference and its failure boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines the face-based quasidifference and contrasts it with the gradient-based Demyanov difference.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For convex compact sets \(U,V\), define the face-based quasidifference by
\[
U\mathbin{\ddot{-}}V:=\operatorname{cl}\operatorname{co}\bigcup_{x\ne0}\bigl(G_x(U)-G_x(V)\bigr),
\]
where \(G_x(C)\) is the maximizing face of \(C\) in direction \(x\), and the inner subtraction is Minkowski subtraction. Then
\[
U\mathbin{\ddot{-}}V\supseteq U\doteq V.
\]
If a nonsingleton convex compact set \(V\) lies in a hyperplane orthogonal to some \(x_0\ne0\), then \(V\mathbin{\ddot{-}}V=V-V\ne\{0\}\), despite \(V+\{0\}=V\). Moreover, this quasidifference need not be invariant under equivalence of pairs: equivalent \([U,-V]\) and \([W,-Z]\) may satisfy \(U\mathbin{\ddot{-}}V\ne W\mathbin{\ddot{-}}Z\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The face-based quasidifference is the closed convex hull of all Minkowski differences of corresponding maximizing faces. It contains the Demyanov difference, but it can fail cancellation and invariance under equivalent pair representations.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: U\mathbin{\ddot{-}}V\supseteq U\doteq V,\quad V\mathbin{\ddot{-}}V\text{ may differ from }\{0\},\quad\text{and }\mathbin{\ddot{-}}\text{ need not respect pair equivalence}.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Max-faces and general position of convex compact set pairs
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines the exposed max-face of a compact set and the general-position condition for two convex compact sets.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a compact set V\subset\mathbb{R}^n and x\in\mathbb{R}^n, define G_x(V)=\{v\in V:\langle v,x\rangle=\max_{v'\in V}\langle v',x\rangle\}. Then G_x(V)=\partial p_V(x), where p_V is the support function of V, and G_0(V)=V. An ordered pair [U,V] of convex compact subsets of \mathbb{R}^n is in general position if, for every g\in\mathbb{R}^n, G_g(V) is not contained in G_g(U).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The max-face of a compact set in a direction consists of its maximizers in that direction. It equals the subdifferential of the support function, and at the zero direction it is the whole set. Two convex compact sets are in general position when, in every direction, the max-face of the second is not contained in the max-face of the first.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: G_x(V)=\partial p_V(x),\quad G_0(V)=V,\quad [U,V]\text{ is in general position}\iff \forall g\in\mathbb{R}^n,\ G_g(V)\not\subseteq G_g(U).

knowledge_statements.scope_note: A sufficient minimality criterion expressed through compatible exposed points of the Minkowski sum and difference.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let $U,V\subset\mathbb{R}^n$ be nonempty convex compact sets. Suppose that for every exposed point $w=u+v$ of $U+V$, at least one of the following holds: (i) there is an exposed point $v_1$ of $V$ such that $u+v_1$ is exposed in $U+V$ and $u-v_1$ is exposed in $U-V$; or (ii) there is an exposed point $u_1$ of $U$ such that $u_1+v$ is exposed in $U+V$ and $u_1-v$ is exposed in $U-V$. Then $[U,V]$ is minimal.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A convex-compact pair is minimal if every exposed point of its sum admits, through at least one component, an exposed-point companion that is compatible with exposed points of both the sum and the Minkowski difference.
assumptions_latex: For every exposed $w=u+v\in U+V$, either $\exists v_1\in\operatorname{exp}(V)$ with $u+v_1\in\operatorname{exp}(U+V)$ and $u-v_1\in\operatorname{exp}(U-V)$, or $\exists u_1\in\operatorname{exp}(U)$ with $u_1+v\in\operatorname{exp}(U+V)$ and $u_1-v\in\operatorname{exp}(U-V)$.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: [U,V]\text{ is minimal}.

knowledge_statements.title: Quasidifferential Equivalence Classes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional equivalence of ordered compact-convex representatives.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Two ordered pairs \((A,B)\) and \((C,D)\) of nonempty compact convex sets are quasidifferentially equivalent when they represent the same support-function difference: \[\sigma_A(d)-\sigma_B(d)=\sigma_C(d)-\sigma_D(d)\quad\text{for every }d\in\mathbb R^n.\] Since support functions satisfy \(\sigma_{A+D}=\sigma_A+\sigma_D\) and uniquely determine nonempty compact convex sets, this is equivalent to \(A+D=B+C\). The equivalence class of \((A,B)\) is \([(A,B)]=\{(C,D):(C,D)\sim(A,B)\}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Two compact-convex pairs are equivalent exactly when their support-function differences agree in every direction, equivalently when their crosswise Minkowski sums coincide.
assumptions_latex: \(A,B,C,D\subset\mathbb R^n\) are nonempty compact convex sets.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[(A,B)\sim(C,D)\iff \sigma_A-\sigma_B=\sigma_C-\sigma_D\iff A+D=B+C.\]

source_refs.locator: A. Convex Sets and Functions p. 38

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Linear Structure of Quasidifferential Equivalence Classes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Representative-independent addition, additive inversion, and real scaling of finite-dimensional quasidifferential classes.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \((A,B)\sim(C,D)\) and \((E,F)\sim(G,H)\), then \((A+E,B+F)\sim(C+G,D+H)\). Swapping components preserves equivalence, so \((B,A)\sim(D,C)\). For \(\lambda\in\mathbb R\), define \(\lambda\odot(A,B)=(\lambda A,\lambda B)\) when \(\lambda\ge0\), and \(\lambda\odot(A,B)=((-\lambda)B,(-\lambda)A)\) when \(\lambda<0\). Then \(\lambda\odot(A,B)\sim\lambda\odot(C,D)\). Thus addition, additive inversion, and real scaling are well defined on equivalence classes.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Componentwise Minkowski addition, component swapping as additive inversion, and sign-aware real scaling depend only on the quasidifferential equivalence class.
assumptions_latex: All displayed sets are nonempty compact convex subsets of \(\mathbb R^n\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: [(A,B)]+[(E,F)]=[(A+E,B+F)],\quad-[(A,B)]=[(B,A)],\quad\lambda[(A,B)]=[\lambda\odot(A,B)].

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Quasidifferential as an Equivalence Class of Representative Pairs
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines the quasidifferential independently of the choice of compact-convex representative pair.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
If \(f\) is quasidifferentiable at \(x\), its quasidifferential \(\mathcal Df(x)\) is the equivalence class of compact convex pairs \([U,V]\) satisfying
\[
f'(x;g)=\max_{u\in U}\langle u,g\rangle+\min_{v\in V}\langle v,g\rangle\qquad\forall g\in\mathbb R^n.
\]
By convention, an individual representative pair in this class may also be denoted by \(\mathcal Df(x)\).

children.top_down_role: Irreducible or inclusion-minimal representatives within quasidifferential equivalence classes.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Inclusion-Minimal Representatives Need Not Be Unique or Least
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of uniqueness under the componentwise inclusion-minimal convention proposed by the deferred seed.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the zero directional model \(q(d)\equiv0\), every singleton pair \((\{a\},\{a\})\), \(a\in\mathbb R^n\), represents \(q\). Under componentwise inclusion-minimality among nonempty compact-convex representatives, each such pair is minimal. If \(a\neq b\), the pairs \((\{a\},\{a\})\) and \((\{b\},\{b\})\) are distinct and incomparable. Hence the equivalence class has neither a unique minimal representative nor a componentwise least representative.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The zero directional model has infinitely many incomparable singleton inclusion-minimal representatives, so minimal does not mean unique or least.
assumptions_latex: Minimality means componentwise inclusion-minimality among nonempty compact-convex pairs.
The ambient space contains two distinct points.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[a\neq b\Rightarrow(\{a\},\{a\})\sim(\{b\},\{b\}),\quad\text{both are inclusion-minimal and incomparable}.\]
knowledge_statements.title: Inclusion-Minimal Representatives Need Not Be Unique or Least

assumptions_latex: \(A,B\subset\mathbb R^n\) are nonempty compact convex sets.
Equivalence is defined by equality of support-function differences.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[(A,B)\text{ is minimal}\iff \nexists(C,D)\sim(A,B): C\subseteq A, D\subseteq B, (C,D)\neq(A,B).\]
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: componentwise inclusion gives a precise irreducibility notion within a quasidifferential equivalence class
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Componentwise inclusion-minimality; other notions of minimal representative may require separate treatment.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A representative \((A,B)\) is inclusion-minimal in its quasidifferential equivalence class if no distinct equivalent pair can reduce both components componentwise. Formally, whenever \((C,D)\sim(A,B)\), \(C\subseteq A\), and \(D\subseteq B\), one must have \(C=A\) and \(D=B\). Thus minimality is relative to the equivalence relation and the componentwise inclusion order; it does not assert minimum diameter, minimum volume, uniqueness, or the existence of a least representative in the class.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A representative is inclusion-minimal when no distinct equivalent pair has both compact-convex components contained in its corresponding components.

children.title: Representative Reduction Criteria
children.top_down_role: Structural criteria used to simplify representatives without changing their encoded information.

knowledge_statements.title: Representative Reduction Criteria
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sufficient equivalence-preserving reduction criterion based on cancelling a common Minkowski summand; strict componentwise reduction requires additional inclusion hypotheses.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If both components of a representative have a common Minkowski summand, that summand may be cancelled without changing the represented function. If \(A=A_0+K\) and \(B=B_0+K\), support-function additivity gives \[\sigma_A-[3~\sigma_B=(\sigma_{A_0}+\sigma_K)-(\sigma_{B_0}+\sigma_K)=\sigma_{A_0}-\sigma_{B_0}.\] Hence \((A,B)\sim(A_0,B_0)\). This establishes equivalence; whether \((A_0,B_0)\) is componentwise smaller requires separate inclusion conditions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A common Minkowski summand in both representative sets can be cancelled because its support function appears with opposite signs; strict componentwise reduction requires additional inclusion conditions.
assumptions_latex: \(A_0,B_0,K\subset\mathbb R^n\) are nonempty compact convex sets.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[(A,B)\sim(A_0,B_0),\qquad \sigma_A-\sigma_B=\sigma_{A_0}-\sigma_{B_0}.\]

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Exact Componentwise Reduction Test
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Necessary and sufficient test for a proposed componentwise-smaller pair to preserve its represented support-function difference.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C\subseteq A\) and \(D\subseteq B\), with all four sets nonempty, compact, and convex. Then \((C,D)\) is an equivalence-preserving componentwise reduction of \((A,B)\) exactly when \[A+D=B+C.\] The componentwise inclusions alone are insufficient.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A componentwise-smaller pair is a valid reduction exactly when its crosswise Minkowski sums agree with those of the original pair.
assumptions_latex: \(A,B,C,D\subset\mathbb R^n\) are nonempty compact convex sets.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: (C,D)\sim(A,B)\iff A+D=B+C.
knowledge_statements.title: Exact Componentwise Reduction Test

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Componentwise Inclusion Does Not Preserve a Representative
knowledge_statements.scope_note: One-dimensional failure of inclusion-only reduction criteria.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Take \(A=[0,1]\), \(B=\{0\}\), and \(C=D=\{0\}\). Although \(C\subsetneq A\) and \(D\subseteq B\), \[\sigma_A(1)-\sigma_B(1)=1\ne0=\sigma_C(1)-\sigma_D(1).\] Hence \((C,D)\not\sim(A,B)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Deleting points componentwise can change the represented directional function even when the reduced sets remain compact and convex.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: C\subsetneq A,\quad D\subseteq B,\quad(C,D)\not\sim(A,B).

Quasidifferential Calculus
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sum and scalar-multiplication rules under the difference-of-support-functions convention.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Under the convention \(f_i'(x;d)=\sigma_{A_i}(d)-\sigma_{B_i}(d)\), quasidifferential representatives obey algebraic calculus rules modulo representative equivalence. A representative for \(f_1+f_2\) is \((A_1+A_2,B_1+B_2)\). For \(\lambda\geq0\), a representative for \(\lambda f_1\) is \((\lambda A_1,\lambda B_1)\). For \(\lambda<0\), multiplication reverses the difference, so a representative is \((|\lambda|B_1,|\lambda|A_1)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Quasidifferential representatives add by Minkowski addition; positive scaling scales both sets, while negative scaling also swaps them.
assumptions_latex: The functions \(f_1,f_2:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) are directionally differentiable at \(x\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\mathcal Q_x(f_1+f_2)=(A_1+A_2,B_1+B_2),\qquad \mathcal Q_x(\lambda f_1)=\begin{cases}(\lambda A_1,\lambda B_1),&\lambda\geq0,\\(|\lambda|B_1,|\lambda|A_1),&\lambda<0.\end{cases}\]

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Finite Maximum and Minimum Rules
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Explicit representative formulas for finite pointwise extrema at a fixed base point.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose \(f_i'(x;d)=\sigma_{A_i}(d)-\sigma_{B_i}(d)\). For \(f=\max_i f_i\), let \(I_+(x)=\{i:f_i(x)=f(x)\}\). A representative is \[B=\sum_{i\in I_+(x)}B_i,\qquad A=\operatorname{conv}\bigcup_{i\in I_+(x)}\left(A_i+\sum_{j\in I_+(x)\setminus\{i\}}B_j\right).\] For \(g=\min_i f_i\), with active set \(I_-(x)\), a representative is \[A=\sum_{i\in I_-(x)}A_i,\qquad B=\operatorname{conv}\bigcup_{i\in I_-(x)}\left(B_i+\sum_{j\in I_-(x)\setminus\{i\}}A_j\right).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Finite maxima and minima remain quasidifferentiable, with representatives formed from active pairs using Minkowski sums and convex hulls.
assumptions_latex: Every component function is quasidifferentiable at \(x\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[(\max_i f_i)'(x;d)=\max_{i\in I_+(x)}f_i'(x;d),\qquad (\min_i f_i)'(x;d)=\min_{i\in I_-(x)}f_i'(x;d),\] with the displayed representatives.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Smooth Outer Composition and Product Rules
knowledge_statements.scope_note: First-order calculus for a differentiable scalar outer function, with products as a specialization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F=(f_1,\ldots,f_m)\), where each \(f_i\) is quasidifferentiable at \(x\) with representative \((A_i,B_i)\), and let \(\Phi:\mathbb R^m\to\mathbb R\) be differentiable at \(F(x)\). Then \[(\Phi\circ F)'(x;d)=\sum_{i=1}^m\partial_i\Phi(F(x))f_i'(x;d).\] A representative is obtained by Minkowski-adding the signed scalar multiples of \((A_i,B_i)\), interchanging the components for negative coefficients. In particular, \((fg)'(x;d)=g(x)f'(x;d)+f(x)g'(x;d)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A differentiable outer map combines inner quasidifferentials using its gradient; the product rule follows by signed scaling and Minkowski addition.
assumptions_latex: Each \(f_i:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) is quasidifferentiable at \(x\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[(\Phi\circ F)'(x;d)=\sum_{i=1}^m\partial_i\Phi(F(x))f_i'(x;d).\]
knowledge_statements.title: Smooth Outer Composition and Product Rules

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Algebraic Closure Rules for Quasidifferentiable Functions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Gives sum, product, scalar-multiple, and reciprocal rules at a fixed point.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(f_1,f_2\) be quasidifferentiable at \(x\). Then \(f_1+f_2\) and \(f_1f_2\) are quasidifferentiable at \(x\), with
\[
\mathcal D(f_1+f_2)(x)=\mathcal Df_1(x)+\mathcal Df_2(x),
\]
\[
\mathcal D(f_1f_2)(x)=f_1(x)\mathcal Df_2(x)+f_2(x)\mathcal Df_1(x).
\]
For every \(\lambda\in\mathbb R\), \(\lambda f\) is quasidifferentiable and
\[
\mathcal D(\lambda f)(x)=\lambda\mathcal Df(x),
\]
where multiplication by a negative scalar swaps the lower and upper representative components. If \(f\) is quasidifferentiable at \(x\) and \(f(x)\ne0\), then \(1/f\) is quasidifferentiable at \(x\) and
\[
\mathcal D(1/f)(x)=-\frac{1}{f(x)^2}\mathcal Df(x).
\]
For representative pairs, scalar coefficients in the product rule act with the corresponding sign-dependent interchange of lower and upper components.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Quasidifferentiability is preserved by sums, products, arbitrary scalar multiplication, and reciprocals at nonzero values. Their quasidifferentials obey the usual linear, product, and reciprocal identities, with negative scalar factors interchanging the two representative components.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \mathcal D(f_1+f_2)(x)=\mathcal Df_1(x)+\mathcal Df_2(x),\quad \mathcal D(f_1f_2)(x)=f_1(x)\mathcal Df_2(x)+f_2(x)\mathcal Df_1(x),\quad \mathcal D(\lambda f)(x)=\lambda\mathcal Df(x),\quad \mathcal D(1/f)(x)=-f(x)^{-2}\mathcal Df(x)

knowledge_statements.statement_title: K-Spaces and Banach K-Spaces
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Includes the order-theoretic definitions and notation for largest and smallest elements.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An ordered vector space \(Y\) is a K-space if every subset of \(Y\) that is bounded above has a supremum. A K-space that is also a Banach space with a monotone norm, meaning \(|x|\le |y|\Rightarrow \|x\|\le \|y\|\), is a Banach K-space. For \(\Omega\subset Y\), \(\max_{x\in\Omega}x\) and \(\min_{x\in\Omega}x\) denote the largest and smallest elements when they exist.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A K-space is an ordered vector space in which every upper-bounded set has a supremum. A Banach K-space is a K-space that is Banach and has a monotone norm. Max and min denote actual largest and smallest elements when present.
assumptions_latex: Y\text{ is an ordered vector space}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Y\text{ is a K-space}\iff \text{every upper-bounded subset of }Y\text{ has a supremum; a Banach K-space additionally has a monotone norm.}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Difference-of-Sublinear Closure under Order-Bounded Composition
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Operator decomposition underlying composition of quasidifferentiable mappings in Banach K-spaces.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let $X$ be a Banach space and let $Y,Z$ be Banach $K$-spaces. Suppose $S,T\in\mathcal P(X,Y)$ and $P,Q\in\mathcal P(Y,Z)$, with $P$ and $Q$ order bounded. Then the composite operator $R=(P-Q)\circ(S-T)$ can be represented as the difference of two sublinear operators.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Difference and Quotient Rules for Quasidifferentials
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Derived algebraic rules for differences and quotients at a fixed point.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
If \(f_1\) and \(f_2\) are quasidifferentiable at \(x\), then \(f_1-f_2\) is quasidifferentiable at \(x\) and
\[
\mathcal D(f_1-f_2)(x)=\mathcal Df_1(x)-\mathcal Df_2(x).
\]
If additionally \(f_2(x)\ne0\), then \(f_1/f_2\) is quasidifferentiable at \(x\) and
\[
\mathcal D\!\left(\frac{f_1}{f_2}\right)(x)=\frac{1}{f_2(x)^2}\left(f_2(x)\mathcal Df_1(x)-f_1(x)\mathcal Df_2(x)\right).
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The difference of two quasidifferentiable functions is quasidifferentiable. Their quotient is also quasidifferentiable whenever the denominator is nonzero at the point, with the stated difference and quotient formulas.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \mathcal D(f_1-f_2)(x)=\mathcal Df_1(x)-\mathcal Df_2(x),\qquad \mathcal D(f_1/f_2)(x)=f_2(x)^{-2}\bigl(f_2(x)\mathcal Df_1(x)-f_1(x)\mathcal Df_2(x)\bigr)

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Quasidifferentiability of Banach K-Space Compositions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Composition rule for quasidifferentiable mappings with an order-bounded outer quasidifferential.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let $X$ be a Banach space, let $Y,Z$ be Banach $K$-spaces, and let $\Omega_1\subset X$, $\Omega_2\subset Y$ be open. Suppose $H:\Omega_1\to\Omega_2$ is quasidifferentiable at $x\in\Omega_1$, and $G:\Omega_2\to Z$ is both Hadamard differentiable and quasidifferentiable at $y=H(x)$. If $G$ admits a quasidifferential $\mathcal DG(y)=[\partial G(y),\bar\partial G(y)]$ whose two representing sets are bounded in the space of regular operators, then $F=G\circ H$ is quasidifferentiable at $x$.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A quasidifferentiable inner mapping composed with an outer mapping that is both Hadamard differentiable and quasidifferentiable remains quasidifferentiable, provided the two sets in an outer quasidifferential are bounded sets of regular operators.
assumptions_latex: G:\Omega_2\to Z\text{ is Hadamard differentiable and quasidifferentiable at }y
\mathcal DG(y)=[\partial G(y),\bar\partial G(y)]\text{ with }\partial G(y),\bar\partial G(y)\text{ bounded in the space of regular operators}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: F=G\circ H\text{ is quasidifferentiable at }x.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Order-Bounded Sublinear Operator
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Definition and subdifferential characterization for operators between Banach K-spaces.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let $Y,Z$ be Banach $K$-spaces and $P\in\mathcal P(Y,Z)$. The operator $P$ is order bounded if there exist regular linear operators $\Lambda_1,\Lambda_2\in\mathcal L(Y,Z)$ such that $\Lambda_1(y)\le -P(-y)\le P(y)\le\Lambda_2(y)$ for every $y\ge0$. A linear operator is regular when it is the difference of two positive operators. Equivalently, $P$ is order bounded if and only if every operator in $\partial P$ is regular and $\partial P$ is bounded in the space of regular operators.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A sublinear operator between Banach K-spaces is order bounded when its positive-direction values and reflected values lie between two regular linear operators. This holds exactly when its subdifferential is a bounded set of regular operators.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: P\text{ is order bounded}\iff \exists\Lambda_1,\Lambda_2\in\mathcal L(Y,Z)\text{ regular}:\ \Lambda_1(y)\le-P(-y)\le P(y)\le\Lambda_2(y)\ \forall y\ge0\iff \partial P\text{ is a bounded set of regular operators}.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Finite Maximum and Minimum Rules for Quasidifferentials
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Calculus formulas for pointwise extrema of finitely many quasidifferentiable functions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(f_1,\ldots,f_m\) be defined on an open set \(X\subset\mathbb R^n\) and quasidifferentiable at \(x\in X\), with representative pairs \([\partial f_i(x),\bar\partial f_i(x)]\). Define
\[
\varphi_1=\max_{1\le i\le m}f_i,\qquad \varphi_2=\min_{1\le i\le m}f_i,
\]
\[
R(x)=\{i:f_i(x)=\varphi_1(x)\},\qquad Q(x)=\{i:f_i(x)=\varphi_2(x)\}.
\]
Then \(\varphi_1\) and \(\varphi_2\) are quasidifferentiable at \(x\), and representatives may be chosen as
\[
\partial\varphi_1(x)=\operatorname{co}\!\bigcup_{k\in R(x)}\left(\partial f_k(x)-\sum_{\substack{i\in R(x)\\i\ne k}}\bar\partial f_i(x)\right),\qquad
\bar\partial\varphi_1(x)=\sum_{k\in R(x)}\bar\partial f_k(x),
\]
\[
\partial\varphi_2(x)=\sum_{k\in Q(x)}\partial f_k(x),\qquad
\bar\partial\varphi_2(x)=\operatorname{co}\!\bigcup_{k\in Q(x)}\left(\bar\partial f_k(x)-\sum_{\substack{i\in Q(x)\\i\ne k}}\partial f_i(x)\right).
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Finite pointwise maxima and minima of quasidifferentiable functions remain quasidifferentiable. Their representative components are obtained from the active maximum or minimum indices using convex hulls, unions, and Minkowski sums and differences as displayed.
assumptions_latex: f_i:X\to\mathbb R\text{ is quasidifferentiable at }x\text{ for }i=1,\ldots,m
[\partial f_i(x),\bar\partial f_i(x)]\text{ is a quasidifferential representative}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \varphi_1=\max_{1\le i\le m}f_i\text{ and }\varphi_2=\min_{1\le i\le m}f_i\text{ are quasidifferentiable at }x\text{ with the stated active-index formulas}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Quasidifferentiable Mapping into a Banach K-Space
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Definition and elementary algebraic closure of operator-valued quasidifferentiability.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let $X$ be a Banach space, $\Omega\subset X$ be open, and $Y$ be a Banach $K$-space. A mapping $H:\Omega\to Y$ is quasidifferentiable at $x\in\Omega$ if it is directionally differentiable at $x$ and $H'_x$ is the sum of a continuous sublinear operator and a continuous superlinear operator. Its quasidifferential $\mathcal DH(x)$ is the corresponding equivalence class of pairs $[U,V]$ of support sets satisfying $H'_x(g)=\max_{A\in U}A(g)+\min_{B\in V}B(g)$ for every $g\in X$. If $H_1,H_2$ are quasidifferentiable at $x$, then $H_1+H_2$ is quasidifferentiable and $\mathcal D(H_1+H_2)(x)=\mathcal DH_1(x)+\mathcal DH_2(x)$. If $H$ and a scalar function $f$ are quasidifferentiable at $x$, then $G=fH$ is quasidifferentiable at $x$.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A mapping into a Banach K-space is quasidifferentiable when its directional derivative decomposes into continuous sublinear and superlinear parts. The quasidifferential is the equivalence class of support-set pairs representing that derivative. Quasidifferentiable mappings are closed under addition and under multiplication by a quasidifferentiable scalar function.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: H\text{ is quasidifferentiable at }x\iff H'_x(g)=\max_{A\in U}A(g)+\min_{B\in V}B(g)\ \forall g\in X\text{ for a quasidifferential class }[U,V];\quad \mathcal D(H_1+H_2)=\mathcal DH_1+\mathcal DH_2,\quad fH\text{ is quasidifferentiable}.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Sublinear Operators, Support Operators, and Subdifferentials
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Order-valued operator definitions used by quasidifferential representations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\) be a vector space and \(Y\) a K-space. An operator \(P:X\to Y\) is sublinear if \(P(x+y)\le P(x)+P(y)\) for all \(x,y\in X\) and \(P(\lambda x)=\lambda P(x)\) for all \(x\in X\) and \(\lambda>0\). A linear operator \(A:X\to Y\) supports \(P\) if \(A(x)\le P(x)\) for every \(x\in X\). The subdifferential is \(\partial P=\{A\in\mathcal L(X,Y):A(x)\le P(x)\ \forall x\in X\}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A sublinear operator is subadditive and positively homogeneous. Its support operators are the linear operators lying below it pointwise, and their collection is its subdifferential.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \partial P=\{A\in\mathcal L(X,Y):A(x)\le P(x)\ \forall x\in X\}.

children.title: Epsilon-Quasidifferentials
children.top_down_role: Tolerance-indexed quasidifferential representations used for inexact local information.

assumptions_latex: \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) is directionally differentiable at \(x\).
\(A,B\subset\mathbb R^n\) are nonempty compact convex sets and \(\varepsilon\geq0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\left|f'(x;d)-\bigl(\sigma_A(d)-\sigma_B(d)\bigr)\right|\leq\varepsilon\lVert d\rVert\quad\text{for every }d\in\mathbb R^n.\]
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: uniform norm-scaled directional error gives a self-contained approximate support-difference model
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Uniform directional-error convention for an epsilon-quasidifferential.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the uniform directional-error convention, an \(\varepsilon\)-quasidifferential of \(f\) at \(x\) is an ordered pair \((A,B)\) of nonempty compact convex sets satisfying \[\left|f'(x;d)-\left(\sigma_A(d)-\sigma_B(d)\right)\right|\leq\u0007varepsilon\lVert d\rVert\quad\text{for every }d\in\mathbb R^n.\] Equivalently, the error is at most \(\varepsilon\) on the unit sphere and scales linearly with direction length. At \(\varepsilon=0\), the pair is an exact quasidifferential representative under the difference-of-support-functions convention.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An epsilon-quasidifferential approximates every directional derivative by a support-function difference with error at most epsilon times the direction norm.
knowledge_statements.title: Epsilon-Quasidifferentials

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The proposed uniform directional-error definition is coherent, but epsilon-quasidifferential terminology has multiple conventions and requires a specialized source. The statement also contains an invalid control character before varepsilon.

children.title: Approximate Quasidifferential Representations
children.top_down_role: Broader approximate representations of quasidifferential structure.

assumptions_latex: \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) is directionally differentiable at \(x\).
For each index \(k\), \(A_k,B_k\subset\mathbb R^n\) are nonempty compact convex sets.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\sup_{\lVert d\rVert\leq1}\left|f'(x;d)-\bigl(\sigma_{A_k}(d)-\sigma_{B_k}(d)\bigr)\right|\leq\varepsilon_k.\]
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: uniform approximation on the unit ball is the sequence form of the selected epsilon-quasidifferential convention
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sequential uniform approximation of a directional derivative by differences of support functions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A sequence \((A_k,B_k)\) is an approximate quasidifferential representation of \(f\) at \(x\) with errors \(\varepsilon_k\) when \[\sup_{\lVert d\rVert\leq1}\left|f'(x;d)-\left(\sigma_{A_k}(d)-\sigma_{B_k}(d)\right)\right|\leq\varepsilon_k\quad\text{for every }k.\] Positive homogeneity then extends the bound to all directions as \(\varepsilon_k\lVert d\rVert\). The representation is asymptotically exact if \(\varepsilon_k\to0\); it is uniformly bounded-accuracy if only \(\sup_k\u0007varepsilon_k<infty\) is required.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A sequence of compact-convex pairs approximately represents the directional derivative when its support-function differences converge uniformly on the unit ball.
knowledge_statements.title: Approximate Quasidifferential Representations

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: No source supports this selected sequential convention. Moreover, the plain statement asserts uniform convergence although the assumptions only impose bounds by epsilon_k and do not require epsilon_k to tend to zero. The LaTeX also contains an invalid control character and malformed infinity notation.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: ε-Quasidifferential
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Approximate paired convex-set representation of a directional derivative at a point.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:X\to\mathbb R\), where \(X\subset\mathbb R^n\) is open, be directionally differentiable at \(x\in X\), and let \(\varepsilon>0\). A pair of compact sets \([\partial_\varepsilon f(x),\bar\partial_\varepsilon f(x)]\) is an \(\varepsilon\)-quasidifferential of \(f\) at \(x\) if, for every \(g\in\mathbb R^n\), \[\left|f'(x;g)-\left(\max_{v\in\partial_\varepsilon f(x)}\langle v,g\rangle+\min_{w\in\bar\partial_\varepsilon f(x)}\langle w,g\rangle\right)\right|\le \varepsilon\|g\|.\] This property is invariant under equivalence of representing pairs; distinct nonequivalent pairs may satisfy it, and every \(\varepsilon\)-quasidifferential is an \(\varepsilon'\)-quasidifferential whenever \(\varepsilon'>\varepsilon\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a directionally differentiable function on an open subset of Euclidean space, an ε-quasidifferential is a pair of compact sets whose max-plus-min support representation approximates every directional derivative with error at most ε times the direction norm. Equivalent pairs preserve the property, representations need not be equivalent, and the property remains valid for every larger error tolerance.
assumptions_latex: f:X\to\mathbb R\text{ is directionally differentiable at }x
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \forall g\in\mathbb R^n:\ \left|f'(x;g)-\max_{v\in\partial_\varepsilon f(x)}\langle v,g\rangle-\min_{w\in\bar\partial_\varepsilon f(x)}\langle w,g\rangle\right|\le\varepsilon\|g\|

children.title: Approximation-Fidelity Regimes
children.top_down_role: Structural distinctions among exact, tolerance-controlled, or coarse representations.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Vanishing Error Does Not Determine Summability
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sequence-level separation of vanishing, summable, and step-weighted-summable fidelity predicates; no algorithmic convergence conclusion is asserted.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\varepsilon_k=(k+1)^{-1}\). Then \(\varepsilon_k\to0\), but \(\sum_{k=0}^{\infty}\varepsilon_k=\infty\). Moreover, \(\sum_k\alpha_k\varepsilon_k\) diverges for \(\alpha_k=1\) and converges for \(\alpha_k=(k+1)^{-1}\). Thus vanishing error neither implies unweighted summability nor determines weighted summability without the weights.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The errors 1/(k+1) vanish but are not summable, and their weighted summability changes with the chosen step weights.
assumptions_latex: The comparison weights are either \(\alpha_k=1\) or \(\alpha_k=(k+1)^{-1}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\varepsilon_k\to0,\qquad \sum_k\varepsilon_k=\infty,\qquad \sum_k\frac{\varepsilon_k}{k+1}<\infty.\]

notation.meaning: directional-representation error bound at iteration k

knowledge_statements.title: Vanishing Error Does Not Determine Summability

assumptions_latex: At iteration \(k\), an approximate representative has directional error at most \(\varepsilon_k\lVert d\rVert\).
The nonnegative sequence \((\alpha_k)\) denotes algorithmic step weights when weighted accumulation is relevant.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\text{exact: }\varepsilon_k=0;\qquad \text{vanishing: }\varepsilon_k\to0;\qquad \text{weighted-summable: }\sum_{k=0}^{\infty}\alpha_k\varepsilon_k<\infty.\]
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: exact, vanishing-error, and weighted-summable-error conditions are distinct mathematically checkable fidelity regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Error-sequence regimes only; no convergence conclusion is asserted without an algorithm-specific theorem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Approximation fidelity can be classified by conditions on the directional-error sequence. The representation is exact when \(\varepsilon_k=0\) for every \(k\); asymptotically faithful when \(\varepsilon_k	o0\); uniformly inexact when \(0<sup_k\u0007varepsilon_k<infty\) without vanishing; and weighted-summable relative to step weights \(\alpha_k\geq0\) when \(\sum_{k=0}^{infty}alpha_k\u0007varepsilon_k<infty\). These predicates describe representation quality. Their optimization consequences depend additionally on the update rule, step conditions, and regularity of the objective.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Exact, vanishing-error, uniformly inexact, and weighted-summable regimes distinguish how closely approximate quasidifferentials track the directional derivative.
knowledge_statements.title: Approximation-Fidelity Regimes

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The conditions are distinguishable and no convergence theorem is overclaimed, but this particular taxonomy of fidelity regimes—especially the weighted-summable regime—is algorithm-dependent and unsourced. Several formulas also contain invalid control characters or missing backslashes.

children.title: Quasidifferential Regularization
children.top_down_role: Regularized quasidifferential representations aimed at stability or tractability.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Dual Projection Formula and Selectionwise Zero-Step Test
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact primal-dual solution of the quadratically regularized support-function subproblem occurring in the deferred method proposal.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A\subset\mathbb R^n\) be nonempty compact convex, \(b\in\mathbb R^n\), and \(t>0\). Then \[\min_d\left\{\sigma_A(d)-\langle b,d\rangle+\frac{1}{2t}\|d\|^2\right\}=\max_{a\in A}\left(-\frac t2\|a-b\|^2\right)=-\frac t2\operatorname{dist}(b,A)^2.\] The primal minimizer is unique and equals \(d_t=t(b-P_A(b))\). Hence \(d_t=0\) if and only if \(b\in A\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The regularized support-function subproblem is dual to projection onto A, and its step vanishes exactly when the selected vector b lies in A.
assumptions_latex: \(A\subset\mathbb R^n\) is nonempty, compact, and convex.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[d_t=t(b-P_A(b)),\qquad d_t=0\iff b\in A,\qquad \min=-\frac t2\operatorname{dist}(b,A)^2.\]
knowledge_statements.title: Dual Projection Formula and Selectionwise Zero-Step Test

assumptions_latex: At \(x\), \(f'(x;d)=\sigma_A(d)-\sigma_B(d)\) for nonempty compact convex \(A,B\subset\mathbb R^n\).
A vector \(b\in B\) and a parameter \(t>0\) are selected.
The convex subproblem attains a minimizer.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[d_t\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{d\in\mathbb R^n}\left\{\sigma_A(d)-\langle b,d\rangle+\frac{1}{2t}\lVert d\rVert^2\right\},\qquad x^+=x+d_t.\]

notation.meaning: selected element of the subtractive representative

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: selecting a subtractive support vector and adding a positive quadratic produces a strongly convex regularized directional subproblem
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Quadratically regularized convex directional subproblem for a selected subtractive representative element.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a quasidifferential representative \((A,B)\) at \(x\), select \(b\in B\) and a parameter \(t>0\). Compute \[d_t\u0007in\operatorname*{argmin}_{d\in\mathbb R^n}\left\{\sigma_A(d)-\langle b,d\rangle+\frac{1}{2t}\lVert d\rVert^2\right\}.\] The quadratic term makes the displayed convex directional model strongly convex, hence its minimizer is unique whenever the objective is proper. Form the trial point \(x^+=x+d_t\), optionally subject to a feasibility or line-search rule. Stop when \(\lVert d_t\rVert\) is below a prescribed tolerance; otherwise update the representative and repeat.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Select an element from the subtractive set, solve a quadratically regularized convex directional subproblem, and use its minimizer as the trial step.
knowledge_statements.title: Quasidifferential Regularization

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind fits the leaf, but a specialized source is necessary to validate the selected element, sign convention, quadratic model, full-step update, and stopping rule as a quasidifferential regularization method. The displayed argmin relation also contains an invalid control character.

children.title: Quasidifferential Convexification
children.top_down_role: Convexifying transformations of quasidifferential representation components.

knowledge_statements.title: Quasidifferential Convexification
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact convex-hull replacement of compact sets in a quasidifferential directional representation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(P,Q\subset\mathbb{R}^n\) be nonempty compact sets and define \(\phi(d)=\max_{p\in P}\langle p,d\rangle+\min_{q\in Q}\langle q,d\rangle\). Set \(A=\operatorname{cl}\operatorname{conv}P\) and \(B=\operatorname{cl}\operatorname{conv}Q\). Then \(A\) and \(B\) are compact convex sets and
\[
\phi(d)=\max_{a\in A}\langle a,d\rangle+\min_{b\in B}\langle b,d\rangle\qquad(d\in\mathbb{R}^n).
\]
Thus replacing each generating set by its closed convex hull produces a quasidifferential representation without changing the represented directional derivative.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Closed convexification of both compact generating sets preserves every value of the represented directional derivative.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\phi(d)=\max_{a\in A}\langle a,d\rangle+\min_{b\in B}\langle b,d\rangle\) for every \(d\in\mathbb{R}^n\).

notation.meaning: Closed convex hulls of the two generating sets.

review_flags: Exact quasidifferential source and locator are missing.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation claim and content kind fit the convexification leaf, and the finite-dimensional convex-hull identity is mathematically plausible. No citation or inspectable locator is supplied, so its identification as quasidifferential convexification cannot be source-validated.

children.title: Representation-Distortion Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Limits beyond which stabilization or convexification changes essential local information.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Sharp Singleton Distortion and Failure of a Converse
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sharpness and nonconverse witnesses for the functional-distortion boundary.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(u\neq0\). For \((A,B)=(\{u\},\{0\})\) and \((\widetilde A,\widetilde B)=(\{0\},\{0\})\), the Hausdorff bound is attained: \[\sup_{\|d\|\leq1}|(\sigma_A-\sigma_B)(d)-(\sigma_{\widetilde A}-\sigma_{\widetilde B})(d)|=\|u\|=d_H(A,\widetilde A)+d_H(B,\widetilde B).\] Conversely, for any \(v\), the equivalent zero-model pairs \((\{0\},\{0\})\) and \((\{v\},\{v\})\) have zero functional distortion while their componentwise Hausdorff distances sum to \(2\|v\|\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Translated singleton pairs attain the additive distortion bound, while common translations show that zero functional distortion does not control componentwise Hausdorff distance.

notation.meaning: uniform functional distortion on the unit ball

knowledge_statements.title: Sharp Singleton Distortion and Failure of a Converse

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Functional Distortion Bound and Zero-Distortion Criterion
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Quantitative boundary between equivalent and perturbed compact-convex representatives under the support-difference convention.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For nonempty compact convex sets \(A,B,\widetilde A,\widetilde B\subset\mathbb R^n\), define \(q=\sigma_A-\sigma_B\) and \(\widetilde q=\sigma_{\widetilde A}-\sigma_{\widetilde B}\). Then \[\sup_{\|d\|\leq1}|q(d)-\widetilde q(d)|\leq d_H(A,\widetilde A)+d_H(B,\widetilde B).\] The left side is zero exactly when the two pairs represent the same directional function, equivalently when they belong to the same quasidifferential equivalence class. A small componentwise Hausdorff perturbation therefore controls functional distortion, but the converse componentwise estimate fails because equivalent pairs can be far apart.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Componentwise Hausdorff errors bound directional-model distortion; zero functional distortion is exactly representative equivalence, while equivalence need not make the individual sets close.
assumptions_latex: \(A,B,\widetilde A,\widetilde B\subset\mathbb R^n\) are nonempty compact convex sets.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\sup_{\|d\|\leq1}|q(d)-\widetilde q(d)|\leq d_H(A,\widetilde A)+d_H(B,\widetilde B),\qquad q=\widetilde q\iff(A,B)\sim(\widetilde A,\widetilde B).\]
knowledge_statements.title: Functional Distortion Bound and Zero-Distortion Criterion
Representation-Distortion Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Hausdorff perturbation boundary for finite-dimensional quasidifferential representations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For nonempty compact sets \(A,B,\widetilde A,\widetilde B\subset\mathbb{R}^n\), define \(\phi(d)=\max_{a\in A}\langle a,d\rangle+\min_{b\in B}\langle b,d\rangle\) and define \(\widetilde\phi\) analogously. If \(d_H\) denotes Hausdorff distance, then
\[
|\phi(d)-\widetilde\phi(d)|\leq\bigl(d_H(A,\widetilde A)+d_H(B,\widetilde B)\bigr)\|d\|.
\]
Consequently, a set perturbation of total size \(\varepsilon\) can distort the represented derivative by at most \(\varepsilon\|d\|\); this coefficient is sharp already for translated singleton sets.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Hausdorff errors in the two representing sets add linearly, and their sum sharply bounds directional-model distortion.
assumptions_latex: \(A,B,\widetilde A,\widetilde B\subset\mathbb{R}^n\) are nonempty and compact.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(|\phi(d)-\widetilde\phi(d)|\leq(d_H(A,\widetilde A)+d_H(B,\widetilde B))\|d\|\).

notation.meaning: Hausdorff distance induced by the Euclidean norm.

review_flags: A source treating this bound in the quasidifferential setting is missing.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure-boundary kind fits the leaf, and the stated Hausdorff stability estimate is plausible for compact finite-dimensional representations. The quasidifferential interpretation and sharpness assertion have no supporting citation or locator.

knowledge_statements.title: Directed-Subdifferentiable Models
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional directed-set encoding of a chosen local DC model.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(f=g-h\) near \(x\in\mathbb{R}^n\), where \(g\) and \(h\) are finite convex functions, and let \(J_n\) be the canonical embedding of compact convex subsets of \(\mathbb{R}^n\) into directed sets. The directed subdifferential assigned to this DC model is
\[
\vec\partial f(x)=J_n(\partial g(x))-J_n(\partial h(x)).
\]
It represents the directional derivative because \(f'(x;d)=\sigma_{\partial g(x)}(d)-\sigma_{\partial h(x)}(d)\) for every \(d\in\mathbb{R}^n\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A local DC decomposition yields a directed subdifferential by subtracting the embedded convex subdifferentials of its two components.
assumptions_latex: \(g\) and \(h\) are finite convex functions on a neighborhood of \(x\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\vec\partial f(x)=J_n(\partial g(x))-J_n(\partial h(x))\) represents \(f'(x;\cdot)\).

notation.meaning: Canonical embedding of compact convex sets into directed sets.
Support function of a compact convex set.
Directed subdifferential of the selected DC model.

review_flags: The precise directed-set convention and decomposition-invariance theorem require a specialized source.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: A representation is the appropriate knowledge kind, but the formula depends on the precise directed-set embedding and sign convention. It is also unclear from the unsourced statement whether the object is attached only to the chosen DC decomposition or is decomposition-independent. A specialized source is required.

knowledge_statements.title: Codifferentiable Models
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Demyanov-style first-order codifferential model in finite dimensions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A function \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\) is codifferentiable at \(x\) if there exist nonempty compact convex sets \(\underline d f(x),\overline d f(x)\subset\mathbb{R}\times\mathbb{R}^n\) such that
\[
f(x+h)-f(x)=\max_{(a,v)\in\underline d f(x)}(a+\langle v,h\rangle)+\min_{(b,w)\in\overline d f(x)}(b+\langle w,h\rangle)+o(\|h\|),
\]
as \(h\to0\), with normalization \(\max_{(a,v)\in\underline d f(x)}a+\min_{(b,w)\in\overline d f(x)}b=0\). The ordered pair is a codifferential of \(f\) at \(x\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Codifferentiability means that the increment is modeled to first order by a maximum affine term plus a minimum affine term.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \((\underline d f(x),\overline d f(x))\) is a normalized codifferential model of \(f\) at \(x\).
review_flags: A specialized codifferential reference with the selected normalization is required.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition kind fits the codifferentiable-model container, but codifferential normalization conventions vary. No specialized source establishes that the single summed normalization used here is the intended convention.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Reciprocal closure of twice codifferentiable functions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Reciprocation preserves twice codifferentiability at points where the denominator is nonzero.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let f_1 be twice codifferentiable at x and suppose f_1(x)\ne0. Then the reciprocal function g=1/f_1 is twice codifferentiable at x. If f_1 is twice continuously codifferentiable at x, then g is twice continuously codifferentiable at x.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At a point where its value is nonzero, the reciprocal of a twice codifferentiable function is twice codifferentiable. The continuous version holds under the same nonvanishing condition.
assumptions_latex: f_1\text{ is twice codifferentiable at }x\quad\text{(respectively, twice continuously codifferentiable at }x\text{)}.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: g=\frac1{f_1}\text{ is twice codifferentiable at }x\quad\text{(respectively, twice continuously codifferentiable at }x\text{)}.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Smooth outer-composition rule for twice codifferentiable functions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A twice differentiable scalar outer function preserves twice codifferentiability of a finite tuple of inner functions at the corresponding point.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Twice codifferentiable and twice continuously codifferentiable functions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines the paired second-order max–min quadratic approximation, its continuity regime, nonuniqueness, and one-sided hypo/hyperdifferentiable cases.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let f:X\to\mathbb R be finite on an open set X\subset\mathbb R^n and let x\in X. The function f is twice codifferentiable at x if there exist convex compact sets \underline d^2f(x),\bar d^2f(x)\subset\mathbb R\times\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb R^{n\times n} such that, for admissible \Delta with \operatorname{co}\{x,x+\Delta\}\subset X, f(x+\Delta)=f(x)+\max_{(a,v,A)\in\underline d^2f(x)}\left(a+\langle v,\Delta\rangle+\tfrac12\langle A\Delta,\Delta\rangle\right)+\min_{(b,w,B)\in\bar d^2f(x)}\left(b+\langle w,\Delta\rangle+\tfrac12\langle B\Delta,\Delta\rangle\right)+r_x(\Delta), where r_x(\alpha d)/\alpha^2\to0 as \alpha\downarrow0 for every d\in\mathbb R^n. The pair D^2f(x)=[\underline d^2f(x),\bar d^2f(x)] is a second-order codifferential and need not be unique. If f is twice codifferentiable in a neighborhood of x and D^2f is Hausdorff-continuous at x, then f is twice continuously codifferentiable at x. It is twice hypodifferentiable, respectively twice hyperdifferentiable, if a second-order codifferential can be chosen with \bar d^2f(x)=\{(0,0,0)\}, respectively \underline d^2f(x)=\{(0,0,0)\}.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A finite function on an open Euclidean set is twice codifferentiable at a point when its increment has a paired maximum-plus-minimum quadratic model over convex compact sets with a directionwise second-order-small remainder. The pair is a generally nonunique second-order codifferential. Local twice codifferentiability together with Hausdorff continuity of the codifferential gives twice continuous codifferentiability. A zero hyperdifferential or hypodifferential gives the corresponding one-sided notion.
assumptions_latex: X\subset\mathbb R^n\text{ is open},\quad f:X\to\mathbb R\text{ is finite},\quad x\in X.
\underline d^2f(x),\bar d^2f(x)\subset\mathbb R\times\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb R^{n\times n}\text{ are convex and compact}.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: f(x+\Delta)=f(x)+\max_{(a,v,A)\in\underline d^2f(x)}\left(a+\langle v,\Delta\rangle+\tfrac12\langle A\Delta,\Delta\rangle\right)+\min_{(b,w,B)\in\bar d^2f(x)}\left(b+\langle w,\Delta\rangle+\tfrac12\langle B\Delta,\Delta\rangle\right)+r_x(\Delta),\quad r_x(\alpha d)/\alpha^2\to0\ \forall d\in\mathbb R^n.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Finite maximum and minimum calculus for second-order codifferentials
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite extrema preserve twice codifferentiability and admit explicit convex-hull and Minkowski-sum codifferential representations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let I=\{1,\ldots,N\} and suppose each \varphi_i is twice codifferentiable at x. Define f_1(y)=\max_{i\in I}\varphi_i(y) and f_2(y)=\min_{i\in I}\varphi_i(y). Then f_1 and f_2 are twice codifferentiable at x, with \underline d^2f_1(x)=\operatorname{co}\!\bigcup_{k\in I}\!\left(\underline d^2\varphi_k(x)-\sum_{i\in I\setminus\{k\}}\bar d^2\varphi_i(x)+\{(\varphi_k(x)-f_1(x),0,0)\}\right), \quad \bar d^2f_1(x)=\sum_{i\in I}\bar d^2\varphi_i(x), \quad \underline d^2f_2(x)=\sum_{i\in I}\underline d^2\varphi_i(x), \quad \bar d^2f_2(x)=\operatorname{co}\!\bigcup_{k\in I}\!\left(\bar d^2\varphi_k(x)-\sum_{i\in I\setminus\{k\}}\underline d^2\varphi_i(x)+\{(\varphi_k(x)-f_2(x),0,0)\}\right). The corresponding assertions hold when all \varphi_i are twice continuously codifferentiable at x.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The finite pointwise maximum and minimum of twice codifferentiable functions remain twice codifferentiable. Their second-order hypo- and hyperdifferentials are given by the stated convex-hull and Minkowski-sum formulas. The continuous version is also preserved.
assumptions_latex: \forall i\in I,\ \varphi_i\text{ is twice codifferentiable at }x\quad\text{(respectively, twice continuously codifferentiable at }x\text{)}.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: f_1=\max_{i\in I}\varphi_i\text{ and }f_2=\min_{i\in I}\varphi_i\text{ are twice (continuously) codifferentiable at }x\text{ with the displayed second-order codifferential formulas}.

children.title: Upper Convex Approximators
children.top_down_role: Convex upper-side local models used in quasi-DC representations.

knowledge_statements.title: Upper Convex Approximators
knowledge_statements.scope_note: First-order convex upper model of a local objective increment.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\) be finite near \(x\). A finite convex function \(U_x:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\) is an upper convex approximator at \(x\) if \(U_x(0)=0\) and there exists a remainder \(r_x(h)=o(\|h\|)\) as \(h\to0\) such that
\[
f(x+h)-f(x)\leq U_x(h)+r_x(h)
\]
for all sufficiently small \(h\). It is exact in direction \(d\) when \(f'(x;d)=U_x'(0;d)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An upper convex approximator is a normalized convex model that bounds the objective increment up to first-order negligible error.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is finite on a neighborhood of \(x\).

notation.meaning: Upper convex approximator based at x.

review_flags: Terminology varies between convex approximation and codifferential frameworks; a defining source is needed.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition kind fits the leaf and the formula is internally coherent, but the exact term "upper convex approximator" is framework-dependent. A defining source with a specific locator is needed to establish that this one-sided first-order model is the intended object.

children.title: Lower Convex Approximators
children.top_down_role: Convex lower-side local models used in quasi-DC representations.

knowledge_statements.title: Lower Convex Approximators
knowledge_statements.scope_note: First-order convex lower model of a local objective increment.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\) be finite near \(x\). A finite convex function \(L_x:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\) is a lower convex approximator at \(x\) if \(L_x(0)=0\) and there exists a remainder \(s_x(h)=o(\|h\|)\) as \(h\to0\) such that
\[
L_x(h)+s_x(h)\leq f(x+h)-f(x)
\]
for all sufficiently small \(h\). It is exact in direction \(d\) when \(L_x'(0;d)=f'(x;d)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A lower convex approximator is a normalized convex model lying below the objective increment up to first-order negligible error.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is finite on a neighborhood of \(x\).

notation.meaning: Lower convex approximator based at x.

review_flags: Terminology varies between convex approximation and codifferential frameworks; a defining source is needed.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition kind fits the leaf and the formula is internally coherent, but the exact term "lower convex approximator" is framework-dependent. A defining source with a specific locator is needed to establish that this one-sided first-order model is the intended object.

children.title: Approximator Compatibility Regimes
children.top_down_role: Regimes governing whether upper-side or lower-side approximators jointly encode usable local structure.

knowledge_statements.title: Approximator Compatibility Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Compatibility condition for paired lower and upper convex local models.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A lower-upper pair \((L_x,U_x)\) is first-order compatible for \(f\) at \(x\) when both functions are finite and convex, \(L_x(0)=U_x(0)=0\), and
\[
L_x(h)+o(\|h\|)\leq f(x+h)-f(x)\leq U_x(h)+o(\|h\|)
\]
as \(h\to0\). The pair is strongly compatible when additionally \(U_x(h)-L_x(h)=o(\|h\|)\). In the strong regime, whenever the directional derivatives exist, \(L_x'(0;d)=f'(x;d)=U_x'(0;d)\) for every direction \(d\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Compatible convex models bracket the increment to first order; strong compatibility forces both models to have the same directional slopes as the objective.
assumptions_latex: \(L_x\) and \(U_x\) are finite convex functions with value zero at the origin.
\(f\) is directionally differentiable at \(x\) for the slope conclusion.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Strong compatibility implies \(L_x'(0;d)=f'(x;d)=U_x'(0;d)\) for every \(d\).

notation.meaning: Paired lower and upper convex approximators.

review_flags: The intended taxonomy of compatibility regimes needs a specialized source.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: A condition is the correct role for this leaf, but the named weak and strong compatibility regimes are uncited. The two occurrences of little-o in the bracketing display should also be tied to explicitly introduced remainder functions before the slope consequence is source-validated.

knowledge_statements.title: Constrained Quasi-DC Models
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional constrained program represented by convex differences.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A constrained quasi-DC model has the form
\[
\min_{x\in C}\;g_0(x)-h_0(x)\quad\text{subject to}\quad g_i(x)-h_i(x)\leq0\quad(i=1,\ldots,m),
\]
where \(C\subset\mathbb{R}^n\) is nonempty, closed, and convex, and every \(g_i,h_i:C\to\mathbb{R}\) is convex. The feasible set is \(F=\{x\in C:g_i(x)-h_i(x)\leq0\text{ for all }i\}\). The qualifier quasi-DC records that the convex ambient constraint \(x\in C\) is retained explicitly rather than absorbed into a finite-valued DC expression.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A constrained quasi-DC program minimizes one convex difference subject to convex-difference inequalities and an explicit convex ambient constraint.
assumptions_latex: \(g_i\) and \(h_i\) are finite convex functions on \(C\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F=\{x\in C:g_i(x)-h_i(x)\leq0,\ i=1,\ldots,m\}\) is the feasible region of the quasi-DC model.
review_flags: The project-specific meaning of quasi-DC requires a defining source.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: A definition fits the model container, but the proposed meaning of "quasi-DC" is not sufficiently standard to accept without a defining source. In particular, the claim that the qualifier specifically records retention of the ambient convex set requires authoritative support.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: First-Order DC Inclusion Is Not Sufficient
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure boundary for the necessary component-subgradient inclusion.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(g(x)=x^2\), \(h(x)=2x^2\), and \(f=g-h=-x^2\). At \(\bar x=0\), \(\partial g(0)=\partial h(0)=\{0\}\), so the necessary inclusion holds. Nevertheless, \(f(x)<f(0)\) for every \(x\neq0\), and zero is a strict local maximum.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The full component-subgradient inclusion can hold at a strict local maximum and therefore is only necessary.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\partial h(0)\subseteq\partial g(0)\) but \(0\notin\operatorname*{argmin}_{\mathrm{loc}}(g-h)\).
knowledge_statements.title: First-Order DC Inclusion Is Not Sufficient

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Constrained DC Subgradient-Inclusion Condition
knowledge_statements.scope_note: First-order necessary condition for a finite DC objective on a closed convex set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C\subset\mathbb R^n\) be nonempty, closed, and convex. Let \(g,h\) be convex and finite on a neighborhood of \(\bar x\in C\). If \(\bar x\) locally minimizes \(g-h\) over \(C\), then \[\partial h(\bar x)\subseteq\partial g(\bar x)+N_C(\bar x).\] Equivalently, every \(y\in\partial h(\bar x)\) can be written as \(y=u+n\), where \(u\in\partial g(\bar x)\) and \(n\in N_C(\bar x)\). For \(C=\mathbb R^n\), this reduces to \(\partial h(\bar x)\subseteq\partial g(\bar x)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At a constrained local DC minimum, every subgradient of the subtracted component equals a subgradient of the first component plus a feasible-set normal.
assumptions_latex: \(g,h\) are convex and finite near \(\bar x\in C\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\partial h(\bar x)\subseteq\partial g(\bar x)+N_C(\bar x)\).

notation.meaning: Convex-analytic normal cone to C at the candidate point.

review_flags: This record includes the deferred unconstrained condition as the special case C equal to the whole space.
knowledge_statements.title: Constrained DC Subgradient-Inclusion Condition
Necessary Local Optimality Families
knowledge_statements.scope_note: First-order necessary condition for an unconstrained finite DC problem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(g,h:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\) be convex and finite on a neighborhood of \(\bar x\), and set \(f=g-h\). If \(\bar x\) is a local minimizer of \(f\), then
\[
\partial h(\bar x)\subseteq\partial g(\bar x).
\]
Equivalently, every affine minorant of \(h\) supported at \(\bar x\) has the same slope as an affine minorant of \(g\) supported there. In particular, \(\partial g(\bar x)\cap\partial h(\bar x)\neq\varnothing\) whenever \(\partial h(\bar x)\neq\varnothing\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At a local minimizer of a finite DC function, every subgradient of the subtracted convex component is also a subgradient of the first component.
assumptions_latex: \(g\) and \(h\) are convex and finite near \(\bar x\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\partial h(\bar x)\subseteq\partial g(\bar x)\).

notation.meaning: Convex subdifferential of g at the candidate point.

review_flags: An exact DC optimality theorem locator is missing.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The theorem kind fits a necessary-optimality-family container, and the inclusion is a plausible finite-dimensional DC necessary condition under the stated local finiteness assumptions. No exact theorem citation or locator is supplied.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Uniform Directional-Growth Sufficiency
knowledge_statements.scope_note: First-order sharp-local-minimum condition for a finite unconstrained DC objective.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(g,h:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) be convex and finite near \(\bar x\), and set \(f=g-h\). If some \(\sigma>0\) satisfies \[g'(\bar x;d)-h'(\bar x;d)\geq\sigma\|d\|\qquad\text{for every }d\in\mathbb R^n,\] then, on some neighborhood \(U\) of \(\bar x\), \[f(x)\geq f(\bar x)+\frac{\sigma}{2}\|x-\bar x\|.\] Thus \(\bar x\) is a sharp strict local minimizer.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A uniform positive gap between the directional derivatives of the convex components gives linear local growth and a sharp strict local minimum.
assumptions_latex: \(g,h\) are convex and finite near \(\bar x\).
The displayed uniform directional gap holds for some \(\sigma>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \((g-h)(x)\geq(g-h)(\bar x)+(\sigma/2)\|x-\bar x\|\) locally.

notation.meaning: One-sided directional derivative of q at the reference point in direction d.

knowledge_statements.title: Uniform Directional-Growth Sufficiency

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Common-Subgradient Criticality Is Not Sufficient
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure boundary for weak DC criticality as a local-minimum certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(g(x)=0\), \(h(x)=|x|\), and \(f=g-h=-|x|\). At zero, \[\partial g(0)=\{0\},\qquad\partial h(0)=[-1,1],\qquad\partial g(0)\cap\partial h(0)=\{0\}.\] Thus the components have a common subgradient, but zero is a strict local maximum.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The downward absolute-value cusp has a common component subgradient at zero, although zero is a strict local maximum.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\partial g(0)\cap\partial h(0)\neq\varnothing\) but \(0\notin\operatorname*{argmin}_{\mathrm{loc}}f\).
knowledge_statements.title: Common-Subgradient Criticality Is Not Sufficient

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Curvature-Dominance Sufficiency
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Strong-convexity versus smoothness sufficient condition without boundary-subgradient ambiguity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(g:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) be \(\mu\)-strongly convex and let \(h:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) be differentiable with \(L\)-Lipschitz gradient. If \(\mu>L\) and \(\nabla h(\bar x)\in\partial g(\bar x)\), then for every \(x\in\mathbb R^n\), \[(g-h)(x)\geq(g-h)(\bar x)+\frac{\mu-L}{2}\|x-\bar x\|^2.\] Hence \(\bar x\) is the unique global minimizer and, in particular, a strict local minimizer.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Component stationarity is sufficient when the first component's strong convexity strictly dominates the subtracted component's gradient-Lipschitz curvature.
assumptions_latex: \(h:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) is differentiable with \(L\)-Lipschitz gradient.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \((g-h)(x)\geq(g-h)(\bar x)+\frac{\mu-L}{2}\|x-\bar x\|^2\) for every x.

notation.meaning: Lipschitz constant of the gradient of h.

review_flags: The whole-space formulation removes the deferred seed's relative-boundary convention ambiguity.
knowledge_statements.title: Curvature-Dominance Sufficiency
Sufficient Local Optimality Families
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Strong-convexity versus smoothness sufficient condition for DC minimality.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(C\subset\mathbb{R}^n\) be convex, let \(g:C\to\mathbb{R}\) be \(\mu\)-strongly convex, and let \(h:C\to\mathbb{R}\) be differentiable with \(L\)-Lipschitz gradient. If \(\mu>L\) and \(\nabla h(\bar x)\in\partial g(\bar x)\), then for every \(x\in C\),
\[
(g-h)(x)\geq(g-h)(\bar x)+\frac{\mu-L}{2}\|x-\bar x\|^2.
\]
Hence \(\bar x\) is the unique global minimizer on \(C\), and therefore a strict local minimizer, whenever \(C\) contains points other than \(\bar x\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: DC stationarity becomes sufficient when the first convex component is more strongly convex than the smoothness curvature of the subtracted component.
assumptions_latex: \(g\) is \(\mu\)-strongly convex on the convex set \(C\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \((g-h)(x)\geq(g-h)(\bar x)+\frac{\mu-L}{2}\|x-\bar x\|^2\) for all \(x\in C\).

notation.meaning: Lipschitz constant of the gradient of h.

review_flags: A source explicitly stating this DC sufficient condition is missing.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The theorem kind fits the sufficient-optimality container and the curvature comparison is plausible. A source is needed for the exact formulation, including whether gradients and subgradients on a possibly nonopen convex set C are ambient or relative and which boundary regularity is assumed.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Zero-Epsilon Inclusion Is Not Globally Sufficient
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure boundary showing why the global test requires every epsilon.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(g(x)=0\), \(h(x)=x^4\), and \(f=g-h=-x^4\). At \(\bar x=0\), \(\partial h(0)=\partial g(0)=\{0\}\), but \(f(x)<f(0)\) for every \(x\neq0\). Thus the inclusion at \(\varepsilon=0\) does not characterize global optimality.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Ordinary component-subgradient inclusion can hold at a strict maximum, so the global characterization genuinely needs all epsilon-subdifferentials.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\partial h(0)\subseteq\partial g(0)\) while \(0\notin\operatorname*{argmin}(g-h)\).
knowledge_statements.title: Zero-Epsilon Inclusion Is Not Globally Sufficient

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Finite-Valued Toland Dual Optimality Pairing
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Qualified primal-conjugate characterization for finite convex DC components.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(g,h:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) be finite closed convex functions. Then \[\inf_x\{g(x)-h(x)\}=\inf_y\{h^*(y)-g^*(y)\}.\] If \(\bar y\in\partial h(\bar x)\), then \(\bar x\) is a primal global minimizer and \(\bar y\) is a dual global minimizer if and only if \(\bar y\in\partial g(\bar x)\). For such a pair, \[g(\bar x)-h(\bar x)=h^*(\bar y)-g^*(\bar y).\] In particular, every primal global minimizer pairs with every element of \(\partial h(\bar x)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For finite closed convex components, primal and Toland-dual global minimizers are linked by a common component subgradient, and their objective values agree.
assumptions_latex: \(g,h:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) are finite closed convex functions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\bar x\in\operatorname*{argmin}(g-h)\) and \(\bar y\in\operatorname*{argmin}(h^*-g^*)\) exactly when \(\bar y\in\partial g(\bar x)\), with equality of the paired values.

notation.meaning: Fenchel conjugates of g and h.
Primal-dual pair linked by a common convex subgradient.

review_flags: This finite-valued theorem replaces the deferred unqualified extended-valued formulation; boundary-domain variants require additional nonemptiness and difference conventions.
knowledge_statements.title: Finite-Valued Toland Dual Optimality Pairing

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Epsilon-Subdifferential Global-Minimum Characterization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact global-optimality test for a finite unconstrained DC objective.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(g,h:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) be finite convex functions and let \(f=g-h\). Then \(\bar x\) globally minimizes \(f\) if and only if \[\partial_\varepsilon h(\bar x)\subseteq\partial_\varepsilon g(\bar x)\qquad\text{for every }\varepsilon\geq0.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A finite DC objective is globally minimized exactly when every epsilon-subgradient of the subtracted component is an epsilon-subgradient of the first component, for every nonnegative epsilon.
assumptions_latex: \(g,h:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) are finite convex functions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\bar x\in\operatorname*{argmin}(g-h)\iff(\forall\varepsilon\geq0)\;\partial_\varepsilon h(\bar x)\subseteq\partial_\varepsilon g(\bar x)\).

notation.meaning: Vectors v satisfying q(z) at least q(x) plus the inner product of v with z-x minus epsilon for every z.

review_flags: Restricted to finite convex components so the DC difference and all pointwise subdifferentials are unambiguous.
knowledge_statements.title: Epsilon-Subdifferential Global-Minimum Characterization
Global Optimality Characterizations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conjugate-space characterization of global minimizers for finite DC objectives.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(g,h:\mathbb{R}^n\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) be proper lower-semicontinuous convex functions and suppose \(\partial h(\bar x)\neq\varnothing\). Then \(\bar x\) globally minimizes \(g-h\) if and only if there exists \(\bar y\in\partial h(\bar x)\) such that \(\bar x\in\partial g^*(\bar y)\) and \(\bar y\) globally minimizes \(h^*-g^*\). For such a pair,
\[
g(\bar x)-h(\bar x)=h^*(\bar y)-g^*(\bar y)=\inf_x(g(x)-h(x))=\inf_y(h^*(y)-g^*(y)).
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A DC global minimizer corresponds to a conjugate-space global minimizer linked through reciprocal convex subgradient relations.
assumptions_latex: \(g\) and \(h\) are proper lower-semicontinuous convex functions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\bar x\in\operatorname*{argmin}(g-h)\) exactly when a linked \(\bar y\in\operatorname*{argmin}(h^*-g^*)\) exists.

notation.meaning: Fenchel conjugates of g and h.

review_flags: An authoritative DC duality locator and its qualification conditions are required.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: A duality characterization is an appropriate role for this leaf, but the extended-valued formulation does not specify where g-h and h*-g* are well-defined and may require domain or continuity qualifications for the asserted primal-dual equivalence and equality of infima. An authoritative DC duality theorem with exact hypotheses is required.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The feasible tangent geometry decomposes as \(T_C(\bar x)=\bigcup_{i\in I(\bar x)}K_i\). For every \(i\in I(\bar x)\) and \(d\in K_i\), the directional derivative satisfies \(f'(\bar x;d)=\langle\nabla f_i(\bar x),d\rangle\); compatibility of the continuous pieces makes this value independent of the selected active region when \(d\) lies in more than one active cone. Consequently, \(f'(\bar x;d)\geq0\) for every \(d\in T_C(\bar x)\) if and only if \(\langle\nabla f_i(\bar x),d\rangle\geq0\) for every \(i\in I(\bar x)\) and every \(d\in K_i\). This equivalence characterizes the active-region form of directional stationarity; by itself it does not assert local minimality.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The feasible tangent cone is the union of the active-region tangent cones. Directional stationarity can therefore be checked region by region, but this first-order test alone does not guarantee a local minimum.
knowledge_statements.title: Active-Region Optimality Geometry
