knowledge_statements.statement_title: Active-Cone Stationarity Need Not Give a Minimum
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Concrete failure boundary for the seed's nonnegative regionwise first-order test.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Take \(C=\mathbb R\), one polyhedral region \(P_1=\mathbb R\), and \(f_1(x)=-x^2\). At \(\bar x=0\), \(K_1=\mathbb R\) and \(\langle\nabla f_1(0),d\rangle=0\) for every \(d\in K_1\), so the active-cone directional-stationarity test holds. Nevertheless, \(f(x)<f(0)\) for every \(x\neq0\), and zero is a strict local maximum.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: All active-region first-order inequalities may hold at a strict local maximum.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\langle\nabla f_1(0),d\rangle\geq0\) for every \(d\in K_1\), but \(0\) is not a local minimizer.
knowledge_statements.title: Active-Cone Stationarity Need Not Give a Minimum

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Uniform Active-Cone Growth Certificate
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sharp local-minimum certificate for the seed's continuous piecewise-smooth active-region model.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Under the active-region assumptions of the accepted seed, suppose that some \(\sigma>0\) satisfies \[\langle\nabla f_i(\bar x),d\rangle\geq\sigma\|d\|\qquad(i\in I(\bar x),\ d\in K_i).\] Then, on some neighborhood \(V\) of \(\bar x\), \[f(x)\geq f(\bar x)+\frac{\sigma}{2}\|x-\bar x\|\qquad(x\in C\cap V).\] Hence \(\bar x\) is a sharp strict local minimizer over \(C\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Uniformly positive first-order growth on every active-region cone yields sharp local growth and strict local optimality.
assumptions_latex: The finite polyhedral active-region model and notation \(I(\bar x),K_i\) are those of the accepted seed.
Some \(\sigma>0\) satisfies the displayed inequality on every active cone.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(f(x)\geq f(\bar x)+(\sigma/2)\|x-\bar x\|\) locally on \(C\).

notation.meaning: Tangent cone to the feasible portion of active region i at the reference point.

knowledge_statements.title: Uniform Active-Cone Growth Certificate

children.title: DC Criticality Targets
children.top_down_role: Criticality concepts tied to a selected DC decomposition.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Criticality Can Change with the DC Decomposition
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Explicit demonstration that common-subgradient criticality is not intrinsic to the represented function.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the same function \(f(x)=x\), consider the decompositions \[f(x)=x-0\qquad\text{and}\qquad f(x)=(x+|x|)-|x|.\] At \(\bar x=0\), the first decomposition has component subdifferentials \(\{1\}\) and \(\{0\}\), whose intersection is empty. The second has component subdifferentials \([0,2]\) and \([-1,1]\), whose intersection is \([0,1]\). Hence zero is DC-critical for the second decomposition but not for the first, although both represent the same function.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The linear function is critical at zero under one valid DC decomposition and noncritical there under another.
assumptions_latex: Both displayed component pairs consist of finite convex functions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(0\) is decomposition-relative DC-critical for \((x+|x|)-|x|\) but not for \(x-0\).
knowledge_statements.title: Criticality Can Change with the DC Decomposition

assumptions_latex: \(g,h:\mathbb R^n\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) are proper lower-semicontinuous convex functions, and \(f=g-h\) is finite at \(\bar x\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\bar x\) is critical relative to the displayed decomposition exactly when \(\partial g(\bar x)\cap\partial h(\bar x)\neq\varnothing\).
review_flags: definition depends on the selected DC decomposition
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Classical convex-subdifferential criticality for a fixed DC decomposition.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The point \(\bar x\) is DC-critical relative to the specified decomposition \(f=g-h\) when there exists \(y\in\mathbb R^n\) satisfying \(y\in\partial g(\bar x)\cap\partial h(\bar x)\). Equivalently, \(0\in\partial g(\bar x)-\partial h(\bar x)\), where the right-hand side is the Minkowski difference. This predicate is decomposition-relative: replacing \((g,h)\) by another convex pair representing the same function may alter the two subdifferentials and hence the set of certified critical points.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a fixed DC decomposition, a point is critical when the two convex components have a common subgradient there; this status may change under another decomposition.
knowledge_statements.title: Decomposition-Relative DC Criticality

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The fixed-decomposition common-subgradient definition and its Minkowski-difference equivalence are coherent, and content_kind definition fits the leaf. An authoritative DC-specific citation with a precise locator is required before candidate-review acceptance.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Fenchel-Gap Residual for a Candidate Critical Pair
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Nonnegative scalar certificate extending the exact Fenchel equalities to approximate candidate pairs.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For proper closed convex \(g,h\), define \[\Delta_g(x,y)=g(x)+g^*(y)-\langle x,y\rangle,\qquad \Delta_h(x,y)=h(x)+h^*(y)-\langle x,y\rangle.\] Whenever finite, both gaps are nonnegative, and \[\Delta_g(x,y)+\Delta_h(x,y)=0\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad y\in\partial g(x)\cap\partial h(x).\] Thus their sum is an exact scalar residual for a proposed primal–dual DC critical pair. Without additional curvature or error-bound assumptions, a small positive gap need not control a normwise subgradient mismatch.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The sum of the two Fenchel–Young gaps is nonnegative and vanishes exactly when the dual vector supports both convex components.
assumptions_latex: Both displayed Fenchel gaps are finite at \((x,y)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\Delta_g(x,y)+\Delta_h(x,y)=0\iff y\in\partial g(x)\cap\partial h(x)\).
knowledge_statements.title: Fenchel-Gap Residual for a Candidate Critical Pair

assumptions_latex: \(g,h:\mathbb R^n\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) are proper closed convex functions, and \(f=g-h\) is finite at \(\bar x\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \((\bar x,\bar y)\) is a primal-dual DC critical pair exactly when \(\bar y\in\partial g(\bar x)\cap\partial h(\bar x)\).

notation.meaning: Fenchel conjugates of the convex components

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Fenchel-equality certificate for criticality of a fixed DC decomposition.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A pair \((\bar x,\bar y)\in\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb R^n\) is a primal-dual DC critical pair when \(\bar y\in\partial g(\bar x)\) and \(\bar y\in\partial h(\bar x)\). By Fenchel equality, these two memberships are equivalently verified by \(g(\bar x)+g^*(\bar y)=\langle\bar x,\bar y\rangle\) and \(h(\bar x)+h^*(\bar y)=\langle\bar x,\bar y\rangle\). Thus the dual vector simultaneously supports both convex components at the primal point and certifies decomposition-relative DC criticality.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A primal-dual critical pair consists of a point and one dual vector supporting both convex components, equivalently satisfying both Fenchel equalities.
knowledge_statements.title: Primal–Dual DC Critical Pairs

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The common-subgradient pair and the two Fenchel equalities form a valid certificate for a fixed closed-convex DC decomposition, and content_kind certificate is appropriate. No source is supplied for the DC-specific terminology or formulation.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Ordinary DC Criticality Need Not Satisfy Subdifferential Inclusion
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Strict separation between common-subgradient criticality and the proposed inclusion-based strong condition.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(g(x)=0\), \(h(x)=|x|\), and \(\bar x=0\). Then \[\partial g(0)=\{0\},\qquad \partial h(0)=[-1,1].\] Their intersection is nonempty, so zero is decomposition-relative DC-critical. However, \(\partial h(0)\nsubseteq\partial g(0)\), so it fails the proposed inclusion-based strong condition. Moreover, \(g-h=-|x|\) has a strict local maximum at zero.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For minus absolute value, the component subdifferentials intersect but do not satisfy inclusion.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\partial g(0)\cap\partial h(0)\ne\varnothing\) but \(\partial h(0)\nsubseteq\partial g(0)\).
knowledge_statements.title: Ordinary DC Criticality Need Not Satisfy Subdifferential Inclusion

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Local Minimality Implies Component-Subdifferential Inclusion
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Terminology-independent necessary condition underlying the proposed inclusion-based strong-criticality convention.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(g,h\) be proper convex functions, suppose \(f=g-h\) is finite on a neighborhood of \(\bar x\), and let \(\bar x\) be a local minimizer of \(f\). Then \[\partial h(\bar x)\subseteq\partial g(\bar x).\] Consequently, when \(\partial h(\bar x)\ne\varnothing\), local minimality implies the proposed inclusion-based strong condition and ordinary decomposition-relative criticality.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At a local minimizer of a fixed DC decomposition, every subgradient of the subtracted component also supports the first component.
assumptions_latex: \(f=g-h\) is finite on a neighborhood of \(\bar x\).
\(\bar x\) is a local minimizer of \(f\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\partial h(\bar x)\subseteq\partial g(\bar x)\).
knowledge_statements.title: Local Minimality Implies Component-Subdifferential Inclusion

assumptions_latex: \(g,h:\mathbb R^n\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) are proper lower-semicontinuous convex functions, and \(f=g-h\) is finite at \(\bar x\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\bar x\) is strongly DC-critical when \(\partial h(\bar x)\neq\varnothing\) and \(\partial h(\bar x)\subseteq\partial g(\bar x)\).
review_flags: authoritative source required for inclusion-based definition
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Inclusion-based strong criticality for a fixed convex DC decomposition.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The point \(\bar x\) is strongly DC-critical relative to \(f=g-h\) when \(\partial h(\bar x)\) is nonempty and every subgradient of the subtracted component is also a subgradient of the first component: \(\partial h(\bar x)\subseteq\partial g(\bar x)\). This condition implies ordinary decomposition-relative criticality because any \(y\in\partial h(\bar x)\) then belongs to \(\partial g(\bar x)\cap\partial h(\bar x)\). The converse generally fails when the two subdifferentials merely intersect without satisfying inclusion.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Strong DC criticality requires every subgradient of the subtracted convex component to support the first component, and therefore implies ordinary DC criticality.
knowledge_statements.title: Strong DC Criticality

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The inclusion condition implies ordinary decomposition-relative criticality as stated, but the term strong DC criticality is not uniform across the literature. The exact inclusion-based definition requires an authoritative source and locator.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The feasible point \(\bar x\) is directionally stationary for minimizing \(f\) over \(C\) when \[f'(\bar x;d)=\lim_{t\downarrow0}\frac{f(\bar x+td)-f(\bar x)}{t}\geq0\qquad\text{for every }d\in T_C(\bar x).\] Thus no Bouligand tangent direction has a strictly negative ambient directional derivative.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A feasible point is directionally stationary when the ambient objective has no negative one-sided directional derivative along any Bouligand tangent direction.
knowledge_statements.title: Directional Stationarity

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Directional Stationarity Is Not Sufficient for Local Minimality
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Elementary unconstrained separation between directional stationarity and local optimality.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(f(x)=x^3\) on \(\mathbb R\), \[f'(0;d)=0\qquad(d\in\mathbb R),\] so \(0\) is directionally stationary. Nevertheless \(f(x)<f(0)\) for every \(x<0\), hence \(0\) is not a local minimizer.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The cubic origin passes every first-order directional test but is not a local minimum.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: f'(0;d)=0\ \forall d,\qquad 0\text{ is not a local minimizer}.
knowledge_statements.title: Directional Stationarity Is Not Sufficient for Local Minimality

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Local Minimizers Are Directionally Stationary
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Necessary condition using feasible tangent directions and Hadamard directional derivatives.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C\subset\mathbb R^n\) be closed, let \(\bar x\in C\) be a local minimizer of \(f\) over \(C\), and suppose the Hadamard directional derivative \(f'_H(\bar x;d)\) exists for every \(d\in T_C(\bar x)\). Then \[f'_H(\bar x;d)\ge0\qquad(d\in T_C(\bar x)).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A constrained local minimizer has no feasible tangent direction with a negative Hadamard directional derivative.
assumptions_latex: C\subset\mathbb R^n\text{ is closed and }\bar x\in C.
\bar x\text{ is a local minimizer of }f\text{ over }C.
f'_H(\bar x;d)\text{ exists for every }d\in T_C(\bar x).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: f'_H(\bar x;d)\ge0\quad\forall d\in T_C(\bar x).
knowledge_statements.title: Local Minimizers Are Directionally Stationary

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Smooth Constrained Bouligand Stationarity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Standard Bouligand-stationarity convention for a differentiable objective on a closed, possibly nonconvex feasible set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C\subset\mathbb R^n\) be closed, let \(f\) be continuously differentiable near \(\bar x\in C\), and let \(T_C(\bar x)\) be the Bouligand tangent cone. The point \(\bar x\) is Bouligand stationary when \[\langle\nabla f(\bar x),d\rangle\geq0\qquad\text{for every }d\in T_C(\bar x).\] Equivalently, \[-\nabla f(\bar x)\in\widehat N_C(\bar x)=T_C(\bar x)^\circ,\] or \(0\in\widehat\partial(f+\delta_C)(\bar x)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a smooth objective, Bouligand stationarity means that the gradient has no negative pairing with any Bouligand tangent direction; equivalently, its negative is a regular normal.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is continuously differentiable near \(\bar x\in C\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\langle\nabla f(\bar x),d\rangle\geq0\ \forall d\in T_C(\bar x)\iff-\nabla f(\bar x)\in\widehat N_C(\bar x)\iff0\in\widehat\partial(f+\delta_C)(\bar x)\).

notation.meaning: Bouligand or contingent tangent cone to C.
Fréchet regular normal cone, equal to the polar of the Bouligand tangent cone.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The feasible point \(\bar x\) is Bouligand stationary when \(0\in\widehat\partial F(\bar x)\), meaning \[\liminf_{x\to\bar x,\,x\neq\bar x}\frac{F(x)-F(\bar x)}{\lVert x-\bar x\rVert}\geq0.\] If \(f\) is locally Lipschitz and directionally differentiable at \(\bar x\), and the feasible tangent approximation is exact for first-order arcs, this condition is equivalent to \(f'(\bar x;d)\geq0\) for every \(d\in T_C(\bar x)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Bouligand stationarity requires zero to be a regular subgradient of the constrained objective; under standard directional regularity it equals directional stationarity.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: For a general proper lower-semicontinuous extended-real objective, membership of zero in the regular subdifferential is Fréchet regular-subgradient stationarity; it is not, without substantially stronger structure, the standard Bouligand tangent-direction stationarity condition. The asserted equivalence under the vague 'exact first-order arcs' qualification is unsupported and not valid at this level of generality.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The feasible point \(\bar x\) is limiting-subdifferential stationary for minimizing \(f\) over \(C\) when \(0\in\partial F(\bar x)\). Here \(v\in\partial F(\bar x)\) means that sequences \(x_k\to\bar x\), \(F(x_k)\to F(\bar x)\), and \(v_k\to v\) exist with \(v_k\in\widehat\partial F(x_k)\). Since \(\widehat\partial F(\bar x)\subseteq\partial F(\bar x)\), Bouligand stationarity implies limiting-subdifferential stationarity whenever both are expressed through these subdifferentials.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Limiting stationarity means zero is a limit of regular subgradients at nearby objective-consistent points; regular-subgradient stationarity implies it.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Limiting Stationarity Is Not Sufficient for Local Minimality
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Smooth boundary showing that a zero limiting subgradient is only a first-order certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(F(x)=-x^2\) on \(\mathbb R\), \[\partial F(0)=\{0\},\] so \(0\) is limiting-subdifferential stationary. Yet \(F(x)<F(0)\) for every \(x\ne0\), and therefore \(0\) is a strict local maximizer rather than a local minimizer.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A zero limiting subgradient can occur at a strict local maximum, so limiting stationarity does not certify optimality.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: 0\in\partial F(0),\qquad 0\text{ is not a local minimizer}.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The point \(\bar x\) is Clarke stationary when \(0\in\partial^{\mathrm C}F(\bar x)\). For a finite locally Lipschitz function, \[\partial^{\mathrm C}F(\bar x)=\{v\in\mathbb R^n:\langle v,d\rangle\leq F^{\circ}(\bar x;d)\text{ for every }d\in\mathbb R^n\}.\] In finite dimensions, \(\partial^{\mathrm C}F(\bar x)=\operatorname{co}\partial F(\bar x)\). Hence \(0\in\partial F(\bar x)\) implies Clarke stationarity, whereas the converse can fail.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a finite locally Lipschitz objective, Clarke stationarity places zero in the Clarke subdifferential, which is the convex hull of the limiting subdifferential in finite dimensions; limiting stationarity therefore implies Clarke stationarity, but not conversely.
knowledge_statements.title: Clarke Stationarity

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let $\mathcal O\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ be open and convex, and let $f:\mathcal O\to\mathbb R$ be a DC function. Then the following are equivalent: (i) $f$ is Clarke regular; (ii) $f$ is favorable; and (iii) $f$ is dd-convex.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Stationarity equivalence for favorable DC functions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conditional equivalence of three constrained stationarity notions, including the stated weakly convex quadratic-DC specialization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let $X\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ be closed and convex, let $f$ be a favorable DC function on $X$, and let $\bar x\in X$. In particular, the equivalence holds if $f$ is $\varphi$-weakly convex with the DC decomposition $(f+\sigma\|\cdot\|^2)-\sigma\|\cdot\|^2$ for some $\sigma>0$.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a favorable DC objective over a closed convex set, d-stationarity, DC criticality, and Clarke stationarity coincide. The same conclusion applies to the stated quadratic DC decomposition of a varphi-weakly convex function.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Coincidence Under Explicit Subdifferential and Directional Regularity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Unconstrained locally Lipschitz functions under explicit regularity equalities, avoiding dependence on an ambiguous regularity convention.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) be locally Lipschitz and directionally differentiable at \(\bar x\). Assume \(\widehat\partial F(\bar x)=\partial F(\bar x)\) and \(F'(\bar x;d)=F^\circ(\bar x;d)\) for every \(d\). Since \(\partial^{\mathrm C}F(\bar x)=\operatorname{co}\partial F(\bar x)\) and \(\widehat\partial F(\bar x)\) is convex, \[\widehat\partial F(\bar x)=\partial F(\bar x)=\partial^{\mathrm C}F(\bar x).\] Consequently, regular-subdifferential, limiting-subdifferential, Clarke, and directional stationarity are equivalent at \(\bar x\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: When the regular and limiting subdifferentials agree and the ordinary and Clarke directional derivatives agree, all four stationarity tests coincide.
assumptions_latex: F\text{ is locally Lipschitz and directionally differentiable at }\bar x.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: 0\in\widehat\partial F(\bar x)\iff0\in\partial F(\bar x)\iff0\in\partial^{\mathrm C}F(\bar x)\iff F'(\bar x;d)\ge0\ \forall d.
knowledge_statements.title: Coincidence Under Explicit Subdifferential and Directional Regularity

assumptions_latex: \(F:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) is locally Lipschitz, directionally differentiable, and subdifferentially regular at \(\bar x\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Directional, Bouligand, limiting-subdifferential, and Clarke stationarity coincide at \(\bar x\).
review_flags: verify regularity convention ensuring equality with Clarke subdifferential
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Unconstrained locally Lipschitz functions regular in the standard variational sense.

source_refs.locator: 3.4.2 Relationship Between Quasidifferential and Clarke Subdifferential p. 109
source_refs.source_title: Introduction to Nonsmooth Optimization: Theory, Practice and Software

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Subdifferential regularity and local Lipschitz continuity yield \[\widehat\partial F(\bar x)=\partial F(\bar x)=\partial^{\mathrm C}F(\bar x).\] Directional regularity also gives \(F'(\bar x;d)=F^{\circ}(\bar x;d)\) for every \(d\in\mathbb R^n\). Consequently, \(F'(\bar x;d)\geq0\) for all \(d\) is equivalent to \(0\in\widehat\partial F(\bar x)\), and the displayed equality makes this equivalent to both limiting-subdifferential and Clarke stationarity.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At a locally Lipschitz, directionally differentiable, subdifferentially regular point, the directional, regular, limiting, and Clarke stationarity tests agree.
knowledge_statements.title: Regular Coincidence Regimes

source_witnesses.locator: 3.4.2 Relationship Between Quasidifferential and Clarke Subdifferential p. 109

A precise authoritative source is required.

children.title: Coincidence Breakdown Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Loss of structural conditions needed for stationarity notions to coincide.

assumptions_latex: \(F:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R\) is defined by \(F(x)=-|x|\), and the reference point is \(\bar x=0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(0\in\partial^{\mathrm C}F(0)\) but \(0\notin\partial F(0)\) and \(F'(0;d)<0\) for every \(d\neq0\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Concrete one-dimensional separation caused by failure of subdifferential regularity.

source_refs.locator: 3.4.2 Relationship Between Quasidifferential and Clarke Subdifferential p. 109
source_refs.source_title: Introduction to Nonsmooth Optimization: Theory, Practice and Software

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At \(0\), the directional derivative is \(F'(0;d)=-|d|\), so directional stationarity fails. The limiting subdifferential is \(\partial F(0)=\{-1,1\}\), hence limiting-subdifferential stationarity also fails. However, convexification gives \(\partial^{\mathrm C}F(0)=[-1,1]\), so \(0\in\partial^{\mathrm C}F(0)\) and Clarke stationarity holds. Thus loss of subdifferential regularity permits Clarke stationarity without limiting or directional stationarity.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For the downward cusp minus absolute value at zero, Clarke stationarity holds although limiting and directional stationarity fail, marking a regularity breakdown boundary.
knowledge_statements.title: Coincidence Breakdown Boundaries

source_witnesses.locator: 3.4.2 Relationship Between Quasidifferential and Clarke Subdifferential p. 109

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Limiting Stationarity Without Regular or Directional Stationarity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A nonregular one-dimensional separation complementary to the Clarke-versus-limiting cusp example owned by the breakdown-boundary leaf.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F(x)=x-|x|\) and \(\bar x=0\). Then \(\widehat\partial F(0)=\varnothing\), \(\partial F(0)=\{0,2\}\), and \(\partial^{\mathrm C}F(0)=[0,2]\). Hence \(0\in\partial F(0)\) and \(0\in\partial^{\mathrm C}F(0)\), but regular-subdifferential stationarity fails. Moreover, \(F'(0;d)=d-|d|\), which is negative for every \(d<0\), so directional stationarity fails.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At the kink of x minus absolute value, limiting and Clarke stationarity hold while regular and directional stationarity fail.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: 0\in\partial F(0)\cap\partial^{\mathrm C}F(0),\qquad 0\notin\widehat\partial F(0),\qquad \exists d:\ F'(0;d)<0.
knowledge_statements.title: Limiting Stationarity Without Regular or Directional Stationarity
Nonregular Stationarity Separations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Separates Clarke stationarity from directional stationarity at a nonregular DC point.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R\) be the DC function \(f(x)=-|x|=0-|x|\). At \(\bar x=0\), its Clarke subdifferential is \(\partial_C f(0)=[-1,1]\), so \(0\in\partial_C f(0)\). Nevertheless, the directional derivative satisfies \(f'(0;d)=-|d|<0\) for every \(d\ne0\). Thus Clarke stationarity does not imply the directional necessary condition \(f'(\bar x;d)\ge0\) for all directions when Clarke regularity fails.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For negative absolute value, zero is Clarke stationary but admits strict descent in every nonzero direction, separating Clarke and directional stationarity.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(0\in\partial_C f(0)\), while \(f'(0;d)<0\) for every \(d\ne0\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The counterexample is mathematically correct and fits the separation container, but it has no citation or inspectable locator.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Equivalent Decompositions Can Reverse DC Criticality
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Decomposition dependence of the component-subdifferential intersection certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f(x)=x\) and \(\bar x=0\). For \(f=g_1-h_1\), where \(g_1(x)=x\) and \(h_1(x)=0\), \(\partial g_1(0)=\{1\}\) and \(\partial h_1(0)=\{0\}\), so their intersection is empty. For the equivalent decomposition \(f=g_2-h_2\), where \(g_2(x)=x+|x|\) and \(h_2(x)=|x|\), \(\partial g_2(0)=[0,2]\) and \(\partial h_2(0)=[-1,1]\), so their intersection is \([0,1]\). Thus the certificate \(\partial g(\bar x)\cap\partial h(\bar x)\ne\varnothing\) is not invariant under equivalent DC decompositions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The same affine function satisfies the component-subdifferential DC-criticality test under one convex decomposition but not another.
assumptions_latex: \(f=g-h\) with finite convex components near \(\bar x\).
DC criticality for the selected decomposition means \(\partial g(\bar x)\cap\partial h(\bar x)\ne\varnothing\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \partial g_1(0)\cap\partial h_1(0)=\varnothing,\qquad \partial g_2(0)\cap\partial h_2(0)=[0,1].

notation.meaning: the j-th convex decomposition of f

knowledge_statements.title: Equivalent Decompositions Can Reverse DC Criticality
Decomposition-Induced Stationarity Gaps
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Shows that DC criticality can depend on the selected convex decomposition.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \(f(x)=x\) at \(\bar x=0\). For the decomposition \(f=g_1-h_1\) with \(g_1(x)=x\) and \(h_1(x)=0\), one has \(\partial g_1(0)=\{1\}\) and \(\partial h_1(0)=\{0\}\), so their intersection is empty. For the equivalent decomposition \(f=g_2-h_2\) with \(g_2(x)=x+|x|\) and \(h_2(x)=|x|\), one has \(\partial g_2(0)=[0,2]\) and \(\partial h_2(0)=[-1,1]\), whose intersection is nonempty. Hence decomposition-based DC criticality is not intrinsic to \(f\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The same affine function is DC-critical at zero under one convex decomposition but not another.
assumptions_latex: DC criticality means \(\partial g(\bar x)\cap\partial h(\bar x)\ne\varnothing\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\partial g_1(0)\cap\partial h_1(0)=\varnothing\), whereas \(\partial g_2(0)\cap\partial h_2(0)\ne\varnothing\).

notation.meaning: the j-th convex decomposition of f

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Both convex decompositions and their subdifferentials are correct, and the counterexample fits the container. An authoritative source with a specific locator is still required.

children.title: Constrained DC Criticality
children.top_down_role: Criticality systems for convex-constrained, DC-constrained, and penalized models.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Feasible-Direction Criticality Is Not Sufficient
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Elementary failure of sufficiency for the directional first-order condition.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C=\mathbb R\) and \(f(x)=-x^2=g(x)-h(x)\), with \(g=0\) and \(h(x)=x^2\). At \(\bar x=0\), \(T_C(0)=\mathbb R\) and \(f'(0;d)=0\) for every \(d\). Thus \(0\) is feasible-direction critical although it is a strict local maximizer and not a local minimizer.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The negative quadratic is directionally critical at its strict maximum, so feasible-direction criticality alone does not certify local minimality.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(f'(0;d)\ge0\) for all \(d\in T_C(0)\), but \(0\) is not a local minimizer.
knowledge_statements.title: Feasible-Direction Criticality Is Not Sufficient
Feasible-Direction Criticality
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Directional first-order condition for a DC objective over a closed feasible set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(C\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be closed, let \(f=g-h\) with finite convex directionally differentiable functions \(g,h\), and let \(\bar x\in C\). The point \(\bar x\) is feasible-direction critical when
\[g'(\bar x;d)-h'(\bar x;d)=f'(\bar x;d)\ge0\qquad\text{for every }d\in T_C(\bar x),\]
where \(T_C(\bar x)\) is the Bouligand tangent cone. Equivalently, no feasible tangent direction has strictly negative directional derivative.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A feasible point is directionally critical when the DC directional derivative is nonnegative along every tangent direction.
assumptions_latex: \(C\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) is closed and \(\bar x\in C\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(f'(\bar x;d)\ge0\) for all \(d\in T_C(\bar x)\).

notation.meaning: Bouligand tangent cone to C at the feasible point
directional derivative of the DC objective

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition is internally coherent and correctly distinguished from multiplier criticality, but the selected feasible-direction criticality convention needs an authoritative DC-optimization locator.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Multiplier Criticality Does Not Imply Minimality
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Active constrained example showing that the DC multiplier system is not sufficient for local optimality.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Minimize \(f(x)=-x^2=0-x^2\) subject to \(c(x)=x\le0\), represented by \(g_1(x)=x\) and \(h_1(x)=0\). At \(\bar x=0\), the constraint is active. Choosing \(v_0=0\), \(v_1=0\), and \(\lambda_1=0\) satisfies the multiplier-based DC stationarity and complementarity system. Nevertheless, \(0\) is a strict local maximizer relative to the feasible half-line \(( -\infty,0]\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The constrained multiplier system can hold at a strict feasible local maximum.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\bar x=0\) is multiplier-based DC-critical but is not a local minimizer over \(\{x:x\le0\}\).
knowledge_statements.title: Multiplier Criticality Does Not Imply Minimality

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Convex-Set and Affine-Equality Multiplier Form
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Extension of selected-subgradient DC criticality to a convex base set and affine equalities.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider minimizing \(g_0-h_0\) over a closed convex set \(X\), subject to \(g_i-h_i\le0\) for \(i=1,\ldots,m\) and \(Ax=b\). A feasible point \(\bar x\) has the extended multiplier-based DC criticality representation if there exist \(v_i\in\partial h_i(\bar x)\), \(\lambda_i\ge0\), and \(\mu\) such that \[0\in\partial g_0(\bar x)-v_0+\sum_{i=1}^m\lambda_i\bigl(\partial g_i(\bar x)-v_i\bigr)+A^\top\mu+N_X(\bar x),\qquad \lambda_i(g_i(\bar x)-h_i(\bar x))=0.\] Taking \(X=\mathbb R^n\) and omitting the affine equality recovers the inequality-only form.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A convex-set normal and free affine-equality multiplier append to the selected-subgradient DC KKT inclusion.
assumptions_latex: The convex components are subdifferentiable at \(\bar x\).
\(\bar x\in X\), \(A\bar x=b\), and all DC inequalities are feasible.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed stationarity, feasibility, sign, and complementarity system is the extended multiplier-based DC criticality representation.

notation.meaning: convex normal cone to the base set
free multiplier for the affine equality

knowledge_statements.title: Convex-Set and Affine-Equality Multiplier Form
Multiplier-Based DC Criticality
knowledge_statements.scope_note: KKT-type criticality for inequality-constrained DC programs with selected subgradients of the subtracted convex terms.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Consider minimizing \(g_0-h_0\) subject to \(g_i-h_i\le 0\) for \(i=1,\ldots,m\), where \(g_i,h_i:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) are convex for \(i=0,\ldots,m\). A feasible point \(\bar x\) is multiplier-based DC-critical if there exist \(v_i\in\partial h_i(\bar x)\) for \(i=0,\ldots,m\) and \(\lambda_i\ge 0\) for \(i=1,\ldots,m\) such that
\[0\in\partial g_0(\bar x)-v_0+\sum_{i=1}^m\lambda_i\bigl(\partial g_i(\bar x)-v_i\bigr),\qquad \lambda_i\bigl(g_i(\bar x)-h_i(\bar x)\bigr)=0\quad(i=1,\ldots,m).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A feasible point is multiplier-based DC-critical when selected subgradients of all subtracted convex terms and nonnegative complementary inequality multipliers satisfy the convexified KKT inclusion.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\exists v_i\in\partial h_i(\bar x)\ (i=0,\ldots,m)\) and \(\exists\lambda_i\ge0\ (i=1,\ldots,m)\) satisfying the displayed stationarity and complementarity conditions.

notation.meaning: selected subgradient of the subtracted convex term h_i

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Selection Dependence of a Linearized DC Qualification
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Duplicated DC constraints showing that a selectionwise qualification depends on the chosen subgradients of the subtracted components.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider two identical constraints \(g_i(x)-h_i(x)=-|x|\le0\), where \(g_i=0\) and \(h_i=|\cdot|\), at \(\bar x=0\). Both are active and \(\partial h_i(0)=[-1,1]\). For \((v_1,v_2)=(1,1)\), every \(d>0\) satisfies \(g_i'(0;d)-v_i d=-d<0\) for both indices. For \((v_1,v_2)=(1,-1)\), the required inequalities are \(-d<0\) and \(d<0\), which have no common solution. Thus the selectionwise strict-direction condition can hold or fail at the same feasible point and decomposition solely according to the selected subgradients.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The same active DC constraints can pass or fail a selectionwise linearized qualification under different valid subgradient selections.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The strict-direction condition holds for \((v_1,v_2)=(1,1)\) and fails for \((v_1,v_2)=(1,-1)\).

notation.meaning: selected subgradient of the subtracted constraint component

knowledge_statements.title: Selection Dependence of a Linearized DC Qualification
Constraint-Qualification Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A selection-dependent DC analogue of Mangasarian–Fromovitz constraint qualification.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For feasible \(\bar x\), define \(I(\bar x)=\{i:g_i(\bar x)-h_i(\bar x)=0\}\) and fix \(v_i\in\partial h_i(\bar x)\). The linearized DC-MFCQ holds for these selections if there exists \(d\in\mathbb R^n\) such that
\[g_i'(\bar x;d)-\langle v_i,d\rangle<0\qquad\text{for every }i\in I(\bar x).\]
With equality constraints \(A x=b\), one additionally requires \(A d=0\) and full row rank of \(A\). This qualification excludes abnormal multipliers for the selected convexification.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: DC-MFCQ requires a direction strictly decreasing every active convexified inequality while respecting independent linear equalities.
assumptions_latex: Each constraint has the form \(g_i-h_i\le0\) with convex \(g_i,h_i\).
A selection \(v_i\in\partial h_i(\bar x)\) is fixed for every active constraint.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A direction \(d\) satisfies all displayed strict linearized inequalities and, when present, \(A d=0\).

notation.meaning: selected subgradient used to convexify h_i

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The displayed selection-dependent linearized condition is plausible, but both its designation as DC-MFCQ and the abnormal-multiplier conclusion depend on the precise literature convention and require a specific source.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Penalized Stationarity Does Not Ensure Feasibility
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of the penalty-to-KKT implication when feasibility is not separately imposed.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f(x)=0\), \(c(x)=1-x^2\), and \(P_\rho(x)=\rho[1-x^2]_+\) with \(\rho>0\). The feasible set of \(c(x)\le0\) is \(\{|x|\ge1\}\), so \(x=0\) is infeasible. Nevertheless, near zero \(P_\rho(x)=\rho(1-x^2)\), and therefore \(0\in\partial_C P_\rho(0)=\{0\}\). Thus stationarity of the hinge penalty alone does not imply feasibility or a KKT certificate for the original problem.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A smooth hinge penalty can be stationary at an infeasible point, so feasibility is indispensable in the penalty-to-KKT direction.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(0\in\partial_C P_\rho(0)\) while \(c(0)=1>0\).
knowledge_statements.title: Penalized Stationarity Does Not Ensure Feasibility
Penalty–Stationarity Correspondence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Smooth exact-penalty correspondence between KKT stationarity and penalized stationarity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f,c_1,\ldots,c_m:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) be continuously differentiable DC functions and define \(P_\rho(x)=f(x)+\rho\sum_i[c_i(x)]_+\). If feasible \(\bar x\) satisfies KKT stationarity with multipliers \(\lambda_i\ge0\), then \(0\in\partial_C P_\rho(\bar x)\) for every \(\rho\ge\max_i\lambda_i\). Conversely, if \(\bar x\) is feasible and \(0\in\partial_C P_\rho(\bar x)\), then there exist \(0\le\lambda_i\le\rho\), vanishing on inactive constraints, such that \(\nabla f(\bar x)+\sum_i\lambda_i\nabla c_i(\bar x)=0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At a feasible smooth point, KKT stationarity and Clarke stationarity of the hinge penalty correspond when the penalty dominates the multipliers.
assumptions_latex: \(f,c_i\) are continuously differentiable and \(\bar x\) is feasible.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: KKT multipliers bounded by \(\rho\) are equivalent to Clarke stationarity of \(P_\rho\) at \(\bar x\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The smooth hinge-penalty correspondence is mathematically plausible and the theorem kind fits the container, but the bidirectional Clarke-subdifferential claim requires an authoritative theorem or section locator.

children.title: Algorithmic Criticality Certificates
children.top_down_role: Computable certificate families used for termination and complexity measurement.

children.title: DC Step Residuals
children.top_down_role: Residual measures derived from displacement across a DC algorithmic iteration.

knowledge_statements.title: DC Step Residuals
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Residual generated by one selected proximal DC convexification step.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(g,h:\mathbb R^n\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) be proper closed convex functions, let \(x\in\operatorname{dom}g\), choose \(y\in\partial h(x)\), and let \(\alpha>0\). Define the proximal DC update
\[x^+=\operatorname*{argmin}_{z\in\mathbb R^n}\left\{g(z)-\langle y,z\rangle+\frac{1}{2\alpha}\|z-x\|^2\right\}\]
and the selected-step residual \(R_{\mathrm{step}}(x;y,x^+)=\alpha^{-1}\|x^+-x\|\). Then
\[R_{\mathrm{step}}(x;y,x^+)=0\iff y\in\partial g(x).\]
Because \(y\in\partial h(x)\), vanishing of the residual certifies \(\partial g(x)\cap\partial h(x)\ne\varnothing\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The scaled displacement of a selected proximal DC step vanishes exactly when its selected subgradient also belongs to the objective's first convex subdifferential, thereby certifying DC criticality.
assumptions_latex: \(g,h:\mathbb R^n\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) are proper closed convex functions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(R_{\mathrm{step}}(x;y,x^+)=0\iff y\in\partial g(x)\), and hence \(\partial g(x)\cap\partial h(x)\ne\varnothing\).

children.title: DC Fixed-Point Residuals
children.top_down_role: Residual measures associated with fixed-point characterizations of DC updates.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Closedness Boundary for Distance Residuals
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact zero-set boundary for the distance-to-update-set certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(T_\alpha(x)\subset\mathbb R^n\) be nonempty and let \(R_{\mathrm{fp}}(x)=\alpha^{-1}\operatorname{dist}(x,T_\alpha(x))\), where \(\alpha>0\). Without closedness, \[R_{\mathrm{fp}}(x)=0\iff x\in\overline{T_\alpha(x)}.\] Hence distance zero certifies an actual fixed point only under closedness of \(T_\alpha(x)\), or another condition implying \(x\in\overline{T_\alpha(x)}\Rightarrow x\in T_\alpha(x)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Distance zero detects membership in the closure of the update set and detects a genuine fixed point only under an appropriate closedness condition.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(R_{\mathrm{fp}}(x)=0\iff x\in\overline{T_\alpha(x)}\); if \(T_\alpha(x)\) is closed, this is equivalent to \(x\in T_\alpha(x)\).

notation.meaning: closure of the DC update-value set at x

knowledge_statements.title: Closedness Boundary for Distance Residuals
DC Fixed-Point Residuals
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Set-valued fixed-point residual for the proximal DC update map.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(g,h:\mathbb R^n\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) be proper closed convex functions and let \(\alpha>0\). Define
\[T_\alpha(x)=\bigcup_{y\in\partial h(x)}\operatorname*{argmin}_{z\in\mathbb R^n}\left\{g(z)-\langle y,z\rangle+\frac{1}{2\alpha}\|z-x\|^2\right\}.\]
At any \(x\in\mathbb R^n\) for which \(T_\alpha(x)\) is nonempty and closed, define \(R_{\mathrm{fp}}(x)=\alpha^{-1}\operatorname{dist}(x,T_\alpha(x))\). Then
\[R_{\mathrm{fp}}(x)=0\iff x\in T_\alpha(x)\iff\partial g(x)\cap\partial h(x)\ne\varnothing.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: When the proximal DC update-value set is nonempty and closed, distance to that set vanishes exactly at a decomposition-dependent DC-critical point.
assumptions_latex: \(g,h:\mathbb R^n\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) are proper closed convex functions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(R_{\mathrm{fp}}(x)=0\iff x\in T_\alpha(x)\iff\partial g(x)\cap\partial h(x)\ne\varnothing\).

children.title: Residual Comparability Regimes
children.top_down_role: Conditions under which step-based or fixed-point certificates convey comparable criticality information.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Quasi-Nearest Selection Regime
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Selection condition yielding two-sided residual comparability.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(T_\alpha(x)\ne\varnothing\), \(x^+\in T_\alpha(x)\), and \(\alpha>0\). If, for some \(\kappa\ge1\), \[\|x^+-x\|\le\kappa\operatorname{dist}(x,T_\alpha(x)),\] then \[R_{\mathrm{fp}}(x)\le R_{\mathrm{step}}(x;x^+)\le\kappa R_{\mathrm{fp}}(x).\] Thus a uniformly quasi-nearest selection rule makes the residuals uniformly equivalent; \(\kappa=1\) gives equality.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An update chosen within a fixed factor of the nearest update yields two-sided comparability of step and fixed-point residuals.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(R_{\mathrm{fp}}(x)\le R_{\mathrm{step}}(x;x^+)\le\kappa R_{\mathrm{fp}}(x)\).
knowledge_statements.title: Quasi-Nearest Selection Regime

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Failure of Reverse Comparability Under Arbitrary Selection
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A proximal DC family with an unbounded selected-to-best residual ratio.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(M\ge1\), take \(g\equiv0\), \(h_M(t)=\max\{t,Mt\}\), \(x=0\), and \(\alpha=1\). Then \(\partial h_M(0)=[1,M]\), and the update generated by \(y\in[1,M]\) is \(t^+=y\). Hence \(T_1(0)=[1,M]\), \(R_{\mathrm{fp}}(0)=1\), while selecting \(y=M\) gives \(R_{\mathrm{step}}(0;M,M)=M\). Therefore no uniform reverse bound \(R_{\mathrm{step}}\le\kappa R_{\mathrm{fp}}\) holds for arbitrary selections.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Arbitrary subgradient selection can make the step residual arbitrarily larger than the best-selection fixed-point residual.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(R_{\mathrm{fp}}(0)=1\) and \(R_{\mathrm{step}}(0;M,M)=M\), so their ratio tends to infinity.
knowledge_statements.title: Failure of Reverse Comparability Under Arbitrary Selection
Residual Comparability Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Comparison of selected-step and best-selection fixed-point residuals.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Assume \(T_\alpha(x)\) is nonempty, let \(y\in\partial h(x)\), and choose a corresponding proximal DC update \(x^+\in T_\alpha(x)\). Then
\[R_{\mathrm{fp}}(x)=\alpha^{-1}\operatorname{dist}(x,T_\alpha(x))\le \alpha^{-1}\|x^+-x\|=R_{\mathrm{step}}(x;y,x^+).\]
Equality holds whenever \(x^+\) realizes the distance from \(x\) to \(T_\alpha(x)\). Thus a selected-step residual always upper-bounds the best-selection fixed-point residual, but reverse comparability requires a controlled selection rule.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every selected DC step bounds the fixed-point residual above; equality holds for a nearest update, while reverse bounds require selection control.
assumptions_latex: \(x^+\) is an update generated by some \(y\in\partial h(x)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(R_{\mathrm{fp}}(x)\le R_{\mathrm{step}}(x;y,x^+)\), with equality for a nearest update.

notation.meaning: residual of a selected DC step

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The displayed upper bound is a direct consequence of the distance definition and fits the property container. The final reverse-comparability statement is qualitative and needs a sourced, precise selection regime.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Zero Infimum Residual Without a Critical Pair
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of the zero-residual equivalence when the distance between the component subdifferentials is not attained.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: In \(\mathbb R^2\), let \(A=\{(s,t):t\ge e^s\}\), \(B=\mathbb R\times\{0\}\), \(g=\sigma_A\), and \(h=\sigma_B\). Then \(g,h\) are proper closed convex functions, \(\partial g(0)=A\), and \(\partial h(0)=B\). Hence \[\operatorname{dist}(\partial g(0),\partial h(0))=0,\qquad \partial g(0)\cap\partial h(0)=\varnothing.\] Thus a zero infimal primal–dual residual certifies criticality only when the distance is attained or another condition guarantees intersection.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Closed convex subdifferentials can be disjoint while having distance zero, so attainment is essential to the zero-residual certificate.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{dist}(\partial g(0),\partial h(0))=0\) while \(\partial g(0)\cap\partial h(0)=\varnothing\).

notation.meaning: support function of the closed convex set C

knowledge_statements.title: Zero Infimum Residual Without a Critical Pair
Primal–Dual Criticality Residuals
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Subgradient mismatch certificate for decomposition-dependent DC criticality.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(f=g-h\) with proper closed convex \(g,h\). For \(x\in\operatorname{dom}g\cap\operatorname{dom}h\), \(u\in\partial g(x)\), and \(v\in\partial h(x)\), define the primal–dual residual \(R_{\mathrm{pd}}(x,u,v)=\|u-v\|\). Its best attainable value is
\[\widehat R_{\mathrm{pd}}(x)=\operatorname{dist}\bigl(\partial g(x),\partial h(x)\bigr).\]
Provided both subdifferentials are nonempty and the distance is attained, \(\widehat R_{\mathrm{pd}}(x)=0\) if and only if \(\partial g(x)\cap\partial h(x)\ne\varnothing\), which certifies DC criticality.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The distance between the two convex subdifferentials measures criticality and vanishes precisely when they share a subgradient, under attainment.
assumptions_latex: Both subdifferentials at \(x\) are nonempty and their distance is attained.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\widehat R_{\mathrm{pd}}(x)=0\iff\partial g(x)\cap\partial h(x)\ne\varnothing\).

notation.meaning: residual for a chosen subgradient pair

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Under the stated nonemptiness and attainment assumptions, the residual equivalence is correct and fits the certificate container. A specific source locator is required.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Steepest Directional DC Certificate
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Direction-free aggregation of DC directional descent over normalized directions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f=g-h\), where \(g,h:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) are convex, and define \[\delta(x)=\min_{\|d\|=1}\bigl(g'(x;d)-h'(x;d)\bigr).\] The minimum is attained. Moreover, \[\delta(x)<0\iff\exists d\ (\|d\|=1,\ f'(x;d)<0),\] and \[\delta(x)\ge0\iff f'(x;d)\ge0\quad\forall d\in\mathbb R^n.\] Any minimizing direction with negative value is a directional descent certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Minimizing the DC directional derivative on the unit sphere either supplies a descent direction or certifies the absence of negative directional derivatives.
assumptions_latex: \(g,h:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) are finite convex functions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\delta(x)<0\iff\exists d,\ \|d\|=1,\ f'(x;d)<0\), while \(\delta(x)\ge0\iff f'(x;d)\ge0\) for every \(d\).

notation.meaning: minimum DC directional derivative over the Euclidean unit sphere

knowledge_statements.title: Steepest Directional DC Certificate
Directional Descent Certificates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A negative DC directional derivative certifies local descent along a ray.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(f=g-h\) on \(\mathbb R^n\), where \(g,h\) are finite convex functions, and let \(x,d\in\mathbb R^n\). The computable quantity
\[\Delta(x;d)=g'(x;d)-h'(x;d)=f'(x;d)\]
is a directional descent certificate. If \(\Delta(x;d)<0\), then there exists \(\bar t>0\) such that \(f(x+t d)<f(x)\) for all sufficiently small \(t\in(0,\bar t)\). For a constrained problem, the same certificate applies when \(d\in T_C(x)\) and the ray is locally feasible.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A strictly negative DC directional derivative certifies objective decrease along sufficiently short feasible steps in that direction.
assumptions_latex: For the constrained form, \(x+t d\in C\) for all sufficiently small positive \(t\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\Delta(x;d)<0\) implies \(f(x+t d)<f(x)\) for all sufficiently small \(t>0\).

notation.meaning: DC directional derivative used as a descent certificate
tangent cone to the feasible set

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: A strictly negative finite directional derivative gives decrease for all sufficiently small positive steps, and local ray feasibility handles the constrained case. The certificate remains uncited.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Objective-Gap Subproblem Certificate
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Alternative inexactness certificate for the strongly convex proximal DC subproblem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(q_x\) be the \(\alpha^{-1}\)-strongly convex proximal DC subproblem objective, and let \(z^\star=\operatorname*{argmin}q_x\). If \(L\le q_x(z^\star)\) is a certified lower bound and \(q_x(z)-L\le\varepsilon\), then \[0\le q_x(z)-q_x(z^\star)\le\varepsilon,\qquad \|z-z^\star\|\le\sqrt{2\alpha\varepsilon}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A certified gap to a valid lower bound controls both subproblem suboptimality and distance to the exact proximal DC update.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(q_x(z)-q_x(z^\star)\le\varepsilon\) and \(\|z-z^\star\|\le\sqrt{2\alpha\varepsilon}\).

notation.meaning: certified lower bound on the convex-subproblem optimum

knowledge_statements.title: Objective-Gap Subproblem Certificate
Inexact Convex-Subproblem Certificates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Residual certificate for an approximately solved proximal DC convexification.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Fix \(x\), choose \(y\in\partial h(x)\), and define
\[q_x(z)=g(z)-\langle y,z\rangle+\frac{1}{2\alpha}\|z-x\|^2,\qquad \alpha>0.\]
A candidate \(z\) has an \(\eta\)-stationarity certificate if a vector \(e\) is supplied with \(e\in\partial q_x(z)\) and \(\|e\|\le\eta\). Since \(q_x\) is \(\alpha^{-1}\)-strongly convex, this verifiable inclusion implies
\[q_x(z)-\min_w q_x(w)\le\frac{\alpha}{2}\eta^2,\qquad \|z-z^\star\|\le\alpha\eta,\]
where \(z^\star\) is the unique exact minimizer.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A small subgradient of the strongly convex DC subproblem certifies both a bounded objective gap and proximity to its exact minimizer.
assumptions_latex: \(g\) is proper closed convex, \(y\in\partial h(x)\), and \(\alpha>0\).
The proximal subproblem has the exact minimizer \(z^\star\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(e\in\partial q_x(z)\) and \(\|e\|\le\eta\) imply the displayed gap and distance bounds.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The objective-gap and distance bounds have the correct constants for alpha^{-1}-strong convexity, and the certificate kind fits the container. An authoritative convex-analysis or inexact-DCA locator is required.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Primal DC Well-Posedness Is Not Automatic
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite closed convex components do not guarantee a finite primal value or attainment.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(g(x)=0\) and \(h(x)=x^2\) on \(\mathbb R\). Both functions are finite, proper, lower-semicontinuous, and convex, whereas \(\inf_{x\in\mathbb R}\{g(x)-h(x)\}=-\infty\) and \(\operatorname*{argmin}(g-h)=\varnothing\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A difference of finite closed convex functions can be unbounded below and unattained.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\inf_{x\in\mathbb R}(g-h)=-\infty\) and \(\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in\mathbb R}(g-h)=\varnothing\).
knowledge_statements.title: Primal DC Well-Posedness Is Not Automatic

assumptions_latex: \(X\) is a finite-dimensional real vector space with dual \(X^*\).
\(g,h:X\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) are proper lower-semicontinuous convex functions, and \(\operatorname{dom}g\cap\operatorname{dom}h\neq\varnothing\).

notation.meaning: Fenchel conjugate of a proper convex function
optimal value of the primal DC program

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: standard finite-dimensional Toland-Fenchel primal formulation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional unconstrained extended-real DC formulation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The primal DC program generated by \(g\) and \(h\) is
\[
(P)\qquad p:=\inf_{x\in X}\bigl(g(x)-h(x)\bigr).
\]
Its feasible domain is \(\operatorname{dom}g\cap\operatorname{dom}h\), and a primal solution is any \(\bar x\) in this domain satisfying \(g(\bar x)-h(\bar x)=p\). Values of the indeterminate form \(+\infty-(+\infty)\) are excluded by restricting evaluation to the feasible domain.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A primal DC program minimizes the difference of two proper closed convex functions over their common effective domain.
knowledge_statements.title: Primal DC Programs

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition and content kind fit the primal-program leaf, but no inspectable authoritative citation supports the stated Toland–Fenchel convention.

children.title: Dual DC Programs
children.top_down_role: Dual-side formulations induced by conjugate DC representations.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Dual DC Well-Posedness Is Not Automatic
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite closed convex dual components do not guarantee a finite dual value or attainment.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(u(y)=0\) and \(v(y)=y^2\) on \(\mathbb R\). Both functions are finite, proper, lower-semicontinuous, and convex, whereas \(\inf_{y\in\mathbb R}\{u(y)-v(y)\}=-\infty\) and \(\operatorname*{argmin}(u-v)=\varnothing\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Even finite closed convex dual components can produce an unbounded, unattained dual DC program.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\inf_{y\in\mathbb R}(u-v)=-\infty\) and \(\operatorname*{argmin}_{y\in\mathbb R}(u-v)=\varnothing\).
knowledge_statements.title: Dual DC Well-Posedness Is Not Automatic

assumptions_latex: \(X\), \(g\), and \(h\) satisfy the assumptions of the associated primal DC program.

notation.meaning: Fenchel conjugates of the primal convex components
optimal value of the dual DC program

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: standard finite-dimensional Toland-Fenchel dual formulation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Toland-Fenchel dual obtained by interchanging the convex components and conjugating.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The Toland-Fenchel dual DC program associated with \((P)\) is
\[
(D)\qquad d:=\inf_{y\in X^*}\bigl(h^*(y)-g^*(y)\bigr).
\]
Its feasible domain is \(\operatorname{dom}h^*\cap\operatorname{dom}g^*\), and a dual solution is any \(\bar y\) in this domain satisfying \(h^*(\bar y)-g^*(\bar y)=d\). Thus the ordered primal pair \((g,h)\) corresponds to the ordered dual pair \((h^*,g^*)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The Toland-Fenchel dual minimizes the difference of the conjugates in reversed order.
knowledge_statements.title: Dual DC Programs

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The reversed-conjugate formulation and definition role fit the dual-program leaf, but the record has no inspectable source for this duality convention.

children.title: Primal–Dual Program Correspondence
children.top_down_role: Structural relationships linking primal-side or dual-side DC formulations.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Toland–Fenchel Optimal-Value Equality
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Primal and reversed-conjugate dual values are the same joint infimum under explicit finite-difference domain assumptions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(g,h\) be proper lower-semicontinuous convex functions on a finite-dimensional space, with \(\operatorname{dom}g\subseteq\operatorname{dom}h\) and \(\operatorname{dom}h^*\subseteq\operatorname{dom}g^*\). Then
\[
\inf_{x\in\operatorname{dom}g}(g(x)-h(x))
=
\inf_{\substack{x\in\operatorname{dom}g\\y\in\operatorname{dom}h^*}}
\bigl(g(x)+h^*(y)-\langle y,x\rangle\bigr)
=
\inf_{y\in\operatorname{dom}h^*}(h^*(y)-g^*(y)).
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under explicit domain inclusions, the primal and reversed-conjugate dual DC programs have the same extended optimal value because both equal one joint infimum.
assumptions_latex: \(g,h\) are proper lower-semicontinuous convex functions on a finite-dimensional real vector space.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\inf(g-h)=\inf(h^*-g^*)\), with both sides interpreted on the displayed effective domains.
knowledge_statements.title: Toland–Fenchel Optimal-Value Equality

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Global Minimizer Transfer Through a Common Subgradient
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Subdifferentiability of the subtracted component transfers a global primal minimizer to a global dual minimizer, with a symmetric converse.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Under the assumptions of the optimal-value equality, let \(\bar x\) globally minimize \(g-h\). If \(\partial h(\bar x)\neq\varnothing\), then every \(\bar y\in\partial h(\bar x)\) also satisfies \(\bar y\in\partial g(\bar x)\) and globally minimizes \(h^*-g^*\). Conversely, if \(\bar y\) globally minimizes \(h^*-g^*\) and \(\partial g^*(\bar y)\neq\varnothing\), then every \(\bar x\in\partial g^*(\bar y)\) belongs to \(\partial h^*(\bar y)\) and globally minimizes \(g-h\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A global minimizer transfers across the Toland–Fenchel pair when the subdifferential needed to construct a common-subgradient pair is nonempty.
assumptions_latex: The assumptions of Toland–Fenchel optimal-value equality hold.
\(\bar x\in\operatorname*{argmin}(g-h)\) and \(\partial h(\bar x)\neq\varnothing\), or symmetrically \(\bar y\in\operatorname*{argmin}(h^*-g^*)\) and \(\partial g^*(\bar y)\neq\varnothing\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\bar y\in\partial g(\bar x)\cap\partial h(\bar x)\) and \(\bar y\in\operatorname*{argmin}(h^*-g^*)\), with the stated symmetric converse.
knowledge_statements.title: Global Minimizer Transfer Through a Common Subgradient

assumptions_latex: \(g,h\) are proper lower-semicontinuous convex functions on a finite-dimensional space.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If \(y\in\partial g(x)\cap\partial h(x)\), then \(g(x)-h(x)=h^*(y)-g^*(y)\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: follows from the Fenchel-Young equality at a common subgradient
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Pointwise correspondence through simultaneous Fenchel-Young equalities.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A pair \((x,y)\) is a primal-dual critical pair when
\[
y\in\partial g(x)\cap\partial h(x).
\]
Equivalently, convex conjugacy gives \(x\in\partial g^*(y)\cap\partial h^*(y)\). For every such pair, both Fenchel-Young equalities hold, and subtraction yields
\[
g(x)-h(x)=h^*(y)-g^*(y).
\]
Consequently, corresponding critical points of the primal and dual DC objectives have identical objective values.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A common subgradient links primal and dual critical points, and their DC objective values coincide.
knowledge_statements.title: Primal–Dual Program Correspondence

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The common-subgradient correspondence and value equality are mathematically standard and fit a duality record, but no citation is supplied and the statement includes a derivational argument that should not appear in a proof-free knowledge statement.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Critical-Pair Correspondence Need Not Be One-to-One
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Elementary examples showing nonuniqueness of both coordinate projections of the critical-pair relation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: On \(X=\mathbb R\), if \(g=h\equiv0\), the critical-pair relation is \(\mathbb R\times\{0\}\). If \(g=h=|\cdot|\), the relation contains \(\{0\}\times[-1,1]\). Thus one dual critical point can have infinitely many primal partners, and one primal critical point can have infinitely many dual partners.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Simple convex component pairs show that a primal or dual critical point may have infinitely many critical partners.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The critical-pair relation need not be single-valued in either coordinate projection.
knowledge_statements.title: Critical-Pair Correspondence Need Not Be One-to-One

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Critical-Pair Primal-Dual Value Identity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Objective-value identity at every Toland-Fenchel critical pair.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\) be a finite-dimensional real vector space with dual \(X^*\), and let \(g,h:X\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) be proper lower-semicontinuous convex functions. Every pair satisfying \(y\in\partial g(x)\cap\partial h(x)\) obeys \[g(x)+g^*(y)=\langle y,x\rangle=h(x)+h^*(y)\] and \[g(x)-h(x)=h^*(y)-g^*(y).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The primal and dual DC objectives have identical values at every critical pair.
assumptions_latex: \(g\) and \(h\) are proper lower-semicontinuous convex functions

notation.meaning: Fenchel conjugates of g and h

knowledge_statements.title: Critical-Pair Primal-Dual Value Identity

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(y\in\partial g(x)\cap\partial h(x)\iff x\in\partial g^*(y)\cap\partial h^*(y)\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: convex subdifferential inversion under Fenchel conjugacy
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Set-valued correspondence; uniqueness is not asserted.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Define the critical-pair relation
\[
\mathcal C:=\{(x,y)\in X\times X^*:y\in\partial g(x)\cap\partial h(x)\}.
\]
For proper closed convex functions, \(y\in\partial f(x)\) is equivalent to \(x\in\partial f^*(y)\). Hence
\[
(x,y)\in\mathcal C
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
x\in\partial g^*(y)\cap\partial h^*(y).
\]
The coordinate projections of \(\mathcal C\) are respectively \(C_P\) and \(C_D\); without strict convexity or differentiability, this correspondence may be many-to-many.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Common primal subgradients correspond exactly to common dual subgradients, possibly through a many-to-many relation.
knowledge_statements.title: DC Critical-Pair Correspondence

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The many-to-many critical-pair correspondence fits the leaf, but the record does not independently specify the finite-dimensional space and dual pairing needed for conjugate-subdifferential inversion, and it supplies no citation.
