children.top_down_role: Local optimality relationships across primal or dual DC formulations.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Smooth Legendre Local Optimality Transfer
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Nondegenerate local transfer under hypotheses ensuring conjugate localization and inverse-Hessian identities.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(g,h:\mathbb R^n	o(-\infty,+\infty]\) be Legendre convex functions that are twice continuously differentiable near \( ar x\in\operatorname{int}(\operatorname{dom}g)\cap\operatorname{int}(\operatorname{dom}h)\). Suppose \( ar y=
abla g( ar x)=
abla h( ar x)\), and set \(A=
abla^2g( ar x)\), \(B=
abla^2h( ar x)\). If \(A\) and \(B\) are positive definite, then \(g^*\) and \(h^*\) are twice differentiable near \( ar y\), with \[
abla^2(h^*-g^*)( ar y)=B^{-1}-A^{-1}.\] In particular, \[A-B\succ0\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad B^{-1}-A^{-1}\succ0,\] and under either equivalent condition \( ar x\) and \( ar y\) are strict local minimizers of \(g-h\) and \(h^*-g^*\), respectively.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For smooth Legendre components with nonsingular local curvature, positive primal curvature difference is equivalent to positive dual inverse-curvature difference and gives strict local minima on both sides.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\nabla^2(h^*-g^*)(\bar y)=B^{-1}-A^{-1}\succ0\), and \(\bar x,\bar y\) are strict local minimizers of their respective DC objectives.

notation.meaning: Hessian of g at the primal critical point
Hessian of h at the primal critical point
common primal gradient and corresponding dual point

knowledge_statements.title: Smooth Legendre Local Optimality Transfer

assumptions_latex: \(g,h\) are twice continuously differentiable and strongly convex near \(\bar x\), with positive-definite Hessians.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\bar x\) and \(\bar y\) are strict local minimizers of their respective primal and dual DC objectives.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: smooth strongly-convex second-order transfer via inverse Hessians
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Smooth nondegenerate sufficient condition, not a general local-duality assertion.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Under the stated assumptions, the second-order condition gives a strict local minimum of \(F\) at \( ar x\). Local conjugate differentiability gives
\[

abla^2F_D( ar y)=
abla^2h( ar x)^{-1}-
abla^2g( ar x)^{-1}.
\]
Since \(
abla^2g( ar x)\succ
abla^2h( ar x)\succ0\), order reversal under matrix inversion implies \(
abla^2F_D( ar y)\succ0\). Therefore \( ar y\) is a strict local minimizer of \(F_D\), and the two local minimum values coincide by Fenchel-Young equality.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nondegenerate smooth primal local minimum transfers to a dual local minimum through the common gradient and inverse-Hessian ordering.
knowledge_statements.title: Duality-Based Local Optimality Transfer

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Local strong convexity near the primal point alone does not justify twice differentiability of the global Fenchel conjugates or the asserted inverse-Hessian identities at the dual point. An exact local-duality theorem with sufficient Legendre-type or localization hypotheses is required; the current text also contains proof material.

children.title: Duality-Based Global Optimality Transfer
children.top_down_role: Global optimality relationships across primal or dual DC formulations.

assumptions_latex: The primal and dual DC programs attain finite minima.
\((\bar x,\bar y)\) is a critical pair.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\bar x\in\operatorname{argmin}(g-h)\iff\bar y\in\operatorname{argmin}(h^*-g^*)\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: zero-gap transfer combined with critical-pair value equality
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conditional global transfer under attainment and strong Toland-Fenchel duality.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For the critical pair, Fenchel-Young equality gives
\[
g(\bar x)-h(\bar x)=h^*(\bar y)-g^*(\bar y).
\]
If \(\bar x\) is primal optimal, this common value equals \(p\); because \(p=d\), the dual value at \(\bar y\) equals the dual infimum, so \(\bar y\) is dual optimal. Conversely, dual optimality of \(\bar y\), the same equality, and \(d=p\) imply primal optimality of \(\bar x\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: With attainment and zero duality gap, either member of a critical pair is globally optimal exactly when the other is.
knowledge_statements.title: Duality-Based Global Optimality Transfer

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Conditioned on a finite common optimum and critical-pair value equality, the global-optimality equivalence is sound and the theorem role fits the leaf. However, no authoritative source is supplied, and the statement is written as a proof rather than a terminal theorem statement.

children.title: Local–Global Duality Gaps
children.top_down_role: Regimes where local correspondence does not extend to global optimality correspondence.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: A Critical Local Minimum Need Not Be Global
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Explicit piecewise-linear DC example separating primal-dual criticality and strict local minimality from global optimality.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define \(g(x)=|x|+|x-2|+1\), \(h(x)=\max\{|x|,|x-2|+1\}\), and \(F=g-h=\min\{|x|,|x-2|+1\}\). Both \(g\) and \(h\) are finite convex functions. The points \(0\) and \(2\) are strict local minimizers of \(F\), with \(F(0)=0\) and \(F(2)=1\); hence \(2\) is not globally minimizing. Moreover, \(1\in\partial g(2)\cap\partial h(2)\), so \(2\) belongs to a primal-dual critical pair despite its nonglobal value.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A finite piecewise-linear DC function has a strict nonglobal local minimum that also satisfies the common-subgradient primal-dual criticality condition.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(2\) is a strict nonglobal local minimizer of \(g-h\), and \(1\in\partial g(2)\cap\partial h(2)\).
knowledge_statements.title: A Critical Local Minimum Need Not Be Global

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The DC objective \(g-h=(x^2-1)^2+\varepsilon x\) has two strict local minima with unequal values.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: explicit tilted double-well DC example
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Concrete separation between critical/local correspondence and global optimality.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Both \(g\) and \(h\) are convex, since \(g''(x)=12x^2+2>0\) and \(h''(x)=6\). The equation
\[
F'(x)=4x(x^2-1)+\varepsilon=0
\]
has three distinct roots for the stated range of \(\varepsilon\): two are strict local minima and one is a local maximum. The linear tilt makes the two local-minimum values unequal, so one local minimum is not global. Thus critical-pair value equality alone does not turn every local DC solution into a global one or eliminate local optimality gaps.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A tilted double-well DC objective has unequal local minima, showing that critical correspondence alone does not imply global optimality.
knowledge_statements.title: Local–Global Duality Gaps

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The tilted double-well example and parameter range plausibly establish the intended local-versus-global failure boundary, but the root classification and unequal-minimum claim lack cited or registered symbolic evidence, and the statement contains a verification argument.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Global Exactness and Its Threshold
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Solution-set definition of global optimal-solution exactness for a nonnegative violation penalty.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(v\ge0\), \(C=v^{-1}(0)\), \(P_\lambda=f+\lambda v\), and \(S=\operatorname{argmin}_{x\in C}f\neq\varnothing\). A parameter \(\lambda\ge0\) is globally exact when \(\operatorname{argmin}P_\lambda=S\). Define \[\lambda_*:=\inf\left\{\lambda\ge0:\operatorname{argmin}P_\mu=S\ \text{for every }\mu>\lambda\right\},\] with \(\inf\varnothing=+\infty\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Global exactness means equality between the penalized and constrained global-minimizer sets; the threshold records the onset of eventual exactness.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \lambda_*\in[0,+\infty]\text{ is the eventual global-exactness threshold}.
knowledge_statements.title: Global Exactness and Its Threshold

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Upward Closure of Globally Exact Parameters
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Parameter monotonicity for nonnegative penalties with an exact feasible zero set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose \(v\ge0\), \(v^{-1}(0)=C\), and \(\operatorname{argmin}(f+\lambda_0v)=\operatorname{argmin}_{x\in C}f\neq\varnothing\). Then for every \(\lambda>\lambda_0\), \[\operatorname{argmin}(f+\lambda v)=\operatorname{argmin}_{x\in C}f.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Once a nonnegative violation penalty is globally exact, every larger parameter is also globally exact.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \lambda>\lambda_0\quad\Longrightarrow\quad\operatorname{argmin}(f+\lambda v)=\operatorname{argmin}_{C}f.
knowledge_statements.title: Upward Closure of Globally Exact Parameters

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Convex Multiplier Bound for Global Exactness
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Primal-dual sufficient threshold for a positive-part l1 penalty in convex inequality optimization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \[p^*=\min_{x\in D}\{f(x):c_i(x)\le0,\ i=1,\ldots,m\},\] where \(D\) is closed convex and \(f,c_i\) are proper convex on \(D\). Suppose the primal optimum is attained and strong duality holds with an optimal multiplier \(\mu^*\in\mathbb R_+^m\). Define \(v(x)=\sum_i[c_i(x)]_+\). Then every \(\lambda>\|\mu^*\|_\infty\) satisfies \[\operatorname{argmin}_{x\in D}\bigl(f(x)+\lambda v(x)\bigr)=\operatorname{argmin}_{x\in D,\ c(x)\le0}f(x).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a convex inequality problem with an attained optimal multiplier, an l1 penalty weight exceeding its largest multiplier component is globally exact.
assumptions_latex: \text{Strong duality holds and }\mu^*\ge0\text{ is dual optimal}.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \lambda>\|\mu^*\|_\infty\Longrightarrow\operatorname{argmin}_{D}(f+\lambda\sum_i[c_i]_+)=\operatorname{argmin}_{D,\,c\le0}f.
knowledge_statements.title: Convex Multiplier Bound for Global Exactness

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Sharp Ratio Characterization of Global Exactness
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact global threshold for a nonnegative violation penalty, including endpoint behavior.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(D\neq\varnothing\), let \(v:D\to[0,+\infty]\), let \(C=\{x\in D:v(x)=0\}\), and suppose \(f_C^*:=\min_{x\in C}f(x)\in\mathbb R\) is attained. Define \[R:=\sup_{x\in D\setminus C}\frac{f_C^*-f(x)}{v(x)},\qquad \sup\varnothing:=-\infty.\] Then \[\operatorname{argmin}_{x\in D}(f(x)+\lambda v(x))=\operatorname{argmin}_{x\in C}f(x)\] if and only if \[f(x)+\lambda v(x)>f_C^*\qquad(x\in D\setminus C).\] Hence every \(\lambda>\max\{0,R\}\) is globally exact, no \(0\le\lambda<R\) is globally exact, and at \(\lambda=R\) exactness holds exactly when the strict inequality holds at every infeasible point.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The sharp global exactness threshold is the supremal objective improvement per unit violation, with endpoint exactness requiring strict domination at every infeasible point.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \lambda>\max\{0,R\}\Rightarrow\operatorname{argmin}_D(f+\lambda v)=\operatorname{argmin}_C f,\qquad 0\le\lambda<R\Rightarrow\text{nonexactness}.

notation.meaning: supremal objective-improvement-to-violation ratio over infeasible points

knowledge_statements.title: Sharp Ratio Characterization of Global Exactness

assumptions_latex: \(C\subset\mathbb R^n\) is nonempty and closed, and \(v\ge0\) satisfies \(C=\{x:v(x)=0\}\).
\(f\) is globally \(L\)-Lipschitz on the region considered.
\(\operatorname{dist}(x,C)\le\kappa v(x)\), and nearest points in \(C\) exist.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For every \(\lambda>L\kappa\), \(\operatorname{argmin}(f+\lambda v)=\operatorname{argmin}_{x\in C}f\), provided the constrained minimum is attained.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: Lipschitz objective plus global error bound gives exact penalization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Global exactness from a Lipschitz bound and a global error bound.

source_refs.locator: 5.2.3 Refined Lower Subdifferential Conditions for MPECs via Exact Penalization p. 61
source_refs.source_title: Variational Analysis and Generalized Differentiation II

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(f_C^*:=\min_{z\in C}f(z)\). For any \(x\), choose \(z_x\in C\) with \(\|x-z_x\|=\operatorname{dist}(x,C)\). Then
\[
f(x)+\lambda v(x)\ge f(z_x)+(\lambda-L\kappa)v(x)\ge f_C^*.
\]
When \(\lambda>L\kappa\), equality is possible only if \(v(x)=0\), hence only at a feasible point minimizing \(f\) on \(C\). Conversely, every constrained minimizer has penalty zero and minimizes the penalized objective.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A penalty exceeding the Lipschitz constant times an error-bound modulus reproduces exactly the attained constrained global minimizers.
knowledge_statements.title: Exact Penalties for Optimal Solutions

The region on which the Lipschitz estimate must hold is also underspecified, and the statement contains proof text. A directly supporting exact-penalty theorem is needed.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Multiplier-Bounded Preservation of Feasible Stationarity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: One-way Clarke-stationarity certificate for smooth equalities penalized by an l1 norm.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) and \(c:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^m\) be continuously differentiable. If \(c(\bar x)=0\) and there is \(\mu\in\mathbb R^m\) such that \[\nabla f(\bar x)+\nabla c(\bar x)^T\mu=0,\] then every \(\lambda\ge\|\mu\|_\infty\) satisfies \[0\in\partial_C\bigl(f+\lambda\|c\|_1\bigr)(\bar x).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A feasible equality-constrained KKT point is Clarke-stationary for the l1 penalty when the penalty weight dominates the multiplier infinity norm.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \lambda\ge\|\mu\|_\infty\quad\Longrightarrow\quad0\in\partial_C(f+\lambda\|c\|_1)(\bar x).
knowledge_statements.title: Multiplier-Bounded Preservation of Feasible Stationarity

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Global Infeasible Stationary Points Can Persist at Every Weight
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of global stationary-set exactness despite exact zero detection by the violation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f\equiv0\), \(C=\{-1,1\}\), and \(v(x)=(x^2-1)^2\). For every \(\lambda>0\), \(P_\lambda=\lambda v\) satisfies \[P_\lambda'(0)=0\qquad\text{and}\qquad0\notin C.\] Thus no finite positive parameter makes every stationary point of \(P_\lambda\) feasible, although \(v\ge0\) and \(v^{-1}(0)=C\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A smooth violation can retain an infeasible critical point for every positive penalty weight.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: 0\in\partial P_\lambda(0)\ \text{and}\ 0\notin C\quad\forall\lambda>0.
knowledge_statements.title: Global Infeasible Stationary Points Can Persist at Every Weight

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Local Clarke-Stationary Exactness
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Stationary exactness specialized to locally Lipschitz data, Clarke subgradients, and Clarke normals.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f,v:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) be locally Lipschitz near \(\bar x\), let \(v\ge0\), and let \(C=v^{-1}(0)\) be closed near \(\bar x\in C\). The family \(P_\lambda=f+\lambda v\) is locally Clarke-stationary exact at \(\bar x\) if there exist a neighborhood \(U\) of \(\bar x\) and \(\bar\lambda\ge0\) such that, for every \(\lambda\ge\bar\lambda\), \[\{x\in U:0\in\partial_C P_\lambda(x)\}=\{x\in U\cap C:0\in\partial_C f(x)+N_C^C(x)\}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Above one local threshold, penalized Clarke-stationary points coincide with feasible Clarke-stationary points of the constrained problem.
assumptions_latex: f,v\text{ are locally Lipschitz near }\bar x.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \exists U,\bar\lambda\ \forall\lambda\ge\bar\lambda:\{x\in U:0\in\partial_C P_\lambda(x)\}=\{x\in U\cap C:0\in\partial_C f(x)+N_C^C(x)\}.

notation.meaning: Clarke normal cone to the feasible set C

knowledge_statements.title: Local Clarke-Stationary Exactness

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Uniform Clarke-Slope Exclusion of Infeasible Stationary Points
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local sufficient condition excluding infeasible Clarke-stationary points of a penalty family.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f,v:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) be locally Lipschitz on a neighborhood \(U\), with \(v\ge0\) and \(C=v^{-1}(0)\). Suppose \[\|a\|\le L\quad(a\in\partial_C f(x),\ x\in U),\qquad \|b\|\ge\tau>0\quad(b\in\partial_C v(x),\ x\in U\setminus C).\] Then every \(\lambda>L/\tau\) satisfies \[0\notin\partial_C(f+\lambda v)(x)\qquad(x\in U\setminus C).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Uniformly bounded objective subgradients and violation subgradients separated from zero exclude nearby infeasible Clarke-stationary points at sufficiently large weights.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \lambda>L/\tau\Longrightarrow0\notin\partial_C(f+\lambda v)(x)\quad\forall x\in U\setminus C.

notation.meaning: uniform off-feasible lower bound on violation-subgradient norms

knowledge_statements.title: Uniform Clarke-Slope Exclusion of Infeasible Stationary Points

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Uniform Two-Way Clarke-Stationary Exactness
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local two-way exactness for a smooth-equality l1 penalty under exact feasible calculus, uniformly bounded multipliers, and off-feasible slope separation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) be locally Lipschitz on a neighborhood \(U\), let \(c\in C^1(U;\mathbb R^m)\), set \(C=c^{-1}(0)\), \(v=\|c\|_1\), and \(P_\lambda=f+\lambda v\). Suppose \(\|a\|\le L\) for every \(a\in\partial_Cf(x)\), \(x\in U\), and \(\|b\|\ge\tau>0\) for every \(b\in\partial_Cv(x)\), \(x\in U\setminus C\). At every \(x\in U\cap C\), assume \(\partial_Cv(x)=\nabla c(x)^T[-1,1]^m\), \(\partial_CP_\lambda(x)=\partial_Cf(x)+\lambda\partial_Cv(x)\), and constrained Clarke stationarity is equivalent to the existence of \(\mu\) with \(0\in\partial_Cf(x)+\nabla c(x)^T\mu\); assume such a multiplier can always be chosen with \(\|\mu\|_\infty\le M\). Then every \(\lambda>\max\{M,L/\tau\}\) satisfies
\[
\{x\in U:0\in\partial_CP_\lambda(x)\}
=
\{x\in U\cap C:0\in\partial_Cf(x)+N_C^C(x)\}.
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Exact feasible Clarke calculus and a uniform multiplier bound preserve nearby constrained stationary points, while uniform violation-slope separation excludes infeasible stationary points.
assumptions_latex: f\text{ is locally Lipschitz on }U\text{ and }c\in C^1(U;\mathbb R^m).
0\in\partial_Cf(x)+N_C^C(x)\text{ is equivalent to a multiplier inclusion having a choice }\|\mu\|_\infty\le M.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \lambda>\max\{M,L/\tau\}\Longrightarrow\{x\in U:0\in\partial_CP_\lambda(x)\}=\{x\in U\cap C:0\in\partial_Cf(x)+N_C^C(x)\}.

notation.meaning: Clarke normal cone to the feasible set
uniform infinity-norm bound for compatible multipliers

knowledge_statements.title: Uniform Two-Way Clarke-Stationary Exactness

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Local stationary exactness means \(0\in\partial(f+\lambda v)(x)\iff x\in C\) and \(0\in\partial f(x)+N_C(x)\), locally, for all sufficiently large \(\lambda\).

notation.meaning: normal cone compatible with the chosen stationarity notion

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: precise local definition relative to a chosen generalized subdifferential
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Definition is relative to the selected generalized subdifferential and normal cone.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The family \(P_\lambda=f+\lambda v\) is locally exact for stationary solutions at a feasible point \(\bar x\) if there exist a neighborhood \(U\) of \(\bar x\) and \(\bar\lambda\ge0\) such that, for every \(\lambda\ge\bar\lambda\) and \(x\in U\),
\[
0\in\partial P_\lambda(x)
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
x\in C\ \text{ and }\ 0\in\partial f(x)+N_C(x).
\]
The definition requires both exclusion of infeasible penalized stationary points and preservation of constrained stationary points.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A stationary-exact penalty locally makes penalized stationary points coincide with feasible constrained stationary points for every sufficiently large parameter.
knowledge_statements.title: Exact Penalties for Stationary Solutions

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition depends materially on the selected generalized subdifferential, compatible normal cone, and associated calculus. Those objects are left generic, so the asserted two-way stationary correspondence cannot be assessed without a source-specific stationarity framework.

children.title: Pull-Out Penalization
children.top_down_role: Penalty constructions that externalize selected difficult terms or constraints.

assumptions_latex: \(f_i=g_i-h_i\) for \(i=1,\ldots,m\), with every \(g_i,h_i\) finite convex functions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(v=G-H\), where \(H=\sum_{j=1}^m h_j\) and \(G=\max\{H,g_i+\sum_{j\ne i}h_j:i=1,\ldots,m\}\).

notation.meaning: convex components of the pulled-out representation

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: algebraic pull-out representation of a maximum of DC functions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite maximum-violation penalty for DC inequality constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Pull the sum of all concave components outside the maximum by setting
\[
H(x):=\sum_{j=1}^m h_j(x),
\qquad
G(x):=\max\left\{H(x),\ g_i(x)+\sum_{j\ne i}h_j(x):1\le i\le m\right\}.
\]
Every expression inside the maximum defining \(G\) is convex, so \(G\) is convex. Direct subtraction gives
\[
G(x)-H(x)=\max\{0,g_1(x)-h_1(x),\ldots,g_m(x)-h_m(x)\}=v(x).
\]
Thus \(f_0+\lambda v\) inherits an explicit DC representation whenever \(f_0\) is DC.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A maximum of finitely many DC constraint violations becomes DC by pulling the sum of all concave components outside the maximum.
knowledge_statements.title: Pull-Out Penalization

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The finite-maximum pull-out identity is algebraically correct and representation is the appropriate content kind, but no dedicated source is cited and the statement includes the derivation rather than only the representation.

children.title: Composite Penalization
children.top_down_role: Penalty constructions embedded within composite DC structures.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Convex-Inner Composite DC Regime
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Safe sufficient regime in which a composite violation penalty preserves a DC objective.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(D\) be convex, let \(f_0=g_0-h_0\) with finite convex \(g_0,h_0\) on \(D\), let every \(r_i:D\to\mathbb R\) be convex, and let \(\psi:\mathbb R^m\to\mathbb R\) be finite, convex, and coordinatewise nondecreasing on a convex set containing \(r(D)\). Then \(\psi\circ r\) is convex on \(D\), and for every \(\lambda\ge0\), \[f_0(x)+\lambda\psi(r(x))=\bigl(g_0(x)+\lambda\psi(r(x))\bigr)-h_0(x)\] is a valid DC decomposition on \(D\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Convex residual components and a convex coordinatewise nondecreasing aggregator yield a convex composite penalty and therefore preserve DC structure.
assumptions_latex: r_i\text{ is convex on }D\text{ for every }i.
\psi\text{ is finite, convex, and coordinatewise nondecreasing on a convex set containing }r(D).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: f_0+\lambda\psi\circ r=(g_0+\lambda\psi\circ r)-h_0\text{ is DC on }D.
knowledge_statements.title: Convex-Inner Composite DC Regime

assumptions_latex: \(F:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^m\) has componentwise DC entries.
\(\psi:\mathbb R^m\to[0,+\infty)\) is convex, coordinatewise nondecreasing, and \(\psi(F(x))=0\) exactly on the feasible set.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The composite penalty family is \(P_\lambda(x)=f_0(x)+\lambda\psi(F(x))\), with \(\lambda\ge0\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: standard convex-composite violation penalty specialized to DC residuals
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Convex-composite aggregation of vector DC residuals.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Given the residual vector \(F(x)=(F_1(x),\ldots,F_m(x))\), composite penalization forms
\[
P_\lambda(x):=f_0(x)+\lambda(\psi\circ F)(x),
\qquad \lambda\ge0.
\]
The zero-set requirement ensures that the added term vanishes precisely at feasible points. Coordinatewise monotonicity permits positive residuals to be aggregated without reversing constraint order. A DC decomposition of \(\psi\circ F\) requires an applicable DC composition rule or an explicit algebraic representation; it does not follow from componentwise DC structure alone.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Composite penalization applies a convex nondecreasing violation aggregator to a vector of DC residuals and adds the result to the objective.
knowledge_statements.title: Composite Penalization

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The penalty-family definition is coherent, but componentwise DC residuals and a convex coordinatewise-nondecreasing aggregator do not alone ensure that the composite is DC. A source identifying the intended composite DC regime or sufficient composition hypotheses is required.

children.title: Penalty-Structure Equivalence Regimes
children.top_down_role: Settings where pull-out or composite penalty forms preserve comparable solution targets.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Common Zero Sets Do Not Transfer Exactness
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary separating feasibility equivalence from quantitative penalty equivalence.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f(x)=-|x|\), \(C=\{0\}\), \(v_1(x)=|x|\), and \(v_2(x)=x^2\). Although \(v_1^{-1}(0)=v_2^{-1}(0)=C\), every \(\lambda>1\) makes \(0\) a global minimizer of \(f+\lambda v_1=(\lambda-1)|x|\), whereas for every finite \(\lambda>0\), \[-|x|+\lambda x^2<0=(f+\lambda v_2)(0)\] for all sufficiently small nonzero \(x\). Thus the \(v_2\)-penalty is not locally exact at \(0\) for any finite weight.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Two penalties can detect the same feasible set while only one has sufficient local growth for finite exactness.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: v_1^{-1}(0)=v_2^{-1}(0)=C\text{, but exactness does not transfer from zero-set equality alone}.
knowledge_statements.title: Common Zero Sets Do Not Transfer Exactness

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Exactness Transfer under Comparable Penalties
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Quantitative regime transferring global optimal-solution exactness between two penalty structures.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(v_1,v_2:D\to[0,+\infty]\) have the same zero set \(C\), and suppose \(0<a\le b<\infty\) satisfies \[a v_1(x)\le v_2(x)\le b v_1(x)\qquad(x\in D).\] If \(f+\rho v_1\) is globally exact for every \(\rho>\rho_1\), then \(f+\lambda v_2\) is globally exact for every \(\lambda>\rho_1/a\). Conversely, if \(f+\rho v_2\) is globally exact for every \(\rho>\rho_2\), then \(f+\lambda v_1\) is globally exact for every \(\lambda>b\rho_2\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Uniform two-sided comparability transfers global exactness between composite and pull-out penalties after rescaling their parameters.
assumptions_latex: 0<a\le b<\infty\text{ and }a v_1\le v_2\le b v_1\text{ on }D.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \rho_1\text{-eventual exactness of }v_1\Rightarrow(\rho_1/a)\text{-eventual exactness of }v_2,\quad \rho_2\text{-eventual exactness of }v_2\Rightarrow(b\rho_2)\text{-eventual exactness of }v_1.
knowledge_statements.title: Exactness Transfer under Comparable Penalties

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Sum-Max Comparison for Nonnegative Residuals
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Explicit comparison constants for sum and maximum aggregation of finitely many nonnegative violations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(r_i:D\to[0,+\infty]\), and define \(v_\infty(x)=\max_{1\le i\le m}r_i(x)\) and \(v_1(x)=\sum_{i=1}^m r_i(x)\). Then \[v_\infty(x)\le v_1(x)\le m v_\infty(x)\qquad(x\in D),\] and \[v_\infty^{-1}(0)=v_1^{-1}(0)=\{x:r_i(x)=0\ \forall i\}.\] Thus Exactness Transfer under Comparable Penalties applies with comparison constants \(a=1\) and \(b=m\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Maximum and sum penalties for finitely many nonnegative residuals are uniformly comparable and therefore admit explicit exactness-transfer constants.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: v_\infty\le v_1\le m v_\infty\text{ and }v_\infty^{-1}(0)=v_1^{-1}(0)=\bigcap_i r_i^{-1}(0).
knowledge_statements.title: Sum-Max Comparison for Nonnegative Residuals

assumptions_latex: \(F_i=g_i-h_i\) for finitely many scalar DC residuals.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \((\psi\circ F)(x)=G(x)-H(x)\), so composite and pull-out penalized objectives coincide for every \(\lambda\ge0\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: exact algebraic identity for maximum aggregation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact equivalence for finite maximum aggregation, not arbitrary composite aggregators.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For the maximum aggregator,
\[
(\psi\circ F)(x)=\max\{0,g_1(x)-h_1(x),\ldots,g_m(x)-h_m(x)\}=G(x)-H(x).
\]
Consequently, the composite penalty \(f_0+\lambda(\psi\circ F)\) and the pull-out penalty \(f_0+\lambda(G-H)\) are the same function for every \(\lambda\ge0\). For a general convex nondecreasing \(\psi\), such equivalence holds only when an identity \(\psi\circ F=\widetilde G-\widetilde H\) has been established; componentwise DC decompositions alone are insufficient.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Maximum aggregation makes composite and pull-out penalties identical; general aggregators require a separate valid DC representation.
knowledge_statements.title: Penalty-Structure Equivalence Regimes

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The maximum-aggregator identity correctly gives equality of the composite and pull-out penalty structures and the condition role fits the equivalence-regime leaf, but no inspectable source supports the selected regime.

children.title: Successive Penalty Models
children.top_down_role: Sequences of DC penalty models indexed by changing enforcement strength.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Convergence of Approximately Solved Successive Penalty Models
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Global cluster-point convergence for increasing linear penalties on a compact domain.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\) be compact, let \(f,v:X\to\mathbb R\) be continuous, let \(v\ge0\), and suppose \(C=\{x\in X:v(x)=0\}\ne\varnothing\). Let \(\rho_k\to\infty\), \(\varepsilon_k\to0\), and choose \(x^k\in X\) such that \(f(x^k)+\rho_kv(x^k)\le\inf_{x\in X}\{f(x)+\rho_kv(x)\}+\varepsilon_k\). Then \(v(x^k)\to0\), every cluster point of \((x^k)\) belongs to \(\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in C}f(x)\), and \(f(x^k)\to\min_{x\in C}f(x)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: On a compact domain, increasingly penalized models solved to vanishing global objective error become feasible, and every cluster point globally solves the constrained problem.
assumptions_latex: \(\rho_k\to\infty\), \(\varepsilon_k\to0\), and each stage is solved within global objective error \(\varepsilon_k\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(v(x^k)\to0\), \(\operatorname{clust}(x^k)\subseteq\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in C}f(x)\), and \(f(x^k)\to\min_{x\in C}f(x)\).
knowledge_statements.title: Convergence of Approximately Solved Successive Penalty Models
Successive Penalty Models
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional exterior-penalty sequence for a DC-compatible constrained problem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(X\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be nonempty and convex, let \(f:X\to\mathbb R\), and let \(v:X\to\mathbb R_+\) satisfy \(v(x)=0\) exactly on the feasible set \(C\subseteq X\). Given \(0<\rho_k\uparrow\infty\), define
\[
F_k(x)=f(x)+\rho_kv(x),\qquad \min_{x\in X}F_k(x).
\]
If \(f=g-h\) and \(v=p-q\), where \(g,h,p,q:X\to\mathbb R\) are finite convex functions, then
\[
F_k=(g+\rho_kp)-(h+\rho_kq)
\]
is a DC decomposition for every \(k\). Thus the constrained problem is represented by unconstrained DC penalty models with increasing violation cost.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: On a convex finite-dimensional domain, a constrained DC problem can be represented by DC penalty models whose parameters increase and whose nonnegative violation term vanishes exactly at feasible points.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F_k=(g+\rho_kp)-(h+\rho_kq)\) is a DC penalty model for every \(k\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Successively increased penalty method
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Generic outer penalty-parameter method using a supplied unconstrained minimization routine; it provides no convergence, exactness, or finite-feasibility guarantee.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Given an objective \(f\), penalty function \(p\), initial iterate \(x\), iteration limit \(k_{\max}\), initial parameter \(\rho>0\), and multiplier \(\gamma>1\), repeat for at most \(k_{\max}\) iterations:
\[
x\leftarrow \operatorname{minimize}\bigl(z\mapsto f(z)+\rho p(z),\,x\bigr).
\]
If \(p(x)=0\), return \(x\); otherwise update
\[
\rho\leftarrow\gamma\rho.
\]
If the limit is reached, return the last iterate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Repeatedly apply a suitable unconstrained minimization method to the current penalized objective. Return an iterate when its penalty is zero; otherwise multiply the penalty parameter by a factor greater than one, and return the last iterate at the iteration limit.
assumptions_latex: \operatorname{minimize}\ \text{is a suitable unconstrained minimization procedure initialized at the current iterate}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: p(x)=0\Rightarrow\text{return }x;\qquad p(x)\ne0\Rightarrow\rho\leftarrow\gamma\rho,\ \text{with the last iterate returned after at most }k_{\max}\text{ iterations.}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Global Penalty-Path Monotonicity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Tradeoff monotonicity along globally solved linear-penalty models.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\ne\varnothing\), \(f:X\to\mathbb R\), \(v:X\to\mathbb R_+\), \(F_\rho=f+\rho v\), and \(q(\rho)=\inf_{x\in X}F_\rho(x)\). Then \(q\) is an extended-real-valued nondecreasing concave function on \([0,\infty)\). If \(0\le\rho_1<\rho_2\) and \(x_j\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in X}F_{\rho_j}(x)\), then \(v(x_2)\le v(x_1)\) and \(f(x_1)\le f(x_2)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Along globally minimized linear-penalty models, increasing the parameter cannot increase violation or decrease the selected unpenalized objective; the optimal value is nondecreasing and concave.
assumptions_latex: Global minimizers exist at the parameters used in the minimizer comparison.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(q\) is nondecreasing and concave, and \(\rho_1<\rho_2\Rightarrow v(x_2)\le v(x_1),\ f(x_1)\le f(x_2)\).
knowledge_statements.title: Global Penalty-Path Monotonicity
Penalty Continuation Models
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Warm-started continuation across an increasing sequence of DC penalty parameters.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input \(x^0\in X\), \(\rho_0>0\), a multiplier \(\gamma>1\), tolerances \(\varepsilon_k\downarrow0\), and a stopping tolerance \(\tau\ge0\). At stage \(k\), approximately minimize \(F_k(x)=f(x)+\rho_kv(x)\) from the warm start \(x^k\), producing \(x^{k+1}\) with \(\operatorname{dist}(0,\partial F_k(x^{k+1})+N_X(x^{k+1}))\le\varepsilon_k\). Stop and output \(x^{k+1}\) when \(v(x^{k+1})\le\tau\); otherwise set \(\rho_{k+1}=\gamma\rho_k\) and continue. For a DC model, the inner minimization may use a DC criticality oracle.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Approximately solve increasingly penalized models, warm-start each stage from the preceding solution, and stop when the violation meets the prescribed tolerance.
assumptions_latex: \(v:X\to\mathbb R_+\) vanishes exactly on the feasible set
\(\partial\) is a specified limiting or convex subdifferential appropriate to \(F_k\)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The output satisfies \(v(x^{k+1})\le\tau\); otherwise the algorithm generates \(\rho_k\uparrow\infty\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Exactness-Threshold Endpoint Alternatives
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Examples showing that exactness and coexistence at the least threshold are not determined by the open exact regime above it.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X=[0,1]\), \(v(x)=x\), and \(C=\{0\}\). If \(f(x)=-x\), then the least exactness threshold is \(\rho_*=1\), and at \(\rho=1\) every point of \(X\) minimizes \(f+\rho v\), so feasible and infeasible minimizers coexist. If instead \(f(x)=-x+x^2\), the least threshold is again \(\rho_*=1\), but at \(\rho=1\) the unique minimizer is the feasible point \(0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Two elementary penalty paths have the same least exactness threshold but different endpoint behavior: one has feasible–infeasible coexistence, while the other is already exact at the threshold.
assumptions_latex: The two objective choices are \(f(x)=-x\) and \(f(x)=-x+x^2\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\rho_*=1\) in both examples, but exactness fails at the endpoint in the first example and holds at the endpoint in the second.
knowledge_statements.title: Exactness-Threshold Endpoint Alternatives

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Persistence after a Feasible Global Penalty Minimizer
knowledge_statements.scope_note: One-sided transition from a parameter admitting a feasible global minimizer to strict larger-parameter exactness.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(v:X\to\mathbb R_+\), \(F_\rho=f+\rho v\), and suppose that for some \(\rho_0\ge0\) there exists \(\bar x\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in X}F_{\rho_0}(x)\) with \(v(\bar x)=0\). Then \(\bar x\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in X}F_\rho(x)\) for every \(\rho\ge\rho_0\). For every \(\rho>\rho_0\), every global minimizer of \(F_\rho\) is feasible and minimizes \(f\) over \(C=\{x:v(x)=0\}\). At \(\rho=\rho_0\), infeasible global minimizers may coexist with \(\bar x\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Once a parameter admits a feasible global minimizer, that minimizer persists, and every global minimizer is constrained-optimal at every strictly larger parameter; infeasible ties may remain at the transition parameter.
assumptions_latex: A feasible global minimizer of \(F_{\rho_0}\) exists.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\bar x\in S(\rho)\) for \(\rho\ge\rho_0\), and \(\rho>\rho_0\Rightarrow S(\rho)\subseteq\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in C}f(x)\).

notation.meaning: global minimizer set of the penalty model

knowledge_statements.title: Persistence after a Feasible Global Penalty Minimizer
Penalty-Path Transition Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Least exact-penalty threshold separating nonexact and exact portions of a global minimizer path.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(X\) be compact, let \(f,v:X\to\mathbb R\) be continuous, and suppose \(v\ge0\) with \(C=\{x\in X:v(x)=0\}\ne\varnothing\). Define
\[
S(\rho)=\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in X}\{f(x)+\rho v(x)\}
\]
and suppose the set
\[
E=\{\eta\ge0:S(\rho)\subseteq\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in C}f(x)\text{ for every }\rho>\eta\}
\]
is nonempty. With \(\rho_*=\inf E\), every \(\rho>\rho_*\) lies in the exact regime, whereas for every \(0\le\rho<\rho_*\), not all members of \(S(\rho)\) are feasible constrained minimizers. At \(\rho=\rho_*\), exactness may hold or fail, and feasible and infeasible global minimizers may coexist.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The least finite exact-penalty threshold separates parameters below which the penalty model is not globally exact from parameters above which every global minimizer solves the constrained problem; behavior at the threshold can vary.
assumptions_latex: The global exactness-threshold set \(E\) is nonempty
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\rho>\rho_*\Rightarrow S(\rho)\subseteq\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in C}f(x)\), while \(0\le\rho<\rho_*\Rightarrow S(\rho)\nsubseteq\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in C}f(x)\).

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A vector \bar x\in\widehat{\mathbf X}\text{ is blockwise d-stationary for (7.30) if and only if, for every }\beta>0,\ \sigma_i>0,\text{ and every active-index tuple }(j_i)\in\prod_{i=1}^{I}\mathcal A_i(\bar x^i),\quad \bar x\in\arg\min_{x\in\widehat{\mathbf X}}\left[\nabla\varphi(\bar x)^\top(x-\bar x)+\sum_{i=1}^{I+1}H(x^i,\bar x^{-i})-\sum_{i=1}^{I}\nabla g_{ij_i}(\bar x^i)^\top(x^i-\bar x^i)+\frac{\beta}{2}\sum_{i=1}^{I+1}\|A^ix^i-A^i\bar x^i\|_2^2+\sum_{i=1}^{I+1}\frac{\sigma_i}{2}\|x^i-\bar x^i\|_2^2\right].

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Method-specific convergence result for the quadratic bilevel DC reformulation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For iterates generated by the XY procedure: (i) if $\rho_s>0$ for all $s$ and $\sum_{s=1}^{\infty}\rho_s<\infty$, then $\Phi_s:=\Phi(x^s,y^s,v^s)$ converges; (ii) if $(x^s,y^s,v^s)\to(\widehat x,\widehat y,\widehat v)$, then $\Phi(\widehat x,\widehat y,\widehat v)\leq\Phi(\widehat x,\widehat y,v)$ for every $v\in\mathcal F(\widehat x,\widehat y)$ and $\Phi(\widehat x,\widehat y,\widehat v)\leq\Phi(x,y,\widehat v)$ for every $(x,y)\in\mathcal F(\widehat v)$.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Demyanov difference of convex compact sets
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Includes the exposed-face construction and invariance under equivalent representing pairs.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For convex compact sets $A,B\subset\mathbb R^n$, define $A(g)=\operatorname*{argmax}_{v\in A}\langle v,g\rangle$, $B(g)=\operatorname*{argmax}_{v\in B}\langle v,g\rangle$, and $C(g)=A(g)-B(g)$. Let $C^*=\{g:C(g)\text{ is a singleton}\}$ and $C^0=\{g\in C^*:\|g\|=1\}$. The Demyanov difference is $A-B=\operatorname{cl}\operatorname{co}\{C(g):g\in C^0\}$. Moreover, $C(\lambda g)=C(g)$ for every $g\in\mathbb R^n$ and $\lambda>0$, $C^*$ has full measure, and equivalent pairs $[U,-V]$ and $[W,-Z]$ satisfy $U-V=W-Z$.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For convex compact sets A and B, take the difference of their exposed faces in each direction for which that difference is a singleton, restrict to unit directions, and form the closed convex hull. The exposed-face difference is unchanged by positive rescaling of the direction, singleton directions have full measure, and equivalent representing pairs have the same resulting difference.
assumptions_latex: A,B,U,V,W,Z\subset\mathbb R^n\text{ are convex and compact}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A-B=\operatorname{cl}\operatorname{co}\{A(g)-B(g):g\in C^0\},\quad C(\lambda g)=C(g),\quad [U,-V]\sim[W,-Z]\Rightarrow U-V=W-Z.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Deep multicomposite models with diff-max piecewise-affine activations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Recursive network and multicomposite empirical-risk models with piecewise-affine scalar activations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let (N_0,\ldots,N_L) be positive integers with N_0=d and N_L=1. An L-layer network with parameters x=\{(W^\ell,w^\ell)\}_{\ell=1}^L is defined recursively by
\[
u^0=\xi,\qquad u^\ell=\Xi^\ell(W^\ell u^{\ell-1}+w^\ell),\quad \ell=1,\ldots,L,
\]
where \Xi^\ell(u)=(\sigma_\ell(u_j))_{j=1}^{N_\ell}, and its scalar output is m(x;\xi)=u^L. Given data \{(\xi^s,z_s)\}_{s=1}^N, training minimizes N^{-1}\sum_s\varphi(m(x;\xi^s);z_s). More generally, for closed convex sets X^\ell and layer maps m^\ell, the multicomposite problem is
\[
\min_{x\in\prod_{\ell=1}^L X^\ell}\frac1N\sum_{s=1}^N\varphi_s\!\left(m^L(x^L,\cdot)\circ\cdots\circ m^1(x^1;\xi^s)\right).
\]
Every scalar-valued piecewise-affine activation admits a finite diff-max representation
\[
\sigma(t)=\max_{1\le i\le k_1}(a_it+\alpha_i)-\max_{1\le i\le k_2}(b_it+\beta_i).
\]
Moreover, every continuous scalar function on a closed interval can be uniformly approximated arbitrarily closely by continuous piecewise-affine functions. ReLU is itself convex piecewise affine, while smooth activations such as sigmoid and hyperbolic tangent may therefore be approximated by such activations.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A deep network is a recursion of affine transformations and separable activations, and training is empirical-loss minimization over its layer parameters. This extends to an abstract multicomposite optimization problem over closed convex layer-parameter sets. Every scalar piecewise-affine activation can be written as a difference of two finite maxima of affine functions. Continuous functions on closed intervals can be uniformly approximated arbitrarily well by continuous piecewise-affine functions, so such activations cover ReLU directly and can approximate smooth activations.
assumptions_latex: X^\ell\subseteq\mathbb R^{N_{x;\ell}}\text{ is closed and convex for }\ell=1,\ldots,L
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: m(x;\xi)\text{ is an }L\text{-fold composite model used in empirical-loss minimization, and each scalar piecewise-affine activation }\sigma\text{ admits the stated finite diff-max representation.}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Finite Max–Min Decomposition Identities
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Purely pointwise identities; no convexity assumptions are required.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let f_i=\varphi_i+\psi_i:X\to\mathbb{R} for i=1,\ldots,k. Then, for every x\in X,\quad \max_{1\le i\le k}f_i(x)=\max_{1\le j\le k}\left(\varphi_j(x)-\sum_{i\ne j}\psi_i(x)\right)+\sum_{i=1}^k\psi_i(x),\quad \min_{1\le i\le k}f_i(x)=\sum_{i=1}^k\varphi_i(x)+\min_{1\le j\le k}\left(\psi_j(x)-\sum_{i\ne j}\varphi_i(x)\right).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For any finite family of functions decomposed as f_i=φ_i+ψ_i, its pointwise maximum and minimum admit explicit rearrangements separating sums from one finite maximum or minimum.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Generalized critical point of an ICC function
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines constrained generalized criticality through partial convex subdifferentials of the associated bifunction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let $X\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ be closed and convex, let $g:X\to\mathbb R$ be an ICC function with associated convex-concave bifunction $h(x,z)$, and let $\bar x\in X$. Then $\bar x$ is a generalized critical point of $g$ on $X$ if $0\in\partial_x h(\bar x,\bar x)-\partial_z(-h)(\bar x,\bar x)+\mathcal N(\bar x;X)$, where the two partial subdifferentials are those of the convex functions $h(\cdot,\bar x)$ and $-h(\bar x,\cdot)$ at $\bar x$.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A feasible point is generalized critical for an ICC function when zero belongs to the first-variable convex subdifferential of its bifunction representation minus the second-variable convex subdifferential of the negated bifunction, plus the normal cone to the feasible set.

g:X\to\mathbb R\text{ is an ICC function}
h\text{ is the associated convex-concave bifunction}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Global Search Algorithm for quadratic bilevel DC problems
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Procedural specification only. The extract supplies a stopping rule but no convergence, finite-termination, or global-optimality guarantee, and some sample-exhaustion paths are underspecified.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Given \((x_0,y_0,v_0)\in\mathcal F\), positive sequences \(\tau_k\downarrow0\) and \(\delta_k\downarrow0\), a finite nonzero direction set \(\mathrm{Dir}\), bounds \(\gamma_-:=\inf(g,\mathcal F)\) and \(\gamma_+:=\sup(g,\mathcal F)\), \(M\in\mathbb N_{>0}\), and \(\mu\in\mathbb R_+\), set \(\Delta\gamma=(\gamma_+-\gamma_-)/M\). At each outer iteration, compute a \(\tau_k\)-critical point \((x^k,y^k,v^k)\) and set \(\zeta_k:=\Phi(x^k,y^k,v^k)\). For successive directions and levels \(\gamma\), construct samples satisfying
\[
H(z^i,u^i,w^i)=\gamma-\zeta_k.
\]
Reject a sample when \(G(z^i,u^i,w^i)>\gamma+\mu\gamma\). For each retained sample, compute a \(\delta_k\)-solution of
\[
\min_{(x,y,v)\in\mathcal F}G(x,y,v)-\langle\nabla H(z^i,u^i,w^i),(x,y,v)\rangle,
\]
then apply the local-search method to obtain a \(\tau_k\)-critical point \((\widehat x^i,\widehat y^i,\widehat v^i)\). If
\[
\Phi(\widehat x^i,\widehat y^i,\widehat v^i)<\Phi(x^k,y^k,v^k),
\]
restart the outer iteration from that point and reset \(\gamma=\gamma_-\). Otherwise continue through the directions and level grid, stopping under the stated condition at \(i=N\) and \(\gamma=gamma_+\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The algorithm alternates local DC critical-point computation with a global escape phase based on sampled DC level surfaces, filtered samples, linearized subproblems, local refinement, and strict-improvement restarts. The stopping instruction is procedural and is not itself a global-optimality theorem.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \Phi(\widehat x^i,\widehat y^i,\widehat v^i)<\Phi(x^k,y^k,v^k)\Rightarrow\text{restart from }(\widehat x^i,\widehat y^i,\widehat v^i);\quad i=N,\ \gamma=\gamma_+,\ \Phi(\widehat x^i,\widehat y^i,\widehat v^i)\geq\Phi(x^k,y^k,v^k)\Rightarrow\text{stop}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Double-Min Duality for a Structured DC Pair
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Strong value equality and stationary-point correspondence for a primal-dual pair of difference-of-convex objectives.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let A:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^m, c\in\mathbb R^n, b\in\mathbb R^m. Let k:\mathbb R^n\to\overline{\mathbb R} be convex, proper, lsc, fully coercive, and almost strictly convex, and let h:\mathbb R^m\to\mathbb R be convex, finite, and differentiable. Define \varphi(x)=\langle c,x\rangle+k(x)-h(Ax-b) and \psi(y)=\langle b,y\rangle+h^*(y)-k^*(A^*y-c). Then h^* is lsc, proper, fully coercive, and almost strictly convex; k^* is finite and differentiable; \varphi and \psi are amenable; and \inf\varphi=\inf\psi. Moreover, with S:=\{(x,y):y=\nabla h(Ax-b),\ A^*y-c\in\partial k(x)\}=\{(x,y):x=\nabla k^*(A^*y-c),\ Ax-b\in\partial h^*(y)\}, one has 0\in\partial\varphi(\bar x)\iff\exists\bar y\,((\bar x,\bar y)\in S), 0\in\partial\psi(\bar y)\iff\exists\bar x\,((\bar x,\bar y)\in S), and (\bar x,\bar y)\in S\Rightarrow\varphi(\bar x)=\psi(\bar y).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For the stated coercive and almost-strictly-convex function k and finite differentiable convex function h, the associated primal and conjugate dual DC minimization problems have equal infima. Their generalized stationary points correspond exactly through the set S, and every paired point in S has equal primal and dual objective values.
assumptions_latex: A:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^m,\quad c\in\mathbb R^n,\quad b\in\mathbb R^m
k:\mathbb R^n\to\overline{\mathbb R}\text{ is convex, proper, lsc, fully coercive, and almost strictly convex}
h:\mathbb R^m\to\mathbb R\text{ is convex, finite, and differentiable}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \inf_{x\in\mathbb R^n}\varphi(x)=\inf_{y\in\mathbb R^m}\psi(y),\quad 0\in\partial\varphi(\bar x)\iff\exists\bar y:(\bar x,\bar y)\in S,\quad 0\in\partial\psi(\bar y)\iff\exists\bar x:(\bar x,\bar y)\in S,\quad (\bar x,\bar y)\in S\Rightarrow\varphi(\bar x)=\psi(\bar y)

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define $L(x)=\bigcap_{w\in\bar\partial h(x)}[\partial f(x)+\operatorname{cl}(\operatorname{cone}(\partial h(x)+w))]$. knowledge_statements.statement_title: Quasi-Secant Method (QSM) iteration
knowledge_statements.scope_note: The extracted pseudocode contains a notation mismatch between the computed \(\bar v_{k_s}\) and the tested \(\widetilde v_{k_s}\); the test is retained as stated.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Initialize \(x_1\in\mathbb R^n\), \(d_{1_1}\in S_1\), and \(k=1\). At outer iteration \(k\), set \(s=1\), \(x_{k_s}=x_k\), choose \(h_k>0\) with \(h_k\downarrow0\), compute a first quasi-secant \(v_{k_1}(x_{k_1},d_{k_1},h_k)\), and set \(\bar V(x_{k_1})=\{v_{k_1}\}\). At each inner iteration compute \(\bar v_{k_s}\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{v\in\bar V(x_{k_s})}\|v\|^2\). If the stated termination test \(\|\widetilde v_{k_s}\|\le\delta_k\), where \(\delta_k>0\) and \(\delta_k\downarrow0\), holds, set \(x_{k+1}=x_{k_s}\) and begin the next outer iteration. Otherwise set \(d_{k_s}=-\bar v_{k_s}/\|\bar v_{k_s}\|\) and find \(t_{k_s}\). If the descent condition holds, set \(x_{k_{s+1}}=x_{k_s}+t_{k_s}d_{k_s}\), compute a new quasi-secant there, and reset its collection to the singleton containing it. If descent fails, keep \(x_{k_{s+1}}=x_{k_s}\), compute a new quasi-secant at that point in direction \(d_{k_s}\), and set \(\bar V(x_{k_{s+1}})=\operatorname{conv}(\bar V(x_{k_s})\cup\{v_{k_{s+1}}\})\). Increment \(s\) and repeat until termination.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: QSM repeatedly forms the minimum-norm vector in a maintained convex set of quasi-secants. A sufficiently small tested vector accepts the current point as the next outer iterate. Otherwise, the normalized negative minimum-norm vector is used as a search direction: a successful descent step moves the point and restarts the quasi-secant set, while a failed step keeps the point and enlarges the set by convexifying it with a new quasi-secant.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{The procedure returns its final outer iterate }x_k.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Two-Sided CVaR as a Structured DC Tail Functional
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Weighted combination of pessimistic upper-tail and optimistic lower-tail sample averages.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(y_{[1]}\ge\cdots\ge y_{[N]}\), let \(k_{\mathrm p},k_{\mathrm o}\in\{1,\ldots,N\}\), and let \(w_{\mathrm p},w_{\mathrm o}>0\). If the probability ambiguity sets are the unit simplex and their indicator costs impose \(0\le p_s\le1/k_{\mathrm p}\) and \(0\le p_s\le1/k_{\mathrm o}\), respectively, then
\[
v_{\mathrm{op}}^{\mathrm{pr}}(y)=w_{\mathrm p}\operatorname{sCVaR}_{k_{\mathrm p}}(y)-w_{\mathrm o}\operatorname{sCVaR}_{k_{\mathrm o}}(-y)
=\frac{w_{\mathrm p}}{k_{\mathrm p}}\sum_{s=1}^{k_{\mathrm p}}y_{[s]}+\frac{w_{\mathrm o}}{k_{\mathrm o}}\sum_{s=N-k_{\mathrm o}+1}^{N}y_{[s]}.
\]
Hence the two-sided CVaR is a difference of two convex sampled-CVaR functions and therefore a DC functional.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under capped-simplex probability ambiguity, the optimistic–pessimistic value is the weighted average of the largest k_p samples plus the weighted average of the smallest k_o samples. knowledge_statements.statement_title: Convex composite diff-max function
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines the objective class on a closed convex feasible set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let $X\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n$ be closed and convex, let $\varphi:\mathbb{R}\to\mathbb{R}$ be convex, and let $J_1,J_2$ be positive integers. If $\psi_{ij}:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}$ are convex and differentiable and
\[\psi(x)=\max_{1\le j\le J_1}\psi_{1j}(x)-\max_{1\le j\le J_2}\psi_{2j}(x),\qquad f(x)=(\varphi\circ\psi)(x),\]

knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A convex composite diff-max function is the composition of a univariate convex function with the difference of two finite maxima of differentiable convex functions.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Fischer–Burmeister function and its generalized gradients
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Includes the function's Lipschitz and first-order semismooth regularity, its B-subdifferential and generalized gradient, and their uniform bounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define \(\phi^{FB}:\mathbb{R}^2\to\mathbb{R}\) by \(\phi^{FB}(x)=x_1+x_2-\sqrt{x_1^2+x_2^2}\). Then \(\phi^{FB}\) is globally Lipschitz continuous and first-order semismooth. Writing \(f(x)=x_1+x_2\), \(\partial_B\phi^{FB}(x)=f'(x)-\partial_B\|x\|_2\) and \(\partial\phi^{FB}(x)=f'(x)-\partial\|x\|_2\). If \(x\ne0\), both sets equal \(\{(1,1)-x^T/\|x\|_2\}\). At \(x=0\), \(\partial_B\phi^{FB}(0)=\{(1,1)-y^T:\|y\|_2=1\}\) and \(\partial\phi^{FB}(0)=\{(1,1)-y^T:\|y\|_2\le1\}\). For every \(x\in\mathbb{R}^2\) and \(v\in\partial\phi^{FB}(x)\), \(v_1,v_2\ge0\) and \(2-\sqrt2\le v_1+v_2\le2+\sqrt2\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The Fischer–Burmeister function is x1+x2 minus the Euclidean norm of x. It is globally Lipschitz continuous and first-order semismooth. Away from zero its B-subdifferential and generalized gradient are the singleton containing (1,1)−x/||x||; at zero they correspond respectively to subtracting vectors on the Euclidean unit sphere and in the closed unit ball from (1,1). Every generalized gradient has nonnegative components, with component sum between 2−sqrt(2) and 2+sqrt(2).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \phi^{FB}\text{ is globally Lipschitz and first-order semismooth, with the stated subdifferential formulas and }v_1,v_2\ge0,\quad 2-\sqrt2\le v_1+v_2\le2+\sqrt2.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Michel–Penot subdifferential as a limit of approximate quasidifferential differences
knowledge_statements.scope_note: The compactness conclusion requires uniform boundedness of the associated differences, not necessarily of the two quasidifferential components separately.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let $X\subset\mathbb R^n$ be open and let $f:X\to\mathbb R$ be Lipschitz and directionally differentiable at $x\in X$. Then $h(g)=f'(x;g)$ is continuous and positively homogeneous. For every $\varepsilon>0$ there are convex compact sets $\underline\partial_\varepsilon f(x)$ and $\bar\partial_\varepsilon f(x)$ such that $h_\varepsilon(g)=\max_{v\in\underline\partial_\varepsilon f(x)}\langle v,g\rangle+\min_{w\in\bar\partial_\varepsilon f(x)}\langle w,g\rangle$ satisfies $|h(g)-h_\varepsilon(g)|\le\varepsilon$ for all $\|g\|=1$. Put $Q_\varepsilon(x)=\underline\partial_\varepsilon f(x)-(-\bar\partial_\varepsilon f(x))$. If $\{Q_\varepsilon(x):0<\varepsilon\le1\}$ is uniformly bounded, then some sequence $\varepsilon_k\downarrow0$ has a Hausdorff limit $Q^*(x)$, which is convex and compact. If $f$ is quasidifferentiable at $x$ with quasidifferential $[\underline\partial f(x),\bar\partial f(x)]$, then $Q^*(x)=\underline\partial f(x)-(-\bar\partial f(x))$, and this set is the Michel\text{--}Penot subdifferential of $f$ at $x$.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At a point where a Lipschitz function is directionally differentiable, its directional derivative is continuous and positively homogeneous and can be uniformly approximated on the unit sphere by differences of convex positively homogeneous functions represented by convex compact pairs. If the corresponding set differences are uniformly bounded as the error tends to zero, a subsequence converges in the Hausdorff metric to a convex compact set. For a quasidifferentiable function, this limit is the difference associated with its quasidifferential and equals the Michel–Penot subdifferential.
assumptions_latex: f:X\to\mathbb R\text{ is Lipschitz and directionally differentiable at }x
f\text{ is quasidifferentiable at }x\text{ for the final identification}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \exists\,\varepsilon_k\downarrow0:\ Q_{\varepsilon_k}(x)\xrightarrow{d_H}Q^*(x),\quad Q^*(x)\text{ is convex compact};\qquad f\text{ quasidifferentiable}\Rightarrow Q^*(x)=\underline\partial f(x)-(-\bar\partial f(x))=\partial_{MP}f(x).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Semismoothness via convergent generalized-gradient actions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sequential directional definition for a locally Lipschitz scalar function at a reference point.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A locally Lipschitz function $z:\mathbb{R}^p\to\mathbb{R}$ is semismooth at $x^0$ if, for every $r\ne0$, the sequence $\{g^k r\}$ converges whenever $x^k\ne x^0$, 
\[
\frac{x^k-x^0}{\|x^k-x^0\|}\to\frac{r}{\|r\|},
\]
and $g^k\in\partial z(x^k)$ for every $k$.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A locally Lipschitz scalar function is semismooth at a point when generalized gradients along every sequence approaching in a fixed nonzero direction have convergent actions on that direction.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \{g^k r\}_{k=1}^{\infty}\text{ converges}.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: DC Representation of an OCE with Piecewise-Linear Utility
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Expresses the optimized certainty equivalent of a scenario-wise DC function as a convex term plus a concave term.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(\mathcal O\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be convex and, for every \(\omega\in\Xi\), let \(f(x,\omega)=p(x,\omega)-q(x,\omega)\) be a DC decomposition on \(\mathcal O\). If \(u(t)=\min_{1\le i\le I}(a_it+\alpha_i)\), where \(I\ge1\) and \(a_i\ge0\), then
\[\mathcal O_u(f(x,\widetilde\omega))=\Big(\sum_{i=1}^I a_i\Big)\mathbb E[p(x,\widetilde\omega)]+\sup_{\eta\in\mathbb R}\left\{\eta-\mathbb E\left[\max_{1\le i\le I}\left\{\Big(\sum_{i'\ne i}a_{i'}\Big)p(x,\widetilde\omega)+a_i(q(x,\widetilde\omega)+\eta)-\alpha_i\right\}\right]\right\}.\]
The first summand is convex in \(x\), while the second is concave in \(x\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a scenario-wise DC payoff and a concave piecewise-linear utility with nonnegative slopes, the optimized certainty equivalent has an explicit DC representation: a scaled expectation of the convex component plus a concave value term obtained by optimizing over the allocation variable.
assumptions_latex: \forall\omega\in\Xi:\ f(\cdot,\omega)=p(\cdot,\omega)-q(\cdot,\omega)\text{ is a DC decomposition on }\mathcal O
u(t)=\min_{1\le i\le I}(a_it+\alpha_i),\quad I\in\mathbb N,\quad a_i\ge0

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Subdifferential and Exactness of Infimal Convolution
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equates subgradients of an attained infimal convolution with common subgradients and gives the converse attainment condition.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f,g\in\Gamma_0(\mathcal H)\), let \(x\in\operatorname{dom}(f\square g)\), and let \(y\in\mathcal H\). If \[(f\square g)(x)=f(y)+g(x-y),\] then \[\partial(f\square g)(x)=\partial f(y)\cap\partial g(x-y).\] Conversely, if \(\partial f(y)\cap\partial g(x-y)\neq\varnothing\), then \((f\square g)(x)=f(y)+g(x-y)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: When y gives an exact decomposition for an infimal convolution, the resulting subdifferential is the intersection of the two component subdifferentials. A common subgradient conversely certifies that the decomposition is exact.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: (f\square g)(x)=f(y)+g(x-y)\Rightarrow\partial(f\square g)(x)=\partial f(y)\cap\partial g(x-y),\qquad \partial f(y)\cap\partial g(x-y)\neq\varnothing\Rightarrow(f\square g)(x)=f(y)+g(x-y)

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Semiconcavity with a General Modulus
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines semiconcavity on a convex subset of a normed space using a vanishing upper-semicontinuous modulus.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\Omega\) be a convex subset of a normed space and let \(\varphi:\Omega\to\mathbb{R}\). The function \(\varphi\) is semiconcave if there exists a nondecreasing upper semicontinuous function \(\omega:\mathbb{R}_+\to\mathbb{R}_+\), with \(\omega(\rho)\to0\) as \(\rho\downarrow0\), such that for every \(x_1,x_2\in\Omega\) and every \(\lambda\in[0,1]\), \[\lambda\varphi(x_1)+(1-\lambda)\varphi(x_2)-\varphi\bigl(\lambda x_1+(1-\lambda)x_2\bigr)\le \lambda(1-\lambda)\lVert x_1-x_2\rVert\,\omega\bigl(\lVert x_1-x_2\rVert\bigr).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A real-valued function on a convex domain is semiconcave if its concavity defect along every line segment is bounded by lambda times one minus lambda, the distance between the endpoints, and a nondecreasing upper-semicontinuous modulus that vanishes at zero.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \forall x_1,x_2\in\Omega\;\forall\lambda\in[0,1],\quad \lambda\varphi(x_1)+(1-\lambda)\varphi(x_2)-\varphi(\lambda x_1+(1-\lambda)x_2)\le\lambda(1-\lambda)\lVert x_1-x_2\rVert\omega(\lVert x_1-x_2\rVert).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Second-Order Necessary Conditions for a Twice Codifferentiable Global Minimum
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Necessary conditions for unconstrained minimization of a twice codifferentiable function; all directional alternatives and universal quantifiers are retained.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let $f$ be twice codifferentiable and suppose that $x^*\in\mathbb{R}^n$ attains the smallest value of $f$ on $\mathbb{R}^n$. Then inclusion $(6.3)$ holds. Moreover, for every $g\in\mathbb{R}^n$ with $\|g\|=1$, either $f'(x^*,g)>0$, or $f'(x^*,g)=0$ and, for every $w\in\partial f(x^*)$, either $\max_{v\in\partial f(x^*)}(v+w,g)>0$, or $\max_{v\in\underline{\partial}f(x^*)}(v+w,g)=0$ and
\[
\max_{[v,A]\in C(w,g)}\bigl[(v+w,q)+((A+B)g,g)\bigr]\ge 0
\]
for every $q\in\mathbb{R}^n$ and every $B$ such that $[0,w,B]\in d^2f(x^*)$, where
\[
C(w,g)=\{[v,A]:[0,v,A]\in\underline d^{\,2}f(x^*),\ (v+w,g)=0\}.
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At a global minimum of a twice codifferentiable function, the first-order inclusion holds. In every unit direction, either the directional derivative is positive, or it is zero and every admissible first-order codifferential element satisfies one of the stated positive-pairing or second-order nonnegativity alternatives, uniformly over all q and admissible B.
assumptions_latex: f\text{ is twice codifferentiable on the relevant domain}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: (6.3)\text{ holds, and the stated directional alternatives and inequality }(6.4)\text{ hold for every unit }g.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Equivalent characterizations of the bilevel PFC
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equivalence for a fixed pair $(\alpha_2,\alpha_3)\in\mathcal P(\alpha_0)$ in the source's bilevel multiplier notation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For $(\alpha_2,\alpha_3)\in\mathcal P(\alpha_0)$, the following are equivalent. (i) PFC holds for $(\alpha_2,\alpha_3)$. (ii) Every $(\kappa,\omega,\zeta,\tau,\xi)$ satisfying
\[
\kappa^\top(0,\nabla_yG(y^0))+\nabla(\nabla_xL(z^0,\nu^0)\omega)+\zeta^\top\nabla g(z^0)+\tau^\top\nabla h(z^0)=0,
\]
\[
(\nabla_xg(z^0),\nabla_xh(z^0))^\top\omega-(\xi,0)^\top=0,
\quad g_i(z^0)\zeta_i=0,
\quad \xi_i=0\ (i\in I^0),
\quad \kappa^\top G(y^0)=0
\]
also satisfies $\zeta_i=0$ for every $i\in\alpha_2$ and $\xi_i=0$ for every $i\in\alpha_3$. (iii) For every $i_0\in\alpha_2$ there exist $(d,r,\gamma,\eta)$ such that
\[
(\nabla(\nabla_xL(x^0,y^0,\lambda^0,\mu^0)),\nabla_x^\top g(x^0,y^0),\nabla_x^\top h(x^0,y^0))(d,r,\gamma,\eta)^\top=0,
\]
\[
\nabla g_i(x^0,y^0)(d,r)^\top=0\quad(i\in I(x^0,y^0)\setminus\{i_0\}),
\quad \nabla g_{i_0}(x^0,y^0)(d,r)^\top<0,
\]
\[
\gamma_i=0\quad(i\notin J(\lambda^0)),\qquad
\nabla h(x^0,y^0)(d,r)^\top=0,
\qquad \nabla G_i(y)r=0\quad(G_i(y^0)=0),
\]
and, for every $i_0\in\alpha_3$, there exist $(d,r,\gamma,\eta)$ satisfying the same first equation together with
\[
\nabla g_i(x^0,y^0)(d,r)^\top=0\quad(i\in I(x^0,y^0)),
\quad \gamma_i=0\quad(i\notin J(\lambda^0),\ i\ne i_0),
\quad \gamma_{i_0}>0,
\]
\[
\nabla h(x^0,y^0)(d,r)^\top=0,
\qquad \nabla G_i(y)r=0\quad(G_i(y^0)=0).
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a fixed admissible pair of index sets, PFC is equivalent both to a multiplier-annihilation implication and to the existence, for every index in either set, of a solution of the corresponding linearized system having the prescribed strict primal or positive multiplier component.
assumptions_latex: \text{All derivatives, active sets, and multiplier sets are those of the stated bilevel reformulation at }(x^0,y^0,\lambda^0,\mu^0).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \mathrm{PFC}\iff\text{the multiplier implication in (ii)}\iff\text{the two indexed solvability conditions in (iii)}.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Proximal Bundle and Bundle-Trust Algorithm
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Algorithmic template with step-size selection, bundle-index updates, and proximal-parameter updates left to separate rules.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Initialize $x_1\in\mathbb{R}^n$, $\mathcal J_1=\{1\}$, $\bar t\in(0,1]$, $m_L\in(0,\tfrac12)$, $u_1>0$, $\varepsilon>0$, and $v_0\le-\varepsilon$; evaluate $f(x_1)$ and $\xi_1\in\partial f(x_1)$. For $k=1,2,\ldots$ while $|v_{k-1}|>\varepsilon$, compute $d_k\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{d\in\mathbb R^n}\{\widehat f_k(x_k+d)+\tfrac12u_k d^Td\}$ and $v_k=\widehat f_k(x_k+d_k)-f(x_k)$, then choose $t_L^k,t_R^k$. If $f(x_k+t_L^kd_k)\le f(x_k)+m_Lt_L^kv_k$, take a serious step: when $t_L^k>\bar t$, set $x_{k+1}=y_{k+1}=x_k+t_L^kd_k$ and choose $\xi_{k+1}\in\bar\partial f(y_{k+1})$; otherwise set $x_{k+1}=x_k+t_L^kd_k$, $y_{k+1}=x_k+t_R^kd_k$, and choose $\xi_{k+1}\in\partial f(y_{k+1})$. If the decrease test fails, take a null step by setting $x_{k+1}=x_k$, $y_{k+1}=x_k+t_R^kd_k$, and choosing $\xi_{k+1}\in\partial f(y_{k+1})$. Update $\mathcal J_k$ and $u_k$ by prescribed rules and return $x_k$ when $|v_{k-1}|\le\varepsilon$.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Starting from an initial point, bundle, proximal parameter, and tolerance, repeatedly minimize the cutting-plane model plus a quadratic proximal term. Use the predicted model decrease and an actual-decrease test to select a long serious step, short serious step, or null step; evaluate a subgradient at the resulting trial point, update the bundle and proximal parameter, and stop when the model-decrease magnitude is at most the tolerance.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: |v_{k-1}|\le\varepsilon\quad\Longrightarrow\quad\text{return }x_k

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Nondegeneracy and Zero-Normal Pruning of Max-Min Separators
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Extraction-grounded result; problem (7.28), its notion of optimality, and the index set \(\mathcal I\) retain their source-context meanings. Part (i) requires only the common separability assumption, whereas part (ii) additionally requires conditions (a) and (b).
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Assume that \(A\) and \(B\) are max-min linearly separable using \(\{(\mathbf{x}_j,y_j):j\in\mathcal J\}\), where \(\mathcal J=\{1,\ldots,l\}\), and the partition \(\mathcal J^r=\{\mathcal J_1,\ldots,\mathcal J_r\}\). Then the assignment \(\mathbf{x}_j=0\) for every \(j\in\mathcal J\) cannot be an optimal solution of problem (7.28). Furthermore, suppose that for every \(t\in\mathcal I\) there exists \(\mathbf b\in B\) such that \[\max_{j\in\mathcal J_t}\{-\mathbf{x}_j^T\mathbf b+y_j+1\}=\min_{i\in\mathcal I}\max_{j\in\mathcal J_i}\{-\mathbf{x}_j^T\mathbf b+y_j+1\},\] and that subsets \(\widetilde{\mathcal J}_t\subseteq\mathcal J_t\) exist for all \(t\in\mathcal I\), with at least one \(\widetilde{\mathcal J}_t\) nonempty and \(\mathbf{x}_j=0\) for every \(j\in\widetilde{\mathcal J}_t\). Then \(A\) and \(B\) remain max-min linearly separable using the retained index sets \(\overline{\mathcal J}_t=\mathcal J_t\setminus\widetilde{\mathcal J}_t\) and \(\mathcal J^0=\bigcup_{i=1}^r\overline{\mathcal J}_i\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a max-min separator, setting every hyperplane normal to zero cannot solve the associated optimization problem. In addition, under the stated block-attainment condition, designated zero-normal hyperplanes may be deleted—provided at least one is designated—without destroying max-min linear separability.
assumptions_latex: A,B\text{ are max-min linearly separable using }\{(\mathbf{x}_j,y_j):j\in\mathcal J\}\text{ and the partition }\{\mathcal J_1,\ldots,\mathcal J_r\}.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: (\forall j\in\mathcal J,\ \mathbf{x}_j=0)\text{ is not optimal for (7.28); moreover, conditions (a)--(b) imply that }A,B\text{ remain max-min linearly separable after replacing }\mathcal J_t\text{ by }\overline{\mathcal J}_t=\mathcal J_t\setminus\widetilde{\mathcal J}_t.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Weakly convex Moreau envelope: fixed points, stationarity, and minimizers
knowledge_statements.scope_note: The constrained conclusions require the proximal mapping and envelope to be taken over \(X\), equivalently for \(f+\delta_X\); this makes explicit the constraint implicit in the extracted proposition.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) be weakly convex with modulus \(\sigma/2>0\), let \(X\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be closed and convex, and define
\[
P_{\lambda,X}f(x):=\operatorname*{argmin}_{y\in X}\left\{f(y)+\frac\lambda2\|x-y\|^2\right\},\qquad
e_{\lambda,X}f(x):=\min_{y\in X}\left\{f(y)+\frac\lambda2\|x-y\|^2\right\}.
\]
For every \(\lambda>\sigma\): (i) \(P_{\lambda,X}f(x)\) is single-valued for every \(x\in X\); (ii) for \(\bar x\in X\), Clarke stationarity for \(\min_{x\in X}f(x)\), the fixed-point condition \(P_{\lambda,X}f(\bar x)=\bar x\), and \(\nabla e_{\lambda,X}f(\bar x)=0\) are equivalent; and (iii)
\[
\min_{x\in X}e_{\lambda,X}f(x)=\min_{x\in X}f(x),\qquad
\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in X}e_{\lambda,X}f(x)=\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in X}f(x).
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a weakly convex function on a closed convex set and any quadratic parameter exceeding the weak-convexity threshold, the constrained proximal map is single-valued. Its fixed points coincide with the constrained Clarke stationary points and with the stationary points of the Moreau envelope. The envelope also has the same minimum value and global minimizers as the original function.
assumptions_latex: f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\text{ is weakly convex with modulus }\sigma/2>0
X\subseteq\mathbb R^n\text{ is closed and convex}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: P_{\lambda,X}f\text{ is single-valued};\quad \bar x\text{ is Clarke stationary}\iff P_{\lambda,X}f(\bar x)=\bar x\iff\nabla e_{\lambda,X}f(\bar x)=0;\quad \min_X e_{\lambda,X}f=\min_X f,\ \operatorname*{argmin}_X e_{\lambda,X}f=\operatorname*{argmin}_X f

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Clarke stationarity, limiting stationarity, and DC criticality on a convex set
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines three exact stationarity notions at a feasible point.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let $X$ be closed and convex, let $\mathcal O$ be open with $X\subseteq\mathcal O$, and let $f:\mathcal O\to\mathbb R$ be locally Lipschitz. For $\bar x\in X$, Clarke stationarity means $0\in\partial_C f(\bar x)+\mathcal N(\bar x;X)$, and limiting stationarity means $0\in\partial f(\bar x)+\mathcal N(\bar x;X)$. If $f=g-h$ with convex $g,h$, criticality means $\partial h(\bar x)\cap[\partial g(\bar x)+\mathcal N(\bar x;X)]\ne\varnothing$.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A feasible point is Clarke stationary when the negative normal cone contains a Clarke subgradient, limiting stationary when it contains a limiting subgradient, and—under a DC decomposition—critical when a subgradient of the subtracted convex component also belongs to the subgradient-plus-normal set of the other component.
assumptions_latex: X\subseteq\mathbb R^n\text{ is closed and convex}
f:\mathcal O\to\mathbb R\text{ is locally Lipschitz}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \begin{aligned}\bar x\text{ Clarke stationary}&\iff0\in\partial_Cf(\bar x)+\mathcal N(\bar x;X),\\ \bar x\text{ limiting stationary}&\iff0\in\partial f(\bar x)+\mathcal N(\bar x;X),\\ \bar x\text{ critical for }g-h&\iff\partial h(\bar x)\cap\bigl(\partial g(\bar x)+\mathcal N(\bar x;X)\bigr)\ne\varnothing.\end{aligned}

Assume that for every x\in C\setminus\operatorname{FIX}(\Xi), there are \widehat i with x^{\widehat i}\notin\Xi^{\widehat i}(x^{-\widehat i}) and a unit vector w^{\widehat i}\in\mathcal T(x^{\widehat i};C^{\widehat i}) such that (g_k^{\widehat i})'(x^{\widehat i};w^{\widehat i})\le-1 for k\in\mathcal A_{+;\widehat i}^{\le}(x), (g_k^{\widehat i})'(x^{\widehat i};w^{\widehat i})\le0 for k\in\mathcal A_{0;\widehat i}^{\le}(x), \operatorname{sgn}(h_j^{\widehat i}(x))(h_j^{\widehat i})'(x^{\widehat i};w^{\widehat i})\le-1 for j\in\mathcal A_{\ne;\widehat i}^{=}(x), and (h_j^{\widehat i})'(x^{\widehat i};w^{\widehat i})=0 for j\in\mathcal A_{0;\widehat i}^{=}(x), with the other players' variables fixed in each directional derivative. \zeta_i(\bullet,x^{-i})\text{ is directionally differentiable and Lipschitz on }C^i\text{ with constant }\operatorname{Lip}_\zeta>0

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Global Search Scheme for DC minimization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Procedural escape scheme at iteration k. The extract does not specify behavior when the index set I_k is empty.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Choose \(\gamma\) with \(\inf(g,\mathcal D)\leq\gamma\leq\sup(g,\mathcal D)\), and construct a finite approximation
\[
\mathcal A_k(\gamma)=\{v^1,\ldots,v^{N_k}:h(v^i)=\gamma-\zeta_k\}
\]
of the corresponding level surface. For each sample, compute the stated global \(\delta_k\)-solutions \(u^i\in\mathcal D\) of the linearized problem and \(w^i\) of the level problem. Define
\[
I_k:=\{i\in\{1,\ldots,N_k\}:g(v^i)\leq\gamma\},
\]
\[
\eta_k(\gamma):=\gamma+\min_{i\in I_k}\bigl\{g(u^i)-\langle\nabla h(w^i),u^i-w^i\rangle\bigr\}.
\]
If \(\eta_k(\gamma)<0\), restart local search from the corresponding minimizing point \(u^j\); if \(\eta_k(\gamma)\geq0\), choose another value of \(\gamma\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The scheme samples a level surface of h, solves the specified approximate linearized and level subproblems, and evaluates η_k(γ). A negative value identifies a better restart point; otherwise γ is changed.
assumptions_latex: \mathcal A_k(\gamma)\text{ is a finite approximation of the stated level surface}
u^i\text{ and }w^i\text{ satisfy the stated global }\delta_k\text{-solution conditions}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \eta_k(\gamma)<0\Rightarrow u^j\text{ is an improving restart point};\qquad \eta_k(\gamma)\geq0\Rightarrow\gamma\text{ is changed}
