knowledge_statements.statement_title: DC structure, bounds, and pointwise limits of chance-indicator envelopes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Applies to the upper and lower envelopes generated by convex and concave functions satisfying the preceding construction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For every fixed \(\gamma>0\),
\[
\phi_\gamma^{\rm ub}(t)=\theta_{\rm cvx}\!\left(1+\frac t\gamma\right)-\max\!\left\{\theta_{\rm cvx}\!\left(1+\frac t\gamma\right)-1,0\right\},
\]
\[
\phi_\gamma^{\rm lb}(t)=\max\!\left\{0,-\theta_{\rm cve}\!\left(\frac t\gamma\right)\right\}+\theta_{\rm cve}\!\left(\frac t\gamma\right),
\]
so both envelopes are differences of convex functions on \(\mathbb R\). Moreover, for every \(t\in\mathbb R\),
\[
\phi_\gamma^{\rm ub}(t)\geq\mathbf1_{[0,\infty)}(t)\geq\mathbf1_{(0,\infty)}(t)\geq\phi_\gamma^{\rm lb}(t),
\]
and
\[
\mathbf1_{[0,\infty)}(t)=\inf_{\gamma>0}\phi_\gamma^{\rm ub}(t)=\lim_{\gamma\downarrow0}\phi_\gamma^{\rm ub}(t),
\qquad
\mathbf1_{(0,\infty)}(t)=\lim_{\gamma\downarrow0}\phi_\gamma^{\rm lb}(t).
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For each positive scale, the upper and lower chance-indicator envelopes have explicit difference-of-convex decompositions. The upper envelope majorizes the closed-half-line indicator, the lower envelope minorizes the open-half-line indicator, and they converge pointwise to those respective indicators as the scale tends to zero. The closed-half-line indicator is also the infimum of the upper envelopes over all positive scales.
assumptions_latex: \theta_{\rm cvx}:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R_+\text{ is convex},\ \theta_{\rm cvx}(t)=0\ (t\leq0),\ \theta_{\rm cvx}(1)=1
\theta_{\rm cve}:\mathbb R\to(-\infty,1]\text{ is concave},\ \theta_{\rm cve}(0)=0,\ \theta_{\rm cve}(t)=1\ (t\geq1)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \phi_\gamma^{\rm ub},\phi_\gamma^{\rm lb}\text{ are DC};\quad \phi_\gamma^{\rm ub}\geq\mathbf1_{[0,\infty)}\geq\mathbf1_{(0,\infty)}\geq\phi_\gamma^{\rm lb};\quad \mathbf1_{[0,\infty)}=\inf_{\gamma>0}\phi_\gamma^{\rm ub};\quad \phi_\gamma^{\rm ub}\to\mathbf1_{[0,\infty)},\ \phi_\gamma^{\rm lb}\to\mathbf1_{(0,\infty)}\text{ pointwise as }\gamma\downarrow0.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Optimized Certainty Equivalent
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines the admissible utility class, essential boundedness, and the optimized certainty equivalent.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal U\) consist of proper, concave, nondecreasing, upper-semicontinuous functions \(u:\mathbb R\to[-\infty,\infty)\) with \(\operatorname{dom}u\neq\varnothing\), \(u(0)=0\), and \(1\in\partial(-u)(0)\). As stated, these conditions imply \(u(t)\ge 0\) for every \(t\ge0\) and \(u(t)\le t\) for every \(t\in\mathbb R\). A random variable \(\mathcal Z\) is essentially bounded if some \(\Gamma>0\) satisfies \(\mathbb P(|\mathcal Z|>\Gamma)=0\). For such \(\mathcal Z\), its optimized certainty equivalent is \(\mathcal O_u(\mathcal Z):=\sup_{\eta\in\mathbb R}\{\eta+\mathbb E[u(\mathcal Z-\eta)]\}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An admissible utility is proper, concave, nondecreasing, upper semicontinuous, has nonempty effective domain, is normalized at zero, and satisfies the stated subgradient normalization. An essentially bounded random variable is bounded almost surely. Its optimized certainty equivalent is the supremum, over cash allocations eta, of eta plus the expected utility of the residual.
assumptions_latex: u:\mathbb R\to[-\infty,\infty)\text{ is proper, concave, nondecreasing, and upper semicontinuous}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \mathcal O_u(\mathcal Z)=\sup_{\eta\in\mathbb R}\left\{\eta+\mathbb E[u(\mathcal Z-\eta)]\right\}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Quasi-secant and SR-quasi-secant mapping
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines directional quasi-secants, their fixed-direction limit points, and the subgradient-related condition.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(x\in\mathbb R^n\), \(g\in S_1\), and \(h>0\), a vector \(v\in\mathbb R^n\) is a quasi-secant of \(f\) at \(x\) in direction \(g\) with length \(h\) if \(f(x+hg)-f(x)\le h v^Tg\). Let \(QSec(x,h)=\{w\in\mathbb R^n:\exists g\in S_1,\ w=v(x,g,h)\}\), and let \(QSL(x)\) consist of all \(w\) for which there exist \(g\in S_1\) and \(h_k\downarrow0\) such that \(w=\lim_{k\to\infty}v(x,g,h_k)\). The mapping \(x\mapsto QSec(x,h)\) is subgradient-related if \(QSL(x)\subseteq\partial f(x)\) for every \(x\in\mathbb R^n\); its elements are then called SR-quasi-secants.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A quasi-secant is a vector whose directional pairing bounds the corresponding finite function increment. Its limit set uses one fixed unit direction and lengths tending to zero. A quasi-secant mapping is subgradient-related when every such limit belongs to the subdifferential at every point.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: QSL(x)\subseteq\partial f(x)\quad\text{for all }x\in\mathbb R^n

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Scaled SCAD sparsity penalty
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines the normalized SCAD function and records its zero, regularity, saturation, and displayed convex-difference representation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(a>2\), \(\delta>0\), and \(t\in\mathbb R\), define \[\rho_a^{\mathrm{SCAD}}(t;\delta)=\begin{cases}\dfrac{2a}{(a+1)\delta}|t|,&|t|\le\delta/a,\\1-\dfrac{(\delta-|t|)^2}{(1-a^{-2})\delta^2},&\delta/a\le|t|\le\delta,\\1,&|t|\ge\delta.\end{cases}\] It has the origin as its unique zero, is continuously differentiable on \(\mathbb R\setminus\{0\}\), and satisfies the surrogate conditions (R1)--(R3). Moreover, \[\rho_a^{\mathrm{SCAD}}(t;\delta)=\frac{2a}{(a+1)\delta}|t|-\max\left\{\frac{((|t|/\delta-1/a)_+)^2}{1-a^{-2}},\frac{2}{1+1/a}\frac{|t|}{\delta}-1\right\}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The scaled SCAD penalty is linear near zero, transitions quadratically to a plateau, and equals one beyond the threshold. Its unique zero is the origin, it is continuously differentiable away from zero, and it has the displayed convex-difference representation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \rho_a^{\mathrm{SCAD}}(t;\delta)=0\iff t=0,\qquad \rho_a^{\mathrm{SCAD}}(t;\delta)=1\text{ whenever }|t|\ge\delta.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Generalized critical point of a two-stage stochastic program
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Stationarity definition using the two partial convex subdifferentials of a lifted expected recourse function.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A point \(\bar x\in X\) is a generalized critical point if \[0\in \partial\varphi(\bar x)+\partial_x\mathbb E_{\widetilde\xi}[\bar\psi(\bar x,\bar x,\widetilde\xi)]-\partial_z\mathbb E_{\widetilde\xi}[-\bar\psi(\bar x,\bar x,\widetilde\xi)]+\mathcal N(\bar x;X),\] where the first partial subdifferential is that of the convex function \(x\mapsto\mathbb E_{\widetilde\xi}[\bar\psi(x,\bar x,\widetilde\xi)]\) at \(\bar x\), and the second is defined analogously for \(z\mapsto\mathbb E_{\widetilde\xi}[-\bar\psi(\bar x,z,\widetilde\xi)]\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Second-order local optimality conditions for a twice semidifferentiable composite program
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Necessary local and sufficient strong-local conditions along critical tangent directions; the referenced first-order condition (9.38) is retained because its formula is absent from the extract.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(h:\mathbb R^m\to\mathbb R\) and \(G_j:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\), \(j=1,\ldots,m\), be twice semidifferentiable, let \(X\) be polyhedral, and let \(\bar x\in X\). Suppose \(\operatorname{Lip}_h>0\) is a Lipschitz constant of \(h\) near \(G(\bar x)\). (a) If \(\bar x\) is a local minimizer of (9.35), then condition (9.38) holds and, for every \(v\in\mathcal T(\bar x;X)\) satisfying \(h'(G(\bar x);G'(\bar x;v))=0\), \[h^{(2)}(G(\bar x);G'(\bar x;v))+\operatorname{Lip}_h\sum_{j=1}^m\lvert G_j^{(2)}(\bar x;v)\rvert\ge0.\] (b) If condition (9.38) holds and there exists \(\rho>\operatorname{Lip}_h\) such that, for every nonzero \(v\in\mathcal T(\bar x;X)\) with \(h'(G(\bar x);G'(\bar x;v))=0\) and every partition \(J_+\cup J_-=\{1,\ldots,m\}\), \(J_+\cap J_-=\varnothing\), \[h^{(2)}(G(\bar x);G'(\bar x;v))+\rho\left(\sum_{j\in J_+}G_j^{(2)}(\bar x;v)-\sum_{j\in J_-}G_j^{(2)}(\bar x;v)\right)>0,\] then \(\bar x\) is a strong local minimizer of (9.35).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a composite program with twice semidifferentiable data and a polyhedral feasible set, local minimality requires the referenced first-order condition and a nonnegative second-order expression on every critical tangent direction. Conversely, that first-order condition together with strict positivity, for one penalty parameter above the local Lipschitz constant and for every nonzero critical tangent direction and every sign partition of the component second-order terms, guarantees strong local minimality.
assumptions_latex: h:\mathbb R^m\to\mathbb R\text{ and }G_j:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\ (j=1,\ldots,m)\text{ are twice semidifferentiable}
X\subseteq\mathbb R^n\text{ is polyhedral},\qquad \bar x\in X
\operatorname{Lip}_h>0\text{ is a Lipschitz constant of }h\text{ near }G(\bar x)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \bar x\text{ locally minimizes (9.35)}\Rightarrow\text{(9.38) and the stated nonnegative second-order condition};\quad \text{(9.38) and the stated strict condition for some }\rho>\operatorname{Lip}_h\Rightarrow\bar x\text{ strongly locally minimizes (9.35)}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: The ℓ0 cardinality function and sparse feasible sets
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines scalar and vector ℓ0 functions and records their basic topology and optimization role.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(t\in\mathbb R\), define \(|t|_0=0\) if \(t=0\) and \(|t|_0=1\) otherwise. For \(x\in\mathbb R^n\), \(\|x\|_0:=\sum_{i=1}^n|x_i|_0\) counts the nonzero components. The scalar function is lower semicontinuous, and for every positive integer \(k\), \(\{x\in\mathbb R^n:\|x\|_0\le k\}\) is closed. Using \(\|x\|_0\) as a regularizer promotes sparse solutions; common alternatives replace its summands by continuous sparsity surrogates or use equivalent epigraphical or complementarity-constrained formulations.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The scalar l0 function is zero at zero and one elsewhere, while the vector l0 function counts nonzero coordinates. It is lower semicontinuous, its at-most-k-sparse sublevel set is closed, and it can be handled through surrogates or equivalent epigraphical and complementarity formulations.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \|x\|_0=\sum_{i=1}^n|x_i|_0,\qquad \{x:\|x\|_0\le k\}\text{ is closed.}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Distinct-Value and Cardinality Constraint Reformulations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Characterizes a bound on the number of distinct vectors using prototypes and scalar cardinality constraints, and represents scalar cardinality through a top-component norm difference.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(v^1,\ldots,v^M\in\mathbb{R}^n\) and let \(k\ge 1\). Then
\[
\operatorname{distinct}[v^1\ \cdots\ v^M]\le k
\iff
\exists w^1,\ldots,w^k\in\mathbb{R}^n:\ 
\sum_{j=1}^k\left|\|v^i-w^j\|_1\right|_0\le k-1
\quad\forall i.
\]
Equivalently, there exist \(w^1,\ldots,w^k\) and real variables \(t_{ji}\) such that
\[
t_{ji}\ge \|v^i-w^j\|_1\quad\forall j,i,
\qquad
\sum_{j=1}^k|t_{ji}|_0\le k-1\quad\forall i.
\]
Separately, for \(x\in\mathbb{R}^d\) and \(q\in\{0,\ldots,d\}\),
\[
\sum_{i=1}^d|x_i|_0\le q
\iff
\|x\|_1-\|x\|_{[q]}\le 0,
\]
where \(\|x\|_{[q]}\) is the sum of the \(q\) largest absolute components of \(x\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At most k distinct vectors occur exactly when k prototypes can be chosen so that every vector equals at least one prototype. Auxiliary distance variables express this condition using scalar zero-count constraints. A scalar cardinality bound is equivalently the nonpositivity of the l1 norm minus the sum of the largest prescribed number of absolute components.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{distinct}[v^1\ \cdots\ v^M]\le k\iff\text{the displayed prototype and auxiliary-variable systems are feasible},\qquad \sum_{i=1}^d|x_i|_0\le q\iff\|x\|_1-\|x\|_{[q]}\le0

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(U,V\in\mathcal N\), define the Pontryagin difference by \[U\div V:=\{x\mid x+V\subseteq U\}.\] The set \(U\div V\) may be empty; in all cases it is convex and compact.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The Pontryagin difference of U by V is the set of translations x for which x+V lies in U. It may be empty and is convex and compact.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: U\div V=\{x\mid x+V\subseteq U\}\text{ is convex and compact, possibly empty}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Truncated Transformed-ℓ1 Penalty
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines the scalar truncated transformed-ℓ1 family and records the source's assertion of properties (R1)–(R3), whose definitions are not included in this extract.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For parameters \(a>0\) and \(\delta>0\), define, for every \(t\in\mathbb R\),
\[
\rho_a^{\mathrm{TTL}\ell_1}(t;\delta)=\min\left\{\frac{(a+\delta)|t|}{\delta(a+|t|)},1\right\}.
\]
This family satisfies conditions \((R1)\), \((R2)\), and \((R3)\) for \((t,\delta)\in\mathbb R\times(0,\infty)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Given a>0 and δ>0, the truncated transformed-ℓ1 penalty at t is the minimum of (a+δ)|t|/[δ(a+|t|)] and 1. The extract states that this family satisfies conditions (R1), (R2), and (R3) on R × (0,∞).

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let f:\mathcal H\to(-\infty,+\infty] be proper, u\in\mathcal H, and \mu\in\mathbb R. Then \sigma_{\operatorname{epi}f}(u,-\mu)=\begin{cases}\mu f^*(u/\mu),&\mu>0,\\ \sigma_{\operatorname{dom}f}(u),&\mu=0,\\ +\infty,&\mu<0.\end{cases}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: B-stationarity of accumulation points of the feasible surrogation algorithm
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Stationarity guarantee for accumulation points generated by Algorithm 7.1.2 on problem (7.13).
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let X be closed and convex, and let \varphi_0,\{g_i\}_{i=0}^m,\{h_i\}_{i=0}^m be convex. Suppose
\[
\partial g_0(x^\infty)\times\prod_{i=0}^m\partial h_i(x^\infty)=\{\nabla g_0(x^\infty)\}\times\prod_{i=0}^m\{\nabla h_i(x^\infty)\}.
\]
Let \mathcal A(x^\infty)=\{i\in\{1,\ldots,m\}:f_i(x^\infty)=0\}, and suppose there exists \widehat x\in X such that
\[
f_i'(x^\infty;\widehat x-x^\infty)<0\quad\text{for every }i\in\mathcal A(x^\infty).
\]
If x^\infty is an accumulation point of iterates generated by Algorithm 7.1.2, then x^\infty is a B-stationary solution of (7.13).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a closed convex domain and convex component functions, an accumulation point of the surrogation iterates is B-stationary if the relevant subdifferentials at that point are singletons and a direction strictly decreases every active constraint.
assumptions_latex: \exists\widehat x\in X\;\forall i\in\mathcal A(x^\infty):\ f_i'(x^\infty;\widehat x-x^\infty)<0
x^\infty\text{ is an accumulation point of the iterates of Algorithm 7.1.2}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: x^\infty\text{ is a B-stationary solution of (7.13)}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Finite min-max DC representation of PLQ functions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Representation of a possibly nonconvex PLQ function using its quadratic pieces and elementary DC correction functions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:\operatorname{dom}f\to\mathbb R\) be PLQ on a polyhedral domain \(\operatorname{dom}f=\bigcup_{i=1}^I P^i\), where each \(P^i\) is polyhedral and \(f(x)=q_i(x)\) on \(P^i\) for a quadratic function \(q_i\). For each \(i\), there are finitely many functions \(f_{i\hat k}=\sum_{j=1}^{J^+_{i\hat k}}f^+_{i\hat k j}-\sum_{j=1}^{J^-_{i\hat k}}f^-_{i\hat k j}\), where every \(f^\pm_{i\hat k j}\) is a square of an affine or plus-composite-affine function, such that \(f(x)=\min_{1\leq i\leq I}[q_i(x)+\max_{1\leq\hat k\leq\widehat K_i}f_{i\hat k}(x)]\) for every \(x\in\operatorname{dom}f\). Moreover, the zero set of \(\widehat\phi_i(x)=\max_{1\leq\hat k\leq\widehat K_i}f_{i\hat k}(x)\) is exactly \(P^i\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every PLQ function on a finite polyhedral partition has a finite lower-envelope representation. Each branch is its defining quadratic plus a maximum of DC correction functions built from squared affine and squared ReLU-type functions. The correction for a branch vanishes exactly on that branch's polyhedral piece.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: f(x)=\min_i\left[q_i(x)+\max_{\hat k}f_{i\hat k}(x)\right]\quad\forall x\in\operatorname{dom}f,\qquad \{x:\widehat\phi_i(x)=0\}=P^i.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Convex-program characterization of B-stationarity for piecewise dd-convex programs
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Characterizes B-stationarity through directional convex subproblems indexed by the active pieces.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(S\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be closed, and let \(f\) and every \(h_{ij}\) be dd-convex near a feasible point \(\bar x\in X\). Assume \(\mathcal T(\bar x;S)\) is convex, KTCQ holds for \(S\) at \(\bar x\), and there exists \(\bar v\in\mathcal T(\bar x;S)\) such that \(h'_{ij}(\bar x;\bar v)<0\) for every \(i\in\mathcal P(\bar x)\) and \(j\in J_i(\bar x):=\{j:h_{ij}(\bar x)=0\}\). Then \(\bar x\) is B-stationary for \(\min_{x\in X}f(x)\) if and only if, for every \(i\in\mathcal P(\bar x)\), \[\bar x\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in\bar x+\mathcal T(\bar x;S)} f'(\bar x;x-\bar x)\quad\text{subject to}\quad h'_{ij}(\bar x;x-\bar x)\le0\ \ \forall j\in J_i(\bar x).\] Each displayed directional problem is convex.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a feasible point of the piecewise dd-convex program, if the base tangent cone is convex, KTCQ holds, and one common tangent direction strictly decreases every active branch constraint, then B-stationarity is equivalent to the point solving, for every active piece, the convex directional problem formed from the objective directional derivative and all active constraint directional derivatives.
assumptions_latex: f\text{ and all }h_{ij}\text{ are dd-convex near }\bar x
\exists\bar v\in\mathcal T(\bar x;S)\ \forall i\in\mathcal P(\bar x)\ \forall j\in J_i(\bar x):\ h'_{ij}(\bar x;\bar v)<0
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \bar x\text{ is B-stationary}\iff\forall i\in\mathcal P(\bar x),\ \bar x\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{\substack{x\in\bar x+\mathcal T(\bar x;S)\\h'_{ij}(\bar x;x-\bar x)\le0\ \forall j\in J_i(\bar x)}}f'(\bar x;x-\bar x).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Truncated CVaR and Empirical VaR as Structured DC Functionals
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Order-statistic truncation that removes upper and lower sample tails, including the single-order-statistic VaR specialization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(y_{[1]}\ge\cdots\ge y_{[N]}\) and let \(1\le k_2<k_1\le N\). Removing the first \(k_2-1\) and last \(N-k_1+1\) ordered observations gives
\[
\operatorname{tCVaR}_{k_1,k_2}(y)=\sum_{s=1}^Ny_s-\left[(k_2-1)\operatorname{sCVaR}_{k_2-1}(y)-(N-k_1+1)\operatorname{sCVaR}_{N-k_1+1}(-y)\right],
\]
with zero-size tails omitted at the boundary. Consequently the truncated functional is DC. Under the extract's empirical quantile convention, when \(\alpha=k/N\) and \(k_2=k=k_1-1\), this truncation selects the corresponding empirical order statistic and represents \(\operatorname{VaR}_{k/N}(y)\), where \(\operatorname{VaR}_{\alpha}(X)=\inf\{t:F_X(t)\ge1-\alpha\}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A truncated CVaR removes prescribed upper and lower order-statistic tails. It equals the total sample sum minus a two-sided CVaR term, so it has a difference-of-convex representation. In the stated single-order-statistic specialization it yields empirical VaR under the source's quantile convention.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{tCVaR}_{k_1,k_2}(y)=\sum_{s=1}^Ny_s-\operatorname{twoSidedCVaR}(y;k_2-1,N-k_1+1),\quad\text{hence }\operatorname{tCVaR}_{k_1,k_2}\text{ is DC}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Active-model characterization of diff-max directional stationarity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Characterizes directional stationarity by global minimization of every active-pair model; affine pieces strengthen the characterization to local optimality.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let $X\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n$ be convex, let $\varphi:\mathbb{R}\to\mathbb{R}$ be convex, and let
\[f=\varphi\circ\psi,\qquad \psi(x)=\max_{1\le j\le J_1}\psi_{1j}(x)-\max_{1\le j\le J_2}\psi_{2j}(x),\]
where every $\psi_{ij}$ is convex and differentiable. For $\bar x\in X$, $\bar x$ is d-stationary for $f$ on $X$ if and only if
\[\bar x\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in X}\widehat f_{j_1j_2}(x;\bar x)\]
for every $(j_1,j_2)\in\mathcal A_1(\bar x)\times\mathcal A_2(\bar x)$. If all $\psi_{ij}$ are affine, these equivalent conditions are also equivalent to $\bar x$ being a local minimizer of $f$ on $X$.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A feasible point is directionally stationary for a convex composite diff-max objective exactly when it globally minimizes every model indexed by a pair of active inner pieces. When all inner pieces are affine, this is also equivalent to local minimality.
assumptions_latex: \psi_{ij}\text{ is convex and differentiable for every }i,j
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \bar x\text{ is d-stationary}\iff \forall(j_1,j_2)\in\mathcal A_1(\bar x)\times\mathcal A_2(\bar x),\ \bar x\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in X}\widehat f_{j_1j_2}(x;\bar x);\quad (\forall i,j,\ \psi_{ij}\text{ affine})\implies\bigl[\text{either condition}\iff\bar x\text{ is a local minimizer}\bigr]

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Difference-of-Sublinear Function Space
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional, everywhere-defined sublinear and superlinear functions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let P be the family of sublinear functions on \mathbb{R}^n, let Q be the family of superlinear functions, and define L=P+Q. Equivalently, every \ell\in L is a difference of two sublinear functions. Then L\subset C(\mathbb{R}^n) is a real linear subspace. Under the pointwise order, if \ell_1,\ldots,\ell_k\in L, then \max_{1\le i\le k}\ell_i and \min_{1\le i\le k}\ell_i also belong to L.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The functions expressible as a sublinear plus a superlinear function, equivalently as a difference of two sublinear functions, form a linear subspace of the continuous functions on R^n and are closed under finite pointwise maxima and minima.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: L\subset C(\mathbb{R}^n),\quad L\text{ is a real linear subspace, and }\ell_1,\ldots,\ell_k\in L\Rightarrow \max_i\ell_i,\min_i\ell_i\in L.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Quasidifferentiation under the integral sign
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Integral quasidifferentiability under an integrated remainder condition and measurable integrably bounded sublinear components.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \varphi(x)=\int_S f(s,x)\,d\mu(s). Suppose that, for every g\in\mathbb R^n, the directional expansion of f(s,\cdot) at x has a remainder o_{s,x,g}(\alpha) satisfying \alpha^{-1}\int_So_{s,x,g}(\alpha)\,d\mu(s)\to0 as \alpha\downarrow0. Assume the expansion admits sublinear components p(s,g) and q(s,g) such that p(\cdot,g) and q(\cdot,g) are measurable for every g and s\mapsto\|p(s,\cdot)\| and s\mapsto\|q(s,\cdot)\| are integrable. Then \varphi is quasidifferentiable at x. Its lower quasidifferential consists exactly of vectors \int_Sw(s)\,d\mu(s), where w is coordinatewise measurable and w(s)\in\partial p(s,\cdot) almost everywhere; its upper quasidifferential is described analogously by coordinatewise measurable selections w(s)\in\bar\partial q(s,\cdot) almost everywhere.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If the pointwise directional expansions have an integrated remainder that is little-o of the step size, and their sublinear components are measurable and integrably norm-bounded, then the integral functional is quasidifferentiable. Its two quasidifferential sets are precisely the componentwise integrals of measurable selections from the corresponding pointwise sets.
assumptions_latex: f(s,\cdot)\text{ has the stipulated directional decomposition with sublinear components }p(s,\cdot),q(s,\cdot)
p(\cdot,g)\text{ and }q(\cdot,g)\text{ are measurable for every }g
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \varphi\text{ is quasidifferentiable at }x,\quad \partial\varphi(x)=\left\{\int_Sw(s)\,d\mu(s):w(s)\in\partial p(s,\cdot)\text{ a.e., }w\text{ coordinatewise measurable}\right\},\quad \bar\partial\varphi(x)=\left\{\int_Sw(s)\,d\mu(s):w(s)\in\bar\partial q(s,\cdot)\text{ a.e., }w\text{ coordinatewise measurable}\right\}.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Largest OCE Maximizer
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Records attainment under compact interval support and defines the largest maximizing allocation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If the support of \(\mathcal Z\) is a compact interval, then the supremum in \(\mathcal O_u(\mathcal Z)=\sup_{\eta\in\mathbb R}\{\eta+\mathbb E[u(\mathcal Z-\eta)]\}\) is attained. Its largest maximizer is \(m_u(\mathcal Z):=\max\operatorname*{argmax}_{\eta\in\mathbb R}\{\eta+\mathbb E[u(\mathcal Z-\eta)]\}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: When the random variable has compact interval support, the OCE optimization attains its supremum. The utility-based VaR extension m_u is defined by selecting the largest maximizing allocation, thereby resolving ties.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname*{argmax}_{\eta\in\mathbb R}\{\eta+\mathbb E[u(\mathcal Z-\eta)]\}\neq\varnothing,\qquad m_u(\mathcal Z)=\max\operatorname*{argmax}_{\eta\in\mathbb R}\{\eta+\mathbb E[u(\mathcal Z-\eta)]\}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Tangent cone to a single piecewise dd-convex constraint branch
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local tangent geometry for a branch set X_{ij} relative to its base set S.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\bar x\in X_{ij}\), and suppose \(h_{ij}\) is dd-convex at \(\bar x\). If \(h_{ij}(\bar x)<0\), then \(\mathcal T(\bar x;X_{ij})=\mathcal T(\bar x;S)\). If \(h_{ij}(\bar x)=0\), KTCQ holds for \(S\) at \(\bar x\), \(\mathcal T(\bar x;S)\) is convex, and there exists \(\bar v\in\mathcal T(\bar x;S)\) with \(h'_{ij}(\bar x;\bar v)<0\), then \[\mathcal T(\bar x;X_{ij})=\{v\in\mathcal T(\bar x;S):h'_{ij}(\bar x;v)\le 0\},\] and this tangent cone is convex.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a dd-convex constraint branch, a strictly inactive constraint leaves the base-set tangent cone unchanged. At an active constraint, KTCQ, convexity of the base tangent cone, and a strict feasible direction yield the tangent cone by imposing the nonpositive directional-derivative inequality; the resulting cone is convex.
assumptions_latex: h_{ij}(\bar x)<0\quad\text{or}\quad\bigl[h_{ij}(\bar x)=0,\ \mathrm{KTCQ}_S(\bar x),\ \mathcal T(\bar x;S)\text{ convex},\ \exists\bar v\in\mathcal T(\bar x;S):h'_{ij}(\bar x;\bar v)<0\bigr]
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: h_{ij}(\bar x)<0\Rightarrow\mathcal T(\bar x;X_{ij})=\mathcal T(\bar x;S);\quad h_{ij}(\bar x)=0\Rightarrow\mathcal T(\bar x;X_{ij})=\{v\in\mathcal T(\bar x;S):h'_{ij}(\bar x;v)\le0\}\text{ is convex}.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: d-Stationarity equivalence under outer-function linearization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Linearizing the continuously differentiable scalar outer function at the reference composite value preserves d-stationarity at that reference point.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\) be convex, \(\bar x\in X\), and \(f=g-\widetilde\varphi\circ\widetilde\psi\), where \(g\) and \(\widetilde\psi\) are B-differentiable and \(\widetilde\varphi\in C^1\) has scalar derivative. Define, for \(x\in X\), \[\widehat f(x;\bar x)=g(x)-\widetilde\varphi'(\widetilde\psi(\bar x))\bigl(\widetilde\psi(x)-\widetilde\psi(\bar x)\bigr).\] Then \(\bar x\) is d-stationary for \(f\) on \(X\) if and only if it is d-stationary for \(\widehat f(\cdot;\bar x)\) on \(X\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a difference between a B-differentiable function and a smooth scalar outer composite, replacing the outer function by its first-order linearization at the reference composite value preserves directional stationarity of the reference point on the convex feasible set.
assumptions_latex: X\text{ is convex and }\bar x\in X.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \bar x\text{ is d-stationary for }f\text{ on }X\iff\bar x\text{ is d-stationary for }\widehat f(\cdot;\bar x)\text{ on }X.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Exhaustive convex and concave approximation families
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines exhaustive families at a fixed point using the directional derivative and the equivalent directional expansion.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\{p_\lambda\mid\lambda\in\Lambda\}\) be upper convex approximations of \(f\) at \(x\). The family is exhaustive if \(\inf_{\lambda\in\Lambda}p_\lambda(g)=f'_x(g)\) for every \(g\in\mathbb R^n\), equivalently \(f(x+\alpha g)=f(x)+\alpha\inf_{\lambda\in\Lambda}p_\lambda(g)+o_g(\alpha)\), where \(o_g(\alpha)/\alpha\to0\) as \(\alpha\downarrow0\). Analogously, lower concave approximations \(\{q_\lambda\mid\lambda\in\Lambda_1\}\) are exhaustive if \(\sup_{\lambda\in\Lambda_1}q_\lambda(g)=f'_x(g)\) for every \(g\), equivalently with the corresponding supremum in the directional expansion.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A family of upper convex approximations is exhaustive when its pointwise infimum equals the directional derivative in every direction. Dually, a family of lower concave approximations is exhaustive when its pointwise supremum equals that derivative. Each equality is equivalent to the corresponding first-order directional expansion with a direction-dependent little-o remainder.
assumptions_latex: \(\{p_\lambda\}_{\lambda\in\Lambda}\) consists of upper convex approximations of \(f\) at \(x\), or \(\{q_\lambda\}_{\lambda\in\Lambda_1}\) consists of lower concave approximations of \(f\) at \(x\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\inf_{\lambda\in\Lambda}p_\lambda(g)=f'_x(g)\ \forall g\in\mathbb R^n\), respectively \(\sup_{\lambda\in\Lambda_1}q_\lambda(g)=f'_x(g)\ \forall g\in\mathbb R^n\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Nonzero aggregate regular-subdifferential sum implies a nonstationary component
knowledge_statements.scope_note: The component points and regular subdifferentials retain their meanings from the surrounding uncertain-data model.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose each \(\varphi_s\) is dd-convex on \(\mathbb R\). If \[0\notin\frac1N\sum_{s=1}^N\widehat\partial\varphi_s(\widehat y_s),\] then there exists \(s\in\{1,\ldots,N\}\) such that \(\widehat y_s\) is not a d-stationary point of \(\varphi_s\) on \(\mathbb R\).

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \exists s\in\{1,\ldots,N\}:\ \widehat y_s\text{ is not d-stationary for }\varphi_s\text{ on }\mathbb R.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Linear Quotient Space of Convex-Compact Differences
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Quotient construction extending support-function duality from sublinear functions to differences of sublinear functions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let N be the family of convex compact subsets of \mathbb{R}^n and let M=N^2/\!\approx, where [U_1,V_1]\approx[U_2,V_2] iff U_1-V_2=U_2-V_1. Write \llbracket U,V\rrbracket for an equivalence class and define \llbracket U_1,V_1\rrbracket+\llbracket U_2,V_2\rrbracket=\llbracket U_1+U_2,V_1+V_2\rrbracket and \lambda\llbracket U,V\rrbracket=\llbracket\lambda U,\lambda V\rrbracket for \lambda\ge0, while \lambda\llbracket U,V\rrbracket=\llbracket\lambda V,\lambda U\rrbracket for \lambda<0. These operations are well defined and make M a real vector space. The representation map \psi:L\to M is a linear bijection, restricts on sublinear p to the class determined by \partial p, and represents the formal difference of convex compact sets U and V by \llbracket U,-V\rrbracket.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Equivalence classes of ordered convex-compact pairs form a real vector space under componentwise Minkowski addition and sign-dependent scalar multiplication. This quotient space is linearly isomorphic to the space of differences of sublinear functions and realizes formal differences of convex compact sets.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: M\text{ is a real vector space and }\psi:L\to M\text{ is a linear bijection; moreover }\psi(p)=\alpha_{\partial p}\text{ for }p\in P.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Mixing, Composition, and Local-to-Global DC Principles
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Three preservation principles for real-valued DC functions on convex domains.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The following hold. (i) If \(S\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) is open and convex, \(f_1,\ldots,f_I\) are dc on \(S\), and \(f:S\to\mathbb R\) is continuous with \(f(x)\in\{f_1(x),\ldots,f_I(x)\}\) for every \(x\in S\), then \(f\) is dc on \(S\). (ii) If \(S\subseteq\mathbb R^m\) is convex and either open or closed, \(T\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) is open and convex, \(g:T\to\mathbb R\) and \(f_i:S\to\mathbb R\) are dc, and \(F(x)=(f_i(x))_{i=1}^n\in T\) for every \(x\in S\), then \(g\circ F\) is dc on \(S\). (iii) Every locally dc function on a convex set that is open or closed is dc on that set.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: DC structure is preserved by continuous selection from finitely many DC functions, by composition of a DC outer function with a DC vector mapping whose range lies in the outer domain, and globally whenever the function is locally DC on an open or closed convex set.
assumptions_latex: For mixing, \(S\) is open and convex and the selection is continuous and pointwise finite-valued
For composition, \(S\) is convex and open or closed, \(T\) is open and convex, and \(F(S)\subseteq T\)
For localization, the domain is convex and either open or closed
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: f\text{ is dc on }S,\quad g\circ F\text{ is dc on }S,\quad\text{and local dc structure implies global dc structure}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Top-K exact sparsity penalty
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines the ℓ1-minus-top-K penalty and records its zero set, piecewise-linear DC structure, and one-sparse variants.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(x\in\mathbb R^n\), let \(1\le K\le n\), and arrange the component magnitudes so that \(|x_{[1]}|\ge\cdots\ge|x_{[n]}|\). Define \(\|x\|_{[K]}:=\sum_{k=1}^K|x_{[k]}|\) and \(p_{[K]}(x):=\|x\|_1-\|x\|_{[K]}\). Then \(p_{[K]}\) is piecewise linear and nonseparable, has the difference-of-convex form \(\|x\|_1-h(x)\) with \(h=\|\cdot\|_{[K]}\) convex piecewise linear, and satisfies \(p_{[K]}(x)=0\iff\|x\|_0\le K\). For \(K=1\), \(p_{[1]}(x)=\|x\|_1-\|x\|_\infty\). The alternative \(\|x\|_1-\|x\|_2\) has the same at-most-one-sparse zero set; \(\|\cdot\|_\infty\) is nondifferentiable at magnitude ties, whereas \(\|\cdot\|_2\) is differentiable away from the origin.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The l1 norm minus the sum of the K largest coordinate magnitudes is a nonseparable piecewise-linear DC penalty whose zeros are exactly the vectors with at most K nonzero coordinates. For K equal to one, l1 minus l-infinity and l1 minus l2 have the same sparse zero set but different differentiability behavior.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Quadratic DC Equation for Affine Complementarity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact squared-product DC formulation for affine nonnegative complementarity pairs.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(a_i,b_i:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) be affine for \(i=1,\ldots,m\), and impose \(a_i(x)\ge0\), \(b_i(x)\ge0\). Then componentwise complementarity is equivalent to \(\sum_{i=1}^m a_i(x)b_i(x)=0\). Moreover, \[\sum_{i=1}^m a_i(x)b_i(x)=\frac14\sum_{i=1}^m(a_i(x)+b_i(x))^2-\frac14\sum_{i=1}^m(a_i(x)-b_i(x))^2,\] a difference of two finite convex quadratic functions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under nonnegativity, affine complementarity is exactly one zero-sum product equation, and polarization represents it as a difference of convex quadratics.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(0\le a(x)\perp b(x)\ge0\iff \frac14\sum_i(a_i(x)+b_i(x))^2-\frac14\sum_i(a_i(x)-b_i(x))^2=0\).
knowledge_statements.title: Quadratic DC Equation for Affine Complementarity
Complementarity DC Reformulations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Componentwise complementarity represented by a nonnegative DC residual.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For mappings \(a,b:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^m\), impose \(a(x)\ge0\) and \(b(x)\ge0\) componentwise. Then
\[
0\le a(x)\perp b(x)\ge0
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
\sum_{i=1}^m\bigl(a_i(x)+b_i(x)-|a_i(x)-b_i(x)|\bigr)=0.
\]
Every summand equals \(2\min\{a_i(x),b_i(x)\}\) and is nonnegative under the sign constraints. If every \(a_i\) and \(b_i\) is affine, the displayed residual is affine minus a convex sum of absolute values and hence is DC. Its zero level set therefore represents the complementarity system exactly.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under nonnegativity, componentwise complementarity is exactly the zero set of a DC residual built from sums and absolute differences.
assumptions_latex: For the stated DC decomposition, \(a_i,b_i\) are affine
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(0\le a(x)\perp b(x)\ge0\iff\sum_i(a_i(x)+b_i(x)-|a_i(x)-b_i(x)|)=0\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The complementarity identity and affine DC decomposition are mathematically correct and fit the representation leaf, but no inspectable citation or locator is supplied.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Finite Union of DC Constraint Systems
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Single-inequality DC encoding of a finite disjunction of finite DC inequality systems.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For branches \(j=1,\ldots,r\), let \[C_j=\{x:f_{j\ell}(x)\le0\text{ for }\ell=1,\ldots,m_j\},\] where every \(f_{j\ell}:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) is finite-valued DC. Define \(r_j(x)=\max_{1\le\ell\le m_j}f_{j\ell}(x)\) and \(R(x)=\min_{1\le j\le r}r_j(x)\). Then \(r_j\) and \(R\) are finite-valued DC, and \[x\in\bigcup_{j=1}^r C_j\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad R(x)\le0.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A finite union of finite DC inequality systems is represented exactly by taking a maximum within each conjunctive branch and a minimum across branches.
assumptions_latex: There are finitely many branches, each containing finitely many inequalities.
Every \(f_{j\ell}\) is finite-valued DC on \(\mathbb R^n\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\bigcup_{j=1}^r C_j=\{x:\min_j\max_\ell f_{j\ell}(x)\le0\}\), and \(\min_j\max_\ell f_{j\ell}\) is DC.
knowledge_statements.title: Finite Union of DC Constraint Systems
Disjunctive DC Reformulations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Two-term convex-inequality disjunction represented by one DC inequality.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(g,h:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) be finite convex functions. The disjunctive constraint
\[
g(x)\le0\quad\text{or}\quad h(x)\le0
\]
is equivalent to \(\min\{g(x),h(x)\}\le0\). Using
\[
\min\{g(x),h(x)\}=g(x)-\max\{g(x)-h(x),0\},
\]
the disjunction becomes a DC inequality whenever \(g-h\) is affine, in particular when \(g\) and \(h\) are affine. More generally, if \(g=g_1-g_2\) and \(h=h_1-h_2\) are DC, the identity \(\min\{g,h\}=g+h-\max\{g,h\}\) supplies a DC representation using closure of finite DC functions under maximum.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A two-term inequality disjunction equals a minimum inequality, which admits an exact DC representation under standard finite-dimensional DC closure rules.
assumptions_latex: \(g,h:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) are finite DC functions
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(g(x)\le0\ \lor\ h(x)\le0\iff\min\{g(x),h(x)\}\le0\), and \(\min\{g,h\}\) is DC.

notation.meaning: the disjunction that at least one displayed inequality holds

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The pointwise disjunction and minimum identities are correct, and finite-dimensional finite DC functions are closed under finite maxima and minima. An authoritative locator for that closure result is still required.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Complementarity as a Finite Union of Branch Systems
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Active-branch expansion of a finite complementarity system.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For mappings \(a,b\) with \(a(x),b(x)\in\mathbb R_+^m\), define for each \(I\subseteq[m]\) \[C_I=\{x:a_i(x)=0\ (i\in I),\ b_i(x)=0\ (i\notin I),\ a(x)\ge0,\ b(x)\ge0\}.\] Then \[\{x:0\le a(x)\perp b(x)\ge0\}=\bigcup_{I\subseteq[m]}C_I.\] The union need not be disjoint because an index with \(a_i(x)=b_i(x)=0\) admits either branch assignment.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A finite complementarity system is the union of all zero-side branch systems; biactive components make the branch representation nonunique.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\{x:0\le a(x)\perp b(x)\ge0\}=\bigcup_{I\subseteq[m]}C_I\).

Complementarity–Disjunction Reformulation Links
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equivalence between nonnegative complementarity and componentwise zero-value disjunctions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For scalars \(u,v\ge0\),
\[
uv=0
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
(u=0)\ \lor\ (v=0)
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
\min\{u,v\}=0
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
u+v-|u-v|=0.
\]
Applying this identity componentwise shows that \(0\le a(x)\perp b(x)\ge0\) is the intersection, over \(i=1,\ldots,m\), of the disjunctions \(a_i(x)=0\) or \(b_i(x)=0\), together with nonnegativity. Thus the minimum-function, absolute-value DC, and disjunctive formulations have the same feasible set.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Each nonnegative complementarity equation is exactly a zero-value disjunction, equivalently a minimum equation or an absolute-value DC equation.
assumptions_latex: All equalities and disjunctions are interpreted componentwise
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(0\le a(x)\perp b(x)\ge0\iff\bigwedge_{i=1}^m(a_i(x)=0\lor b_i(x)=0)\).

children.title: Rank DC Reformulations
children.top_down_role: DC encodings or surrogates for matrix-rank structure.

knowledge_statements.title: Rank DC Reformulations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact spectral DC equation for a matrix rank upper bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(X\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\), let \(q=\min\{m,n\}\), and let \(0\le r<q\). With singular values \(\sigma_1(X)\ge\cdots\ge\sigma_q(X)\ge0\),
\[
\operatorname{rank}(X)\le r
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
\|X\|_* - \|X\|_{(r)}=0,
\qquad
\|X\|_{(r)}=\sum_{i=1}^r\sigma_i(X).
\]
Both the nuclear norm \(\|X\|_*\) and the Ky Fan \(r\)-norm \(\|X\|_{(r)}\) are convex. Their nonnegative difference equals \(\sum_{i=r+1}^q\sigma_i(X)\), so its zero level set is exactly the rank-constrained set.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Rank at most r is equivalent to the nuclear norm equaling the Ky Fan r-norm, giving an exact spectral DC equation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{rank}(X)\le r\iff\|X\|_* - \|X\|_{(r)}=0\).

notation.meaning: nuclear norm, the sum of all singular values
Ky Fan r-norm, the sum of the r largest singular values

source_refs.locator: 3.2 Low Rankness in Matrix Optimization p. 131

source_witnesses.locator: 3.2 Low Rankness in Matrix Optimization p. 131

children.title: Sparsity DC Reformulations
children.top_down_role: DC encodings or surrogates for sparse vector or matrix structure.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Group-Sparsity DC Reformulation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact ordered-group-norm equation for a bound on the number of active groups.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(G_1,\ldots,G_p\) partition the coordinates of \(x\), set \(a_j=\|x_{G_j}\|_2\), and order these values as \(a_{[1]}\ge\cdots\ge a_{[p]}\). For \(0\le s<p\), \[\#\{j:x_{G_j}\ne0\}\le s\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad \sum_{j=1}^p\|x_{G_j}\|_2-\sum_{j=1}^s a_{[j]}=0.\] Both displayed sums are convex; their nonnegative difference is the ordered group-norm tail.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At most s active groups is exactly characterized by equality between the total group norm and the sum of its s largest group norms.
knowledge_statements.title: Group-Sparsity DC Reformulation
Sparsity DC Reformulations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact ordered-magnitude DC equation for a sparsity upper bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(x\in\mathbb R^n\), let \(|x|_{[1]}\ge\cdots\ge|x|_{[n]}\) be the ordered absolute components, and let \(0\le s<n\). Define \(\|x\|_{(s,1)}=\sum_{i=1}^s|x|_{[i]}\). Then
\[
\|x\|_0\le s
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
\|x\|_1-\|x\|_{(s,1)}=0.
\]
The two terms are convex, while their nonnegative difference equals \(\sum_{i=s+1}^n|x|_{[i]}\). Consequently, its zero level set is exactly the set of vectors having at most \(s\) nonzero components.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At most s nonzeros is equivalent to the l1 norm equaling the sum of the s largest component magnitudes, an exact DC equation.

notation.meaning: number of nonzero components of x
sum of the s largest absolute components

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The ordered-magnitude identity is correct and gives an exact DC representation of the sparsity bound, but no source with a specific locator is supplied.

children.title: Low-Complexity Surrogate Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Limits of DC surrogates for preserving rank or sparsity targets.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Convex Surrogates Can Be Constant Across Complexity Levels
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Concrete failure of standard convex surrogates to distinguish low-complexity points from higher-complexity points.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(S=\{x\in\mathbb R_+^2:x_1+x_2=1\}\). Every \(x\in S\) satisfies \(\|x\|_1=1\), although \((1,0)\) has cardinality one and \((1/2,1/2)\) has cardinality two. Likewise, let \(T=\{X\in\mathbb S_+^2:\operatorname{tr}X=1\}\). Every \(X\in T\) satisfies \(\|X\|_*=1\), although \(\operatorname{diag}(1,0)\) has rank one and \(I/2\) has rank two. Thus \(\ell_1\)- or nuclear-norm minimization over these sets admits higher-complexity minimizers.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Standard convex low-complexity surrogates may be constant on feasible sets containing both low- and high-complexity points.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\ell_1\)- and nuclear-norm minimization need not recover minimum-cardinality or minimum-rank points.

notation.meaning: cone of real symmetric positive-semidefinite two-by-two matrices

knowledge_statements.title: Convex Surrogates Can Be Constant Across Complexity Levels
Low-Complexity Surrogate Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact zero-set reformulation does not itself guarantee exact penalization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(X\) be compact and let \(R:X\to\mathbb R_+\) be a continuous rank or sparsity residual with nonempty zero set \(C=\{x\in X:R(x)=0\}\) and \(R(\bar x)>0\) for some \(\bar x\in X\). For any prescribed \(\rho>0\), define \(f(x)=-(\rho+1)R(x)\). The constrained problem has value \(0\), whereas
\[
f(x)+\rho R(x)=-R(x)
\]
is strictly negative at \(\bar x\). Consequently, every global minimizer of the penalized problem is infeasible. Exactness therefore requires additional control, such as objective regularity and an error bound relating distance to \(C\) to \(R\); DC representability alone is insufficient.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Even a continuous exact rank or sparsity residual need not produce an exact finite penalty; objective regularity and a compatible error bound are additional requirements.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For every fixed \(\rho>0\), there exists a continuous objective \(f\) for which every global minimizer of \(f+\rho R\) is outside \(C\).

children.title: Integrality DC Reformulations
children.top_down_role: DC encodings or penalties for integer-valued decision restrictions.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Bounded-Integer Binary Lifting
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact lifted DC representation of bounded integer variables through binary digits.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\ell,u\in\mathbb Z^n\) with \(\ell\le u\). For each \(i\), choose an integer \(p_i\ge0\) satisfying \(2^{p_i}>u_i-\ell_i\). Then \(x\in[\ell,u]\cap\mathbb Z^n\) if and only if there are \(b_{ij}\in[0,1]\) such that \[x_i=\ell_i+\sum_{j=0}^{p_i-1}2^j b_{ij},\qquad x_i\le u_i,\] and \[\sum_{i=1}^n\sum_{j=0}^{p_i-1}b_{ij}(1-b_{ij})=0.\] The final equality is a DC equation whose nonnegative summands enforce binary digits.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every bounded integer vector has an exact binary lifting whose integrality is enforced by one concave-quadratic DC equality.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x\in[\ell,u]\cap\mathbb Z^n\) is equivalent to the displayed lifted DC system.

notation.meaning: number of digits used for component i

knowledge_statements.title: Bounded-Integer Binary Lifting
Integrality DC Reformulations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact concave-quadratic DC equation for binary integrality on a box.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(x\in[0,1]^n\), define
\[
R_{\mathrm{bin}}(x)=\sum_{i=1}^n x_i(1-x_i)=\mathbf1^\top x-\|x\|_2^2.
\]
Every summand is nonnegative on the box and vanishes exactly when \(x_i\in\{0,1\}\). Therefore
\[
x\in\{0,1\}^n
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
R_{\mathrm{bin}}(x)=0.
\]
Because \(\mathbf1^\top x\) and \(\|x\|_2^2\) are convex, the residual is a DC function. Binary integrality can thus be imposed by the box constraints together with one exact DC equality.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Within the unit box, binary integrality is exactly the zero set of the DC residual summing x_i times one minus x_i.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The box-constrained binary residual is an exact DC representation and fits the leaf, but no authoritative source and locator are provided.

children.title: Cardinality DC Reformulations
children.top_down_role: DC encodings or penalties for cardinality restrictions.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Trimmed-L1 Reformulation of a Cardinality Constraint
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Gap-free exact DC equation for an upper bound on vector support size.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(x\in\mathbb R^n\) and \(k\in\{0,\ldots,n\}\), let \(|x|_{[1]}\ge\cdots\ge|x|_{[n]}\) be the decreasing rearrangement of the component magnitudes and define \(\|x\|_{(k)}=\sum_{i=1}^k|x|_{[i]}\), with \(\|x\|_{(0)}=0\). Then \(\|\cdot\|_{(k)}\) is convex and \[\|x\|_0\le k\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad \|x\|_1-\|x\|_{(k)}=0.\] Thus the cardinality constraint is exactly one DC equality without a minimum-nonzero-magnitude assumption.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A vector has at most k nonzero components exactly when its l1 norm equals the sum of its k largest component magnitudes, giving a gap-free DC equality.

notation.meaning: sum of the k largest component magnitudes

knowledge_statements.title: Trimmed-L1 Reformulation of a Cardinality Constraint
Cardinality DC Reformulations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Capped-magnitude DC representation of cardinality under a nonzero-gap condition.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Fix \(\tau>0\) and suppose \(x\in\mathbb R^n\) satisfies the gap condition \(x_i=0\) or \(|x_i|\ge\tau\) for every \(i\). Then
\[
\|x\|_0=\sum_{i=1}^n\min\left\{1,\frac{|x_i|}{\tau}\right\}
=\frac{\|x\|_1}{\tau}-\sum_{i=1}^n\max\left\{\frac{|x_i|}{\tau}-1,0\right\}.
\]
Both terms on the right are convex, so the cardinality function restricted to this gap domain has the displayed DC representation. Consequently, \(\|x\|_0\le k\) is equivalent there to the corresponding DC expression being at most \(k\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: When every nonzero component has magnitude at least tau, cardinality equals a capped-l1 DC expression, yielding an exact cardinality inequality.

notation.meaning: minimum allowed magnitude of a nonzero component
cardinality of the support of x

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The capped-magnitude identity is correct under the explicitly stated nonzero-gap condition, and the plain and LaTeX statements agree. A source with a specific locator is required.

children.title: Discrete-Structure Exactness Regimes
children.top_down_role: Regimes where continuous DC reformulations preserve targeted discrete structure.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Strict-Threshold Boundary for Residual Exactness
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sharpness of the strict penalty inequality in the residual-dominance criterion.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X=[0,1]\), \(D=\{0\}\), \(R(x)=x\), and \(f(x)=-Lx\), where \(L>0\). Then \(\operatorname{dist}(x,D)=R(x)\) and \[f(x)+\rho R(x)=(\rho-L)x.\] At \(\rho=L\), every point of \(X\) is a penalized minimizer. For \(0\le\rho<L\), the unique penalized minimizer is the infeasible point \(x=1\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At the threshold infeasible points can tie with the discrete solution, and below it an infeasible point can be uniquely optimal.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\rho=L\) need not exclude infeasible minimizers, and \(\rho<L\) need not be exact.
knowledge_statements.title: Strict-Threshold Boundary for Residual Exactness

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Residual-Dominance Exactness for Discrete Sets
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Global exactness criterion for a discrete target represented by a nonnegative residual with a rounding error bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\subset\mathbb R^n\), let \(D\subset X\) be nonempty, and let \(R:X\to\mathbb R_+\) satisfy \(R^{-1}(0)=D\). Suppose \(P:X\to D\) and \(\kappa>0\) satisfy \(\|x-P(x)\|\le\kappa R(x)\) for every \(x\in X\). If \(f:X\to\mathbb R\) is \(L\)-Lipschitz in the same norm, then, for \(\rho>L\kappa\), \[f(x)+\rho R(x)\ge f(P(x))+(\rho-L\kappa)R(x).\] Consequently, \[\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in X}\{f(x)+\rho R(x)\}=\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in D}f(x).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A residual that globally controls rounding distance gives an exact discrete penalty whenever its weight exceeds the Lipschitz constant times the residual-to-distance modulus.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname*{argmin}_{X}(f+\rho R)=\operatorname*{argmin}_{D}f\).
knowledge_statements.title: Residual-Dominance Exactness for Discrete Sets
Discrete-Structure Exactness Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Global exactness threshold for the binary quadratic residual under Lipschitz continuity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(f:[0,1]^n\to\mathbb R\) be \(L\)-Lipschitz in the \(\ell_1\)-norm, and define \(R(x)=\sum_{i=1}^n x_i(1-x_i)\). For each \(x\), let \(z\in\{0,1\}^n\) be obtained by rounding every component to its nearest endpoint. Then \(R(x)\ge\tfrac12\|x-z\|_1\). Consequently, if \(\rho>2L\),
\[
f(x)+\rho R(x)\ge f(z)+(\rho/2-L)\|x-z\|_1,
\]
with strict inequality whenever \(x\) is nonbinary. Hence every global minimizer of \(f+\rho R\) on \([0,1]^n\) is binary and solves \(\min\{f(z):z\in\{0,1\}^n\}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For an l1-Lipschitz objective, penalizing the binary residual with coefficient greater than twice the Lipschitz constant is globally exact.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname*{argmin}_{[0,1]^n}(f+\rho R)\subseteq\operatorname*{argmin}_{\{0,1\}^n}f\).

notation.meaning: componentwise nearest binary rounding of x

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The rounding bound and threshold rho>2L are mathematically consistent and the theorem fits the exactness-regime leaf, but a theorem-level authoritative citation with a specific locator is absent.

children.title: DC Algorithm Families
children.top_down_role: Classical DCA followed by regularized, accelerated, inexact, structured, constrained, and stronger-stationarity variants.

children.title: Classical DCA
children.top_down_role: Foundational primal and primal–dual forms, with the convex–concave procedure represented as a closely related specialization.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Asymptotic Regularity from Sufficient Decrease
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Step-size convergence and best-step bound under a lower objective bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Under the sufficient-decrease inequality, suppose \rho_g+\rho_h>0 and F(x^k)\ge F_{\inf}>-\infty. Then \[\sum_{k=0}^{\infty}\|x^{k+1}-x^k\|_2^2\le\frac{2(F(x^0)-F_{\inf})}{\rho_g+\rho_h},\] so \(\|x^{k+1}-x^k\|_2\to0\), and for every N\ge1, \[\min_{0\le k<N}\|x^{k+1}-x^k\|_2^2\le\frac{2(F(x^0)-F_{\inf})}{(\rho_g+\rho_h)N}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If the objective is bounded below and one component supplies curvature, squared DCA steps are summable and the best squared step is order one over N.
assumptions_latex: The exact sufficient-decrease inequality holds at every iteration.

notation.meaning: finite lower bound for objective values along the trajectory

knowledge_statements.title: Asymptotic Regularity from Sufficient Decrease

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Well-Posed Primal DCA Step Conditions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sufficient conditions ensuring subgradient existence and convex-subproblem attainment.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let g,h:\mathbb R^n\to(-\infty,+\infty] be proper lower-semicontinuous convex functions. At x^k, a primal DCA step is well posed if x^k\in\operatorname{ri}(\operatorname{dom}h) and, for every selected y^k\in\partial h(x^k), the function x\mapsto g(x)-\langle y^k,x\rangle is proper and level-bounded. Then \partial h(x^k)\ne\varnothing, and the next-iterate set is nonempty and compact.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A relative-interior iterate supplies a subgradient, while proper level-bounded tilted subproblems guarantee attained DCA updates.
assumptions_latex: g-\langle y^k,\cdot\rangle\text{ is proper and level-bounded}.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \partial h(x^k)\ne\varnothing,\qquad \arg\min_x\{g(x)-\langle y^k,x\rangle\}\ne\varnothing\text{ and is compact}.
knowledge_statements.title: Well-Posed Primal DCA Step Conditions

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Primal DCA Sufficient Decrease
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Quantitative descent when either selected DC component is strongly convex.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let F=g-h, choose y^k\in\partial h(x^k), and let x^{k+1} minimize g(x)-\langle y^k,x\rangle. If g and h are respectively \rho_g- and \rho_h-strongly convex, allowing either modulus to be zero, then \[F(x^k)-F(x^{k+1})\ge\frac{\rho_g+\rho_h}{2}\|x^{k+1}-x^k\|_2^2.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Primal DCA is monotone, and strong convexity of either component converts step length into guaranteed objective decrease.
assumptions_latex: g\text{ is }\rho_g\text{-strongly convex and }h\text{ is }\rho_h\text{-strongly convex}.

notation.meaning: strong-convexity moduli of the selected DC components

knowledge_statements.title: Primal DCA Sufficient Decrease
Primal DCA
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Classical exact primal DCA for a proper lower-semicontinuous convex decomposition on finite-dimensional space.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Given \(F=g-h\) on \(\mathbb{R}^n\), choose \(x^0\in\operatorname{dom}g\cap\operatorname{dom}h\). For \(k=0,1,\ldots\), select \(y^k\in\partial h(x^k)\) and compute
\[
x^{k+1}\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in\mathbb{R}^n}\{g(x)-\langle y^k,x\rangle\}.
\]
Equivalently, the update satisfies \(y^k\in\partial h(x^k)\cap\partial g(x^{k+1})\). Stop when a prescribed residual or successive-iterate tolerance is met, and return the last iterate. If \(x^{k+1}=x^k\), then \(0\in\partial g(x^k)-\partial h(x^k)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Linearize the subtracted convex term at the current point, minimize the resulting convex model, and stop at a DC-critical fixed point.
assumptions_latex: The displayed subproblem has a minimizer at every executed iteration.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(y^k\in\partial h(x^k)\), \(x^{k+1}\in\partial g^*(y^k)\), and a fixed point satisfies \(0\in\partial g(x^k)-\partial h(x^k)\).

notation.meaning: DC objective and its selected decomposition.
Convex subdifferential of a proper convex function q.

source_refs.locator: 4.4.6 Implicit convex-concave functions p. 239

source_witnesses.locator: 4.4.6 Implicit convex-concave functions p. 239

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The update is standard, but the cited section does not specifically establish classical primal DCA, and the assumptions do not ensure that the required selection from ∂h(x^k) exists at every iteration.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Toland Infimum Equality
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Zero-gap value relation underlying the conjugate-space DCA formulation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: When the extended-real differences are well defined, \[\inf_x\{g(x)-h(x)\}=\inf_y\{h^*(y)-g^*(y)\}.\] The equality concerns infimal values and does not by itself assert attainment or convergence of DCA.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The primal DC problem and its Toland dual have the same infimal value, while attainment and algorithmic convergence require separate assumptions.
assumptions_latex: The primal and dual differences avoid indeterminate \(+\infty-+\infty\) values; for example, the relevant effective-domain inclusions hold.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \inf F=\inf D.
knowledge_statements.title: Toland Infimum Equality

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Toland Dual and Symmetric DCA Steps
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conjugate-space interpretation of exact primal–dual DCA.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(F(x)=g(x)-h(x)\), define \(D(y)=h^*(y)-g^*(y)\). If \(y^k\in\partial h(x^k)\), \(x^{k+1}\in\partial g^*(y^k)\), and \(y^{k+1}\in\partial h(x^{k+1})\), then \(y^{k+1}\in\operatorname*{argmin}_y\{h^*(y)-\langle x^{k+1},y\rangle\}\). Thus alternating primal–dual DCA is DCA on both \(g-h\) and, with exchanged roles, \(h^*-g^*\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Primal–dual DCA alternates compatible DCA steps for the primal objective and its Toland conjugate-space dual.
assumptions_latex: All displayed subdifferential selections are nonempty.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(y^{k+1}\in\operatorname*{argmin}_y\{h^*(y)-\langle x^{k+1},y\rangle\}\).
knowledge_statements.title: Toland Dual and Symmetric DCA Steps

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Primal–Dual Interlacing Descent
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Value relation generated by one exact primal–dual DCA step.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(y^k\in\partial h(x^k)\) and \(x^{k+1}\in\partial g^*(y^k)\), then \[g(x^{k+1})-h(x^{k+1})\le h^*(y^k)-g^*(y^k)\le g(x^k)-h(x^k).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The Toland-dual value lies between two consecutive primal objective values, so exact primal–dual DCA is descending.
assumptions_latex: The displayed selections exist and all displayed differences are well defined and finite.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: F(x^{k+1})\le D(y^k)\le F(x^k).
knowledge_statements.title: Primal–Dual Interlacing Descent
Primal–Dual DCA
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Fenchel-coupled primal–dual form of exact classical DCA.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(F=g-h\), initialize \(x^0\in\operatorname{dom}g\cap\operatorname{dom}h\). At iteration \(k\), choose
\[
y^k\in\partial h(x^k),\qquad x^{k+1}\in\partial g^*(y^k).
\]
The inclusions are equivalent to \(x^k\in\partial h^*(y^k)\) and \(y^k\in\partial g(x^{k+1})\), so the algorithm alternates between the primal and conjugate spaces. Stop when both inclusion residuals satisfy prescribed tolerances, and return \((x^{k+1},y^k)\). A fixed primal iterate obeys the DC criticality inclusion \(0\in\partial g(x)-\partial h(x)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Alternate subgradient selections in the primal and Fenchel-dual spaces; a fixed primal–dual pair certifies DC criticality.
assumptions_latex: Both displayed subdifferential selections are nonempty at every executed iteration.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The generated pair satisfies \(y^k\in\partial h(x^k)\) and \(x^{k+1}\in\partial g^*(y^k)\); fixed points are DC-critical.

source_refs.locator: 4.4.6 Implicit convex-concave functions p. 239

source_witnesses.locator: 4.4.6 Implicit convex-concave functions p. 239

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The Fenchel inclusions are mathematically consistent, but the cited locator does not specifically support this primal–dual DCA algorithm or its residual-based stopping formulation.

knowledge_statements.title: Convex–Concave Procedure
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Differentiable concave-part CCP for constrained DC minimization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(C\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) be nonempty, closed, and convex, and minimize \(F(x)=g(x)-h(x)\) over \(C\). Starting from \(x^0\in C\cap\operatorname{dom}g\), form the convex majorant
\[
M_k(x)=g(x)-h(x^k)-\langle\nabla h(x^k),x-x^k\rangle
\]
and choose \(x^{k+1}\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in C}M_k(x)\). Stop under a prescribed step or stationarity tolerance. Since convexity gives \(F(x)\leq M_k(x)\) and equality at \(x=x^k\), exact updates satisfy \(F(x^{k+1})\leq F(x^k)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Replace the subtracted differentiable convex term by its affine minorant, minimize the resulting convex majorant, and obtain monotone objective decrease from a feasible point with finite objective.
assumptions_latex: \(h:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\) is convex and differentiable on an open set containing \(C\).
\(x^0\in C\cap\operatorname{dom}g\), and each convex model subproblem attains a finite minimum.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F(x^{k+1})\leq M_k(x^{k+1})\leq M_k(x^k)=F(x^k)\).

notation.meaning: Convex majorant obtained by affine linearization of h.

source_refs.locator: 4.4.6 Implicit convex-concave functions p. 239

source_witnesses.locator: 4.4.6 Implicit convex-concave functions p. 239

knowledge_statements.statement_title: CCP Fixed-Point Stationarity Certificate
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Qualification-safe first-order certificate for an exact fixed point of differentiable-part CCP.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \min_{x\in C}g(x)-h(x), suppose h is differentiable at  ar x and  ar x solves its own CCP model: \[ ar x\in\arg\min_x\{g(x)+\delta_C(x)-\langle
abla h( ar x),xangle\}.\] Then \[
abla h( ar x)\in\partial(g+\delta_C)( ar x).\] If a convex subdifferential sum-rule qualification also gives \partial(g+\delta_C)( ar x)=\partial g( ar x)+N_C( ar x), this becomes \[0\in\partial g( ar x)-
abla h( ar x)+N_C( ar x).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An exact CCP fixed point satisfies the qualification-free composite stationarity inclusion; the separated normal-cone form additionally requires a valid sum rule.
assumptions_latex: C\text{ is nonempty, closed, and convex}.
g\text{ is proper lower-semicontinuous and convex}.
h\text{ is convex and differentiable at }\bar x.
\bar x\text{ minimizes its own exact CCP model}.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \nabla h(\bar x)\in\partial(g+\delta_C)(\bar x).

notation.meaning: convex normal cone when the sum rule applies

knowledge_statements.title: CCP Fixed-Point Stationarity Certificate

knowledge_statements.statement_title: CCP Can Fix a Nonoptimal Stationary Point
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary on interpreting monotone descent or fixed-point stationarity as global optimality.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: On C=[-1,1], let \[F(x)=x^4-x^2=g(x)-h(x),\qquad g(x)=x^4+x^2,\quad h(x)=2x^2.\] Both components are convex and h is differentiable. Starting at x^0=0 gives \nabla h(0)=0, so the CCP model uniquely minimizes g at zero and x^k=0 for every k. Nevertheless, F(0)=0 while F(\pm1/\sqrt2)=-1/4.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: CCP can remain at a stationary point whose value is strictly worse than the global minimum.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: x^k=0\ \forall k,\qquad F(0)=0>\min_{x\in[-1,1]}F(x)=-\tfrac14.
knowledge_statements.title: CCP Can Fix a Nonoptimal Stationary Point

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Fixed Points of the DCA Transition
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact relation between transition-map fixed points and DCA criticality.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(T(x)=\bigcup_{y\in\partial h(x)}\partial g^*(y)\), \[x\in T(x)\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad\partial g(x)\cap\partial h(x)\ne\varnothing.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The fixed points of the set-valued DCA transition are exactly the points where the two convex components share a subgradient.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{Fix}T=\{x:\partial g(x)\cap\partial h(x)\ne\varnothing\}.

notation.meaning: Fixed-point set of the DCA transition.

knowledge_statements.title: Fixed Points of the DCA Transition

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Extreme Branching with a Constant Objective
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sharp nonuniqueness boundary for selector-based DCA trajectories.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(g=h\equiv0\) on \(\mathbb R^n\). Then \(g^*=h^*=\delta_{\{0\}}\), \(\partial h(x)=\{0\}\), and \(\partial g^*(0)=\mathbb R^n\). Hence \(T(x)=\mathbb R^n\) for every \(x\), so every sequence is an admissible DCA trajectory although \(g-h\equiv0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Even for a constant objective, the set-valued DCA transition can admit every possible next iterate.
assumptions_latex: The standard convex subdifferential and extended-valued Fenchel conjugate are used.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: T(x)=\mathbb R^n\quad\text{for every }x.
knowledge_statements.title: Extreme Branching with a Constant Objective
Set-Valued DCA Trajectories
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Trajectory representation retaining all admissible subgradient and convex-subproblem choices.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(F=g-h\), define the set-valued DCA transition
\[
T(x)=\bigcup_{y\in\partial h(x)}\partial g^*(y).
\]
A finite or infinite sequence \((x^k)\) is a DCA trajectory precisely when \(x^{k+1}\in T(x^k)\) for every applicable \(k\); equivalently, there exists a selector sequence \((y^k)\) with \(y^k\in\partial h(x^k)\) and \(y^k\in\partial g(x^{k+1})\). Thus nondifferentiability or nonunique convex minimizers can produce multiple trajectories from the same initial point.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: All DCA runs are selections of a set-valued transition formed by composing the subdifferential of the concave component with the inverse subdifferential of the convex component.
assumptions_latex: The transition set \(T(x^k)\) is nonempty along the trajectory.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x^{k+1}\in T(x^k)\) if and only if some \(y^k\in\partial h(x^k)\cap\partial g(x^{k+1})\) exists.

source_refs.locator: Chapter 5. Set-Valued Mappings p. 148
1.5 Elements of Set-Valued Analysis p. 54

source_witnesses.locator: Chapter 5. Set-Valued Mappings p. 148
1.5 Elements of Set-Valued Analysis p. 54

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The set-valued transition formula is consistent with classical DCA, but the supplied sources cover general set-valued analysis rather than this DCA trajectory representation.

knowledge_statements.title: Proximal DCA
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Euclidean proximal regularization of the classical DCA convex subproblem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Given \(F=g-h\), a parameter \(\rho>0\), and \(x^0\in\operatorname{dom}g\cap\operatorname{dom}h\), select \(y^k\in\partial h(x^k)\) and compute
\[
x^{k+1}\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in\mathbb{R}^n}\left\{g(x)-\langle y^k,x\rangle+\frac{\rho}{2}\lVert x-x^k\rVert^2\right\}.
\]
Stop when \(\lVert x^{k+1}-x^k\rVert\) or a stationarity residual is below tolerance. The optimality condition is \(0\in\partial g(x^{k+1})-y^k+\rho(x^{k+1}-x^k)\); the quadratic term makes the subproblem strongly convex.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Add a positive quadratic centered at the current iterate to the DCA convex model, yielding a uniquely determined regularized update.
assumptions_latex: The regularized subproblem is proper and attains its minimum.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(0\in\partial g(x^{k+1})-y^k+\rho(x^{k+1}-x^k)\), and the update is unique when the objective is proper.

notation.meaning: Selected subgradient of h at the current iterate.

source_refs.locator: 2.5.2 The proximal gradient method for convex programs p. 93

source_witnesses.locator: 2.5.2 The proximal gradient method for convex programs p. 93

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The proximal DCA update and optimality condition are mathematically consistent, but a generic convex proximal-gradient section does not support this specific DC algorithm.

knowledge_statements.title: Linearized Proximal DCA
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Proximal DC update linearizing both smooth convex and subtracted convex components.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(F=f+r-h\), where \(f\) is differentiable and convex while \(r,h\) are proper convex functions. Given \(x^0\) and \(L_k>0\), select \(y^k\in\partial h(x^k)\) and set
\[
x^{k+1}\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{x}\left\{r(x)+\langle\nabla f(x^k)-y^k,x-x^k\rangle+\frac{L_k}{2}\lVert x-x^k\rVert^2\right\}.
\]
Choose \(L_k\) large enough for the smooth upper-model inequality for \(f\), stop at a prescribed residual tolerance, and return the last iterate. Equivalently, \(x^{k+1}=\operatorname{prox}_{r/L_k}(x^k-(\nabla f(x^k)-y^k)/L_k)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Linearize the smooth convex and subtracted convex terms, then apply one proximal step to the remaining nonsmooth convex term.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is convex and differentiable with locally Lipschitz gradient on the iterates' region.
Each selected \(L_k\) validates the quadratic upper model of \(f\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x^{k+1}=\operatorname{prox}_{r/L_k}(x^k-(\nabla f(x^k)-y^k)/L_k)\) with \(y^k\in\partial h(x^k)\).

notation.meaning: Nonsmooth convex term retained in the proximal subproblem.

source_refs.locator: 2.5.2 The proximal gradient method for convex programs p. 93

source_witnesses.locator: 2.5.2 The proximal gradient method for convex programs p. 93

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The displayed proximal-linearized update is coherent, but the cited convex proximal-gradient section does not establish its DC specialization or terminology.

knowledge_statements.title: Bregman DCA
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Non-Euclidean DCA using a Bregman distance in the regularized convex subproblem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(F=g-h\), and let \(\phi\) be differentiable and strictly convex on an open convex set containing the iterates. Define \(D_\phi(x,z)=\phi(x)-\phi(z)-\langle\nabla\phi(z),x-z\rangle\). Given \(x^0\) and \(\lambda_k>0\), select \(y^k\in\partial h(x^k)\) and compute
\[
x^{k+1}\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{x}\{g(x)-\langle y^k,x\rangle+\lambda_k^{-1}D_\phi(x,x^k)\}.
\]
Stop at a prescribed Bregman-step or stationarity tolerance. The update satisfies \(0\in\partial g(x^{k+1})-y^k+\lambda_k^{-1}(\nabla\phi(x^{k+1})-\nabla\phi(x^k))\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Replace Euclidean quadratic regularization by a Bregman distance generated by a strictly convex differentiable kernel.
assumptions_latex: \(\phi\) is differentiable and strictly convex on the relevant open convex domain.
Each Bregman-regularized subproblem attains its minimum.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(0\in\partial g(x^{k+1})-y^k+\lambda_k^{-1}(\nabla\phi(x^{k+1})-\nabla\phi(x^k))\).

notation.meaning: Bregman distance generated by the kernel phi.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The stated non-Euclidean update is plausible, but no source is supplied to confirm the exact Bregman DCA variant, kernel assumptions, or parameter convention.

knowledge_statements.title: Double-Proximal DC Methods
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Representative Euclidean double-proximal primal–dual realization of a DC iteration.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(F=g-h\), choose \(x^0,y^{-1}\in\mathbb{R}^n\) and parameters \(\lambda_k,\mu_k>0\). A double-proximal iteration is
\[
y^k=\operatorname{prox}_{\mu_k h^*}(y^{k-1}+\mu_k x^k),\qquad
x^{k+1}=\operatorname{prox}_{\lambda_k g}(x^k+\lambda_k y^k).
\]
Stop when both successive differences satisfy prescribed tolerances, and return \((x^{k+1},y^k)\). The two proximal equations are equivalent to \(x^k-\mu_k^{-1}(y^k-y^{k-1})\in\partial h^*(y^k)\) and \(y^k-\lambda_k^{-1}(x^{k+1}-x^k)\in\partial g(x^{k+1})\); vanishing increments recover the primal–dual DC criticality relations.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Apply proximal mappings to the conjugate concave component and the primal convex component; vanishing update increments yield DC criticality.
assumptions_latex: The proximal mappings are evaluated exactly with positive parameters.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If both increments vanish, then \(x^k\in\partial h^*(y^k)\) and \(y^k\in\partial g(x^k)\), hence \(0\in\partial g(x^k)-\partial h(x^k)\).

notation.meaning: Positive primal and dual proximal parameters.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The proximal identities are algebraically consistent, but “double-proximal DC methods” has multiple variants and no source confirms that this particular coupled iteration is the intended one.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Strict Descent of the DCA Displacement
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Descent property justifying extrapolation beyond an ordinary DCA point.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F=g-h\), choose \(y^k\in\partial h(x^k)\), and let \(z^k\in\operatorname*{argmin}_x\{g(x)-\langle y^k,x\rangle\}\). Set \(d^k=z^k-x^k\). If \(h\) is \(\rho\)-strongly convex and \(g\) is differentiable at \(z^k\), then \(\nabla g(z^k)=y^k\) and \[F'(z^k;d^k)\leq-\rho\lVert d^k\rVert^2.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: When the subtracted component is strongly convex and the first component is differentiable at the DCA point, continuing along the DCA displacement gives strict descent unless the displacement is zero.
assumptions_latex: The DCA subproblem attains its minimum.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: d^k\neq0\Longrightarrow F'(z^k;d^k)\leq-\rho\lVert d^k\rVert^2<0.
knowledge_statements.title: Strict Descent of the DCA Displacement

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Finite Termination of Boosting Backtracking
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Well-posedness of quadratic-decrease backtracking along a feasible strict-descent ray.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose \(d\neq0\), \(F'(z;d)<0\), and \(F\) is directionally differentiable at \(z\) along \(d\). If \(z+td\) is feasible for every sufficiently small \(t\geq0\), then for every \(\alpha>0\), \(\bar\lambda>0\), and \(\beta\in(0,1)\), some \(j<\infty\) satisfies \[F(z+\bar\lambda\beta^j d)\leq F(z)-\alpha(\bar\lambda\beta^j)^2\lVert d\rVert^2.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A feasible strict-descent direction ensures finite acceptance of the quadratic-decrease backtracking test used for boosting.
