assumptions_latex: All sufficiently small nonnegative points on the ray are feasible.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \exists j<\infty:\ F(z+\bar\lambda\beta^j d)\leq F(z)-\alpha(\bar\lambda\beta^j)^2\lVert d\rVert^2.
knowledge_statements.title: Finite Termination of Boosting Backtracking

knowledge_statements.statement_title: A DCA Displacement Need Not Be a Post-DCA Descent Direction
knowledge_statements.scope_note: One-dimensional failure after removing the sufficient differentiability and strong-convexity hypotheses.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let F=g-h on \mathbb R, where g(x)=|x| and h(x)=0. From x^k=1 choose y^k=0\in\partial h(x^k). The DCA subproblem has the unique solution z^k=0, so d^k=z^k-x^k=-1. Nevertheless, \[F'(z^k;d^k)=F'(0;-1)=1>0,\] and F(z^k+td^k)=t>F(z^k) for every t>0.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For absolute value, the DCA step reaches the minimizer, but extrapolating farther along its displacement immediately increases the objective.
assumptions_latex: The exact DCA subproblem solution z^k=0 is used.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: F'(z^k;d^k)>0\quad\text{and}\quad F(z^k+td^k)>F(z^k)\ \forall t>0.

notation.meaning: post-DCA extrapolation direction equal to minus one

knowledge_statements.title: A DCA Displacement Need Not Be a Post-DCA Descent Direction

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Boosting-Decrease Summability
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Consequence of quadratic boosting decrease for a lower-bounded objective.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let d^k=z^k-x^k and x^{k+1}=z^k+\lambda_kd^k. If F(z^k)\le F(x^k), F(x^{k+1})\le F(z^k)-\alpha\lambda_k^2\|d^k\|^2 for fixed \alpha>0, and \inf_kF(x^k)>-\infty, then \sum_{k=0}^\infty\lambda_k^2\|d^k\|^2<\infty and \lambda_k\|d^k\|\to0. If \inf_k\lambda_k>0, then d^k\to0.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Quadratic boosting decrease makes accepted extrapolation lengths square summable; the unscaled DCA displacement vanishes if accepted boosting factors stay bounded away from zero.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \sum_k\lambda_k^2\|d^k\|^2<\infty,\quad\lambda_k\|d^k\|\to0;\qquad\inf_k\lambda_k>0\Longrightarrow d^k\to0.
knowledge_statements.title: Boosting-Decrease Summability

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Zero DCA Displacement Certifies DC Criticality
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact stopping certificate for the ordinary DCA point underlying boosting.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F=g-h\), choose \(y^k\in\partial h(x^k)\), and let \(z^k\in\arg\min_x\{g(x)-\langle y^k,x\rangle\}\). If \(d^k=z^k-x^k=0\), then \(y^k\in\partial g(x^k)\cap\partial h(x^k)\); hence \(x^k\) is critical for the chosen DC decomposition.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A zero ordinary-DCA displacement supplies a shared-subgradient certificate of decomposition-relative criticality.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: d^k=0\Longrightarrow y^k\in\partial g(x^k)\cap\partial h(x^k).
knowledge_statements.title: Zero DCA Displacement Certifies DC Criticality

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Ambient Descent Does Not Ensure a Feasible Boosting Ray
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Constraint boundary for post-DCA extrapolation and line-search well-posedness.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X=[0,\infty)\), \(z=0\), \(d=-1\), and \(F(x)=x\) on \(\mathbb R\). Then \(F'(z;d)=-1<0\), but \(z+td=-t\notin X\) for every \(t>0\). Therefore ambient strict descent alone cannot ensure acceptance of a constrained boosting line search; the direction must be feasible for all sufficiently small steps or the method must use a feasibility safeguard.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A strict ambient descent direction may point immediately outside the feasible set, leaving no admissible boosting step.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: F'(z;d)<0,\qquad\{t>0:z+td\in X\}=\varnothing.
knowledge_statements.title: Ambient Descent Does Not Ensure a Feasible Boosting Ray

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Criticality of Vanishing-Displacement Boosted-DCA Cluster Points
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Cluster-point result for boosted DCA when its underlying exact DCA displacement vanishes.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F=g-h\), where \(g,h\) are proper closed convex functions. Suppose \(y^k\in\partial h(x^k)\), \(z^k\in\arg\min_x\{g(x)-\langle y^k,x\rangle\}\), and \(d^k=z^k-x^k\to0\). If \(x^{k_j}\to\bar x\), \(\{y^{k_j}\}\) is bounded, and \(g,h\) are finite and continuous on a neighborhood of \(\bar x\), then some subsequence satisfies \(y^{k_{j_\ell}}\to\bar y\in\partial g(\bar x)\cap\partial h(\bar x)\). Hence \(\bar x\) is critical for the selected DC decomposition.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A boosted-DCA cluster point is decomposition-critical when the underlying DCA displacement vanishes and the selected subgradients remain bounded.
assumptions_latex: \(g,h\) are proper closed convex and finite and continuous near \(\bar x\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \exists\bar y\in\partial g(\bar x)\cap\partial h(\bar x).

notation.meaning: ordinary-DCA displacement used as the boosting direction
cluster point of the selected convex subgradients

knowledge_statements.title: Criticality of Vanishing-Displacement Boosted-DCA Cluster Points
Boosted DCA
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Classical DCA step followed by safeguarded extrapolation along its displacement.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Starting from \(x^k\), compute a DCA point \(z^k\) by selecting \(y^k\in\partial h(x^k)\) and minimizing \(g(x)-\langle y^k,x\rangle\). Set \(d^k=z^k-x^k\). If \(d^k=0\), stop; otherwise choose the largest trial \(\lambda_k\) in \(\{\bar\lambda\beta^j:j=0,1,\ldots\}\) satisfying feasibility and
\[
F(z^k+\lambda_k d^k)\leq F(z^k)-\alpha\lambda_k^2\lVert d^k\rVert^2,
\]
where \(\alpha>0\), \(\bar\lambda>0\), and \(0<\beta<1\). Set \(x^{k+1}=z^k+\lambda_kd^k\) and return the last iterate when the stopping criterion holds.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: After a standard DCA update, extrapolate farther along the DCA displacement using backtracking that enforces additional objective decrease.
assumptions_latex: Trial points remain in the effective domain, and backtracking finds an acceptable step.
The DCA subproblem is solved exactly.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F(x^{k+1})\leq F(z^k)-\alpha\lambda_k^2\lVert d^k\rVert^2\).

notation.meaning: DCA displacement used as the boosting direction.

source_refs.locator: 2.5.1 Unconstrained problems: Armijo line search p. 89

source_witnesses.locator: 2.5.1 Unconstrained problems: Armijo line search p. 89

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The scheme resembles a boosted DCA variant, but the cited generic Armijo section does not support the specific extrapolation direction, quadratic decrease test, or hypotheses ensuring backtracking acceptance.

knowledge_statements.title: Line-Search DCA
knowledge_statements.scope_note: DCA globalization by backtracking over a descent direction derived from a convex model.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
At \(x^k\), construct a DCA trial point \(z^k\) and a direction \(d^k\) such that \(F'(z^k;d^k)<0\). Given \(0<\sigma<1\), \(0<\beta<1\), and \(\bar t>0\), choose the first \(t_k=\bar t\beta^j\) satisfying feasibility and
\[
F(z^k+t_kd^k)\leq F(z^k)+\sigma t_k F'(z^k;d^k).
\]
Set \(x^{k+1}=z^k+t_kd^k\). Stop when the direction or a stationarity residual is below tolerance. When the directional derivative is available and negative, sufficiently small trial steps satisfy the Armijo test.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Globalize a DCA trial point by backtracking along a verified descent direction until an Armijo decrease condition holds.
assumptions_latex: \(F=g-h\) is directionally differentiable along all tested rays.
The DCA trial point and a feasible strict descent direction are available.
Objective values and the required directional derivative can be evaluated.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The accepted update satisfies \(F(x^{k+1})<F(z^k)\) whenever \(t_k>0\) and \(F'(z^k;d^k)<0\).

notation.meaning: One-sided directional derivative of F at z along d.

source_refs.locator: 2.5.1 Unconstrained problems: Armijo line search p. 89
5.5 Splitting Methods with Line Search p. 429

source_witnesses.locator: 2.5.1 Unconstrained problems: Armijo line search p. 89
5.5 Splitting Methods with Line Search p. 429

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The Armijo statement is valid for an available strict descent direction, but the cited generic line-search sources do not establish how such a direction arises in this DCA variant.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Finite-Memory Nonmonotone Line-Search DCA
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Proposed nonmonotone globalization using a recent objective envelope.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(z^k\) be a DCA trial point and let \(d^k\) satisfy \(F'(z^k;d^k)<0\). For \(M\geq0\), define \(R_k=\max\{F(z^i):\max(0,k-M)\leq i\leq k\}\), and backtrack until \[F(z^k+t_kd^k)\leq R_k+\sigma t_kF'(z^k;d^k).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The proposal applies a generic finite-memory nonmonotone Armijo envelope to an unspecified DCA-derived descent direction.
assumptions_latex: \(F\) is directionally differentiable along tested rays.
All sufficiently small trial steps are feasible.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: F(z^k+t_kd^k)<R_k\quad\text{for every accepted nonzero step}.
knowledge_statements.title: Finite-Memory Nonmonotone Line-Search DCA

intermediate_metadata.reason: No new line-search record is accepted. The proposed finite-memory rule is a generic nonmonotone Armijo template with no verified DCA-specific direction construction or source, so it is deferred. The leaf still requires a canonical DCA line-search algorithm and its convergence theory. Boosting, inertia, restart controls, and quasi-DC model searches were excluded as adjacent scopes.

children.title: Extrapolated DCA
children.top_down_role: DCA variants using extrapolated trial information or iterates.

knowledge_statements.title: Extrapolated DCA
knowledge_statements.scope_note: DCA evaluated at an extrapolated base point with a safeguarded acceptance rule.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Given \(x^{k-1},x^k\), choose \(\beta_k\geq0\) and form \(v^k=x^k+\beta_k(x^k-x^{k-1})\). Select \(y^k\in\partial h(v^k)\) and compute
\[
z^{k+1}\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{x}\{g(x)-\langle y^k,x\rangle\}.
\]
Accept \(x^{k+1}=z^{k+1}\) when a prescribed descent or Lyapunov test holds; otherwise set \(\beta_k=0\), recompute from \(v^k=x^k\), and accept the resulting classical DCA point. Stop when successive iterates or a DC-stationarity residual meet tolerance. The zero-extrapolation fallback ensures that every accepted iteration is at least a safeguarded DCA step.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Apply DCA from an extrapolated base point, but reject unstable extrapolation and fall back to the classical update.
assumptions_latex: Every convex DCA subproblem used by the acceptance or fallback branch attains its minimum.
The safeguard accepts the zero-extrapolation DCA step.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Each iteration accepts either the extrapolated update or a classical DCA fallback obtained with \(\beta_k=0\).

notation.meaning: Candidate DCA point generated from the extrapolated base.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: No source identifies this safeguarded extrapolated-DCA variant, and the unspecified descent or Lyapunov acceptance test prevents verification of its exact mathematical form.

children.title: Inertial DCA
children.top_down_role: DCA variants incorporating momentum-like dependence on prior iterates.

knowledge_statements.title: Inertial DCA
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Representative inertial DCA adding a momentum covector to the convex subproblem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Given \(x^{k-1},x^k\), choose \(\gamma_k\geq0\), select \(y^k\in\partial h(x^k)\), and compute
\[
x^{k+1}\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{x}\left\{g(x)-\left\langle y^k+\gamma_k(x^k-x^{k-1}),x\right\rangle+\frac{\rho}{2}\lVert x-x^k\rVert^2\right\},
\]
where \(\rho>0\). Stop when the step and stationarity residual meet prescribed tolerances. The update obeys \(0\in\partial g(x^{k+1})-y^k-\gamma_k(x^k-x^{k-1})+\rho(x^{k+1}-x^k)\). Setting \(\gamma_k=0\) recovers proximal DCA; admissible momentum bounds must be chosen to preserve the method's descent or Lyapunov condition.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Insert a momentum term based on the previous displacement into a proximal DCA subproblem; zero momentum recovers proximal DCA.
assumptions_latex: \(\rho>0\), and each inertial subproblem is proper and attains its minimum.
The momentum sequence satisfies the stability restriction associated with the selected Lyapunov test.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(0\in\partial g(x^{k+1})-y^k-\gamma_k(x^k-x^{k-1})+\rho(x^{k+1}-x^k)\), with proximal DCA recovered at \(\gamma_k=0\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The optimality inclusion follows from the displayed subproblem, but no source confirms this inertial variant or supplies the momentum restriction needed for its claimed stability regime.

children.title: Acceleration Stability Regimes
children.top_down_role: Parameter or structural regimes governing stable use of extrapolation or inertia.

knowledge_statements.title: Acceleration Stability Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sufficient acceptance regime for inertial or extrapolated DCA steps.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F=g-h\), where \(g,h:\mathbb{R}^n\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) are proper closed convex functions. Given consecutive iterates, form \(z^k=x^k+\beta_k(x^k-x^{k-1})\), with \(0\leq\beta_k\leq\bar\beta<1\), and compute a DCA candidate \(u^{k+1}\) from \(y^k\in\partial h(z^k)\) by minimizing \(g(x)-\langle y^k,x\rangle\). The accelerated step is in a stability regime whenever it is accepted only if \[F(u^{k+1})+c\lVert u^{k+1}-z^k\rVert^2\leq F(x^k)\] for some fixed \(c>0\); otherwise the method must revert to a nonaccelerated accepted DCA step.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Acceleration is stable under bounded inertia and a sufficient-decrease test, with rejection followed by an ordinary DCA step.
assumptions_latex: \(g\) and \(h\) are proper closed convex functions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F(x^{k+1})\leq F(x^k)-c\lVert x^{k+1}-z^k\rVert^2\) for every accepted accelerated step.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: No citation supports this particular extrapolation rule, sufficient-decrease test, constant range, or mandatory fallback. The condition fits the leaf, but its characterization as a stability regime is variant-dependent.

children.title: DCA Restart Mechanisms
children.top_down_role: Policies that reset acceleration, memory, or auxiliary algorithmic state.

knowledge_statements.title: DCA Restart Mechanisms
knowledge_statements.scope_note: State-reset mechanism for a globalized accelerated DCA iteration.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(F=g-h\), maintain \((x^{k-1},x^k,\beta_k)\). Form the accelerated trial point \(z^k=x^k+\beta_k(x^k-x^{k-1})\) and its DCA trial \(u^{k+1}\). If a prescribed restart trigger is true, set \(z^k:=x^k\), \(\beta_k:=0\), discard \(u^{k+1}\), and recompute \(x^{k+1}\) from \(y^k\in\partial h(x^k)\) as a minimizer of \(g(x)-\langle y^k,x\rangle\). Otherwise accept the safeguarded accelerated trial. Stop when the selected DCA stationarity residual is at most \(\varepsilon\); output the latest accepted iterate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A restart discards a failed accelerated trial, resets inertia to zero, and recomputes an ordinary DCA step.
assumptions_latex: Every recomputed convex subproblem has a solution.
A restart trigger and stationarity tolerance \(\varepsilon\geq0\) are specified.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: On every restart iteration, \(\beta_k=0\) and the accepted update is an unaccelerated DCA update from \(x^k\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithmic kind fits the leaf, but no source identifies this reset-and-recompute mechanism as a DCA restart method. The restart trigger, safeguarded acceptance rule, and stationarity residual are unspecified and variant-dependent.

children.title: DCA Safeguard Mechanisms
children.top_down_role: Acceptance controls protecting descent, feasibility, or stability.

knowledge_statements.title: DCA Safeguard Mechanisms
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Objective-based safeguard selecting between accelerated and baseline DCA candidates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At iteration \(k\), compute an accelerated DCA candidate \(u^{k+1}\) and a baseline DCA candidate \(v^{k+1}\) from \(x^k\). Given \(c>0\), accept \(u^{k+1}\) if \[F(u^{k+1})\leq F(x^k)-c\lVert u^{k+1}-x^k\rVert^2.\] If this test fails, set \(x^{k+1}=v^{k+1}\), provided \(F(v^{k+1})\leq F(x^k)\); otherwise reject both candidates and retain \(x^{k+1}=x^k\). Stop when an accepted step or a chosen stationarity residual is at most the prescribed tolerance, and output the last accepted point.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The safeguard accepts acceleration only with sufficient decrease, otherwise using a descending baseline DCA step or retaining the current iterate.
assumptions_latex: \(F=g-h\) is finite at all tested candidates.
A baseline DCA candidate can be computed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F(x^{k+1})\leq F(x^k)\) for every safeguarded iteration.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: No citation supports the proposed two-candidate safeguard or its decrease test. The stopping sentence also compares an accepted step, which is a point or event, directly with a tolerance; a precise step norm or residual would have to be defined from a source.

children.title: Restart Trigger Regimes
children.top_down_role: Structural signals used to distinguish routine progress from restart-worthy behavior.

knowledge_statements.title: Restart Trigger Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Common logical regimes triggering restart of an accelerated DCA step.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(d^k=x^k-x^{k-1}\), let \(u^{k+1}\) be the accelerated candidate, and let \(r_k\geq0\) be a stationarity residual. A restart trigger may be defined by the disjunction \[F(u^{k+1})>F(x^k)-c\lVert u^{k+1}-x^k\rVert^2\quad\text{or}\quad \langle u^{k+1}-x^k,d^k\rangle>0\quad\text{or}\quad r_k>\eta r_{k-1},\] where \(c>0\) and \(0<\eta<1\). These clauses respectively encode failed sufficient decrease, adverse direction alignment, and inadequate residual contraction. When any enabled clause holds, inertia is reset before recomputation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Restart occurs when sufficient decrease fails, the accelerated direction is adversely aligned, or the stationarity residual contracts too slowly.
assumptions_latex: Objective values and residuals are evaluable at tested points.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If any enabled trigger holds, the next recomputation uses zero inertia.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition kind matches the leaf, but the three-clause disjunction appears to combine distinct restart heuristics without evidence that they form one recognized DCA trigger regime. The alignment sign and residual-contraction test require variant-specific sourcing.

knowledge_statements.title: Absolute-Error Inexact DCA
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Inexact DCA with summable absolute subproblem optimality errors.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F=g-h\) with proper closed convex \(g,h:\mathbb{R}^n\to(-\infty,+\infty]\), choose \(x^0\in\operatorname{dom}g\cap\operatorname{dom}h\), and prescribe \(\varepsilon_k\geq0\). At iteration \(k\), select \(y^k\in\partial h(x^k)\) and compute \(x^{k+1}\) satisfying \[g(x^{k+1})-\langle y^k,x^{k+1}\rangle\leq\inf_x\{g(x)-\langle y^k,x\rangle\}+\varepsilon_k.\] Stop when a prescribed stationarity residual is at most the tolerance; otherwise continue. Under the absolute-error regime \(\sum_{k=0}^{\infty}\varepsilon_k<\infty\), the accumulated subproblem error is finite.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Each convex DCA subproblem is solved within an additive error, and the absolute errors are required to be summable.
assumptions_latex: Each convex subproblem has finite infimum.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x^{k+1}\) is an \(\varepsilon_k\)-minimizer of the convex DCA subproblem and the total absolute error is finite.

notation.meaning: selected subgradient of the concave component

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The additive epsilon-minimizer rule and summability statement are mathematically coherent and algorithm is the appropriate kind, but no authoritative source is supplied to establish this as the intended absolute-error inexact DCA variant.

knowledge_statements.title: Relative-Error Inexact DCA
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Inexact DCA controlled relative to the current step size.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F=g-h\), choose \(x^0\in\operatorname{dom}g\cap\operatorname{dom}h\), and fix \(\sigma\geq0\). Given \(x^k\), select \(y^k\in\partial h(x^k)\) and compute \(x^{k+1}\) together with \(e^{k+1}\) such that \[e^{k+1}\in\partial g(x^{k+1})-y^k,\qquad \lVert e^{k+1}\rVert\leq\sigma\lVert x^{k+1}-x^k\rVert.\] Stop when the step and residual satisfy prescribed tolerances; otherwise repeat. Thus the convex-subproblem optimality residual vanishes proportionally whenever the DCA step vanishes.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The convex-subproblem residual is bounded by a fixed multiple of the current DCA step length.
assumptions_latex: Required subgradients and an admissible inexact point exist.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{dist}(y^k,\partial g(x^{k+1}))\leq\sigma\lVert x^{k+1}-x^k\rVert\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The residual inequality is internally coherent and implies the displayed distance bound, but no source establishes this particular step-relative residual criterion as the intended relative-error inexact DCA algorithm.

knowledge_statements.title: Bundle-Based DCA
knowledge_statements.scope_note: DCA using cutting-plane models for an unavailable convex component.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F=g-h\), and suppose a first-order oracle supplies \((h(z),s)\) with \(s\in\partial h(z)\). Maintain a bundle \(B_k=\{(z_i,h(z_i),s_i)\}_{i\in I_k}\) and the polyhedral minorant \[h_k(x)=\max_{i\in I_k}\{h(z_i)+\langle s_i,x-z_i\rangle\}.\] Select an active \(y^k\in\partial h_k(x^k)\), compute a trial point by minimizing \(g(x)-\langle y^k,x\rangle\), query the oracle there, and accept or reject it using a prescribed actual-versus-predicted decrease test. Add the new cut, delete cuts according to the bundle policy, and stop at the chosen stationarity tolerance.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A bundle of subgradient cuts models a convex DC component; DCA trials are accepted by comparing actual and predicted decrease.
assumptions_latex: The oracle returns exact values and subgradients of \(h\).
Each modeled convex subproblem is solvable.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(h_k(x)\leq h(x)\) for every \(x\), and every generated cut remains a valid global affine minorant.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The cutting-plane minorant is valid, but no source supports the overall procedure as a bundle-based DCA variant. The actual-versus-predicted decrease test is not defined, so the algorithm cannot be reliably identified or reproduced.

knowledge_statements.title: Oracle-Based DC Methods
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Generic DCA iteration under value-subgradient oracle access.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F=g-h\), where access to each convex component is through an oracle \(\mathcal O_q(x)=(q(x),s_q)\) with \(s_q\in\partial q(x)\). Starting from \(x^0\), query \(\mathcal O_h(x^k)\) to obtain \(y^k\), then use calls to \(\mathcal O_g\) and a convex solver to produce \(x^{k+1}\) satisfying \[g(x^{k+1})-\langle y^k,x^{k+1}\rangle\leq\inf_x\{g(x)-\langle y^k,x\rangle\}+\varepsilon_k.\] Terminate when an oracle-computable stationarity residual is at most \(\tau\), and return the latest query point.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Oracle-based DC methods obtain component values and subgradients on demand and solve each convexized subproblem to a stated tolerance.
assumptions_latex: The oracles return valid values and subgradients.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Each update is an \(\varepsilon_k\)-accurate DCA update using only oracle information and convex-subproblem computations.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Algorithm is a suitable knowledge kind, but the generic value-subgradient oracle model, epsilon-accurate convex solve, and claimed oracle-computable stationarity test are not tied to a cited DC method. The residual must be specified and sourced.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Block-Coverage Assumptions Are Not Equivalent
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Separation of infinite visitation from bounded-window essentially cyclic coverage.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For selections S_k\subseteq\{1,\ldots,m\}, infinite visitation requires \#\{k:i\in S_k\}=\infty for every i. Bounded-window coverage requires L\ge1 such that \bigcup_{j=k}^{k+L-1}S_j=\{1,\ldots,m\} for every k. Bounded-window coverage implies infinite visitation, but the converse fails: selecting block 2 only at k=2^r and block 1 otherwise visits both infinitely often while leaving unbounded gaps for block 2.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Essentially cyclic coverage is strictly stronger than visiting every block infinitely often.
assumptions_latex: There are at least two blocks.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{bounded-window coverage}\Longrightarrow\text{infinite visitation},\quad\text{but not conversely}.
knowledge_statements.title: Block-Coverage Assumptions Are Not Equivalent

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Coordinatewise Minimality Does Not Imply Directional Stationarity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of blockwise stopping tests for coupled nonsmooth DC objectives.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define \[F(x_1,x_2)=|x_1-x_2|-\tfrac12(|x_1|+|x_2|).\] Holding either coordinate at zero gives F(t,0)=F(0,t)=\tfrac12|t|, so the origin minimizes each one-coordinate restriction. Along d=(1,1), however, \[F'(0;d)=F(d)=-1<0.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The origin is optimal on each coordinate axis but has a strict diagonal descent direction.
assumptions_latex: The blocks are the two scalar coordinates.
The stopping test checks exact one-block restrictions only.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{coordinatewise minimality at }0\not\Rightarrow F'(0;d)\ge0\ \forall d.

notation.meaning: coupled strict-descent direction missed by one-block tests

knowledge_statements.title: Coordinatewise Minimality Does Not Imply Directional Stationarity

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Selected-Block DCA Descent
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Objective decrease from exact minimization of a selected-block convexized subproblem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let F=g-h on X=X_1\times\cdots\times X_m, choose y\in\partial h(x), and let z_{-S}=x_{-S} while \[z_S\in\arg\min_{u_S}\{g(u_S,x_{-S})-\langle y_S,u_S\rangle\}.\] Then F(z)\le F(x). If the selected-block objective is \sigma-strongly convex, then \[F(x)-F(z)\ge\frac\sigma2\|z_S-x_S\|^2.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An exact convexized block update cannot increase the DC objective, and blockwise strong convexity gives quantitative decrease.
assumptions_latex: g and h are proper convex functions and y\in\partial h(x).
The selected-block convex subproblem attains its minimum.
For the quantitative conclusion, the selected-block objective is \sigma-strongly convex under the displayed convention.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: F(z)\le F(x),\qquad F(x)-F(z)\ge(\sigma/2)\|z_S-x_S\|^2\text{ under block strong convexity}.

notation.meaning: iterate after exact selected-block convexized minimization

knowledge_statements.title: Selected-Block DCA Descent

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Uniform Block Curvature Implies Square-Summable Updates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Consequence of quantitative selected-block DCA descent for a lower-bounded objective.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose exact selected-block updates satisfy F(x^k)-F(x^{k+1})\ge(\sigma/2)\|x^{k+1}_{S_k}-x^k_{S_k}\|^2 for fixed \sigma>0, only blocks in S_k change, and \inf_kF(x^k)>-\infty. Then \sum_{k=0}^\infty\|x^{k+1}_{S_k}-x^k_{S_k}\|^2<\infty and \|x^{k+1}-x^k\|\to0.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Uniform selected-block curvature and a lower objective bound force square-summable updates and asymptotic regularity.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \sum_k\|x^{k+1}_{S_k}-x^k_{S_k}\|^2<\infty,\qquad\|x^{k+1}-x^k\|\to0.

notation.meaning: block set selected at iteration k

knowledge_statements.title: Uniform Block Curvature Implies Square-Summable Updates

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Simultaneous Blockwise DCA Fixed-Point Certificate
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Coordinatewise stopping certificate using one common selected subgradient.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F=g-h\) on \(X_1\times\cdots\times X_m\), and let \(y\in\partial h(x)\). If, for every block \(i\), \[x_i\in\arg\min_{u_i\in X_i}\{g(u_i,x_{-i})-\langle y_i,u_i\rangle\},\] then every exact one-block DCA update using this same \(y\) leaves \(x\) unchanged. This certifies a simultaneous blockwise fixed point, not generally full DC criticality or directional stationarity.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Unchanged one-block convexized updates certify a blockwise DCA fixed point but not full stationarity.
assumptions_latex: g,h\text{ are proper convex on the product space}.
Each displayed block problem is minimized at x_i.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \forall i,\ x_i\in\arg\min_{u_i\in X_i}\{g(u_i,x_{-i})-\langle y_i,u_i\rangle\}\Longrightarrow x\text{ is fixed by every one-block update using }y.

notation.meaning: block i of the common selected subgradient

knowledge_statements.title: Simultaneous Blockwise DCA Fixed-Point Certificate

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Parallel Exact Block Minimizers Can Increase the Objective
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary separating sequential block DCA from unsafeguarded Jacobi updates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(g(x)=\tfrac12x^\top Ax\), \(h=0\), and let \(A\in\mathbb R^{3\times3}\) have diagonal entries \(1\) and off-diagonal entries \(c\in(1/2,1)\). Then \(A\succ0\). At \(x=(1,1,1)\), independently minimizing each coordinate while freezing the other two gives the parallel candidate \(z=-2c(1,1,1)\). Since \(g(z)=4c^2g(x)>g(x)\), simultaneous application of individually exact block minimizers can increase the objective, although each sequential coordinate minimization is nonincreasing.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a coupled positive-definite quadratic, three exact coordinate minimizers computed from the same old iterate can collectively increase the objective.
assumptions_latex: All coordinate candidates are computed from the same old iterate and applied simultaneously.
knowledge_statements.title: Parallel Exact Block Minimizers Can Increase the Objective
Block-Coordinate DCA
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Cyclic or selected-block DCA for product-space DC objectives.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X=X_1\times\cdots\times X_m\) and \(F=g-h\) on \(X\). Given \(x^k\), select a nonempty block set \(S_k\subseteq\{1,\ldots,m\}\) and \(y^k\in\partial h(x^k)\). Keep \(x_j^{k+1}=x_j^k\) for \(j\notin S_k\), and choose the remaining blocks to minimize \[g(x_{S_k},x^k_{-S_k})-\langle y^k_{S_k},x_{S_k}\rangle.\] Stop when no block update exceeds the prescribed stationarity tolerance; otherwise repeat. A valid coverage rule requires every block to occur infinitely often, or within every fixed-length iteration window.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At each iteration DCA minimizes the convexized objective over selected blocks while freezing all others, with every block updated regularly.
assumptions_latex: \(g,h\) are proper closed convex on the product space.
Every selected-block subproblem has a minimizer.
The block-selection rule covers every block regularly.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Only blocks in \(S_k\) change, and their update minimizes the current blockwise convex DCA subproblem.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The block-update algorithm fits the leaf, but no source supports this precise convexization and block-subgradient convention. Infinite visitation and bounded-window coverage are different access assumptions and should not be presented as a single equivalent rule without variant-specific evidence.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Persistent Conditional Sampling Gives Infinite Visits
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Probabilistic access guarantee for finitely many randomized DCA blocks.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(I_k\in\{1,\ldots,m\}\) be adapted to histories \(\mathcal F_k\). If for each block \(i\) there is \(p_i>0\) such that \[\mathbb P(I_k=i\mid\mathcal F_k)\ge p_i\quad\text{almost surely for every }k,\] then \[\mathbb P(I_k=i\ \text{infinitely often})=1\qquad(i=1,\ldots,m).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A uniform positive conditional sampling probability forces every block to be selected infinitely often almost surely.
assumptions_latex: \mathbb P(I_k=i\mid\mathcal F_k)\ge p_i>0\text{ almost surely for every }i,k.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \mathbb P(I_k=i\ \mathrm{i.o.})=1\quad\forall i.

notation.meaning: random block selected at iteration k
uniform positive lower bound for selecting block i

knowledge_statements.title: Persistent Conditional Sampling Gives Infinite Visits

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Conditional Expected Descent from Random Block Updates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: One-step expected decrease from deterministic candidate block decreases.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Condition on \(\mathcal F_k\). For each block \(i\), let \(z^{k,i}\) be its exact convexized DCA candidate and suppose \[F(x^k)-F(z^{k,i})\ge\frac{\sigma_i}{2}\|z_i^{k,i}-x_i^k\|^2.\] If \(q_{k,i}=\mathbb P(I_k=i\mid\mathcal F_k)\) and \(x^{k+1}=z^{k,I_k}\), then \[\mathbb E[F(x^{k+1})\mid\mathcal F_k]\le F(x^k)-\frac12\sum_iq_{k,i}\sigma_i\|z_i^{k,i}-x_i^k\|^2.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Random selection weights the deterministic candidate-block decreases by their conditional sampling probabilities.
assumptions_latex: The displayed quantitative decrease holds for every block.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \mathbb E[F(x^{k+1})\mid\mathcal F_k]\le F(x^k)-\frac12\sum_iq_{k,i}\sigma_i\|z_i^{k,i}-x_i^k\|^2.

notation.meaning: conditional probability of selecting block i
candidate iterate after updating block i

knowledge_statements.title: Conditional Expected Descent from Random Block Updates

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Importance-Weighted Sampled Block Residual
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Unbiased diagnostic for a full block-displacement residual under randomized access.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Condition on \(\mathcal F_k\). Let \(r_{k,i}=\|z_i^{k,i}-x_i^k\|^2\) be the squared exact candidate displacement for block \(i\), and let \(q_{k,i}=\mathbb P(I_k=i\mid\mathcal F_k)>0\). Then \[\widehat R_k=\frac{r_{k,I_k}}{q_{k,I_k}}\] satisfies \[\mathbb E[\widehat R_k\mid\mathcal F_k]=\sum_{i=1}^m r_{k,i}=:R_k.\] Moreover, \(R_k=0\) exactly when every candidate block update is zero. A single small realization of \(\widehat R_k\) is not a deterministic stationarity certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Importance weighting makes one sampled block displacement an unbiased estimate of the full squared block-update residual, but one sample cannot certify stationarity.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \mathbb E[\widehat R_k\mid\mathcal F_k]=R_k,\qquad R_k=0\Longleftrightarrow r_{k,i}=0\ \forall i.

notation.meaning: squared exact candidate displacement for block i
full sum of squared candidate block displacements

knowledge_statements.title: Importance-Weighted Sampled Block Residual

knowledge_statements.statement_title: One Sample Cannot Certify the Full Block Residual
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sharp failure of a single sampled block-displacement observation as a deterministic stopping certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let there be two candidate block residuals \(r_1=0\) and \(r_2=1\), sampled with probabilities \(q_1,q_2>0\). The full residual is \(R=r_1+r_2=1\), but on the event \(I=1\), which has probability \(q_1>0\), both the raw sampled residual \(r_I\) and the importance-weighted residual \(r_I/q_I\) equal zero. Hence one zero or small sampled observation does not certify that \(R\) is zero or small.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A sampled block can have zero displacement even while another block has a nonzero displacement, so one sample cannot certify a small full residual.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \mathbb P\!\left(\frac{r_I}{q_I}=0\ \text{and}\ R=1\right)=q_1>0.

notation.meaning: squared candidate displacement for block i
full sum of candidate block residuals

knowledge_statements.title: One Sample Cannot Certify the Full Block Residual

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Expected Best-Iterate Block-Residual Bound
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sublinear expected complexity from uniform randomized block descent.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Under the conditional-descent assumptions above, additionally suppose \(\mathbb E[F(x^0)]<\infty\). Let \(p_{\min}=\min_i p_i\), \(\sigma_{\min}=\min_i\sigma_i\), and \(R_k=\sum_i r_{k,i}\). Then for every \(K\ge1\),
\[\min_{0\le k<K}\mathbb E[R_k]\le\frac{2\bigl(\mathbb E[F(x^0)]-F_{\inf}\bigr)}{Kp_{\min}\sigma_{\min}}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Uniform sampling and block curvature yield an order-one-over-K expected best-iterate bound for the full squared block-update residual.
assumptions_latex: The conditional expected-decrease inequality of Almost-Sure Decay of Full Candidate Block Residuals holds.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \min_{0\le k<K}\mathbb E[R_k]\le\frac{2(\mathbb E[F(x^0)]-F_{\inf})}{Kp_{\min}\sigma_{\min}}.

notation.meaning: full sum of squared exact candidate block displacements

knowledge_statements.title: Expected Best-Iterate Block-Residual Bound

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Almost-Sure Decay of Full Candidate Block Residuals
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Supermartingale consequence of persistent randomized block sampling and quantitative candidate descent.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(F(x^k)\) be integrable and satisfy \(F(x^k)\ge F_{\inf}>-\infty\) almost surely. Suppose
\[\mathbb E[F(x^{k+1})\mid\mathcal F_k]\le F(x^k)-\frac12\sum_{i=1}^m q_{k,i}\sigma_i r_{k,i},\]
where each \(r_{k,i}=\|z_i^{k,i}-x_i^k\|^2\) is nonnegative and \(\mathcal F_k\)-measurable, \(q_{k,i}\ge p_i>0\), and \(\sigma_i>0\). Then
\[\sum_{k=0}^{\infty}\sum_{i=1}^m q_{k,i}\sigma_i r_{k,i}<\infty\quad\text{almost surely},\]
and consequently \(r_{k,i}\to0\) almost surely for every block \(i\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Persistent positive sampling and integrable quantitative conditional descent force every exact candidate block displacement to vanish almost surely.
assumptions_latex: \(F(x^k)\) is integrable and \(F(x^k)\ge F_{\inf}>-\infty\) almost surely.
The displayed conditional expected-decrease inequality holds.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \sum_k\sum_i q_{k,i}\sigma_i r_{k,i}<\infty\ \text{a.s.},\qquad r_{k,i}\to0\ \text{a.s. for every }i.

notation.meaning: squared exact candidate displacement for block i
conditional probability of sampling block i

knowledge_statements.title: Almost-Sure Decay of Full Candidate Block Residuals
Randomized DCA
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Random block DCA with positive conditional selection probabilities.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F=g-h\) on \(X_1\times\cdots\times X_m\). At iteration \(k\), draw a block \(I_k\) conditionally on the history \(\mathcal F_k\), with \(\mathbb P(I_k=i\mid\mathcal F_k)\geq p_i>0\). Select \(y^k\in\partial h(x^k)\), retain \(x_j^{k+1}=x_j^k\) for \(j\neq I_k\), and compute \[x_{I_k}^{k+1}\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{u\in X_{I_k}}\bigl\{g(u,x^k_{-I_k})-\langle y^k_{I_k},u\rangle\bigr\}.\] Stop when a prescribed sampled or full stationarity test is met; output the last iterate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Randomized DCA updates one randomly selected block per iteration, with every block having uniformly positive conditional probability.
assumptions_latex: \(g,h\) are proper closed convex on the product space.
Each sampled block subproblem has a minimizer.
\(\mathbb P(I_k=i\mid\mathcal F_k)\geq p_i>0\) for every block.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every block is sampled infinitely often with probability one under the stated uniform positivity rule.

notation.meaning: random block selected at iteration k

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The positive conditional probability condition does support almost-sure infinite sampling for finitely many blocks, but no source establishes the stated update as the intended randomized DCA variant. The sampled-or-full stationarity test is also undefined.

children.title: Incremental DCA
children.top_down_role: DCA variants accessing component information incrementally.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Stale Aggregates Need Not Be Current Subgradients
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary distinguishing memory-based incremental updates from ordinary full-batch DCA.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(H=m^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^m h_i\) and store \(y_i^k\in\partial h_i(x^{\tau_i^k})\) at possibly stale points. In general, \[\bar y^k:=m^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^m y_i^k\notin\partial H(x^k).\] For example, take \(m=2\), \(h_1(x)=h_2(x)=x^2/2\), \(x^k=0\), \(x^{\tau_1^k}=1\), and \(x^{\tau_2^k}=0\). Then \(\bar y^k=1/2\), whereas \(\partial H(0)=\{0\}\). Thus the ordinary current-subgradient DCA descent argument does not apply without additional memory-error control or a variant-specific Lyapunov analysis.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An average of subgradients stored at different past iterates need not be a subgradient at the current iterate.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \bar y^k\notin\partial H(x^k)\text{ can occur even for smooth quadratic components}.

notation.meaning: iteration at which the stored component subgradient was evaluated

knowledge_statements.title: Stale Aggregates Need Not Be Current Subgradients

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Current-Stationarity Bound with Stale Smooth Components
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A posteriori certificate for memory-based incremental finite-sum DC states with smooth subtracted components.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F=g-H\), where \(H=m^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^m h_i\), each \(h_i\) is differentiable with \(L_i\)-Lipschitz gradient, and \(y_i^k=\nabla h_i(x^{\tau_i^k})\). Set \(\bar y^k=m^{-1}\sum_i y_i^k\), \(r_k=\operatorname{dist}(\bar y^k,\partial g(x^k))\), and \(e_k=m^{-1}\sum_iL_i\|x^k-x^{\tau_i^k}\|\). Then \[\operatorname{dist}\bigl(0,\partial g(x^k)-\nabla H(x^k)\bigr)\le r_k+e_k.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Adding a smoothness-based staleness bound to the stored-aggregate residual gives a valid current-stationarity certificate.
assumptions_latex: g\text{ is proper closed convex and }\partial g(x^k)\ne\varnothing.
h_i\text{ is differentiable with }L_i\text{-Lipschitz gradient for every }i.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{dist}(0,\partial g(x^k)-\nabla H(x^k))\le r_k+e_k.

notation.meaning: residual computed with the stored aggregate
upper bound on the stale-gradient error

knowledge_statements.title: Current-Stationarity Bound with Stale Smooth Components

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Bounded Delays and Vanishing Steps Eliminate Smooth Staleness
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Condition making the incremental smooth-staleness certificate asymptotically exact.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose each \(h_i\) has \(L_i\)-Lipschitz gradient, \(0\le k-\tau_i^k\le q\), and \(\|x^{j+1}-x^j\|\to0\). Then \[\|x^k-x^{\tau_i^k}\|\le\sum_{j=k-q}^{k-1}\|x^{j+1}-x^j\|\to0,\] so \(e_k=m^{-1}\sum_iL_i\|x^k-x^{\tau_i^k}\|\to0\). If the stored-aggregate residual \(r_k\to0\), then \(\operatorname{dist}(0,\partial g(x^k)-\nabla H(x^k))\to0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Bounded component delays and vanishing increments eliminate smooth stale-gradient error.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: e_k\to0,\qquad r_k\to0\Longrightarrow\operatorname{dist}(0,\partial g(x^k)-\nabla H(x^k))\to0.
knowledge_statements.title: Bounded Delays and Vanishing Steps Eliminate Smooth Staleness

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Consistent Timestamp Refresh Invariant
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Minimal state invariant for a memory-based incremental DCA implementation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose the stored state satisfies \(y_i^k\in\partial h_i(x^{\tau_i^k})\) for every component. If component \(I_k\) is refreshed at \(x^k\), choose \(y_{I_k}^{k+1}\in\partial h_{I_k}(x^k)\) and set \(\tau_{I_k}^{k+1}=k\); for \(i\ne I_k\), set \((y_i^{k+1},\tau_i^{k+1})=(y_i^k,\tau_i^k)\). Then \(y_i^{k+1}\in\partial h_i(x^{\tau_i^{k+1}})\) for every \(i\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Refreshing a stored component requires updating its evaluation timestamp while leaving all other subgradient–timestamp pairs unchanged.
assumptions_latex: The refreshed subgradient is evaluated at the current point \(x^k\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: y_i^{k+1}\in\partial h_i(x^{\tau_i^{k+1}})\quad\forall i.

notation.meaning: timestamp of the stored component-i evaluation

knowledge_statements.title: Consistent Timestamp Refresh Invariant
Incremental DCA
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Memory-based incremental DCA for finite sums of convex components.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F(x)=g(x)-m^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^m h_i(x)\), with convex \(g,h_i\). Store \(y_i^k\in\partial h_i(x^{\tau_i^k})\). At iteration \(k\), choose \(I_k\), query \(h_{I_k}\) at \(x^k\), set \(y_{I_k}^{k+1}\in\partial h_{I_k}(x^k)\), and retain \(y_i^{k+1}=y_i^k\) for \(i\neq I_k\). Then compute \[x^{k+1}\in\operatorname*{argmin}_x\left\{g(x)-\left\langle m^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^m y_i^{k+1},x\right\rangle\right\}.\] Stop at the prescribed stationarity tolerance; output the latest iterate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Incremental DCA refreshes one component subgradient, retains the others in memory, and solves a convex problem using their average.
assumptions_latex: The aggregate convex subproblem has a minimizer.
The access rule visits every component infinitely often.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Each iteration requires one fresh component-subgradient evaluation while using the stored aggregate \(m^{-1}\sum_i y_i^{k+1}\).

notation.meaning: iteration of the stored component evaluation

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The incremental memory update is plausible and algorithm is the correct kind, but no source supports this exact finite-sum decomposition and refresh rule. The stored-point indices tau_i^k are introduced but not updated when a component is refreshed, leaving the algorithmic state incomplete.

children.title: Finite-Sum DCA
children.top_down_role: DCA variants specialized to objectives with finitely many component terms.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Qualified Component-Subgradient Aggregation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact condition making componentwise selections valid for the full-batch finite-sum DCA model.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(H=m^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^m h_i\), where every \(h_i:\mathbb R^d\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) is proper, closed, and convex. If \(\bigcap_{i=1}^m\operatorname{ri}(\operatorname{dom}h_i)\neq\varnothing\), then for every \(x\in\bigcap_i\operatorname{dom}h_i\), \[\partial H(x)=\frac1m\sum_{i=1}^m\partial h_i(x).\] Hence selections \(y_i\in\partial h_i(x)\) satisfy \(m^{-1}\sum_i y_i\in\partial H(x)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under the common-relative-interior qualification, averaging current component subgradients produces a valid aggregate subgradient for full-batch finite-sum DCA.
assumptions_latex: h_i\text{ is proper, closed, and convex for every }i.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: y_i\in\partial h_i(x)\ \forall i\quad\Longrightarrow\quad m^{-1}\sum_i y_i\in\partial H(x).
knowledge_statements.title: Qualified Component-Subgradient Aggregation

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Aggregate DC Criticality Residual
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Full-batch decomposition-relative stationarity certificate after qualified component aggregation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let F=G-H with proper closed convex G,H and define r(x)=\operatorname{dist}(\partial G(x),\partial H(x)). Under the common-relative-interior qualification for H=m^{-1}\sum_i h_i, choose y_i\in\partial h_i(x), set \bar y=m^{-1}\sum_i y_i\in\partial H(x), and choose u\in\partial G(x). Then r(x)\le\|u-\bar y\|. In particular, u=\bar y certifies \partial G(x)\cap\partial H(x)\ne\varnothing.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The discrepancy between a positive-component subgradient and a qualified aggregate subtracted-component subgradient upper-bounds the DC criticality residual; equality certifies decomposition-relative criticality.
assumptions_latex: G,H\text{ are proper closed convex and their subdifferentials are nonempty at }x.
H=m^{-1}\sum_i h_i\text{ satisfies the common-relative-interior qualification}.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: r(x)\le\left\|u-\frac1m\sum_i y_i\right\|,\qquad u=\frac1m\sum_i y_i\Longrightarrow\partial G(x)\cap\partial H(x)\ne\varnothing.

notation.meaning: distance between the convex subdifferential sets of G and H

knowledge_statements.title: Aggregate DC Criticality Residual

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Full-Batch Finite-Sum DCA Descent
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Descent after qualified aggregation of current component subgradients.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F=G-H\), where \(H=m^{-1}\sum_i h_i\), and suppose the exact convex sum rule makes \(\bar y^k=m^{-1}\sum_i y_i^k\in\partial H(x^k)\) for \(y_i^k\in\partial h_i(x^k)\). If \(x^{k+1}\) minimizes \(G(x)-\langle\bar y^k,x\rangle\), then \(F(x^{k+1})\le F(x^k)\). If this convexized objective is \(\sigma\)-strongly convex, then \[F(x^k)-F(x^{k+1})\ge\frac{\sigma}{2}\|x^{k+1}-x^k\|^2.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Qualified full-batch aggregation produces an ordinary DCA descent step, with quadratic decrease under strong convexity.
assumptions_latex: G\text{ and all }h_i\text{ are proper closed convex}.
The exact convex sum rule applies at x^k.
The convexized subproblem attains its minimum.
For the quantitative bound, the convexized objective is \sigma-strongly convex.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: F(x^{k+1})\le F(x^k),\qquad F(x^k)-F(x^{k+1})\ge(\sigma/2)\|x^{k+1}-x^k\|^2\text{ under strong convexity}.

notation.meaning: strong-convexity modulus of the convexized subproblem

knowledge_statements.title: Full-Batch Finite-Sum DCA Descent

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Full-Batch Component-Oracle Cost
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Per-iteration component-access cost distinguishing finite-sum DCA from its incremental sibling.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: In a full-batch finite-sum DCA iteration that selects one \(y_i^k\in\partial h_i(x^k)\) for every \(i=1,\ldots,m\), exactly \(m\) component-subgradient selections are required before forming \(\bar y^k=m^{-1}\sum_i y_i^k\). If selection \(i\) costs \(C_i^k\) and vector aggregation costs \(O(md)\) in \(\mathbb R^d\), the pre-subproblem work is \(\sum_iC_i^k+O(md)\). This excludes the cost of solving the aggregate convexized subproblem.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A full-batch iteration accesses every subtracted component and incurs linear-in-component aggregation work before its convex solve.
assumptions_latex: Every component subgradient is freshly evaluated at \(x^k\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: N_{\mathrm{comp}}(k)=m,\qquad W_{\mathrm{pre}}(k)=\sum_{i=1}^mC_i^k+O(md).

notation.meaning: cost of selecting a subgradient of component i at iteration k
work before the aggregate convex-subproblem solve

knowledge_statements.title: Full-Batch Component-Oracle Cost

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Criticality of Qualified Full-Batch Finite-Sum DCA Cluster Points
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Cluster-point theorem retaining the fresh componentwise aggregation that distinguishes full-batch finite-sum DCA.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(G\) and \(h_1,\ldots,h_m\) be proper closed convex functions, set \(H=m^{-1}\sum_i h_i\), and assume the exact convex sum rule applies at every iterate under consideration. Choose \(y_i^k\in\partial h_i(x^k)\), set \(\bar y^k=m^{-1}\sum_i y_i^k\in\partial H(x^k)\), and compute \(x^{k+1}\in\arg\min_x\{G(x)-\langle\bar y^k,x\rangle\}\). Suppose \(\|x^{k+1}-x^k\|\to0\). If \(x^{k_j}\to\bar x\), \(\{\bar y^{k_j}\}\) is bounded, and \(G,H\) are finite and continuous near \(\bar x\), then some subsequence satisfies \(\bar y^{k_{j_\ell}}\to\bar y\in\partial G(\bar x)\cap\partial H(\bar x)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A qualified fresh full-batch finite-sum DCA cluster point is decomposition-critical when consecutive iterates coalesce and aggregate subgradients remain bounded.
assumptions_latex: \(G,h_1,\ldots,h_m\) are proper closed convex and the exact sum rule gives \(m^{-1}\sum_i\partial h_i(x^k)=\partial H(x^k)\).
\(y_i^k\in\partial h_i(x^k)\), \(\bar y^k=m^{-1}\sum_i y_i^k\), and \(\bar y^k\in\partial G(x^{k+1})\).
\(x^{k_j}\to\bar x\), \(\{\bar y^{k_j}\}\) is bounded, and \(G,H\) are finite and continuous near \(\bar x\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \exists\bar y\in\partial G(\bar x)\cap\partial H(\bar x).

notation.meaning: fresh average of all component subgradients

knowledge_statements.title: Criticality of Qualified Full-Batch Finite-Sum DCA Cluster Points
Finite-Sum DCA
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Full-batch DCA for a finite-sum DC decomposition.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \[F(x)=\frac1m\sum_{i=1}^m\bigl(g_i(x)-h_i(x)\bigr)=G(x)-H(x),\] where all \(g_i,h_i\) are proper closed convex. Starting from \(x^0\in\operatorname{dom}G\cap\operatorname{dom}H\), choose \(y_i^k\in\partial h_i(x^k)\), form \(y^k=m^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^m y_i^k\), and compute \[x^{k+1}\in\operatorname*{argmin}_x\left\{m^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^m g_i(x)-\langle y^k,x\rangle\right\}.\] Stop when the step or an aggregate stationarity residual is at most the prescribed tolerance, and output \(x^{k+1}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Finite-sum DCA evaluates every concave-component subgradient, averages them, and solves the resulting full convexized subproblem.
assumptions_latex: The full convexized subproblem has a minimizer.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(y^k\in\partial H(x^k)\), so the update is a full-batch DCA step for \(F=G-H\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The full-batch construction fits the leaf, but the conclusion that the average selected subgradients belongs to the subdifferential of H requires an applicable convex subdifferential sum rule. No source or qualification condition is supplied to validate that claim for extended-valued components.

children.title: Component-Access Regimes
children.top_down_role: Full, partial, cyclic, or sampled access patterns for finite component collections.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Component-Query Accounting
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Oracle-cost distinction among full, single-component, and mini-batch access, independent of convergence.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If querying one component value and subgradient costs one component-oracle call, iteration k costs |B_k| calls and \[Q_T=\sum_{k=1}^T|B_k|.\] Full access has Q_T=nT, single-component access has Q_T=T, and fixed-size b mini-batches have Q_T=bT. These identities count queries only and do not imply equal accuracy after T iterations.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Cumulative component-query cost is the sum of batch sizes; query savings alone do not determine optimization accuracy.
assumptions_latex: Each newly queried component has unit oracle cost.
Cached information is not charged as a new query.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Q_T=\sum_{k=1}^T|B_k|.
knowledge_statements.title: Component-Query Accounting

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Uniform Conditional Sampling Ensures Persistent Component Access
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sufficient stochastic-access condition for almost-sure infinite visitation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let B_k be adapted to a filtration (\mathcal F_k). If for every component i there is p_i>0 such that \[\mathbb P(i\in B_k\mid\mathcal F_{k-1})\ge p_i\quad\text{almost surely for every }k,\] then every component is selected infinitely often almost surely.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A uniform positive conditional inclusion probability prevents any finite-sum component from being abandoned permanently.
assumptions_latex: B_k is sampled using information available through the current iteration.
The displayed conditional lower bound holds almost surely.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \mathbb P(i\in B_k\ \text{infinitely often for every }i)=1.

notation.meaning: uniform conditional inclusion-probability lower bound for component i

knowledge_statements.title: Uniform Conditional Sampling Ensures Persistent Component Access

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Pointwise Positive Sampling Probability Does Not Ensure Infinite Access
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Distinction between iterationwise positivity and persistent stochastic coverage.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For two components, independently include component 2 at iteration k with probability 2^{-k}, and otherwise access component 1. Every iteration gives component 2 positive inclusion probability, but \sum_{k=1}^\infty2^{-k}<\infty, so component 2 is selected only finitely often almost surely.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A component may have positive sampling probability at every iteration yet be visited only finitely often almost surely.
assumptions_latex: The component-2 inclusion events are independent.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: (\forall k,\ \mathbb P(2\in B_k)>0)\not\Rightarrow\mathbb P(2\in B_k\text{ infinitely often})=1.
knowledge_statements.title: Pointwise Positive Sampling Probability Does Not Ensure Infinite Access

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Full, Incremental, and Stochastic Component Access
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Access taxonomy separated from coverage and persistence assumptions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a finite component collection indexed by I=\{1,\ldots,n\}, let B_k\subseteq I be the nonempty set of components newly queried at iteration k. Full access means B_k=I. Deterministic incremental access means B_k is selected by a deterministic rule and may be a proper subset. Stochastic access means B_k is a random subset adapted to the algorithmic history. Infinite visitation, bounded-window coverage, and positive conditional inclusion bounds are additional assumptions on these regimes, not parts of their definitions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An access regime records whether every component, a deterministic subset, or a random subset is newly queried; persistence and coverage are separate assumptions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: B_k=I\text{ defines full access; deterministic }B_k\text{ defines incremental access; random }B_k\text{ defines stochastic access}.

notation.meaning: components newly queried at iteration k

knowledge_statements.title: Full, Incremental, and Stochastic Component Access

assumptions_latex: \(F(x)=n^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^n(g_i(x)-h_i(x))\), where every \(g_i,h_i\) is proper closed convex.
All queried component values and subgradients are well defined at the current iterate.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(B_k=\{1,\ldots,n\}\) gives full finite-sum access, deterministic proper subsets give incremental access, and randomly sampled subsets give stochastic access.

notation.meaning: component indices accessed at iteration k

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-sum access classification for incremental and stochastic DCA variants.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the finite-sum DC objective \(F(x)=n^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^n(g_i(x)-h_i(x))\), a component-access regime specifies a nonempty index set \(B_k\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}\) at iteration \(k\). Full access means \(B_k=\{1,\ldots,n\}\). Incremental access means that \(B_k\) is selected by a deterministic schedule, commonly with every index visited infinitely often. Stochastic access means that \(B_k\) is sampled from a prescribed distribution, commonly with every index having positive sampling probability. Only components indexed by \(B_k\) may be newly evaluated or subdifferentiated at iteration \(k\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A component-access regime determines whether each DCA iteration queries every finite-sum term, a scheduled subset, or a randomly sampled subset.
knowledge_statements.title: Component-Access Regimes

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition fits the Component-Access Regimes leaf and is mathematically plausible, but no inspectable citation supports the precise distinctions, coverage convention, positive-probability convention, or restriction on newly queried components.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Unbiased Sampled Subgradients Do Not Ensure Pathwise Descent
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Elementary obstruction to transferring deterministic DCA descent to a single-sample stochastic update.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(a\) take values \(\pm1\) with equal probability, let \(G(x)=x^2/2\), and let \(H(x,a)=ax\). Then \(F(x)=G(x)-\mathbb E[H(x,a)]=x^2/2\), whose minimizer is \(x_0=0\). For \(\lambda>0\), the sampled proximal step \[x_1=\operatorname*{argmin}_x\left\{\frac{x^2}{2}-a_0x+\frac{(x-x_0)^2}{2\lambda}\right\}=\frac{\lambda a_0}{1+\lambda}\] satisfies \[F(x_1)=\frac{\lambda^2}{2(1+\lambda)^2}>F(x_0)\quad\text{almost surely}.\] Thus conditional unbiasedness of the sampled affine term does not imply pathwise descent of the expected objective.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An unbiased sampled affine model can move a stochastic DCA iterate away from an exact minimizer and increase the expected objective on every realization.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: F(x_1)>F(x_0)\quad\text{almost surely}.

notation.meaning: sample used by the first stochastic update

knowledge_statements.title: Unbiased Sampled Subgradients Do Not Ensure Pathwise Descent

assumptions_latex: \(G:\mathbb R^d\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) is proper closed convex and \(H(\cdot,\xi)\) is convex almost surely.
The conditional estimator satisfies \(\mathbb E[y_k\mid x_k]\in\partial \mathbb E[H(x_k,\xi)]\).
\(\lambda_k>0\), and the displayed convex subproblem attains a minimizer.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Each iteration replaces the concave expectation term by a sampled affine minorant and computes \(x_{k+1}\) from a convex problem.

notation.meaning: sampled subgradient estimator at iteration k

knowledge_statements.scope_note: A proximal stochastic DCA form with sampled concave-part subgradients.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Given \(x_0\in\operatorname{dom}G\), at iteration \(k\) sample \(\xi_k\), choose \(y_k\in\partial_x H(x_k,\xi_k)\), and compute
\[x_{k+1}\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in\mathbb R^d}\left\{G(x)-\langle y_k,x\rangle+\frac{1}{2\lambda_k}\|x-x_k\|^2\right\}.\]
The method stops when a prescribed iteration, sampling, or stationarity budget is reached and returns the last iterate or a specified averaged/random iterate. Mini-batch DCA replaces \(y_k\) by the average of subgradients from independently sampled observations.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Stochastic DCA samples a subgradient of the convex term being subtracted, then minimizes the resulting proximal convex surrogate.
knowledge_statements.title: Stochastic DCA

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind fits the Stochastic DCA container, but the displayed step uses a single sampled subgradient while the assumptions separately impose a conditional expectation property without conditions ensuring interchange with the expected subdifferential. A source is needed to identify the intended stochastic-DCA variant and its estimator requirements.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Constrained DCA Fixed-Point Certificate
knowledge_statements.scope_note: First-order certificate supplied by an unchanged exact constrained update.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose \(x\in C\), \(y\in\partial h(x)\), and \(x\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{z\in C}\{g(z)-\langle y,z\rangle\}\). Under the convex subdifferential sum rule, \[0\in\partial g(x)-y+N_C(x)\subseteq\partial g(x)-\partial h(x)+N_C(x).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An unchanged constrained-DCA update supplies a normal-cone DC-criticality certificate.
assumptions_latex: The convex sum rule \(\partial(g+\delta_C)(x)=\partial g(x)+N_C(x)\) is valid at \(x\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: 0\in\partial g(x)-\partial h(x)+N_C(x).

notation.meaning: Convex normal cone to the feasible set.

knowledge_statements.title: Constrained DCA Fixed-Point Certificate

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Feasible Descent and Proximal Sufficient Decrease
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Descent properties of exact DCA over a fixed convex feasible set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(x_k\in C\), choose \(y_k\in\partial h(x_k)\), and let \(x_{k+1}\) minimize \[g(x)-\langle y_k,x\rangle+\frac{1}{2\lambda_k}\|x-x_k\|^2\quad\text{over }C,\qquad\lambda_k>0.\] Then \(x_{k+1}\in C\) and \[g(x_k)-h(x_k)-g(x_{k+1})+h(x_{k+1})\ge\frac{1}{2\lambda_k}\|x_{k+1}-x_k\|^2.\] Without the proximal term, the objective remains nonincreasing.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Exact convex-feasible-set DCA preserves feasibility and decreases the objective; proximal regularization quantifies the decrease.
assumptions_latex: \(x_k\in C\cap\operatorname{dom}g\cap\operatorname{dom}h\), \(y_k\in\partial h(x_k)\), and the convex subproblem attains a minimizer.
knowledge_statements.title: Feasible Descent and Proximal Sufficient Decrease

assumptions_latex: \(C\subseteq\mathbb R^d\) is nonempty, closed, and convex.
The convex subproblem attains a minimizer at every iteration.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every computed iterate satisfies \(x_{k+1}\in C\), and its update is an ordinary DCA step for \((g+\delta_C)-h\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: indicator-function formulation of constrained DCA
knowledge_statements.scope_note: DCA for a DC objective over a fixed convex feasible set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For
\[\min_{x\in C}\;g(x)-h(x),\]
choose an initial point \(x_0\in C\cap\operatorname{dom}g\cap\operatorname{dom}h\). At iteration \(k\), select \(y_k\in\partial h(x_k)\) and compute
\[x_{k+1}\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in C}\{g(x)-\langle y_k,x\rangle\}.\]
Equivalently, this is unconstrained DCA applied to \((g+\delta_C)-h\). A proximal variant adds \(\|x-x_k\|^2/(2\lambda_k)\) with \(\lambda_k>0\). The method returns an iterate satisfying the chosen termination test.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Convex-feasible-set DCA linearizes the subtracted convex term and minimizes the resulting convex surrogate over the original convex set.
knowledge_statements.title: Convex-Feasible-Set DCA

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The indicator-function formulation and algorithm kind fit the leaf, but the assumptions do not ensure that a subgradient of h exists at every generated iterate. No citation is supplied for the precise constrained-DCA template or its well-definedness conditions.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Feasible-Iterate Invariance
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Feasibility preservation under affine-minorant inner convexification.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \[C_k=\bigcap_i\{x:g_i(x)-h_i(x_k)-\langle v_{i,k},x-x_k\rangle\le0\},\qquad v_{i,k}\in\partial h_i(x_k),\] one has \(C_k\subseteq C:=\{x:g_i(x)-h_i(x)\le0\ \forall i\}\). Moreover, \(x_k\in C\) implies \(x_k\in C_k\). Hence any update chosen from \(C_k\) remains feasible and the next centered inner model is nonempty.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A feasible linearization center belongs to its convex inner model, and every point in that model is feasible for the original DC constraints.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: x_k\in C\Longrightarrow x_k\in C_k\subseteq C.

notation.meaning: Convex inner approximation at iteration k.

knowledge_statements.title: Feasible-Iterate Invariance

assumptions_latex: Each constraint has the form \(g_i(x)-h_i(x)\le 0\), with \(g_i,h_i\) convex.
At the current point \(x_k\), choose \(v_{i,k}\in\partial h_i(x_k)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The linearized feasible set is convex and is contained in the original DC-feasible set.

notation.meaning: subgradient used to linearize the subtracted constraint component
convex inner approximation at iteration k

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Inner convexification of differentiable or nonsmooth DC inequality constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For each DC constraint \(g_i(x)-h_i(x)\le0\), convexity gives
\[h_i(x)\ge h_i(x_k)+\langle v_{i,k},x-x_k\rangle.\]
The method replaces the constraint by
\[g_i(x)-h_i(x_k)-\langle v_{i,k},x-x_k\rangle\le0.\]
Thus it solves the chosen convex objective surrogate over
\[C_k=\bigcap_i\{x:g_i(x)-h_i(x_k)-\langle v_{i,k},x-x_k\rangle\le0\}.\]
Because every surrogate left-hand side majorizes \(g_i-h_i\), one has \(C_k\subseteq\{x:g_i(x)-h_i(x)\le0\ \forall i\}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Each subtracted convex constraint term is affine-minorized, producing a convex inner approximation of the original DC-feasible region.
knowledge_statements.title: DC-Constraint Linearization Methods

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The convex inner-approximation formula, containment direction, and algorithm kind fit the terminal container. The claim is standard, but the record has no source with a section, theorem, definition, or page locator.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Fixed-Penalty Descent and Criticality
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Basic guarantees of exact DCA applied to one fixed penalized DC decomposition.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix \(\rho>0\) and write \(P_\rho=G_\rho-H_\rho\). If \(y_k\in\partial H_\rho(x_k)\) and \(x_{k+1}\in\operatorname*{argmin}_x\{G_\rho(x)-\langle y_k,x\rangle\}\), then \[P_\rho(x_{k+1})\le P_\rho(x_k).\] If \(x_{k+1}=x_k=x\), then \(\partial G_\rho(x)\cap\partial H_\rho(x)\ne\varnothing\). This certifies criticality of the penalized objective, not feasibility of the original constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At a fixed penalty, exact DCA decreases the penalized objective; an unchanged iterate certifies only penalized DC criticality.
assumptions_latex: \(G_\rho,H_\rho\) are proper convex functions on a compatible effective domain.
The selected subgradient and exact convex minimizer exist.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: P_\rho(x_{k+1})\le P_\rho(x_k),\qquad x_{k+1}=x_k\Longrightarrow\partial G_\rho(x_k)\cap\partial H_\rho(x_k)\ne\varnothing.
knowledge_statements.title: Fixed-Penalty Descent and Criticality

assumptions_latex: \(f=g_0-h_0\) and \(c_i=g_i-h_i\), with all component functions proper convex.
The penalized convex DCA subproblem attains a minimizer.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Penalty DCA applies DCA to \(P_{\rho_k}(x)=f(x)+\rho_k\sum_i[c_i(x)]_+\), using \([c_i]_+=\max\{g_i,h_i\}-h_i\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Positive-part penalty DCA for DC inequality constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Define
\[P_\rho(x)=g_0(x)-h_0(x)+\rho\sum_{i=1}^m[g_i(x)-h_i(x)]_+.\]
Using \([g_i-h_i]_+=\max\{g_i,h_i\}-h_i\), write \(P_\rho=G_\rho-H_\rho\), where \(G_\rho=g_0+\rho\sum_i\max\{g_i,h_i\}\) and \(H_\rho=h_0+\rho\sum_i h_i\). Starting from \(x_0\), choose \(y_k\in\partial H_{\rho_k}(x_k)\) and minimize \(G_{\rho_k}(x)-\langle y_k,x\rangle\), optionally with a proximal term. Increase \(\rho_k\) according to a prescribed violation test and return the final penalized iterate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Penalty DCA converts DC inequalities into positive-part penalties, decomposes the penalized objective into convex components, and performs standard DCA updates.
knowledge_statements.title: Penalty DCA

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The positive-part DC decomposition is algebraically correct and the algorithm kind fits Penalty DCA. A source is required for the stated penalty-update method, and the assumptions should establish a common effective domain on which the penalized convex components and subgradients are well defined.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Finite-Penalty Feasibility Failure
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Proposed example is mathematically correct but canonically belongs to general exact-penalty failure theory.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \(\min_x -x\) subject to \(x^2\le0\). For finite \(\rho>0\), \(P_\rho(x)=-x+\rho x^2\) has the infeasible minimizer \(1/(2\rho)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A finite positive-part penalty may have an infeasible minimizer for an irregular constraint.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname*{argmin}P_\rho=\{1/(2\rho)\}\not\subseteq\{0\}.
knowledge_statements.title: Finite-Penalty Feasibility Failure

intermediate_metadata.reason: This leaf owns the positive-part DC decomposition, fixed-penalty DCA update, descent, and penalized fixed-point certificate, with external penalty schedules allowed but not given unsupported universal guarantees. General exact-penalty theorems and the irregular squared-constraint counterexample were excluded to their canonical penalty-theory homes; fixed convex sets, inner constraint linearization, and elastic restoration were excluded as sibling scopes.

children.title: Feasibility-Restoration DCA
children.top_down_role: Constrained DCA variants equipped with phases or submodels targeting recovered feasibility.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Minimax Violation Form of Restoration
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equivalent scalar form of minimum-common-slack restoration.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: With \(a_{i,k}(x)=g_i(x)-h_i(x_k)-\langle v_{i,k},x-x_k\rangle\), the minimum-common-slack value is \[r_k=\min_x\max_{1\le i\le m}[a_{i,k}(x)]_+.\] Thus restoration minimizes the l-infinity aggregate of the current convexified violations; a secondary displacement criterion may select among minimizers without changing \(r_k\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Common-slack restoration is exactly minimization of the maximum positive convexified constraint violation.
assumptions_latex: Every \(a_{i,k}\) is proper convex on a common nonempty effective domain.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: r_k=\min_x\max_i[a_{i,k}(x)]_+.
knowledge_statements.title: Minimax Violation Form of Restoration

assumptions_latex: DC inequalities are \(g_i(x)-h_i(x)\le 0\), where each \(g_i,h_i:\mathbb R^d\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) is proper convex.
The minimum-slack restoration problem attains an optimal solution.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The optimal slack satisfies \(r_k=0\) exactly when the linearized constraint system is feasible; otherwise \(r_k>0\) is its minimum common violation.

notation.meaning: current point at which the subtracted constraint components are linearized
restored point selected from the minimum-slack solutions

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: minimum-common-slack restoration for convexified constraints
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Restoration by first minimizing common violation of the linearized DC constraints; displacement regularization may only be used as a secondary tie-breaker if the stated zero-slack equivalence is retained.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Given \(x_k\), choose \(v_{i,k}\in\partial h_i(x_k)\) and solve
\[r_k=\min_{x\in\mathbb R^d,\,r\ge 0}\left\{r: g_i(x)-h_i(x_k)-\langle v_{i,k},x-x_k\rangle\le r\ \text{for every }i\right\}.\]
Choose \(x_k^R\) from the minimizers, optionally by minimizing \(\|x-x_k\|^2\) over the minimum-slack solution set. Then \(r_k=0\) if and only if the unrelaxed linearized constraint system is feasible. If \(r_k=0\), \(x_k^R\) can initialize the next convexified DCA subproblem; if \(r_k>0\), the method may update the model or invoke a prescribed restoration-failure test.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Feasibility-restoration DCA first minimizes the common slack needed by the convexified constraints; zero optimal slack is equivalent to feasibility of the unrelaxed linearized system.
knowledge_statements.title: Feasibility-Restoration DCA

children.title: Elastic DCA
children.top_down_role: Constrained DCA variants using elastic variables or softened constraint representations.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Elimination of Elastic Slacks
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equivalent positive-part form of the elastic convexified subproblem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(a_{i,k}(x)=g_i(x)-h_i(x_k)-\langle v_{i,k},x-x_k\rangle\). For fixed \(x\), minimizing \(\sum_i s_i\) subject to \(s_i\ge0\) and \(a_{i,k}(x)\le s_i\) gives \(s_i=[a_{i,k}(x)]_+\). Consequently, eliminating \(s\) adds \(\rho_k\sum_i[a_{i,k}(x)]_+\) to the convex objective.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Elastic variables can be eliminated exactly, yielding an l1 positive-part penalty on convexified constraint violations.
assumptions_latex: Every \(a_{i,k}(x)\) is well defined at the candidate point.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \min_{s\ge0,\,a_{i,k}(x)\le s_i}\rho_k\sum_i s_i=\rho_k\sum_i[a_{i,k}(x)]_+.
knowledge_statements.title: Elimination of Elastic Slacks

assumptions_latex: The objective is \(g_0-h_0\), and constraints are \(g_i-h_i\le0\), with convex components.
Subgradients \(v_{i,k}\in\partial h_i(x_k)\) and \(y_k\in\partial h_0(x_k)\) are selected.
\(\rho_k>0\), and the elastic subproblem attains a minimizer.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Elastic variables keep the convexified subproblem feasible whenever its remaining domain is nonempty, while \(\rho_k\sum_i s_i\) penalizes violation.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: DCA subproblems softened by penalized nonnegative constraint slacks.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
At iteration \(k\), compute
\[(x_{k+1},s_{k+1})\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{x,\,s\ge0}\left\{g_0(x)-\langle y_k,x\rangle+\rho_k\sum_{i=1}^m s_i+\frac{1}{2\lambda_k}\|x-x_k\|^2\right\}\]
subject to
\[g_i(x)-h_i(x_k)-\langle v_{i,k},x-x_k\rangle\le s_i,\qquad i=1,\ldots,m.\]
Here \(\lambda_k>0\) is optional. Stop when the selected stationarity and violation tests hold; otherwise update \(\rho_k\), with persistent positive slack signaling failure to recover feasibility.
