knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Elastic DCA adds penalized nonnegative slacks to convexified constraints so the iteration can proceed when the unsoftened surrogate is infeasible.
knowledge_statements.title: Elastic DCA

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind and elastic-slack construction fit the leaf, but the displayed subproblem uses lambda_k without introducing it in the assumptions or notation, and calling the displayed proximal term optional does not specify the nonproximal formula. A source is also needed for the precise update and stopping rules.

children.title: Restoration Failure Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Regimes where feasibility recovery or elastic relaxation cannot restore the targeted constrained model.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Elastic Slacks Cannot Repair Hard-Domain Incompatibility
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary of the claim that elastic variables make a convexified subproblem feasible.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let the elastic subproblem retain the hard set \(C=\{0\}\) and the softened convex inequality \(g(x)\le s\), where \(g=\delta_{\{1\}}\) and \(s\ge0\). Since \(C\cap\operatorname{dom}g=\varnothing\), no finite slack makes the subproblem feasible. Elastic variables repair finite inequality violations but not an empty intersection of hard effective domains.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Elastic slacks do not guarantee subproblem feasibility when the remaining hard domains are incompatible.
assumptions_latex: Extended-valued convex functions retain value \(+\infty\) outside their effective domains.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: C\cap\operatorname{dom}g=\varnothing\Longrightarrow\{(x,s):x\in C,\ s\ge0,\ g(x)\le s\}=\varnothing.

notation.meaning: Indicator of the singleton containing one.

knowledge_statements.title: Elastic Slacks Cannot Repair Hard-Domain Incompatibility

assumptions_latex: Consider the DC constraint \(g(x)-h(x)\le 0\) on \(\mathbb R\), where \(g(x)=x^2+1\) and \(h(x)=2x^2\).
Linearize the convex function \(h\) at \(x_0=0\) using \(h'(0)=0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The original constraint is feasible for \(|x|\ge 1\), whereas its affine-minorant inner linearization at \(x_0=0\) is infeasible.

notation.meaning: point at which the subtracted convex constraint component is linearized

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: explicit one-dimensional counterexample to feasibility of an inner linearization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A feasible DC constraint can have an empty affine-minorant inner approximation when linearized at an infeasible point.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(g(x)=x^2+1\) and \(h(x)=2x^2\). The original constraint is
\[g(x)-h(x)=1-x^2\le 0,\]
so its feasible set is \(( -\infty,-1]\cup[1,+\infty )\). At \(x_0=0\), the affine minorant of \(h\) is
\[h(x_0)+h'(x_0)(x-x_0)=0.\]
The resulting inner linearization is
\[x^2+1\le 0,\]
which is infeasible. Thus feasibility of the original DC constraint does not guarantee feasibility of every inner convexification, particularly when the model is centered at an infeasible point.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A feasible DC constraint can have an empty convex inner approximation: for this example the original feasible set contains all points with absolute value at least one, but linearization at zero yields an impossible inequality.
knowledge_statements.title: Restoration Failure Boundaries

children.title: Directional-Stationarity-Seeking DC Methods
children.top_down_role: Methods designed to strengthen decomposition-relative criticality toward intrinsic directional targets.

children.title: Active-Piece Selection
children.top_down_role: Choice among locally active convex pieces within directional-stationarity-seeking methods.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Directionally Active Piece Characterization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Direction-dependent refinement of active-piece selection for a finite maximum of differentiable convex pieces.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(p(x)=\max_{i\in I}\phi_i(x)\), where \(I\) is finite, and define \(I(x;d)=\operatorname*{argmax}_{i\in I(x)}\langle\nabla\phi_i(x),d\rangle\). Then \[p'(x;d)=\max_{i\in I(x)}\langle\nabla\phi_i(x),d\rangle.\] Consequently, a value-active selection \(i_x\in I(x)\) realizes \(p'(x;d)\) exactly when \(i_x\in I(x;d)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A value-active piece realizes the derivative in a tested direction exactly when its gradient has maximal directional slope among the active pieces.
assumptions_latex: Every \(\phi_i\) is differentiable and convex near \(x\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(i_x\in I(x)\) represents \(p'(x;d)\) if and only if \(i_x\in I(x;d)\).

notation.meaning: indices active in value at x
active indices maximizing directional slope along d

knowledge_statements.title: Directionally Active Piece Characterization

assumptions_latex: \(p(x)=\max_{i\in I}\phi_i(x)\), where \(I\) is finite and every \(\phi_i\) is differentiable and convex.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\partial p(x)=\operatorname{conv}\{\nabla\phi_i(x):i\in I(x)\}\), so an active-piece choice supplies an extreme candidate subgradient.

notation.meaning: indices attaining the pointwise maximum at x

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Selection calculus for finite maxima of smooth convex pieces.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(p(x)=\max_{i\in I}\phi_i(x)\), define the active set
\[I(x)=\{i\in I:\phi_i(x)=p(x)\}.\]
An active-piece selection at \(x\) is any index \(i_x\in I(x)\). Its selected gradient \(\nabla\phi_{i_x}(x)\) belongs to \(\partial p(x)\), and
\[\partial p(x)=\operatorname{conv}\{\nabla\phi_i(x):i\in I(x)\}.\]
When \(I(x)\) is not a singleton, different active selections may generate different DCA models and search directions even though they represent the same maximum value.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An active-piece selection chooses a maximizing smooth component; its gradient is a valid subgradient of the finite maximum.
knowledge_statements.title: Active-Piece Selection

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition kind fits Active-Piece Selection, and the finite-maximum subdifferential formula is correct under the stated finite differentiable convex-piece assumptions. No inspectable citation is supplied for the formula.

children.title: DC Decomposition Selection
children.top_down_role: Choice of DC representation used to generate a directional search model.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Effect of Common Convex Additions on the DCA Majorant
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact effect of a common convex addition on the DCA model, including affine invariance.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f=g-h\), choose \(y_k\in\partial h(x_k)\), and define \[M_k(x)=g(x)-h(x_k)-\langle y_k,x-x_k\rangle.\] For a convex \(q\), choose \(z_k\in\partial q(x_k)\) and use \(y_k+z_k\in\partial(h+q)(x_k)\) for the decomposition \((g+q)-(h+q)\). Its majorant is \[M_k^q(x)=M_k(x)+q(x)-q(x_k)-\langle z_k,x-x_k\rangle\ge M_k(x).\] If \(q\) is affine, the added term is identically zero; a nonlinear common addition generally changes the convex subproblem.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A common convex addition contributes its subgradient divergence to the DCA majorant; affine additions leave the model unchanged, while nonlinear additions generally alter it.
assumptions_latex: \(f=g-h\) on the fixed optimization domain, with proper convex components.
The augmented components \(g+q\) and \(h+q\) are proper on the optimization domain.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(M_k^q(x)=M_k(x)+q(x)-q(x_k)-\langle z_k,x-x_k\rangle\ge M_k(x)\), with equality for every \(x\) when \(q\) is affine.

notation.meaning: DCA convex majorant at iteration k
selected subgradient of the common convex addition

knowledge_statements.title: Effect of Common Convex Additions on the DCA Majorant

assumptions_latex: \(f\) admits at least one representation \(f=g-h\) with proper convex \(g,h\).
The selected decomposition is compatible with the domain and subproblem-solvability requirements of the chosen DCA variant.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Selecting \((g,h)\) fixes the convex majorization model \(g(x)-h(x_k)-\langle y_k,x-x_k\rangle\) for \(y_k\in\partial h(x_k)\).

notation.meaning: selected convex components of the DC representation
convex function added to both components

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: nonuniqueness of DC decompositions and induced DCA models
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Selection of a DC representation as part of the algorithmic model.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A DC decomposition selection for \(f\) chooses an ordered pair \((g,h)\) of proper convex functions satisfying \(f=g-h\) on the optimization domain. The choice is nonunique: for every convex \(q\) for which the sums are proper,
\[f=(g+q)-(h+q).\]
At an iterate \(x_k\), the selected pair determines the DCA majorant
\[M_k(x)=g(x)-h(x_k)-\langle y_k,x-x_k\rangle,\qquad y_k\in\partial h(x_k).\]
Consequently, equivalent decompositions can produce different convex subproblems, selected subgradients, and iterates.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: DC decomposition selection chooses the convex pair representing an objective; equivalent pairs can induce different DCA models and iterates.
knowledge_statements.title: DC Decomposition Selection

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition kind fits the decomposition-selection leaf, and adding a common convex function to both components preserves their difference where both representations are defined. A source and a precise optimization domain are needed to support the majorization-model and iterate-dependence claims without ambiguity from extended-valued domains.

children.title: Selection Compatibility
children.top_down_role: Compatibility between the chosen active piece and the chosen decomposition.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Compatible-Pair Set and Existence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Complete direction-dependent representation of compatible active pairs in a finite max-minus-max decomposition.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \[f(x)=\max_{i\in I}a_i(x)-\max_{j\in J}b_j(x),\] define \[I(x;d)=\operatorname*{argmax}_{i\in I(x)}\langle
abla a_i(x),dangle,\qquad J(x;d)=\operatorname*{argmax}_{j\in J(x)}\langle
abla b_j(x),dangle.\] The complete compatible-pair set is \[\mathcal C(x;d)=I(x;d)	imes J(x;d).\] It is nonempty for every \(d\), and every \((i,j)\in\mathcal C(x;d)\) satisfies \[f'(x;d)=\langle
abla a_i(x)-
abla b_j(x),dangle.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Compatible pairs are exactly the Cartesian product of the directionally maximizing active indices of the two maxima, and at least one exists for every direction.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal C(x;d)=I(x;d)\times J(x;d)\neq\varnothing\), and every pair in it realizes \(f'(x;d)\).

notation.meaning: active index pairs compatible with direction d

knowledge_statements.title: Compatible-Pair Set and Existence

assumptions_latex: \(f(x)=\max_{i\in I}a_i(x)-\max_{j\in J}b_j(x)\), with finite families of differentiable functions.
\(I(x)\) and \(J(x)\) are the corresponding active index sets.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A pair \((i,j)\in I(x)\times J(x)\) is compatible with \(d\) exactly when its selected directional slopes attain both active maxima.

notation.meaning: active indices for the first maximum
active indices for the second maximum

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: directional derivative calculus for finite maxima
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Direction-dependent compatibility of active pieces in a max-minus-max representation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For a direction \(d\), an active pair \((i,j)\in I(x)\times J(x)\) is selection-compatible with \(d\) when
\[\langle\nabla a_i(x),d\rangle=\max_{r\in I(x)}\langle\nabla a_r(x),d\rangle\]
and
\[\langle\nabla b_j(x),d\rangle=\max_{s\in J(x)}\langle\nabla b_s(x),d\rangle.\]
Under these two conditions,
\[f'(x;d)=\langle\nabla a_i(x)-\nabla b_j(x),d\rangle.\]
An arbitrary active pair need not be compatible with the same direction and therefore need not represent the directional derivative of \(f\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An active pair is compatible with a direction when each selected piece attains the relevant active directional maximum, thereby realizing the DC directional derivative.
knowledge_statements.title: Selection Compatibility

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The compatibility condition and directional-derivative identity are correct for finite maxima of differentiable functions, and the condition kind fits the leaf. The assumptions should explicitly require the regularity under which the finite-max directional derivative formula is invoked, consistent with the surrounding convex-piece calculus, and no source locator is supplied.

children.title: Degenerate Selection Regimes
children.top_down_role: Ties, unstable selections, and noninformative directional choices.

assumptions_latex: At \(x=0\), each absolute-value term has active affine pieces \(x\) and \(-x\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Opposite active selections yield the spurious slope \(2d\), although \(f'(0;d)=0\) for every direction \(d\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Tied active pieces can make independently chosen DC selections directionally incompatible.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let
\[f(x)=\max\{x,-x\}-\max\{x,-x\}=0.\]
At \(x=0\), both affine pieces are active in each maximum. Select the gradient \(1\) from the first maximum and the gradient \(-1\) from the second. Their difference is \(2\), so the selected pair predicts the directional slope \(2d\). Nevertheless,
\[f'(0;d)=0\qquad\text{for every }d\in\mathbb R.\]
Thus independent active-piece choices at a tied point can be incompatible with directional calculus; tie handling or direction-dependent joint selection is necessary when directional stationarity is sought.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At tied pieces, independent selections can produce a nonzero apparent slope for an identically zero DC function, invalidating directional conclusions.
knowledge_statements.title: Degenerate Selection Regimes

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The explicit tied-piece example is mathematically correct and the failure_boundary kind exactly fits the terminal container. It correctly shows that independently selected active gradients need not realize the directional derivative, but it has no inspectable citation.

assumptions_latex: \(F(x)=g(x)-h(x)\) on a nonempty closed convex set \(X\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\), where \(g\) and \(h\) are proper closed convex functions.
Near the current iterate \(x^k\), finitely many admissible local DC decompositions \(F=g_j-h_j\), \(j\in J_k\), are available.
Each selected convex subproblem attains a minimizer.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x^{k+1}\) is the trial point having the smallest accepted objective value, or \(x^k\) if no trial passes the acceptance test.

notation.meaning: finite index set of admissible decompositions at iteration k
subgradient selected from the concave component of decomposition j
trial point generated from decomposition j

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite enumeration of locally admissible DC decompositions for seeking directional stationarity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For each \(j\in J_k\), select \(y_j^k\in\partial h_j(x^k)\) and compute
\[
z_j^k\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in X}\bigl\{g_j(x)-\langle y_j^k,x\rangle\bigr\}.
\]
Retain the candidates satisfying a prescribed feasibility and descent test, forming \(A_k\subseteq J_k\). If \(A_k\neq\varnothing\), choose
\[
j_k\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{j\in A_k}F(z_j^k),\qquad x^{k+1}=z_{j_k}^k.
\]
If \(A_k=\varnothing\), return \(x^k\) with a no-accepted-decomposition status. Terminate only when every enumerated decomposition satisfies its specified stationarity or rejection test.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Enumerate admissible local DC decompositions, solve one convex model per decomposition, accept descent-producing trials, and select the accepted trial with smallest objective value.
knowledge_statements.title: Decomposition-Enumeration Methods

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm role fits the decomposition-enumeration leaf, and the variables are adequately introduced. However, no cited source supports this particular enumeration, acceptance, selection, and termination scheme; these choices are not a source-independent canonical DC algorithm.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Finite Extreme-Subgradient Enumeration Certificate
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Proposed finite certificate based on enumerating extreme subgradients of one fixed decomposition.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(f=g-h\) with finite convex \(g,h\) and \(\partial h(x)=\operatorname{conv}\{v_1,\ldots,v_m\}\), then \(f'(x;d)\ge0\) for all \(d\) is equivalent to \(v_\ell\in\partial g(x)\) for every \(\ell\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For one fixed DC decomposition with a polyhedral subdifferential, directional stationarity can be tested at its extreme subgradients.
assumptions_latex: \(g\) and \(h\) are finite convex functions on \(\mathbb R^n\).
\(\partial h(x)\) is generated by finitely many listed extreme points.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(f'(x;d)\ge0\) for all \(d\) if and only if \(v_\ell\in\partial g(x)\) for every \(\ell\).

notation.meaning: extreme points generating the subdifferential of h at x

review_flags: misplaced_claim: enumerates subgradients of one fixed decomposition rather than enumerating DC decompositions
knowledge_statements.title: Finite Extreme-Subgradient Enumeration Certificate

intermediate_metadata.reason: This leaf should own algorithms that enumerate genuinely distinct admissible DC decompositions. The seed does not establish a canonical family, and the Builder's extreme-subgradient certificate belongs primarily to directional-stationarity or subdifferential-inclusion theory, so it is deferred. Active-piece selection and positive-spanning polling remain excluded to sibling method families.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Fixed Positive-Spanning Polls Do Not Certify Nonsmooth Directional Stationarity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sharp boundary showing why positive spanning alone is insufficient for nonsmooth directional stationarity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \[F(x_1,x_2)=|x_1-x_2|-\tfrac12\max\{|x_1|,|x_2|\}\] and \(D=\{e_1,-e_1,e_2,-e_2\}\). The set \(D\) positively spans \(\mathbb R^2\), and for every \(d\in D\) and \(t>0\), \[F(td)=\tfrac12t>F(0).\] Nevertheless, for \(u=(1,1)\), \[F'(0;u)=F(u)=-\tfrac12<0.\] Thus unsuccessful polling over a fixed positive-spanning set does not certify directional stationarity of a nonsmooth DC function.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The four coordinate directions all increase a DC function at the origin, while an unpolled diagonal direction strictly decreases it.
assumptions_latex: Polling is restricted to \(D=\{\pm e_1,\pm e_2\}\).
The objective is the stated positively homogeneous DC function.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Absence of descent along a fixed positive-spanning set does not imply \(F'(0;d)\ge0\) for every direction \(d\).
knowledge_statements.title: Fixed Positive-Spanning Polls Do Not Certify Nonsmooth Directional Stationarity

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Positive-Spanning Sets and Cosine Measure
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Geometric condition used by finite directional polling in the ambient space.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A finite set \(D\subset\mathbb R^n\setminus\{0\}\) is positive spanning when \(\operatorname{cone}(D)=\mathbb R^n\). Equivalently, its cosine measure \[\operatorname{cm}(D)=\min_{\|v\|=1}\max_{d\in D}\frac{\langle v,d\rangle}{\|d\|}\] is strictly positive. A sequence of poll sets has uniformly nondegenerate geometry when \(\inf_k\operatorname{cm}(D_k)>0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A finite direction set positively spans the space exactly when its cosine measure is positive; a uniform lower bound prevents geometric degeneration.
assumptions_latex: \(D\) is finite and contains no zero vector.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{cone}(D)=\mathbb R^n\) if and only if \(\operatorname{cm}(D)>0\).

notation.meaning: conical hull of the poll directions
cosine measure of the finite direction set

knowledge_statements.title: Positive-Spanning Sets and Cosine Measure

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Refining Unsuccessful Polls Certify Directional Stationarity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Unconstrained limit theorem under moving-base-point directional stability and asymptotically dense normalized polls.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let x_j\to\bar x, \Delta_j\downarrow0, and let each finite D_j consist of unit vectors. Suppose every poll is unsuccessful: \[F(x_j+\Delta_jd)>F(x_j)-\rho(\Delta_j)\qquad(d\in D_j),\] where \rho(t)/t\to0. Assume that for every unit v there exist d_j\in D_j with d_j\to v, and that \[\frac{F(x_j+t_jv_j)-F(x_j)}{t_j}\to F'(\bar x;v)\] whenever x_j\to\bar x, t_j\downarrow0, and v_j\to v. Then F'(\bar x;v)\ge0 for every v\in\mathbb R^n.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Unsuccessful vanishing polls imply unconstrained directional stationarity when directions become dense and directional quotients are stable under moving base points.
assumptions_latex: The normalized poll sets are asymptotically dense.
The displayed moving-base-point directional expansion holds.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: F'(\bar x;v)\ge0\quad\text{for every }v\in\mathbb R^n.

notation.meaning: normalized poll set on the refining unsuccessful subsequence
forcing function in the unsuccessful-poll test

knowledge_statements.title: Refining Unsuccessful Polls Certify Directional Stationarity

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Constrained Refining Polls Certify Directional Stationarity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Constrained refining-poll theorem with feasible directions approximating the Bouligand tangent cone.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let X\subseteq\mathbb R^n be closed, x_j\in X satisfy x_j\to\bar x, and \Delta_j\downarrow0. Let each finite D_j contain unit vectors with x_j+\Delta_jd\in X and suppose F(x_j+\Delta_jd)>F(x_j)-\rho(\Delta_j) for every d\in D_j, where \rho(t)/t\to0. Assume every unit v\in T_X(\bar x) admits d_j\in D_j with d_j\to v, and that \frac{F(x_j+t_jv_j)-F(x_j)}{t_j}\to F'(\bar x;v) whenever t_j\downarrow0, v_j\to v, and x_j+t_jv_j\in X. Then F'(\bar x;v)\ge0 for every v\in T_X(\bar x).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Unsuccessful feasible polls at vanishing radii certify constrained directional stationarity when they become dense in the tangent cone and directional quotients are stable under moving feasible base points.
assumptions_latex: X\subseteq\mathbb R^n\text{ is closed and }x_j\in X\to\bar x.
\text{The feasible polls approximate every unit direction in }T_X(\bar x).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: F'(\bar x;v)\ge0\quad\forall v\in T_X(\bar x).

notation.meaning: Bouligand tangent cone to X at the refining limit

knowledge_statements.title: Constrained Refining Polls Certify Directional Stationarity

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Linear Forcing Can Hide a Strict Descent Direction
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Forcing-function boundary for unsuccessful-poll stationarity inference.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(c>0\), \(F(x)=-(c/2)x\), \(D=\{-1,1\}\), and \(\rho(\Delta)=c\Delta\). At \(x=0\), neither trial satisfies \(F(\Delta d)\le F(0)-\rho(\Delta)\), for any \(\Delta>0\), although \(F'(0;1)=-c/2<0\). Thus unsuccessful vanishing polls need not certify stationarity when \(\rho(t)/t\not\to0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A forcing requirement proportional to the poll radius can conceal genuine first-order descent.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \rho(t)/t\not\to0\quad\Longrightarrow\quad\text{unsuccessful fine polls need not imply directional stationarity}.
knowledge_statements.title: Linear Forcing Can Hide a Strict Descent Direction

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Cosine Measure Detects Smooth Descent
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact geometric implication of positive spanning in the smooth unconstrained regime.

Let \(D\subset\mathbb R^n\setminus\{0\}\) be finite with \(\operatorname{cm}(D)>0\), and let \(F\) be differentiable at \(x\). If \(

assumptions_latex: \(F:X\to\mathbb{R}\) is directionally differentiable on a closed set \(X\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\).
The feasible direction cone used by the search is generated by a finite positive-spanning set \(D_k\).
Objective values can be evaluated at feasible trial points.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Failure to find descent as \(\Delta_k\downarrow0\), together with asymptotically dense feasible positive-spanning directions, yields the directional-stationarity test \(F'(\bar x;d)\geq0\) for every feasible direction \(d\).

notation.meaning: positive-spanning search directions at iteration k

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Derivative-free polling formulation adapted to feasible directional-stationarity search.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Given \(x^k\in X\), \(\Delta_k>0\), and finite \(D_k\) with \(\operatorname{cone}(D_k)\) equal to the modeled feasible tangent cone, evaluate feasible points \(x^k+\Delta_k d\), \(d\in D_k\). If some direction satisfies
\[
F(x^k+\Delta_k d)\leq F(x^k)-\rho(\Delta_k),
\]
choose an accepted direction, set \(x^{k+1}=x^k+\Delta_k d\), and optionally enlarge \(\Delta_k\). Otherwise set \(x^{k+1}=x^k\) and reduce \(\Delta_k\). Stop with directional-stationarity tolerance when \(\Delta_k\leq\varepsilon\) and no poll direction passes the decrease test.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Poll feasible positive-spanning directions at a current radius; accept sufficient descent, otherwise shrink the radius and use unsuccessful fine polls as a stationarity diagnostic.
knowledge_statements.title: Positive-Spanning Directional Search

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm role fits the directional-search leaf. The polling procedure is coherent, but the asserted directional-stationarity implication requires precise assumptions on direction density, tangent-cone approximation, refining subsequences, feasibility, and the forcing function. With no citation, the mathematical conclusion cannot be validated.

children.title: DCA Implementation Architecture
children.top_down_role: Implementation mechanisms retained only where they affect the mathematical algorithm family.

assumptions_latex: At DCA iteration \(k\), \(y^k\in\partial h(x^k)\) has been selected for \(F=g-h\).
The convex function \(x\mapsto g(x)-\langle y^k,x\rangle+\delta_X(x)\) is proper and has a nonempty solution set.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A successful response supplies an approximate next DCA iterate and a verifiable convex-subproblem residual; unsuccessful responses cannot be interpreted as DC stationarity.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Abstract request-response contract between a DCA driver and a convex optimization solver.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The driver sends the solver \(q_k(x)=g(x)-\langle y^k,x\rangle+\delta_X(x)\), tolerances, limits, and an optional initial state. The solver returns \((z^k,r_k,s_k,\sigma_k)\), where
\[
r_k=\operatorname{dist}\bigl(0,\partial g(z^k)-y^k+N_X(z^k)\bigr),
\]
\(s_k\) is reusable solver state, and \(\sigma_k\) is a status. The interface may declare success only when \(z^k\in X\), its reported objective is finite, and \(r_k\) meets the requested tolerance; otherwise the driver must propagate an inexact, infeasible, unbounded, interrupted, or failed status.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Pass the convex DCA model, tolerances, and optional state to a solver; return a candidate, residual, reusable state, and status with explicit validity checks.
knowledge_statements.title: Convex-Subproblem Solver Interfaces

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm role is acceptable for this solver-interface procedure, and the residual formula is meaningful under the stated convex assumptions. No source is supplied for the proposed request-response contract, success conditions, or status semantics, so the record remains source-dependent.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Strong-Convexity Calibration of Solver Residuals
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Generic strong-convexity error calibration, not primarily a DCA solver-interface result.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(q_k\) be proper, closed, and \(\mu\)-strongly convex with \(\mu>0\), let \(x_k^\star=\operatorname*{argmin}q_k\), and let \(r_k=\operatorname{dist}(0,\partial q_k(z^k))\). Then \(\|z^k-x_k^\star\|\le r_k/\mu\) and \(0\le q_k(z^k)-q_k(x_k^\star)\le r_k^2/(2\mu)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Strong convexity converts a stationarity residual into distance and objective-gap bounds.
assumptions_latex: q_k\text{ is proper, closed, and }\mu\text{-strongly convex with }\mu>0.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \|z^k-x_k^\star\|\le r_k/\mu,\qquad q_k(z^k)-q_k(x_k^\star)\le r_k^2/(2\mu).
knowledge_statements.title: Strong-Convexity Calibration of Solver Residuals

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Uncalibrated Residuals Do Not Certify Objective Accuracy
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Generic convex-residual counterfamily rather than a DCA-interface-specific claim.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(q(x)=\varepsilon x\) on \(X=[0,M]\) and \(z=M\), \(\operatorname{dist}(0,\partial q(M)+N_X(M))=\varepsilon\), while \(q(M)-\min_{x\in X}q(x)=\varepsilon M\). Thus no residual-only objective-error bound uniform over all proper closed convex problems can tend to zero with the residual.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Valid Subgradient Selections Can Produce Different DCA Iterates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Trajectory dependence caused by tie-breaking in the DCA subgradient oracle.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(g(x)=\tfrac12x^2\), \(h(x)=|x|\), and \(x^0=0\), one has \(\partial h(0)=[-1,1]\). For any selected \(y^0\in[-1,1]\), the exact DCA subproblem \(\min_x\{\tfrac12x^2-y^0x\}\) has the unique solution \(x^1=y^0\). Thus \(y^0=0\) and \(y^0=1\) produce different valid next iterates.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Different valid subgradients at a nonsmooth point can produce different DCA trajectories.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: x^1=y^0,\quad\text{so valid tie-breaking choices can change the trajectory.}
knowledge_statements.title: Valid Subgradient Selections Can Produce Different DCA Iterates

assumptions_latex: \(h:\mathbb{R}^n\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) is proper closed convex and \(x^k\in\operatorname{dom}\partial h\).
The oracle can return at least one member of \(\partial h(x^k)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The selected \(y^k\) defines the affine minorant of \(h\) used by the next convex DCA subproblem.

notation.meaning: subdifferential of the convex component h

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Deterministic or policy-driven selection from the convex subdifferential in DCA.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A subgradient-selection oracle is a map satisfying
\[
S_h(x,	heta)
\subseteq\partial h(x),
\]
where \(\theta\) contains tie-breaking or history data. At iteration \(k\), choose \(y^k\in S_h(x^k,	heta_k)\) and verify, analytically or through the oracle contract, that
\[
h(z)\geq h(x^k)+\langle y^k,z-x^k\rangle
\quad\text{for every }z\in\mathbb{R}^n.
\]
If \(\partial h(x^k)=\varnothing\), return an oracle-domain failure rather than a DCA iterate. Repeated runs are reproducible when \(S_h\) and its tie-breaking data are deterministic.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Select a valid subgradient of the convex component, using explicit tie-breaking or history, and report failure when the subdifferential is empty.
knowledge_statements.title: Subgradient-Oracle Selection

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm role fits the selection procedure, and the subgradient inequality is mathematically correct. The record nevertheless defines a particular oracle contract and reproducibility policy without any inspectable citation.

children.title: Warm-Start Interfaces
children.top_down_role: Reusable primal, dual, decomposition, or solver state supplied to a new DCA run.

assumptions_latex: A parameterized sequence of DC problems \(F_{	au_j}=g_{	au_j}-h_{	au_j}\) is defined on sets \(X_{	au_j}\).
A completed solve at stage \(j\) returns an iterate and optional compatible solver state.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The interface produces a valid initialization for stage \(j+1\) or explicitly rejects incompatible transferred state.

notation.meaning: final iterate and state at stage j

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Initialization contract for consecutive problems in a DCA continuation sequence.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
After stage \(j\), apply a declared transfer map
\[
(	ilde x_{j+1},	ilde s_{j+1})=W_{j\to j+1}(x_j,s_j).
\]
The interface must check \(\tilde x_{j+1}\in X_{	au_{j+1}}\), dimensional and structural compatibility of \(\tilde s_{j+1}\), and finiteness of the new DC components at \(\tilde x_{j+1}\). Compatible data initialize the next DCA and convex solver. If the iterate is compatible but the internal state is not, discard only \(\tilde s_{j+1}\). If the iterate is invalid, use a declared feasibility restoration or cold start and record the fallback.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Map the previous solution and solver state into the next continuation stage, validate compatibility, and fall back selectively when transferred data are invalid.
knowledge_statements.title: Warm-Start Interfaces

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm role fits the warm-start interface leaf. The compatibility checks and selective fallback form a plausible implementation contract, but no source supports this particular transfer protocol or its claimed validity requirements.

children.title: Continuation Schedules
children.top_down_role: Organization of staged parameter, penalty, smoothing, or model changes.

assumptions_latex: The target parameter is \(\tau_\star\), and intermediate DC problems are defined for parameters in an admissible set \(T\).
Each accepted stage supplies diagnostics measuring solve accuracy and continuation progress.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The schedule either reaches \(\tau_\star\) through accepted stages or terminates with a minimum-step or stage-failure status.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Adaptive parameter progression for a sequence of warm-started DC problems.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Initialize \(\tau_0\in T\), \(\Delta_0>0\), and solve the stage at \(\tau_0\). For \(j\geq0\), propose
\[
\hat\tau_{j+1}=P_T(\tau_j+\Delta_j),
\]
clipped toward \(\tau_\star\), warm-start the proposed stage, and accept it only when its solver and diagnostic criteria hold. After acceptance set \(\tau_{j+1}=\hat\tau_{j+1}\) and enlarge or retain \(\Delta_j\) according to declared progress thresholds. After rejection, retain \(\tau_j\), reduce \(\Delta_j\), and retry. Stop successfully at \(\tau_j=\tau_\star\); stop unsuccessfully if \(\Delta_j<\Delta_{\min}\) or a stage limit is reached.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Advance the continuation parameter adaptively, accepting adequately solved stages, enlarging steps after good progress, and shrinking them after failed stages.
knowledge_statements.title: Continuation Schedules

children.title: Cross-Instance State Transfer
children.top_down_role: Transfer of reusable state between neighboring continuation instances.

assumptions_latex: Two DC instances have declared variable and constraint correspondence maps.
The source instance supplies a final primal iterate and possibly dual, active-set, factorization, or quasi-Newton state.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Only state satisfying the target instance's compatibility and validity predicates is transferred; all other components are reinitialized.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Validated reuse of primal and solver state across related, nonidentical DC instances.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Given source output \((x_a,s_a)\), form
\[
	ilde x_b=T_x(I_a,I_b,x_a),\qquad 	ilde s_b=T_s(I_a,I_b,s_a).
\]
Accept \(\tilde x_b\) only if it has the target dimension, belongs to \(\operatorname{dom}g_b\cap\operatorname{dom}h_b\), and satisfies the target feasibility tolerance. Transfer each component of \(\tilde s_b\) only if its indices, dimensions, scaling conventions, and algebraic invariants match instance \(I_b\). Project or restore the primal point only through a declared map. Reinitialize every rejected component and return a transfer mask recording which state was reused.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Map a solution and internal solver state between related instances, validate each component against the target model, and reinitialize incompatible components.
knowledge_statements.title: Cross-Instance State Transfer

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm role fits this state-transfer procedure. The componentwise validation rules are plausible but solver- and representation-specific, and no source is supplied for the asserted interface contract.

children.title: Continuation Failure Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Regime changes that make prior state misleading or unsuitable for reuse.

assumptions_latex: A continuation method produces stage iterates for parameter values approaching a target \(\tau_\star\).
Warm starts are generated from previously accepted stages.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Without branch regularity, basin stability, and controlled stage accuracy, warm-start continuation has no general guarantee of reaching a target stationary point or global minimizer.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conditions under which warm starts cease to provide reliable continuation behavior.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Continuation can fail when the selected stationary branch \(x(\tau)\) disappears, bifurcates, loses local stability, or exits the feasible domain before \(\tau_\star\). It can also fail when a parameter step crosses attraction basins, transferred state becomes incompatible, or accumulated inexactness exceeds the basin's stability margin. Concretely, even if every stage returns a stationary point of \(F_{\tau_j}\), a sequence with \(\tau_j\to\tau_\star\) need not converge to a stationary point of \(F_{\tau_\star}\) unless boundedness and an appropriate closedness property of the stationary mapping are imposed.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Continuation may fail at bifurcations, domain loss, basin changes, incompatible state, or excessive inexactness; stagewise stationarity alone does not guarantee target stationarity.
knowledge_statements.title: Continuation Failure Boundaries

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Stagewise Stationarity Need Not Pass to the Target Problem
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Generic parameterized-optimization counterexample, canonically owned by continuation theory rather than the DCA interface leaf.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\tau_j>0\) satisfy \(\tau_j\downarrow0\), and define \(F_\tau(x)=(x-\tau)^2\) for \(\tau>0\) and \(F_0(x)=x\). Then \(x_j=\tau_j\) is stationary for every \(F_{\tau_j}\) and \((\tau_j,x_j)\to(0,0)\), but \(0\notin\partial F_0(0)=\{1\}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Without closed parameter dependence, exact stationary stage solutions can converge to a nonstationary target point.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: 0\in\partial F_{\tau_j}(x_j)\ \forall j,\quad x_j\to0,\quad 0\notin\partial F_0(0).
knowledge_statements.title: Stagewise Stationarity Need Not Pass to the Target Problem

children.title: Termination-Criterion Interfaces
children.top_down_role: Configurable stopping criteria exposed by a DCA implementation.

assumptions_latex: A DCA run supplies iterates, objective values, subproblem residuals, feasibility measures, and solver statuses.
All tolerances and logical combinations of tests are fixed before a termination decision.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The interface returns exactly one declared terminal or nonterminal status together with the diagnostics used to obtain it.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Explicit logical contract for stopping, continuing, or aborting a DCA run.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Define
\[
d_k=\|x^{k+1}-x^k\|,
\qquad q_k=\frac{|F(x^{k+1})-F(x^k)|}{1+|F(x^k)|}.
\]
A termination interface evaluates a declared predicate such as
\[
(r_k\leq\varepsilon_r)\wedge(d_k\leq\varepsilon_x)
\wedge(q_k\leq\varepsilon_F),
\]
subject to feasibility and valid-solver-status checks. It must distinguish convergence, iteration or time limit, stagnation without stationarity, infeasibility, unbounded subproblem, numerical failure, and user interruption. Small step or objective change alone may trigger stagnation, but must not be labeled stationarity unless the required residual test also holds.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Evaluate explicit residual, step, objective-change, feasibility, and status predicates, and distinguish convergence from limits, stagnation, and solver failures.
knowledge_statements.title: Termination-Criterion Interfaces

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition kind fits a termination-criterion interface. The record correctly distinguishes small-step stagnation from residual-certified stationarity, but the displayed conjunction and status taxonomy are proposed implementation semantics with no supporting citation.

children.title: Diagnostic-Residual Interfaces
children.top_down_role: Residual, decrease, step, and criticality indicators exposed for inspection.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Selected-Subgradient Residual Is a One-Sided Criticality Test
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Relation between a residual using one oracle selection and the full same-point DC criticality residual.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(y\in\partial h(x)\), define \(r_{\mathrm{crit}}(x)=\operatorname{dist}(0,\partial g(x)-\partial h(x)+N_X(x))\) and \(r_y(x)=\operatorname{dist}(y,\partial g(x)+N_X(x))\). Then \(r_{\mathrm{crit}}(x)\le r_y(x)\). Hence \(r_y(x)=0\) certifies DC criticality, but \(r_y(x)>0\) does not exclude it. For \(g\equiv0\), \(h(x)=|x|\), \(X=\mathbb R\), and \(x=0\), \(r_{\mathrm{crit}}(0)=0\), while the valid selection \(y=1\) gives \(r_y(0)=1\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A selected-subgradient residual upper-bounds the full criticality residual; zero certifies criticality, but a positive value can be a false negative.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: r_{\mathrm{crit}}(x)\le r_y(x),\qquad r_y(x)=0\Rightarrow r_{\mathrm{crit}}(x)=0,\text{ but not conversely.}
knowledge_statements.title: Selected-Subgradient Residual Is a One-Sided Criticality Test

assumptions_latex: \(F=g-h\) with proper closed convex \(g,h\), and \(x^{k+1}\in X\).
The convex subproblem supplies \(y^k\in\partial h(x^k)\) and permits evaluation of its first-order residual.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A zero residual certifies the corresponding convex subproblem optimality condition; it certifies DC criticality only when the subgradient and iterate refer to the same point.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Residual contract separating convex-subproblem accuracy from same-point DC criticality.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Report the convex-subproblem residual
\[
r_k^{\mathrm{sub}}=\operatorname{dist}\bigl(y^k,\partial g(x^{k+1})+N_X(x^{k+1})\bigr).
\]
When both convex subdifferentials are evaluated at a common point \(x\), also report
\[
r^{\mathrm{crit}}(x)=\operatorname{dist}\bigl(0,\partial g(x)-\partial h(x)+N_X(x)\bigr).
\]
The interface must identify which residual is returned, its norm, scaling, evaluation accuracy, and any upper-bound character. The equality \(r_k^{\mathrm{sub}}=0\) verifies exact optimality of the linearized convex subproblem; \(r^{\mathrm{crit}}(x)=0\) verifies the displayed DC criticality inclusion.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Report clearly labeled subproblem and same-point criticality residuals; zero has different certification meaning for each residual.
knowledge_statements.title: Diagnostic-Residual Interfaces

children.title: Stagnation Detection
children.top_down_role: Signals for ineffective progress, cycling, or numerical plateaus.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Periodic-Recurrence Cycling Detector
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Detection of nontrivial iterate cycling that a consecutive-small-step test can miss.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix \(p_{\max}\ge2\), \(L\ge2\), and tolerances \(\varepsilon_c,\varepsilon_r\ge0\). For \(k\ge Lp\), a period-\(p\) signal, \(2\le p\le p_{\max}\), is present when \(\max_{0\le\ell<L}\|x^{k-\ell p}-x^{k-(\ell+1)p}\|\le\varepsilon_c\), \(\min_{0\le\ell\le L}r_{k-\ell p}>\varepsilon_r\), and the points in one period are not all mutually within \(\varepsilon_c\). This is a cycling or stagnation signal, not a convergence certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Repeated nonconstant period-p returns with persistently large residuals signal cycling rather than convergence.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{Nonconstant repeated period-}p\text{ recurrence with }r_i>\varepsilon_r\text{ is classified as cycling, not convergence.}
knowledge_statements.title: Periodic-Recurrence Cycling Detector

assumptions_latex: A run has diagnostic sequences \(F(x^k)\), \(x^k\), and a stationarity residual \(r_k\).
A window length \(m\geq1\), tolerances, and a minimum required residual improvement are prescribed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The detector labels stagnation only when progress remains small over the full window while the stationarity residual remains above tolerance.

notation.meaning: objective spread over the recent window

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Windowed separation of numerical stagnation from certified stationarity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(k\geq m\), define
\[
V_k^F=\max_{k-m\leq i\leq k}F(x^i)-\min_{k-m\leq i\leq k}F(x^i),
\qquad
V_k^x=\max_{k-m<i\leq k}\lVert x^i-x^{i-1}\rVert.
\]
Declare stagnation when \(V_k^F\leq\varepsilon_F\), \(V_k^x\leq\varepsilon_x\), and \(r_k>\varepsilon_r\), optionally requiring that \(r_{k-m}-r_k\leq\eta_r\). If \(r_k\leq\varepsilon_r\), classify the event under the convergence criterion instead. Invalid residuals or failed subproblems produce an indeterminate or solver-failure status, not stagnation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Declare stagnation when objective and iterates barely change across a window but the stationarity residual remains too large.
knowledge_statements.title: Stagnation Detection

children.title: Solver-Status Propagation
children.top_down_role: Communication of subproblem outcomes to outer-loop termination logic.

assumptions_latex: Every convex-subproblem call returns a status from a finite documented status set.
The outer DCA driver has a deterministic precedence rule for terminal and recoverable statuses.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The propagated outer status preserves the strongest justified information and never converts an unverified inner solve into convergence.

notation.meaning: inner convex-solver status at iteration k

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Deterministic translation of inner convex-solver outcomes into outer DCA outcomes.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(P\) map each inner status \(\sigma_k\) and its validity diagnostics to an outer action. A certified or tolerance-satisfied inner solve may continue DCA; an iteration-limited solve may continue only under the declared inexactness rule; infeasible, unbounded, numerical-error, and interrupted statuses trigger their corresponding outer statuses unless a documented recovery succeeds. On termination, set
\[
\Sigma=P\bigl(\sigma_k,r_k,\text{feasibility},\text{recovery history}\bigr).
\]
The returned record must retain the original \(\sigma_k\), solver message, residuals, and recovery attempts. Neither unknown status nor missing diagnostics may be translated to converged.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Translate inner solver outcomes through a documented precedence rule, retain original diagnostics, and never report convergence from unknown or invalid inner results.
knowledge_statements.title: Solver-Status Propagation

children.top_down_role: Convergence is ordered from descent and well-posedness through cluster-point results to whole-sequence geometry, special regimes, and nonasymptotic certificates.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Coercive-Tilt Sufficient Regime
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Per-iteration sufficient condition for attainment of the exact DCA convex subproblem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(g:\mathbb R^n\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) be proper, lower semicontinuous, and convex. If \[x\mapsto g(x)-\langle y^k,x\rangle\] is coercive, then its argmin is nonempty and compact. Thus the primal exact-DCA update is well defined for this selection \(y^k\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A proper lower-semicontinuous convex DCA subproblem attains a minimizer whenever its tilted objective is coercive.
assumptions_latex: \(g\) is proper, lower semicontinuous, and convex on \(\mathbb R^n\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \varnothing\ne\operatorname*{argmin}_x\{g(x)-\langle y^k,x\rangle\}\text{ is compact}.

notation.meaning: selected dual subgradient defining the tilt

knowledge_statements.title: Coercive-Tilt Sufficient Regime

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Strong-Convexity Well-Definedness Regime
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Uniform sufficient regime giving a unique primal DCA update for every linear tilt.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(g:\mathbb R^n\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) is proper, lower semicontinuous, and \(\rho\)-strongly convex for some \(\rho>0\), then for every \(y\in\mathbb R^n\), \(g-\langle y,\cdot\rangle\) has a unique minimizer. Hence, whenever \(\partial h(x^k)\ne\varnothing\), every selected \(y^k\in\partial h(x^k)\) produces a unique primal DCA update.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Strong convexity of the retained convex component makes every linearly tilted DCA subproblem uniquely solvable.
assumptions_latex: \(g\) is proper, lower semicontinuous, and \(\rho\)-strongly convex with \(\rho>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \forall y^k\in\partial h(x^k),\quad\operatorname*{argmin}_x\{g(x)-\langle y^k,x\rangle\}\text{ is a singleton}.
knowledge_statements.title: Strong-Convexity Well-Definedness Regime

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Unattained or Unbounded Tilts Break Exact DCA
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Per-iteration failure boundaries for the primal convex subproblem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Subgradient availability alone does not ensure an exact DCA update. If \(g(x)=e^x\) and \(h\equiv0\), then \(y^k=0\) is available but \(\inf_xe^x=0\) is unattained. If \(g\equiv0\), \(h(x)=\langle a,x\rangle\), and \(a\ne0\), then \(y^k=a\) and the tilted subproblem \(\inf_x-\langle a,x\rangle\) is unbounded below. In either case the primal exact-DCA update is absent.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A valid subgradient selection is insufficient because the tilted convex subproblem may have an unattained infimum or be unbounded below.
assumptions_latex: The ambient space is finite dimensional.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \partial h(x^k)\ne\varnothing\centernot\implies\operatorname*{argmin}_x\{g(x)-\langle y^k,x\rangle\}\ne\varnothing.
knowledge_statements.title: Unattained or Unbounded Tilts Break Exact DCA

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Relative-Interior Subgradient Availability
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional sufficient regime for the dual subgradient-selection stage of exact DCA.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(h:\mathbb R^n\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) be proper, lower semicontinuous, and convex. If \(x^k\in\operatorname{ri}(\operatorname{dom}h)\), then \(\partial h(x^k)\ne\varnothing\). Hence every generated iterate in \(\operatorname{ri}(\operatorname{dom}h)\) admits a DCA selection \(y^k\in\partial h(x^k)\); primal well-definedness additionally requires attainment of the corresponding tilted \(g\)-subproblem.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An iterate in the relative interior of the subtracted component's domain admits a convex subgradient, although this alone does not solve the tilted primal subproblem.
assumptions_latex: \(h:\mathbb R^n\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) is proper, lower semicontinuous, and convex.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\partial h(x^k)\ne\varnothing\).
knowledge_statements.title: Relative-Interior Subgradient Availability

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Conjugate Characterization of the Primal DCA Update
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact primal-dual equivalence for existence and representation of a tilted convex-subproblem minimizer.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(g:\mathbb R^n\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) be proper, lower semicontinuous, and convex. For every \(y\in\mathbb R^n\), \[\operatorname*{argmin}_{x}\{g(x)-\langle y,x\rangle\}=\partial g^*(y)=(\partial g)^{-1}(y).\] Consequently, the tilted DCA subproblem has a minimizer exactly when \(\partial g^*(y)\ne\varnothing\), equivalently when \(y\in\operatorname{ran}\partial g\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A tilted DCA subproblem is solvable exactly when the selected tilt has a conjugate subgradient, equivalently when it lies in the range of the retained component's subdifferential.
assumptions_latex: \(g:\mathbb R^n\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) is proper, lower semicontinuous, and convex.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname*{argmin}(g-\langle y,\cdot\rangle)=\partial g^*(y)=(\partial g)^{-1}(y)\).
knowledge_statements.title: Conjugate Characterization of the Primal DCA Update
DCA Well-Definedness Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A finite-dimensional per-iteration condition for exact-DCA well-definedness.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(f=g-h\), where \(g,h:\mathbb{R}^n\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) are proper lower-semicontinuous convex functions, and let \(x^0\in\operatorname{dom}g\cap\operatorname{dom}\partial h\). At iteration \(k\), select \(y^k\in\partial h(x^k)\) and then select
\[
x^{k+1}\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in\mathbb{R}^n}\bigl\{g(x)-\langle y^k,x\rangle\bigr\}.
\]
The trajectory is well defined provided that, for every generated \(x^k\), the set \(\partial h(x^k)\) is nonempty and, for every permitted selection \(y^k\), the displayed argmin set is nonempty.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Exact DCA is well defined when a subgradient of the subtracted convex term exists at every generated iterate and every resulting convex subproblem attains a minimizer.
assumptions_latex: For every generated \(x^k\), \(\partial h(x^k)\neq\varnothing\), and every permitted tilt has a nonempty argmin set.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x^{k+1}\) can be selected for every \(k\geq0\), so the exact-DCA trajectory is well defined.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Convergence of Lower-Bounded DCA Objective Values
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Scalar-value consequence of exact-DCA monotonicity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If an exact DCA trajectory satisfies \(f(x^{k+1})\le f(x^k)\) for every \(k\) and \(\inf_k f(x^k)>-\infty\), then there is \(\ell\in\mathbb R\) such that \[f(x^k)\downarrow\ell.\] This scalar convergence does not imply convergence of the iterates.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A lower-bounded monotone DCA objective sequence converges, although the DCA iterates need not converge.
assumptions_latex: The exact DCA trajectory is well defined.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \exists\ell\in\mathbb R:\ f(x^k)\downarrow\ell.
knowledge_statements.title: Convergence of Lower-Bounded DCA Objective Values

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Majorization Model Underlying Exact DCA Descent
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Tangent-majorization representation of one exact DCA iteration.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f=g-h\) with convex \(g,h\), choose \(y^k\in\partial h(x^k)\), and define \[M_k(x)=g(x)-h(x^k)-\langle y^k,x-x^k\rangle.\] Then \(f(x)\le M_k(x)\) for every \(x\), \(M_k(x^k)=f(x^k)\), and every \(x^{k+1}\in\operatorname*{argmin}M_k\) satisfies \[f(x^{k+1})\le M_k(x^{k+1})\le f(x^k).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Exact DCA minimizes a convex majorant formed by affine minorization of the subtracted convex component, and that majorant touches the objective at the current iterate.
assumptions_latex: \(g\) and \(h\) are proper convex functions at the displayed points.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: f\le M_k,\quad M_k(x^k)=f(x^k),\quad f(x^{k+1})\le f(x^k).
knowledge_statements.title: Majorization Model Underlying Exact DCA Descent

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Arbitrary Inexact Updates Need Not Descend
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary showing why exact model minimization or a quantified inexactness rule is required by the DCA descent principle.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(g(x)=x^2/2\) and \(h\equiv0\) on \(\mathbb R\). At \(x^k=0\), the DCA model is \(M_k(x)=x^2/2\), with exact minimizer zero. If an uncontrolled inexact update selects \(x^{k+1}=1\), then \[f(x^{k+1})=\frac12>0=f(x^k).\] Thus membership in the model domain, without exact minimization or a sufficient model-decrease condition, does not ensure DCA descent.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A merely feasible approximate model update can increase the DC objective; descent requires exact minimization or a quantitative inexactness condition.
knowledge_statements.title: Arbitrary Inexact Updates Need Not Descend

assumptions_latex: \(g\) and \(h\) are convex with strong-convexity moduli \(\rho_g,\rho_h\geq0\).
The exact DCA updates are well defined.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact-DCA descent, including the quantitative strongly convex form.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(f=g-h\), and let the exact DCA step satisfy \(y^k\in\partial h(x^k)\) and
\[
x^{k+1}\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{x}\{g(x)-\langle y^k,x\rangle\}.
\]
If \(g\) and \(h\) are strongly convex with respective moduli \(\rho_g\geq0\) and \(\rho_h\geq0\), then
\[
f(x^{k+1})\leq f(x^k)-\frac{\rho_g+\rho_h}{2}\|x^{k+1}-x^k\|^2.
\]
Consequently, the objective values are nonincreasing; if \(\rho_g+\rho_h>0\), every nonzero step produces strict quantitative decrease.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Exact DCA never increases the objective; strong convexity yields a decrease proportional to the squared step length.
knowledge_statements.title: DCA Descent Principles

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The quantitative descent inequality is mathematically plausible and appropriately classified as a principle, but no inspectable DCA source supports its precise hypotheses and normalization of the strong-convexity moduli.

children.title: Level-Set Boundedness
children.top_down_role: Bounded sublevel geometry relevant to DCA trajectories.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(L_f(f(x^0))\) is bounded.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundedness of the initial sublevel set used to contain descent iterates.

source_refs.locator: 9.1.5 Boundedness of level sets p. 826
source_refs.source_title: Finite-Dimensional Variational Inequalities and Complementarity Problems, Vol. II

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(\alpha\in\mathbb{R}\), define the sublevel set
\[
L_f(\alpha):=\{x\in\mathbb{R}^n:f(x)\leq\alpha\}.
\]
The level-set boundedness regime at the initial point \(x^0\) is the condition that \(L_f(f(x^0))\) is bounded. If an algorithm satisfies \(f(x^{k+1})\leq f(x^k)\) for every \(k\), then \(x^k\in L_f(f(x^0))\) for every \(k\); hence this condition confines the entire trajectory to a bounded set.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A bounded initial sublevel set contains every iterate of a descent method and therefore prevents escape to infinity.
knowledge_statements.title: Level-Set Boundedness

source_witnesses.locator: 9.1.5 Boundedness of level sets p. 826
source_witnesses.source_title: Finite-Dimensional Variational Inequalities and Complementarity Problems, Vol. II

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Sequential Characterization of Bounded Sublevels
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equivalent finite-dimensional characterization of boundedness for a fixed objective sublevel.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(L_f(\alpha):=\{x\in\mathbb R^n:f(x)\le \alpha\}\), the following are equivalent: \(L_f(\alpha)\) is bounded; every sequence in \(L_f(\alpha)\) is bounded; and there is no sequence \((x^j)\subset L_f(\alpha)\) with \(\|x^j\|\to\infty\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A sublevel is bounded exactly when it contains no sequence escaping to infinity.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: L_f(\alpha)\text{ bounded}\iff\nexists (x^j)\subset L_f(\alpha)\text{ with }\|x^j\|\to\infty.

notation.meaning: sublevel set of f at alpha

knowledge_statements.title: Sequential Characterization of Bounded Sublevels

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Compactness of a Bounded Lower-Semicontinuous Sublevel
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional compactness strengthening of the locally owned bounded-sublevel condition.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(f:\mathbb R^n\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) is lower semicontinuous, then \(L_f(\alpha)\) is closed. Hence a bounded \(L_f(\alpha)\) is compact.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A bounded sublevel of a lower-semicontinuous finite-dimensional objective is compact.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(L_f(\alpha)\text{ is compact}.\)

notation.meaning: sublevel set of f at alpha

knowledge_statements.title: Compactness of a Bounded Lower-Semicontinuous Sublevel

children.title: Iterate-Sequence Boundedness
children.top_down_role: Boundedness of the sequence generated by DCA.

assumptions_latex: The initial sublevel set \(L_f(f(x^0))\) is bounded.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\sup_{k\geq0}\|x^k\|<+\infty\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: The direct bounded-trajectory consequence of descent and initial-level boundedness.

source_refs.locator: 9.1.5 Boundedness of level sets p. 826
source_refs.source_title: Finite-Dimensional Variational Inequalities and Complementarity Problems, Vol. II

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Suppose a sequence \((x^k)_{k\geq0}\subset\operatorname{dom}f\) satisfies \(f(x^{k+1})\leq f(x^k)\) for every \(k\). Then
\[
\{x^k:k\geq0\}\subseteq L_f(f(x^0)).
\]
Therefore, if \(L_f(f(x^0))\) is bounded, the iterate sequence is bounded:
\[
\sup_{k\geq0}\|x^k\|<+\infty.
\]
In finite dimensions it consequently has at least one cluster point.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A descent sequence is bounded whenever the sublevel set determined by its initial objective value is bounded.
knowledge_statements.title: Iterate-Sequence Boundedness

source_witnesses.locator: 9.1.5 Boundedness of level sets p. 826
source_witnesses.source_title: Finite-Dimensional Variational Inequalities and Complementarity Problems, Vol. II

children.title: Coercive Regimes
children.top_down_role: Coercive settings that support level or trajectory control.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every nonempty sublevel set \(L_f(\alpha)\) is compact.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional coercivity as a global sufficient condition for bounded DCA levels.

source_refs.locator: 9.1.5 Boundedness of level sets p. 826
source_refs.source_title: Finite-Dimensional Variational Inequalities and Complementarity Problems, Vol. II

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A proper function \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) is coercive when
\[
\|x_j\|\to+\infty\quad\Longrightarrow\quad f(x_j)\to+\infty
\]
for every sequence \((x_j)\). Equivalently, every sublevel set \(L_f(\alpha)=\{x:f(x)\leq\alpha\}\) is bounded. If \(f\) is also lower semicontinuous, these sublevel sets are closed and hence compact in finite dimensions. Thus every descent trajectory beginning at a finite-valued point is bounded.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Coercivity makes all finite sublevel sets bounded; lower semicontinuity then makes them compact and confines every descent trajectory.
knowledge_statements.title: Coercive Regimes

source_witnesses.locator: 9.1.5 Boundedness of level sets p. 826
source_witnesses.source_title: Finite-Dimensional Variational Inequalities and Complementarity Problems, Vol. II

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Existence and Compactness of Minimizers in the Coercive Regime
knowledge_statements.scope_note: General minimizer-attainment result proposed within a DCA trajectory-boundedness partition.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(f:\mathbb R^n\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) is proper, lower semicontinuous, and coercive, then \(\operatorname*{argmin}f\) is nonempty and compact and \(\inf f> -\infty\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A proper lower-semicontinuous coercive objective attains a finite minimum with a compact minimizer set.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \inf f\in\mathbb R,\qquad\varnothing\ne\operatorname*{argmin}f\text{ is compact}.
knowledge_statements.title: Existence and Compactness of Minimizers in the Coercive Regime

children.title: Escape-to-Infinity Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Settings where descent does not prevent unbounded trajectories.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Unique Strictly Descending DCA Steps Can Escape
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Escape example showing that unique subproblem solutions and strict descent do not replace level boundedness.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: On \(\mathbb R\), let \[g(x)=e^{-x}+\tfrac12x^2,\qquad h(x)=\tfrac12x^2,\qquad f(x)=e^{-x}.\] Exact DCA selects \(y^k=x^k\), and its strongly convex subproblem has the unique minimizer characterized by \[x^{k+1}-x^k=e^{-x^{k+1}}>0.\] For every finite \(x^0\), the resulting trajectory satisfies \(f(x^{k+1})<f(x^k)\), \(x^k\to+\infty\), and \(f(x^k)\downarrow0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A smooth DC objective can generate unique exact-DCA steps with strict objective decrease while its iterates escape to infinity.
assumptions_latex: DCA uses the displayed decomposition and exact subproblem minimization.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: x^{k+1}>x^k,\quad f(x^{k+1})<f(x^k),\quad x^k\to+\infty,\quad f(x^k)\downarrow0.

notation.meaning: displayed DC decomposition of the exponential objective

knowledge_statements.title: Unique Strictly Descending DCA Steps Can Escape

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The exact DCA trajectory \(x^k=k\) satisfies \(f(x^{k+1})=f(x^k)\) but \(|x^k|\to+\infty\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A concrete boundary showing that descent alone does not ensure bounded iterates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(g(x)=h(x)=0\) on \(\mathbb{R}\), so \(f=g-h\equiv0\). At every \(x^k\), exact DCA selects \(y^k=0\), and its convex subproblem has
\[
\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in\mathbb{R}}\{g(x)-y^k x\}=\mathbb{R}.
\]
Hence choosing \(x^{k+1}=k+1\) is a valid exact-DCA trajectory. It obeys \(f(x^{k+1})=f(x^k)=0\) for all \(k\), while \(|x^k|\to+\infty\). Thus well-definedness and objective descent do not imply bounded iterates without level boundedness, coercivity, or a bounded selection rule.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For the constant objective, arbitrary minimizer choices are valid DCA steps, so a nonincreasing trajectory can still escape to infinity.
knowledge_statements.title: Escape-to-Infinity Boundaries

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The counterexample is algebraically valid and its kind fits the escape-to-infinity boundary, but the record supplies no cited source or explicit standard-field rationale.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Best-Step Complexity from Quadratic Decrease
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-horizon successive-step bound under uniform quadratic decrease.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \[f(x^{k+1})\le f(x^k)-c\|x^{k+1}-x^k\|^2\quad(c>0)\] for \(k=0,\ldots,N-1\), and \(f(x^k)\ge f_{\inf}>-\infty\), then \[\min_{0\le k<N}\|x^{k+1}-x^k\|^2\le\frac{f(x^0)-f_{\inf}}{cN}.\] Consequently, a step of norm at most \(\varepsilon\) occurs within \(\left\lceil(f(x^0)-f_{\inf})/(c\varepsilon^2)\right\rceil\) iterations.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Uniform quadratic decrease gives an order-one-over-N best squared-step bound and order-epsilon-to-minus-two step-residual complexity.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \min_{0\le k<N}\|x^{k+1}-x^k\|^2\le\frac{f(x^0)-f_{\inf}}{cN}.
knowledge_statements.title: Best-Step Complexity from Quadratic Decrease

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Asymptotically Regular Exact-DCA Trajectory Need Not Converge
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact-DCA counterexample separating vanishing square-summable steps from iterate convergence.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(g\equiv h\equiv0\) on \(\mathbb R\). Then \(y^k=0\), and every point minimizes \(g-\langle y^k,\cdot\rangle\), so any real sequence is an exact-DCA trajectory. Choose \[x^k=\sin(\log(k+1)).\] Then \[|x^{k+1}-x^k|\le\log(k+2)-\log(k+1)\le\frac1{k+1},\] hence \(\sum_k|x^{k+1}-x^k|^2<\infty\) and \(|x^{k+1}-x^k|\to0\), while \((x^k)\) does not converge.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Even an exact-DCA trajectory can have vanishing square-summable steps without converging when the convex subproblem has nonunique minimizers.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\sum_k|x^{k+1}-x^k|^2<\infty\), \(|x^{k+1}-x^k|\to0\), and \((x^k)\) does not converge.
knowledge_statements.title: Asymptotically Regular Exact-DCA Trajectory Need Not Converge

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Square-summability and vanishing steps derived from uniform sufficient decrease.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Suppose a DCA trajectory satisfies, for some \(c>0\),
\[
f(x^{k+1})\leq f(x^k)-c\|x^{k+1}-x^k\|^2
\]
for every \(k\), and suppose \(\inf_k f(x^k)>-\infty\). Summing the decrease inequalities gives
\[
c\sum_{k=0}^{\infty}\|x^{k+1}-x^k\|^2\leq f(x^0)-\inf_k f(x^k)<+\infty.
\]
Consequently, \(\|x^{k+1}-x^k\|\to0\). This vanishing-step property is asymptotic regularity; it does not by itself imply convergence or finite trajectory length.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Uniform quadratic descent and a lower objective bound make squared step lengths summable, so consecutive DCA iterates become asymptotically indistinguishable.
knowledge_statements.title: Asymptotic Regularity of DCA Trajectories

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The square-summability and vanishing-step conclusions are correct under the displayed decrease and lower-bound assumptions, but the record has no source and includes a derivational passage that should be removed from a knowledge statement.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Vanishing and Square-Summable Steps Need Not Give Convergence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Generic sequence example proposed as a boundary for a DCA-trajectory leaf.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(x^k=\sum_{j=1}^k1/j\), the increments vanish and are square summable, while \(x^k\to+\infty\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Harmonic partial sums have vanishing square-summable increments but diverge.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \sum_k|x^{k+1}-x^k|^2<\infty,\quad|x^{k+1}-x^k|\to0,\quad x^k\to+\infty.
knowledge_statements.title: Vanishing and Square-Summable Steps Need Not Give Convergence

intermediate_metadata.reason: Accepted local coverage is the finite-horizon best-step complexity consequence of quadratic decrease. The core infinite-horizon square-summability theorem remains frontiered. Generic sequence counterexamples were excluded, while trajectory boundedness, escape, and full-sequence convergence remain sibling or downstream scopes.

children.title: Subsequential Convergence to DC Critical Points
children.top_down_role: The classical cluster-point result is retained as an internal organizer rather than a statement-level leaf.

knowledge_statements.title: Exact-DCA Cluster-Point Convergence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional exact DCA with bounded primal and dual sequences.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(f=g-h\), where \(g,h:\mathbb{R}^n\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) are proper closed convex functions. Suppose exact DCA generates bounded sequences \((x^k)\) and \((y^k)\) satisfying
\[
y^k\in\partial h(x^k)\cap\partial g(x^{k+1})
\]
for every \(k\geq0\), and suppose \(\|x^{k+1}-x^k\|\to0\). Then every cluster point \(\bar x\) of \((x^k)\) satisfies
\[
\partial g(\bar x)\cap\partial h(\bar x)\neq\varnothing.
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If exact-DCA primal and dual sequences are bounded and successive primal steps vanish, every primal cluster point is DC critical.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every cluster point \(\bar x\) satisfies \(\partial g(\bar x)\cap\partial h(\bar x)\neq\varnothing\).

knowledge_statements.title: Inexact-DCA Cluster-Point Convergence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Additive vanishing-residual version of inexact-DCA subsequential convergence.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(f=g-h\), where \(g,h:\mathbb{R}^n\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) are proper closed convex functions. Suppose bounded sequences \((x^k)\) and \((y^k)\) satisfy
\[
y^k-e^k\in\partial h(x^k),\qquad y^k-r^k\in\partial g(x^{k+1})
\]
for every \(k\geq0\), where \(e^k\to0\), \(r^k\to0\), and \(\|x^{k+1}-x^k\|\to0\). Then every cluster point \(\bar x\) of \((x^k)\) satisfies
\[
\partial g(\bar x)\cap\partial h(\bar x)\neq\varnothing.
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: With bounded primal and dual sequences, vanishing additive subgradient residuals and vanishing primal steps ensure that every primal cluster point is DC critical.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every cluster point \(\bar x\) satisfies \(\partial g(\bar x)\cap\partial h(\bar x)\neq\varnothing\).

knowledge_statements.title: Constrained-DCA Cluster-Point Convergence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Convex-set constrained DCA expressed through the indicator-function decomposition.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(C\subset\mathbb{R}^n\) be nonempty, closed, and convex, and let \(g,h:\mathbb{R}^n\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) be proper closed convex functions. Define \(G=g+\delta_C\), and suppose
\[
\operatorname{ri}(\operatorname{dom}g)\cap\operatorname{ri}C\neq\varnothing.
\]
Assume exact constrained DCA generates bounded sequences \((x^k)\) and \((y^k)\) satisfying
\[
y^k\in\partial h(x^k)\cap\partial G(x^{k+1})
\]
for every \(k\geq0\), and that \(\|x^{k+1}-x^k\|\to0\). Then every cluster point \(\bar x\) belongs to \(C\) and satisfies
\[
\partial h(\bar x)\cap\bigl(\partial g(\bar x)+N_C(\bar x)\bigr)\neq\varnothing.
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every cluster point of a bounded, asymptotically regular exact constrained-DCA trajectory satisfies the convex-normal-cone DC criticality condition.
assumptions_latex: The primal and dual sequences are bounded, \(y^k\in\partial h(x^k)\cap\partial(g+\delta_C)(x^{k+1})\), and \(\|x^{k+1}-x^k\|\to0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every cluster point \(\bar x\in C\) satisfies \(\partial h(\bar x)\cap(\partial g(\bar x)+N_C(\bar x))\neq\varnothing\).
Every cluster pair \((\bar x,\bar y)\) satisfies \(\bar y\in\partial h(\bar x)\cap\partial g(\bar x)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Fenchel-subgradient formulation of exact-DCA primal-dual cluster convergence.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(f=g-h\), where \(g\) and \(h\) are proper closed convex functions. Suppose
\[
y^k\in\partial h(x^k),\qquad x^{k+1}\in\partial g^*(y^k),
\]
the pair sequence is bounded, and \(\|x^{k+1}-x^k\|\to0\). If \((x^{k_j},y^{k_j})\to(\bar x,\bar y)\), then also \(x^{k_j+1}\to\bar x\). Fenchel subgradient inversion and graph closedness yield
\[
\bar y\in\partial h(\bar x),
\qquad
\bar x\in\partial g^*(\bar y)
\Longleftrightarrow
\bar y\in\partial g(\bar x).
\]
Thus every cluster pair satisfies the primal-dual DC criticality relations.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every bounded primal-dual cluster pair with vanishing primal steps satisfies the mutual Fenchel subgradient relations and yields a DC-critical primal point.
knowledge_statements.title: Primal–Dual Cluster-Point Convergence

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The primal-dual conclusion is mathematically consistent under boundedness and vanishing primal steps, and theorem is the correct kind. However, no source supports the exact formulation, and the statement includes a proof-style derivation via Fenchel inversion and graph closedness.
