Nevertheless, \(f(x)=x^4-x^2<0=f(0)\) whenever \(0<|x|<1\), so \(0\) is a strict local maximizer rather than a local minimizer.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: DCA can remain fixed with zero step and zero decrease at a decomposition-critical point that is a strict local maximum.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: s_k=d_k=0\text{ for every }k,\quad\text{but }0\text{ is not a local minimizer of }f.
knowledge_statements.title: Zero Step and Decrease at a Nonminimum DC-Critical Point
Vanishing-Certificate Limits
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Asymptotic consequences of summable descent certificates and closed convex subdifferential graphs.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(F=g-h\) with proper closed convex \(g,h\), and suppose DCA generates \(y^k\in\partial h(x^k)\cap\partial g(x^{k+1})\). If \(F(x^k)-F(x^{k+1})\ge a\lVert x^{k+1}-x^k\rVert^2\) and \(F\) is bounded below, then
\[\lVert x^{k+1}-x^k\rVert\to0,\qquad F(x^k)-F(x^{k+1})\to0.\]
If a subsequence satisfies \((x^{k_j},y^{k_j})\to(\bar x,\bar y)\), then closedness of convex subdifferential graphs yields
\[\bar y\in\partial g(\bar x)\cap\partial h(\bar x),\]
so \(\bar x\) is critical for the chosen DC decomposition.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Quadratic descent and lower boundedness force step and decrease certificates to vanish; convergent primal-subgradient subsequences then approach decomposition-critical points.
assumptions_latex: \(F(x^k)-F(x^{k+1})\ge a\lVert x^{k+1}-x^k\rVert^2\) with \(a>0\), and \(F\) is bounded below.
\((x^{k_j},y^{k_j})\to(\bar x,\bar y)\) for the criticality conclusion.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\lVert x^{k+1}-x^k\rVert\to0\), \(F(x^k)-F(x^{k+1})\to0\), and \(\bar y\in\partial g(\bar x)\cap\partial h(\bar x)\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The asymptotic conclusions are consistent with the hypotheses, including joint convergence of the primal-subgradient subsequence. A source is needed for the intended DCA descent and cluster-criticality result.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Linear-Rate Regime under Eventual Contraction
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Certificate-neutral characterization of a DCA regime in which a specified error measure contracts geometrically.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(M_k\ge0\) be a specified objective-gap, distance, step, or stationarity measure. If for some \(k_0\) and \(q\in(0,1)\),
\[M_{k+1}\le qM_k\quad(k\ge k_0),\]
then
\[M_k\le q^{k-k_0}M_{k_0}.\]
For \(0<\varepsilon<M_{k_0}\), it is sufficient that
\[k-k_0\ge \left\lceil\frac{\log(M_{k_0}/\varepsilon)}{\log(1/q)}\right\rceil,
\]
so the post-transient iteration complexity is \(O(\log(1/\varepsilon))\). This conclusion is measure-specific; linear convergence of one measure does not automatically imply linear convergence of the others.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An eventual uniform contraction gives geometric decay and logarithmic complexity for the particular DCA measure being contracted.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: M_k\le q^{k-k_0}M_{k_0}\text{ and }k-k_0=O(\log(1/\varepsilon)).
knowledge_statements.title: Linear-Rate Regime under Eventual Contraction
Linear-Rate Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Abstract linear convergence regime induced by contraction of an objective or stationarity measure.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(M_k\ge0\) be an objective-gap, distance, or stationarity measure associated with DCA. Assume that after some index \(k_0\), the problem geometry and update rule imply the uniform contraction
\[M_{k+1}\le qM_k\qquad(k\ge k_0),\]
where \(q\in(0,1)\). Then
\[M_k\le q^{k-k_0}M_{k_0}\qquad(k\ge k_0),\]
and achieving \(M_k\le\varepsilon\) requires at most
\[k-k_0\ge\frac{\log(M_{k_0}/\varepsilon)}{\log(1/q)}\]
post-transient iterations. Such a contraction may follow from an error bound, strong convexity combined with regularity, or a Kurdyka–Łojasiewicz inequality of exponent \(1/2\), but it is not automatic for general DC problems.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Whenever problem geometry yields a uniform contraction of the selected DCA error measure, that measure converges geometrically and reaches epsilon accuracy in logarithmically many iterations.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(M_k\le q^{k-k_0}M_{k_0}\) and the post-transient complexity is \(O(\log(1/\varepsilon))\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The geometric estimate follows from the explicitly assumed contraction, and complexity_bound fits the leaf. The listed DCA mechanisms said to yield contraction require authoritative sourcing and precise hypotheses.

children.title: Inexact-Oracle Cost Models
children.top_down_role: Computational accounting for approximate subgradient or related oracle access.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Inexact-Oracle Cost Model
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Accuracy-dependent accounting for approximate convex-oracle calls used by an inexact DCA iteration.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
An inexact-oracle model specifies a query set \(D\), an error predicate \(\mathcal P(x,o,\delta)\), and a resource cost \(C_{\mathrm{or}}(x,\delta)\) for producing an output \(o\) satisfying that predicate. For example, for proper convex \(h\), \(x\in\operatorname{dom}h\), and \(\delta\ge0\), a \(\delta\)-subgradient output \(\tilde y\) satisfies
\[h(z)\ge h(x)+\langle\tilde y,z-x\rangle-\delta\quad(\forall z).\]
For one such query at each outer iteration, cumulative oracle work is
\[W_{\mathrm{or}}(K)=\sum_{k=0}^{K-1}C_{\mathrm{or}}(x^k,\delta_k).\]
The predicate and counted resource are part of the model; no universal accuracy-to-cost law is implied.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An inexact-oracle cost model fixes the allowed queries, the approximation guarantee, and the work charged for meeting each requested accuracy.
assumptions_latex: \(h:\mathbb R^n\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) is proper and convex in the displayed example.
One fixed resource convention is used.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: W_{\mathrm{or}}(K)=\sum_{k=0}^{K-1}C_{\mathrm{or}}(x^k,\delta_k).

notation.meaning: cost of a conforming oracle response

knowledge_statements.title: Inexact-Oracle Cost Model
Inexact-Oracle Cost Models
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Cost model for approximate values or subgradients used by an inexact DCA iteration.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
An inexact-oracle cost model assigns to every requested tolerance \(\delta>0\) a cost \(C_{\mathrm{or}}(\delta)\) for returning an approximation satisfying a declared error predicate. For example, a value-subgradient oracle for a convex function \(h\) may return \((\tilde h(x),\tilde y)\) such that
\[|\tilde h(x)-h(x)|\le\delta,\qquad h(z)\ge h(x)+\langle\tilde y,z-x\rangle-\delta\quad\text{for all }z.\]
For oracle tolerances \((\delta_k)_{k=0}^{K-1}\), the oracle contribution to computational work is
\[W_{\mathrm{or}}(K)=\sum_{k=0}^{K-1}C_{\mathrm{or}}(\delta_k).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The model charges each approximate value or subgradient query according to its requested accuracy and sums these charges over all outer DCA iterations.
assumptions_latex: \(C_{\mathrm{or}}(\delta)\) measures work under a fixed computational model.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(W_{\mathrm{or}}(K)=\sum_{k=0}^{K-1}C_{\mathrm{or}}(\delta_k)\).

notation.meaning: oracle accuracy requested at iteration k
cost of one inexact oracle response

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition fits the cost-model leaf, but its example requires the query point to lie in the effective domain of h, and no source fixes the inexact-oracle predicate or cost convention.

children.title: Inexact-Subproblem Cost Models
children.top_down_role: Computational accounting for approximate convex-subproblem solutions.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Inexact-Subproblem Cost Model
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Accuracy-dependent accounting for approximate solution of convex DCA subproblems.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
At iteration \(k\), let \(Q_k\) be a proper convex objective with finite infimum \(Q_k^*\). A cost model fixes a stopping predicate \(\mathcal S_k(x,ta)\), a counted resource, and a bound \(C_{\mathrm{sub},k}(ta)\) for producing a point satisfying that predicate. An objective-gap predicate is
\[Q_k(x^{k+1})-Q_k^*\le	a_k.\]
Because \(Q_k^*\) may be unknown, a valid primal-dual gap or another certified upper bound on this gap may replace direct evaluation. Cumulative inner work is
\[W_{\mathrm{sub}}(K)=\sum_{k=0}^{K-1}C_{\mathrm{sub},k}(ta_k).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A subproblem cost model fixes a certified stopping rule, a resource unit, and the work needed to reach each requested inner accuracy.
assumptions_latex: Each stopping predicate certifies the accuracy required by the outer analysis.
All costs use a fixed resource convention.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: W_{\mathrm{sub}}(K)=\sum_{k=0}^{K-1}C_{\mathrm{sub},k}(ta_k).

notation.meaning: cost bound for solving subproblem k

knowledge_statements.title: Inexact-Subproblem Cost Model
Inexact-Subproblem Cost Models
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Accuracy-dependent work model for approximately solving each convex DCA subproblem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
At iteration \(k\), let \(Q_k\) be the convex DCA subproblem objective and let \(Q_k^*=\inf_x Q_k(x)\). An objective-accuracy solve returns \(x^{k+1}\) satisfying
\[Q_k(x^{k+1})-Q_k^*\le\eta_k,\]
where \(\eta_k>0\) is prescribed. If \(C_{\mathrm{sub},k}(\eta)\) denotes the number of elementary operations, inner iterations, or oracle calls required to reach accuracy \(\eta\), then the cumulative subproblem work through \(K\) outer iterations is
\[W_{\mathrm{sub}}(K)=\sum_{k=0}^{K-1}C_{\mathrm{sub},k}(\eta_k).\]
The chosen resource and stopping predicate are part of the model.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Each convex DCA subproblem is charged according to the work needed for its requested solution accuracy, and total inner work is summed across outer iterations.
assumptions_latex: \(Q_k\) is a proper convex subproblem objective with \(Q_k^*>-\infty\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(W_{\mathrm{sub}}(K)=\sum_{k=0}^{K-1}C_{\mathrm{sub},k}(\eta_k)\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The accuracy-dependent accounting definition is internally coherent and appropriately typed. A source is needed to connect this model and objective-gap stopping predicate to inexact DCA.

children.title: Coupled Accuracy Budgets
children.top_down_role: Allocation of accuracy across oracle evaluation and subproblem solution.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Coupled Accuracy Budgets
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Abstract allocation of oracle and subproblem errors after an outer analysis has specified their propagation weights.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\delta_k,\eta_k\ge0\). If the applicable inexact-DCA estimate depends on these errors through \(e_k=c_{\mathrm{or},k}\delta_k+c_{\mathrm{sub},k}\eta_k\), with nonnegative weights fixed by that estimate, then a finite-horizon budget is \(\sum_{k=0}^{K-1}e_k\le B_K\). When the outer convergence theorem requires summable perturbations, the corresponding asymptotic budget is \(\sum_{k=0}^{\infty}e_k<\infty\). Neither additivity nor summability is a universal DCA requirement; both are conditional on the chosen perturbation theorem.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Oracle and subproblem accuracies may be traded within the combined error budget specified by the applicable outer analysis.
assumptions_latex: The outer perturbation estimate uses the declared combined errors \(e_k\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\sum_{k=0}^{K-1}e_k\le B_K\), or \(\sum_{k=0}^{\infty}e_k<\infty\) when summability is the outer theorem's hypothesis.
knowledge_statements.title: Coupled Accuracy Budgets

children.title: End-to-End Complexity Accounting
children.top_down_role: Combination of outer DCA progress with inner computational costs.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: End-to-End Complexity Accounting
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Composition rule for outer iterations, accuracy schedules, and compatible component costs.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Suppose a declared \(\varepsilon\)-certificate is guaranteed after at most \(K(\varepsilon)\) outer iterations under tolerances \((\delta_k,\eta_k)\). If all costs use the same resource unit, then total work satisfies
\[W(\varepsilon)\le\sum_{k=0}^{K(\varepsilon)-1}\bigl(C_{\mathrm{out},k}+C_{\mathrm{or},k}(\delta_k)+C_{\mathrm{sub},k}(\eta_k)\bigr).\]
A numerical order bound follows only after substituting an outer horizon, a compatible tolerance schedule, and component cost laws.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: End-to-end work is the sum of compatible outer, oracle, and subproblem costs over the iterations needed for the declared certificate.
assumptions_latex: \(K(\varepsilon)\) is valid for the declared certificate and tolerance schedule.
All component costs measure the same computational resource.
Each component bound applies at its scheduled tolerance.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: W(\varepsilon)\le\sum_{k=0}^{K(\varepsilon)-1}(C_{\mathrm{out},k}+C_{\mathrm{or},k}(\delta_k)+C_{\mathrm{sub},k}(\eta_k)).

notation.meaning: outer horizon for the declared epsilon-certificate

knowledge_statements.title: End-to-End Complexity Accounting

children.title: Quasi-DC Algorithm-Convergence Theory
children.top_down_role: Algorithms and convergence results driven by quasidifferential, directed-subdifferential, codifferential, or convex-approximator models.

top_down_textbook_witnesses.source: Introduction to Nonsmooth Optimization: Theory, Practice and Software

knowledge_statements.title: Quasidifferential Criticality
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Unconstrained first-order criticality for a quasidifferentiable function on a finite-dimensional space.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) be directionally differentiable at \(x\), with quasidifferential \([\underline\partial f(x),\overline\partial f(x)]\), meaning that for every \(d\in\mathbb R^n\),
\[f'(x;d)=\max_{u\in\underline\partial f(x)}\langle u,d\rangle+\min_{v\in\overline\partial f(x)}\langle v,d\rangle,\]
where both sets are nonempty compact convex sets. The point \(x\) is quasidifferentially critical for unconstrained minimization when
\[f'(x;d)\ge0\quad\text{for every }d\in\mathbb R^n.\]
Equivalently, for the displayed quasidifferential representative,
\[-\overline\partial f(x)\subseteq\underline\partial f(x).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A point is quasidifferentially critical when every directional derivative is nonnegative, equivalently when the negative upper quasidifferential is contained in the lower quasidifferential.
assumptions_latex: \(\underline\partial f(x)\) and \(\overline\partial f(x)\) are nonempty compact convex sets.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x\) is critical exactly when \(f'(x;d)\ge0\) for all \(d\), equivalently \(-\overline\partial f(x)\subseteq\underline\partial f(x)\).

notation.meaning: directional derivative at x along d

source_witnesses.locator: 3.4.2 Relationship Between Quasidifferential and Clarke Subdifferential p. 109

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Criticality Is Not Sufficient for Minimality
knowledge_statements.scope_note: First-order sufficiency boundary for unconstrained quasidifferential criticality.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(f(t)=t^3\), \(f'(0;d)=0\) for every \(d\in\mathbb R\). Thus \(0\) is quasidifferentially critical, but it is neither a local minimizer nor a local maximizer.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The cubic is quasidifferentially critical at the origin without having a local extremum there.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(0\) is quasidifferentially critical but is not a local minimizer.
knowledge_statements.title: Criticality Is Not Sufficient for Minimality

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Local-Minimum Necessity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Unconstrained first-order necessity for a quasidifferentiable function.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) is quasidifferentiable at an unconstrained local minimizer \(x\), then \[f'(x;d)\ge0\qquad\forall d\in\mathbb R^n,\] equivalently \[-\overline\partial f(x)\subseteq\underline\partial f(x).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every unconstrained local minimizer of a quasidifferentiable function is quasidifferentially critical.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(-\overline\partial f(x)\subseteq\underline\partial f(x)\).
knowledge_statements.title: Local-Minimum Necessity
Directed-Subdifferential Criticality
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Criticality expressed through the directed-set embedding of a quasidifferential.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) be quasidifferentiable at \(x\), with representative \([A,B]=[\underline\partial f(x),\overline\partial f(x)]\). Under the directed-set embedding \(J_n\), define the directed subdifferential by
\[\vec\partial f(x)=J_n(A)-J_n(-B).\]
The point \(x\) is directed-subdifferentially critical for unconstrained minimization when the directional derivative encoded by \(\vec\partial f(x)\) is nonnegative in every direction. For the representative above, this condition is
\[f'(x;d)\ge0\quad\text{for all }d\in\mathbb R^n,\]
equivalently \(-B\subseteq A\). The condition is invariant under equivalent quasidifferential representatives.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Directed-subdifferential criticality requires the encoded directional derivative to be nonnegative in every direction; in a quasidifferential representative, this is the inclusion of negative upper into lower sets.
assumptions_latex: \(A\) and \(B\) are nonempty compact convex quasidifferential sets.
\(J_n\) is the directed-set embedding of compact convex subsets of \(\mathbb R^n\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x\) is directed-subdifferentially critical exactly when \(f'(x;d)\ge0\) for all \(d\), equivalently \(-B\subseteq A\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition depends on convention-sensitive directed-set notation, especially the embedding and subtraction signs. An authoritative source is required before the displayed representation and claimed invariance can be relied upon.

assumptions_latex: The zero-scalar slices \(A_x=\{v:(0,v)\in\underline d f(x)\}\) and \(B_x=\{w:(0,w)\in\overline d f(x)\}\) are nonempty compact convex sets.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(-B_x\subseteq A_x\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Unconstrained first-order criticality under the max-plus-min codifferential convention.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For every direction \(h\in\mathbb{R}^n\), suppose the directional derivative is represented by \[f'(x;h)=\max_{v\in A_x}\langle v,h\rangle+\min_{w\in B_x}\langle w,h\rangle.\] The point \(x\) is codifferentially critical when \[f'(x;h)\ge 0\quad\text{for every }h\in\mathbb{R}^n,\] equivalently, under the stated compact-convex representation, when \[-B_x\subseteq A_x.\] This condition is necessary for \(x\) to be a local minimizer of a directionally differentiable codifferentiable function.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Codifferential criticality means that every directional derivative is nonnegative; equivalently, the negative upper zero-slice lies inside the lower zero-slice.
knowledge_statements.title: Codifferential Criticality

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The support-function equivalence is mathematically consistent with the stated max-plus-min convention, and the content kind fits the criticality container. An inspectable source is required for this convention and its local-minimum necessary condition.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Constrained Quasi-DC Criticality
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Pointwise constrained criticality for a support-function-difference directional model.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(x\in X\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) and suppose \(f'_H(x;d)=\sigma_A(d)-\sigma_C(d)\), where \(A,C\) are nonempty compact convex sets. The point \(x\) is constrained quasi-DC critical when \[\sigma_A(d)-\sigma_C(d)\ge0\qquad\forall d\in T_X(x).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A feasible point is constrained quasi-DC critical when its directional model is nonnegative on the contingent tangent cone.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(f'_H(x;d)\ge0\) for every \(d\in T_X(x)\).

notation.meaning: contingent tangent cone to X at x

knowledge_statements.title: Constrained Quasi-DC Criticality

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Fixed-Direction Differentiability Is Insufficient on Contingent Directions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Regularity boundary for the tangent-cone necessary condition.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Ordinary one-sided directional differentiability controls quotients along each fixed direction but not necessarily along sequences \(t_k\downarrow0\), \(d_k\to d\) realizing \(d\in T_X(x)\). Hence local minimality and ordinary directional differentiability alone do not generally imply nonnegativity on all of \(T_X(x)\); Hadamard directional differentiability or another suitable uniform directional regularity condition is needed.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A contingent-tangent Fermat condition cannot generally be inferred from fixed-direction differentiability alone.
assumptions_latex: Only ordinary one-sided directional differentiability is assumed.
Contingent directions may be realized by varying feasible directions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The full tangent-cone necessity implication is unavailable without additional uniform directional regularity.
knowledge_statements.title: Fixed-Direction Differentiability Is Insufficient on Contingent Directions

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Convex Feasible-Displacement Equivalence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equivalent criticality test for a convex feasible set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(X\) is convex, \(x\in X\), and \(m(d)=\sigma_A(d)-\sigma_C(d)\), then \[m(d)\ge0\ \forall d\in T_X(x)\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad m(y-x)\ge0\ \forall y\in X.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a convex feasible set, tangent-cone nonnegativity is equivalent to nonnegativity along every feasible displacement.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(m\ge0\) on \(T_X(x)\) exactly when \(m(y-x)\ge0\) for all \(y\in X\).

notation.meaning: continuous positively homogeneous quasi-DC directional model

knowledge_statements.title: Convex Feasible-Displacement Equivalence

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Hadamard Directional Fermat Condition
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Necessary constrained quasi-DC criticality at a local minimizer.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(x\) is a local minimizer of \(f\) over \(X\), \(f\) is Hadamard directionally differentiable at \(x\), and \(f'_H(x;d)=\sigma_A(d)-\sigma_C(d)\), then \[f'_H(x;d)\ge0\qquad\forall d\in T_X(x).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A constrained local minimizer is quasi-DC critical when the directional derivative is Hadamard directional.
assumptions_latex: \(x\) is a local minimizer of \(f\) over \(X\).
The derivative has the stated support-function-difference representation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\sigma_A(d)-\sigma_C(d)\ge0\) for every \(d\in T_X(x)\).
knowledge_statements.title: Hadamard Directional Fermat Condition

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Selected Convex-Programming Direction Step
knowledge_statements.scope_note: One quasi-DC descent step obtained by convexifying a selected concave-side support term.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(m(d)=\sigma_A(d)-\sigma_C(d)\), choose \(c\in C\), and let \(H\succ0\). Compute the unique minimizer \[d_c=\operatorname*{argmin}_d\left\{q_c(d):=\sigma_A(d)-\langle c,d\rangle+\tfrac12\langle Hd,d\rangle\right\}.\] If \(d_c\ne0\), then \(m(d_c)<0\), and the direction may be passed to a sufficient-decrease globalization procedure. If \(d_c=0\), only the selected condition \(c\in A\) has been certified.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Select a concave-side vector, solve a strongly convex support-function program, and globalize a nonzero solution; a zero solution is only a selected-model certificate.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(d_c\ne0\Rightarrow m(d_c)<0\), while \(d_c=0\Rightarrow c\in A\).
knowledge_statements.title: Selected Convex-Programming Direction Step

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Uniform Selected-Subproblem Criticality Certificate
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact full quasi-DC criticality test obtained by quantifying over the concave-side set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(d_c\) denote the selected-subproblem minimizer for every \(c\in C\). Then \[m(d)=\sigma_A(d)-\sigma_C(d)\ge0\ \forall d\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad C\subseteq A\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad d_c=0\ \forall c\in C.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: All selected convex programs return zero exactly when the complete quasi-DC model is nonnegative.
assumptions_latex: A positive-definite regularizer is used for each selected subproblem.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(m\ge0\) on \(\mathbb R^n\Longleftrightarrow d_c=0\) for every \(c\in C\).
knowledge_statements.title: Uniform Selected-Subproblem Criticality Certificate

knowledge_statements.statement_title: One Selected Zero Direction Is Not Full Criticality
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Stopping-rule boundary for selected convex-programming steps.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A zero solution for one selected \(c\in C\) establishes only \(c\in A\). Since \(c\in A\) need not imply \(C\subseteq A\), stopping after one selected zero direction does not generally certify full quasi-DC criticality.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A single selected zero direction is only a selected-model certificate.
assumptions_latex: Only one element \(c\in C\) has been tested.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(d_c=0\) does not generally imply \(m(d)\ge0\) for every \(d\).
knowledge_statements.title: One Selected Zero Direction Is Not Full Criticality

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Selected Zero-Solution Characterization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact interpretation of a zero direction for one selected concave-side element.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \[q_c(d)=\sigma_A(d)-\langle c,d\rangle+\tfrac12\langle Hd,d\rangle\] with \(H\succ0\), its unique minimizer satisfies \[d_c=0\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad c\in A.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The selected convex program returns zero exactly when the selected concave-side vector lies in the support-side set.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(d_c=0\Longleftrightarrow c\in A\).
knowledge_statements.title: Selected Zero-Solution Characterization

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Finite Generator-Selection Algorithm for Polytopal Upper Sets
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Implementable exhaustive selection rule when the concave-side support set is supplied by finitely many generators.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(A\subset\mathbb R^n\) be nonempty compact convex and let \(C=\operatorname{conv}\{c_1,\ldots,c_m\}\). For each generator solve
\[
d_j=\operatorname*{argmin}_d\left\{\sigma_A(d)-\langle c_j,d\rangle+\tfrac12\langle Hd,d\rangle\right\},\qquad H\succ0.
\]
If some \(d_j\ne0\), then \(\sigma_A(d_j)-\sigma_C(d_j)<0\), so \(d_j\) is a strict quasi-DC model-descent direction. If \(d_j=0\) for every \(j\), then every \(c_j\in A\), hence \(C\subseteq A\) and the full model is nonnegative in every direction. Thus at most \(m\) strongly convex subproblems produce descent or certify full criticality.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a finitely generated upper polytope, testing every generator through its selected convex subproblem finitely produces a strict model-descent direction or certifies inclusion of the entire upper set.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\exists j:d_j\ne0\Rightarrow \sigma_A(d_j)-\sigma_C(d_j)<0\); otherwise \(C\subseteq A\), after at most \(m\) selected subproblem solves.

notation.meaning: explicit generator of the concave-side polytope

knowledge_statements.title: Finite Generator-Selection Algorithm for Polytopal Upper Sets

assumptions_latex: \(H_k\) is symmetric positive definite and \(c_k\in C_k\) is selected.
A line search accepts a positive step satisfying a prescribed sufficient-decrease test.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The convex subproblem produces either the zero criticality certificate or a direction with negative selected quasi-DC model value.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A proximal convex-programming realization of quasi-DC descent.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given \(x_k\), choose \(c_k\in C_k\) and solve the strongly convex program \[d_k\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{d\in\mathbb{R}^n}\left\{\sigma_{A_k}(d)-\langle c_k,d\rangle+\tfrac12\langle H_kd,d\rangle\right\}.\] If \(d_k=0\), stop and return the corresponding selected-model criticality certificate. Otherwise choose \(t_k>0\) by sufficient decrease and set \[x_{k+1}=x_k+t_kd_k.\] The optimality comparison with \(d=0\) gives \(q_k(d_k)\le0\), with strict model descent whenever \(d_k\ne0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Select one concave-side subgradient, solve a strongly convex directional subproblem, stop at a zero direction, or line-search along the computed descent direction.
knowledge_statements.title: Convex-Programming Quasi-DC Descent

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The strongly convex subproblem is a plausible algorithm for this container, but the precise quasi-DC construction and interpretation of a zero direction as a selected-model criticality certificate require a source.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Directed-Distance Form of the Steepest Quasidifferential Value
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact finite-dimensional reformulation for the support-function-difference convention used by the deferred seed.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A,C\subset\mathbb R^n\) be nonempty compact convex sets and \(m(d)=\sigma_A(d)-\sigma_C(d)\). For a norm \(\|\cdot\|\) on directions and its dual norm \(\|\cdot\|_*\), \[\min_{\|d\|\le1}m(d)=-\max_{c\in C}\operatorname{dist}_{\|\cdot\|_*}(c,A).\] Consequently the steepest value is zero exactly when \(C\subseteq A\), and it is negative otherwise.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The exact steepest quasidifferential value is the negative directed distance from the second model set to the first; zero value is equivalent to set inclusion.
assumptions_latex: \(A\) and \(C\) are nonempty compact convex subsets of a finite-dimensional space.
The distance uses the norm dual to the direction norm.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\min_{\|d\|\le1}m(d)=-\max_{c\in C}\operatorname{dist}_{\|\cdot\|_*}(c,A)\), with value zero iff \(C\subseteq A\).

notation.meaning: distance from c to A in the dual norm

knowledge_statements.title: Directed-Distance Form of the Steepest Quasidifferential Value

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Exact Polytopal Steepest-Direction Algorithm
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite exact solution of the Euclidean steepest quasidifferential direction problem when the upper set has explicit generators.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(A\subset\mathbb R^n\) be nonempty compact convex and let \(C=\operatorname{conv}\{c_1,\ldots,c_m\}\). Compute Euclidean projections \(p_j=P_A(c_j)\) and choose \(j_*\in\operatorname*{argmax}_j\|c_j-p_j\|_2\). Put \(\delta=\|c_{j_*}-p_{j_*}\|_2\). If \(\delta=0\), then \(C\subseteq A\) and the steepest value is zero. If \(\delta>0\), then
\[
d_* = \frac{c_{j_*}-p_{j_*}}{\delta}
\]
solves
\[
\min_{\|d\|_2\le1}\{\sigma_A(d)-\sigma_C(d)\}=-\delta.
\]
Thus the exact direction is obtained using \(m\) convex projection problems and one finite maximum.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For an explicitly generated upper polytope, project every generator onto the lower set and use a farthest generator to construct an exact Euclidean steepest direction.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\min_{\|d\|_2\le1}(\sigma_A(d)-\sigma_C(d))=-\max_{1\le j\le m}\operatorname{dist}_2(c_j,A)\), attained by the displayed \(d_*\) when the maximum is positive.
knowledge_statements.title: Exact Polytopal Steepest-Direction Algorithm

knowledge_statements.statement_title: A Local Farthest Point Need Not Give the Steepest Direction
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sharp computational boundary for local solution of the directed-distance maximization problem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: In \(\mathbb R\), let \(A=\{0\}\) and \(C=[-2,1]\). The point \(c=1\) is a one-sided strict local maximizer of \(c\mapsto\operatorname{dist}(c,A)=|c|\) over \(C\), but its value is \(1\), whereas the global maximum is \(2\) at \(c=-2\). The direction generated by \(c=1\) is \(d=1\) with model value \(-1\), while the exact steepest direction is \(d=-1\) with model value \(-2\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A locally farthest upper-set point can yield a descent direction that is not the exact quasidifferential steepest direction.
assumptions_latex: The norm is the absolute value.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(c=1\) is locally but not globally farthest from \(A\), and its generated direction has model value \(-1>-2\).
knowledge_statements.title: A Local Farthest Point Need Not Give the Steepest Direction

assumptions_latex: The unit ball is defined by a chosen norm \(\|\cdot\|\).
A step length is chosen to decrease \(f\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A negative optimal value yields a unit direction of steepest decrease for the quasi-DC directional model.

notation.meaning: steepest model value on the unit ball

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact steepest descent for a positively homogeneous quasidifferential model.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At iterate \(x_k\), compute \[d_k\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{\|d\|\le1}\{m_k(d):=\sigma_{A_k}(d)-\sigma_{C_k}(d)\},\qquad \theta_k=m_k(d_k).\] If \(\theta_k=0\), stop with directional criticality. If \(\theta_k<0\), choose \(t_k>0\) by a decrease line search and update \(x_{k+1}=x_k+t_kd_k\). Because \(m_k\) is positively homogeneous, \(d_k\) minimizes the first-order directional model among all normalized directions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Minimize the quasidifferential directional model on the unit ball; stop at value zero or line-search along a negative-model direction.
knowledge_statements.title: Quasidifferential Steepest Descent

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The exact unit-ball minimization correctly describes steepest descent for the stated homogeneous model, but its use as a quasidifferential algorithm, including global solution of the generally nonconvex direction problem, lacks supporting evidence.

assumptions_latex: \(f=g-h\) on a convex set \(X\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\), where \(g,h\) are proper convex functions finite at the iterates.
The convexized subproblem has a minimizer.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The update minimizes a convex majorizing model obtained by affine linearization of the subtracted convex term.

notation.meaning: subgradient of the subtracted convex component

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Classical DC linearization used as the canonical quasi-DC linearization step.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Initialize \(x_0\in X\). At iteration \(k\), select \(u_k\in\partial h(x_k)\) and compute \[x_{k+1}\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in X}\left\{g(x)-h(x_k)-\langle u_k,x-x_k\rangle\right\}.\] Convexity gives \(h(x)\ge h(x_k)+\langle u_k,x-x_k\rangle\), hence \(f(x)\le M_k(x)\) and \(f(x_k)=M_k(x_k)\). Stop when a specified iterate, objective, or stationarity residual tolerance is met.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Linearize the convex term that is subtracted in a DC decomposition, then minimize the resulting convex majorizing model.
knowledge_statements.title: Quasi-DC Linearization Methods

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The displayed update is the classical DC linearization algorithm and its majorization inequality is correct. A source is needed to establish that this classical DC specialization appropriately fills the broader quasi-DC terminal container.

assumptions_latex: \(f\) is codifferentiable at every iterate, with compact codifferential sets \(\underline d f(x_k)\) and \(\overline d f(x_k)\).
A rule selects an upper element and a compatible lower element defining a descent vector.
A decrease line search is available whenever the selected directional derivative is negative.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Each nonterminal iteration uses codifferential data to obtain a negative-directional-derivative step.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Generic codifferential descent template; selection details depend on the codifferential convention.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At \(x_k\), choose \((b_k,w_k)\in\overline d f(x_k)\), then select \((a_k,v_k)\) from the translated set \(\underline d f(x_k)+(b_k,w_k)\) according to the method's minimum-norm or model-minimization rule. If the resulting criticality residual vanishes, stop. Otherwise set \(d_k=-v_k\), verify \(f'(x_k;d_k)<0\), choose \(t_k>0\) by sufficient decrease, and update \[x_{k+1}=x_k+t_kd_k.\] The output is either a codifferential criticality certificate or a decreased objective value.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Select compatible lower and upper codifferential elements, form a descent direction, and globalize it by sufficient-decrease line search.
knowledge_statements.title: Codifferential Descent Methods

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The content kind fits the descent-method container, but no precise selection rule or codifferential normalization is given that guarantees the translated-set vector produces a negative directional derivative. The algorithm is therefore not reliable without a convention-specific source.

assumptions_latex: \(f\) is directionally differentiable and \(m_k(d)=f'(x_k;d)\) is the quasi-DC directional model.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The accepted step satisfies \(f(x_{k+1})\le f(x_k)+\eta t_km_k(d_k)<f(x_k)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Armijo backtracking applied to an exact quasi-DC directional model.

source_refs.locator: 2.5.1 Unconstrained problems: Armijo line search p. 89

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given \(x_k\) and \(d_k\) with \(m_k(d_k)<0\), choose the smallest integer \(j_k\ge0\) such that, for \(t_k=\bar t\beta^{j_k}\), \[f(x_k+t_kd_k)\le f(x_k)+\eta t_km_k(d_k).\] Set \(x_{k+1}=x_k+t_kd_k\). Directional differentiability and strict negativity of \(m_k(d_k)\) ensure that the test holds for all sufficiently small positive trial steps.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Backtrack along a negative quasi-DC model direction until the actual decrease is at least a fixed fraction of the predicted first-order decrease.
knowledge_statements.title: Quasi-DC Line-Search Methods

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Strict Model Descent Is Required for the Local Acceptance Guarantee
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary of finite Armijo acceptance based solely on a directional derivative.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Directional differentiability guarantees eventual Armijo acceptance when \(m_k(d_k)<0\), but not when \(m_k(d_k)\ge0\). For \(f(x)=x^2\), \(x_k=0\), and \(d_k\ne0\), one has \(m_k(d_k)=0\), whereas \(f(x_k+td_k)=t^2d_k^2>f(x_k)+\eta t m_k(d_k)\) for every \(t>0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A zero directional model value can prevent every positive Armijo step, even for a smooth objective.
assumptions_latex: The Armijo right-hand side uses the exact directional model value.
Strict model descent is not assumed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Directional differentiability alone does not guarantee existence of an acceptable positive step.
knowledge_statements.title: Strict Model Descent Is Required for the Local Acceptance Guarantee

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Uniform Armijo Step-Size Lower Bound
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Quantitative geometric-backtracking bound under uniform quadratic model accuracy.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose \(m_k(d_k)\le-c\|d_k\|^2\) and \[f(x_k+td_k)\le f(x_k)+t m_k(d_k)+\frac L2t^2\|d_k\|^2\] for every trial \(t\in[0,\bar t]\), with \(c,L>0\). Then every \(t\le2(1-\eta)c/L\) satisfies the Armijo test, and geometric backtracking returns \[t_k\ge\beta\min\left\{\bar t,\frac{2(1-\eta)c}{L}\right\}>0.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Uniform quadratic model accuracy and uniform model descent prevent accepted Armijo steps from collapsing to zero.
assumptions_latex: The displayed upper estimate holds with uniform \(L>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(t_k\ge\beta\min\{\bar t,2(1-\eta)c/L\}>0\).
knowledge_statements.title: Uniform Armijo Step-Size Lower Bound

assumptions_latex: \(f\) is finite near \(x_k\), and \(M_k(d)\) is a quasi-DC model with \(M_k(0)=f(x_k)\).
The trust-region subproblem over \(\|d\|\le\Delta_k\) yields a trial step with positive predicted reduction.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The ratio of actual to predicted reduction determines acceptance and trust-region-radius adjustment.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Standard trust-region globalization with a quasi-DC local model.

source_refs.locator: 8.4 Trust Region Methods p. 771
source_refs.source_title: Finite-Dimensional Variational Inequalities and Complementarity Problems, Vol. II

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Compute an approximate solution \(d_k\) of \[\min_{\|d\|\le\Delta_k}M_k(d),\] with predicted reduction \(p_k=M_k(0)-M_k(d_k)>0\). Define \[\rho_k=\frac{f(x_k)-f(x_k+d_k)}{p_k}.\] Accept \(x_{k+1}=x_k+d_k\) when \(\rho_k\ge\eta_1\), and otherwise set \(x_{k+1}=x_k\). Decrease \(\Delta_k\) for poor agreement and permit an increase when \(\rho_k\ge\eta_2\) and the step is near the trust-region boundary.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Minimize a quasi-DC model inside a radius, compare actual and predicted reduction, then accept or reject the step and update the radius.
knowledge_statements.title: Quasi-DC Trust-Region Methods

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Uniform First-Order Model Agreement
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Model-accuracy condition ensuring agreement ratios approach one along shrinking accepted-model trials.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Along a subsequence \(K\), suppose \(M_k(0)=f(x_k)\) and \[\sup_{0<\|d\|\le\Delta_k}\frac{|f(x_k+d)-M_k(d)|}{\|d\|}\longrightarrow0\qquad(k\to\infty,\ k\in K).\] If trial steps satisfy \(p_k=M_k(0)-M_k(d_k)\ge c\|d_k\|>0\) for a constant \(c>0\), then \(\rho_k=[f(x_k)-f(x_k+d_k)]/p_k\to1\) along \(K\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Uniform little-o model error and first-order predicted decrease make actual and predicted reductions asymptotically agree.
assumptions_latex: The displayed model error tends to zero uniformly on each shrinking trust region.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\rho_k\to1\) along the shrinking-radius subsequence.
knowledge_statements.title: Uniform First-Order Model Agreement

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Nonpositive Predicted Reduction Invalidates the Agreement Ratio
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Necessary domain and interpretation condition for ratio-based trust-region acceptance.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The standard ratio \(\rho_k=[f(x_k)-f(x_k+d_k)]/[M_k(0)-M_k(d_k)]\) is undefined when predicted reduction is zero and is not a descent-quality ratio when predicted reduction is negative. Hence a trial with \(M_k(0)-M_k(d_k)\le0\) must trigger termination, model improvement, or a new trial rather than standard ratio-based acceptance.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The standard trust-region agreement test requires strictly positive predicted reduction.
assumptions_latex: Trial acceptance is based on the actual-to-predicted reduction ratio.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(M_k(0)-M_k(d_k)>0\) is necessary for the standard agreement test.
knowledge_statements.title: Nonpositive Predicted Reduction Invalidates the Agreement Ratio

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Abstract Trust-Region Subsequential Criticality
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Proposed generic convergence theorem for an unspecified quasi-DC model and radius-update mechanism.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If sufficient model decrease, quadratic model accuracy, and stated radius-management conditions hold, then the proposal claims \(\liminf_k\chi_k=0\) and criticality of consistent cluster limits.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The proposal attempts to infer subsequential criticality from abstract trust-region conditions.
assumptions_latex: The criticality measure and quasi-DC model class are unspecified.
The stated radius conditions do not fully prevent radius collapse away from criticality.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The proposed conclusion is not accepted under the stated hypotheses.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Certified Exact Criticality and Descent Bounds
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Correct orientation of criticality and descent certificates under uniform model error and an inexact approximate-model solve.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\theta_k=\min_{\|d\|\le1}m_k(d)\), suppose \(\sup_{\|d\|\le1}|\widetilde m_k(d)-m_k(d)|\le\varepsilon_k\), and let \(d_k\) satisfy \(\widetilde m_k(d_k)\le\min_{\|d\|\le1}\widetilde m_k(d)+\delta_k\). Then \[0\le-\theta_k\le-\widetilde m_k(d_k)+\varepsilon_k+\delta_k.\] Moreover, \(\widetilde m_k(d_k)<-\varepsilon_k\) certifies \(m_k(d_k)<0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The approximate optimum plus known model and solver errors gives an upper bound on exact directional noncriticality, while sufficiently negative approximate value certifies true descent.
assumptions_latex: The exact and approximate models differ uniformly by at most \(\varepsilon_k\) on the unit ball.
The computed direction is \(\delta_k\)-optimal for the approximate model.
Both directional models vanish at zero, so \(\theta_k\le0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(-\theta_k\le-\widetilde m_k(d_k)+\varepsilon_k+\delta_k\), and \(\widetilde m_k(d_k)<-\varepsilon_k\Rightarrow m_k(d_k)<0\).
knowledge_statements.title: Certified Exact Criticality and Descent Bounds

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Persistent Model Error Can Produce False Criticality
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sharp boundary showing why a nonvanishing model-error allowance cannot certify exact criticality.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: On \(|d|\le1\), let the exact homogeneous model be \(m(d)=d\), so \(\min m=-1\), and let the approximate model be \(\widetilde m(d)=0\). The uniform error is \(\varepsilon=1\), every direction is an exact minimizer of \(\widetilde m\), and choosing \(d=0\) reports zero approximate model value although the exact model has strict descent. Thus persistent error can create false approximate criticality.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A flat approximate model can declare criticality while the exact directional model still has a strict descent direction.
assumptions_latex: No requirement forces the uniform model error to vanish or be small relative to the exact criticality gap.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Zero approximate model value does not imply exact directional criticality when \(\varepsilon>0\).
knowledge_statements.title: Persistent Model Error Can Produce False Criticality

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Adaptive Relative-Accuracy Refinement
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Accuracy refinement until certified model error is dominated by predicted descent.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Compute \(d_k\), \(\varepsilon_k\), and \(\delta_k\) with \(\widetilde m_k(d_k)\le\inf_{\|d\|\le1}\widetilde m_k(d)+\delta_k\). For fixed \(\gamma\in(0,1)\), refine while \[\varepsilon_k+\delta_k>\gamma[-\widetilde m_k(d_k)]_+.\] If refinement terminates with \(q_k=-\widetilde m_k(d_k)>0\), then \[m_k(d_k)\le-q_k+\varepsilon_k\le-(1-\gamma)q_k<0.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Refining until certified errors are a fixed fraction of predicted descent yields an exact-model descent certificate.
assumptions_latex: Uniform model-error and subproblem-tolerance bounds are computable.
The refinement mechanism can reduce the aggregate error when a nonzero descent gap exists.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Termination with \(q_k>0\) certifies \(m_k(d_k)<0\).
knowledge_statements.title: Adaptive Relative-Accuracy Refinement

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Hausdorff-to-Directional-Model Error Transfer
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Transfer from quasidifferential-set approximation to uniform directional-model approximation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(m(d)=\sigma_A(d)-\sigma_C(d)\) and \(\widetilde m(d)=\sigma_{\widetilde A}(d)-\sigma_{\widetilde C}(d)\), where all four sets are nonempty compact convex sets. If \(d_H(A,\widetilde A)\le\alpha\) and \(d_H(C,\widetilde C)\le\beta\), then \[|\widetilde m(d)-m(d)|\le(\alpha+\beta)\|d\|.\] Hence the unit-ball model error is at most \(\alpha+\beta\). No converse controls the individual set errors: translating both sets by the same vector leaves their support-function difference unchanged.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Hausdorff errors in the two model sets add, but directional-model error cannot recover the individual set errors.
assumptions_latex: All model sets are nonempty, compact, and convex.
Hausdorff distance uses the norm dual to the directional norm.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\sup_{\|d\|\le1}|\widetilde m(d)-m(d)|\le\alpha+\beta\), without a converse for the individual Hausdorff errors.
knowledge_statements.title: Hausdorff-to-Directional-Model Error Transfer

assumptions_latex: The exact model is \(m_k(d)=\sigma_{A_k}(d)-\sigma_{C_k}(d)\) on the unit ball.
An approximate model \(\widetilde m_k\) satisfies \(\sup_{\|d\|\le1}|\widetilde m_k(d)-m_k(d)|\le\varepsilon_k\).
The computed direction is \(\delta_k\)-optimal for minimizing \(\widetilde m_k\) on the unit ball.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The exact steepest-model residual is bounded by the computed residual plus \(2\varepsilon_k+\delta_k\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Inexact steepest-model template with explicit representation and subproblem errors.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Choose \(d_k\) with \(\|d_k\|\le1\) satisfying \[\widetilde m_k(d_k)\le\inf_{\|d\|\le1}\widetilde m_k(d)+\delta_k.\] Then \[m_k(d_k)\le\inf_{\|d\|\le1}m_k(d)+2\varepsilon_k+\delta_k.\] If the computed negative value dominates the error bound, globalize \(d_k\) by line search or a trust region. Otherwise return the residual \(-\widetilde m_k(d_k)+2\varepsilon_k+\delta_k\) as an approximate criticality measure. Convergence analyses typically require the aggregate error to vanish along relevant subsequences.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Minimize an approximate quasidifferential model while tracking representation and solver errors; these errors explicitly bound the true directional criticality residual.
knowledge_statements.title: Approximate-Quasidifferential Methods

The quasi-DC procedure accepts such vectors only with a recorded approximation tolerance.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At scale \(\lambda>0\), a discrete-gradient oracle evaluates finite differences near \(x\) and returns \(g_\lambda(x)\). Collections of such vectors are convexified to form a computable set \[G_\lambda(x)=\operatorname{co}\{g_\lambda^{1}(x),\ldots,g_\lambda^{r}(x)\}.\] In a quasi-DC method, \(G_\lambda(x)\) replaces or approximates one convex component of the directional representation. The interface must report \(\lambda\) and a model-error bound so that descent or criticality tests account for approximation error.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Worst-Direction Residual Transfer
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Transfer of uniform directional-model error to an approximate criticality residual.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define \[\rho_f(x)=\max\{0,-\inf_{\|h\|\le1}f'(x;h)\},\qquad \rho_m(x)=\max\{0,-\inf_{\|h\|\le1}m_x(h)\}.\] Under \(|f'(x;h)-m_x(h)|\le\varepsilon\|h\|\), \[|\rho_f(x)-\rho_m(x)|\le\varepsilon.\] Consequently, \(\rho_m(x)\le\eta\) certifies \(f'(x;h)\ge-(\eta+\varepsilon)\|h\|\) for every \(h\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The true and model worst-direction residuals differ by at most the verified uniform model error.
assumptions_latex: The norm-scaled uniform error bound holds.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(|\rho_f(x)-\rho_m(x)|\le\varepsilon\).
knowledge_statements.title: Worst-Direction Residual Transfer

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Model and Accuracy Tolerances Add
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sharp tolerance bookkeeping for approximate directional criticality.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(\inf_{\|h\|\le1}m_x(h)\ge-\eta\) and \(|f'(x;h)-m_x(h)|\le\varepsilon\|h\|\), the guaranteed true bound is \[f'(x;h)\ge-(\eta+\varepsilon)\|h\|.\] In particular, taking \(\eta=\varepsilon\) gives a \(2\varepsilon\), not generally an \(\varepsilon\), guarantee.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Model-solution tolerance and model-accuracy tolerance add in the true criticality guarantee.
assumptions_latex: The model is nonnegative up to tolerance \(\eta\) on the unit ball.
The directional-model error is bounded by \(\varepsilon\|h\|\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The certified true tolerance is \(\eta+\varepsilon\).
knowledge_statements.title: Model and Accuracy Tolerances Add

assumptions_latex: \(m_x:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\) is a positively homogeneous directional model for \(f'(x;\cdot)\).
A known error bound satisfies \(|f'(x;h)-m_x(h)|\le\varepsilon\|h\|\) for every \(h\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If \(m_x(d)+\varepsilon<0\), then \(d\) is a certified strict descent direction.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A posteriori descent certificate for an inexact directional model.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The pair \((d,\varepsilon)\) is a directional-model descent certificate at \(x\) when \[\|d\|\le1\quad\text{and}\quad m_x(d)+\varepsilon<0.\] Indeed, the stated error bound directly yields \[f'(x;d)\le m_x(d)+\varepsilon\|d\|<0.\] The certificate is verifiable from the model value, the norm of \(d\), and the independently established error bound. If instead \(\inf_{\|h\|\le1}m_x(h)\ge-\varepsilon\), the same data certify only \(\varepsilon\)-directional criticality.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A direction is certified as descent when its negative model value strictly exceeds the verified directional-model error.
knowledge_statements.title: Directional-Model Certificates

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The strict-descent test is valid under the stated uniform error bound, but the final criticality claim is ambiguous: the same data generally yield a 2ε bound for the true directional derivative, not ε. The statement also contains proof-style derivation and lacks a source for the certificate formulation.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Exact Strongly Convex Subproblem Certificate
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Value and displacement certificate for an exactly solved regularized directional subproblem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(q(d)=m(d)+R(d)\) be proper closed and \(\mu\)-strongly convex, where \(q(0)=R(0)=0\), \(R(d)\ge0\), and \(\mu>0\). If \(d_*\) minimizes \(q\), then \[q(d_*)\le-\frac{\mu}{2}\|d_*\|^2.\] Consequently, \(d_*\ne0\) implies \(m(d_*)\le q(d_*)<0\), so \(d_*\) is a strict model-descent direction.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nonzero exact minimizer of a strongly convex regularized subproblem certifies strict descent for the underlying directional model.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(d_*\ne0\Longrightarrow m(d_*)<0\).
knowledge_statements.title: Exact Strongly Convex Subproblem Certificate

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Inexact Subgradient-Residual Certificate
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Computable optimality-gap bound for an inexact strongly convex subproblem solution.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(q\) is proper closed and \(\mu\)-strongly convex and \(s\in\partial q(d)\), then \[0\le q(d)-\inf_z q(z)\le\frac{\|s\|_*^2}{2\mu}.\] Thus \(\|s\|_*\) certifies subproblem inexactness. If additionally \(q=m+R\) with \(R\ge0\) and the computed value satisfies \(q(d)<0\), then \(m(d)<0\) independently of whether \(d\) is exact.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A subgradient norm bounds the strongly convex subproblem gap, while a negative computed value certifies model descent when the regularizer is nonnegative.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(q(d)-\inf q\le\|s\|_*^2/(2\mu)\), and \(q(d)<0\Rightarrow m(d)<0\).
knowledge_statements.title: Inexact Subgradient-Residual Certificate

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Subproblem Stationarity Need Not Be Full Quasi-DC Criticality
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary between a selected convex subproblem certificate and the complete quasi-DC condition.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The condition \(0\in\partial q(0)\) certifies optimality of the particular convex subproblem \(q\). When \(q\) is formed using a selected element or branch of a quasi-DC representation, this condition need not certify nonnegativity of the complete quasi-DC directional model. Full criticality requires the selection policy or an additional test to cover the entire representation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A zero residual for one selected subproblem is not automatically a certificate for the full quasi-DC model.
assumptions_latex: The convex subproblem represents only a selected component of the quasi-DC model.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Selected-subproblem optimality does not alone imply full quasi-DC criticality.
knowledge_statements.title: Subproblem Stationarity Need Not Be Full Quasi-DC Criticality

assumptions_latex: \(q_k\) is a proper closed \(\mu_k\)-strongly convex subproblem objective with \(q_k(0)=0\) and \(\mu_k>0\).
\(d_k\) minimizes \(q_k\), and a subgradient \(s_k\in\partial q_k(d_k)\) is available.
The directional model satisfies \(m_k(d)\le q_k(d)\) after removal of any explicitly recorded regularization term.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The primal value and subgradient residual certify approximate subproblem optimality and quantify predicted descent.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Primal-residual certificate for a strongly convex quasi-DC direction subproblem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For an exact minimizer, \(0\in\partial q_k(d_k)\) and comparison with \(d=0\) gives \(q_k(d_k)\le0\). More generally, if \(s_k\in\partial q_k(d_k)\), strong convexity yields the computable gap bound \[q_k(d_k)-\inf_d q_k(d)\le\frac{\|s_k\|_*^2}{2\mu_k}.\] Thus \(q_k(d_k)<0\), together with a sufficiently small residual \(\|s_k\|_*\), certifies predicted descent and quantified inexactness. A zero direction with \(0\in\partial q_k(0)\) certifies stationarity for the selected convex subproblem.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A negative convex-subproblem value certifies predicted descent, while a subgradient residual and strong convexity give a computable optimality-gap bound.
knowledge_statements.title: Convex-Subproblem Descent Certificates

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The strong-convexity gap inequality is standard, but the assumptions call d_k an exact minimizer while the statement develops an inexact residual certificate. The relation between q_k, its regularization, and m_k is not defined precisely enough to support predicted descent, and the record includes proof-style derivation without a source.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Zero-Residual Certificate
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact interpretation of simultaneous zero representation and criticality residuals.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Under the assumptions defining \((\delta_U,r_{g,h})\), \[\delta_U(f;g,h)=0\iff f=g-h\text{ on }U,\qquad r_{g,h}(x)=0\iff\partial g(x)\cap\partial h(x)\ne\varnothing.\] Hence simultaneous vanishing certifies an exact representation on \(U\) and DC criticality at \(x\) for that representation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Both residuals vanish exactly when the representation is exact and its convex subdifferentials intersect.
assumptions_latex: The residual pair is well defined.
The two subdifferentials are nonempty and compact.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\delta_U=r_{g,h}(x)=0\) certifies exact representation and fixed-decomposition DC criticality.
knowledge_statements.title: Zero-Residual Certificate

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Representation-and-Criticality Residual Pair
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Separate residuals for approximation of a function by a selected DC representation and criticality of that representation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f\) be finite on \(U\), let \(g,h\) be convex and finite on \(U\), and suppose \(\partial g(x),\partial h(x)\) are nonempty compact sets. Define \[\delta_U(f;g,h):=\sup_{z\in U}|f(z)-(g(z)-h(z))|,\qquad r_{g,h}(x):=\operatorname{dist}(\partial g(x),\partial h(x)).\] The ordered pair \((\delta_U,r_{g,h})\) records value-representation error separately from fixed-decomposition DC-criticality error.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Approximate DC representations require separate value-error and subdifferential-matching residuals.
assumptions_latex: \(\partial g(x)\) and \(\partial h(x)\) are nonempty compact sets.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\delta_U\) measures representation error, while \(r_{g,h}(x)\) measures criticality mismatch for the selected decomposition.
knowledge_statements.title: Representation-and-Criticality Residual Pair

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Selected-Pair Residual Is Only an Upper Bound
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary between arbitrary subgradient mismatch and intrinsic set distance.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For arbitrary \(u\in\partial g(x)\) and \(v\in\partial h(x)\), \[r_{g,h}(x)\le\|u-v\|.\] The inequality may be strict, so a nonzero selected-pair mismatch does not certify failure of intersection. Equality with the intrinsic residual requires a minimizing or controlled approximately minimizing pair; the special equality \(u=v\) does certify intersection.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An arbitrary subgradient pair can overstate criticality error and is not an intrinsic residual.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\|u-v\|\) cannot generally be identified with \(r_{g,h}(x)\).
knowledge_statements.title: Selected-Pair Residual Is Only an Upper Bound

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Value Accuracy Alone Does Not Control Criticality
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Separation between uniform representation error and derivative or subdifferential accuracy.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A small value residual \(\delta_U(f;g,h)\) alone does not generally bound directional-derivative error or the distance of \(x\) from a critical point of \(f\). Such a transfer requires additional derivative consistency, regularity, or scale-dependent error assumptions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Uniformly accurate function values do not by themselves provide a stationarity guarantee.
assumptions_latex: Only a uniform value-error bound is available.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: No general true-criticality estimate follows from \(\delta_U\) alone.
knowledge_statements.title: Value Accuracy Alone Does Not Control Criticality

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Criticality Residual Depends on the DC Representation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Representation dependence of subdifferential-matching residuals.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(f=g-h=\widetilde g-\widetilde h\), then \[\operatorname{dist}(\partial g(x),\partial h(x))\] and \[\operatorname{dist}(\partial\widetilde g(x),\partial\widetilde h(x))\] need not coincide. The residual is intrinsic to the selected DC representation, not generally to \(f\) alone.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Different DC decompositions of the same function can produce different numerical criticality residuals.
assumptions_latex: Two DC decompositions of the same function are given.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The subdifferential-distance residual is generally decomposition dependent.
knowledge_statements.title: Criticality Residual Depends on the DC Representation
Approximate-Representation Residuals
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A computable certificate for inexact convex representations and approximate DC criticality.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\overline{\mathbb R}\), let \(U\subset\mathbb R^n\), and let \(g_k,h_k\) be proper convex functions finite on \(U\). Given \(x_k\in U\), \(u_k\in\partial g_k(x_k)\), and \(v_k\in\partial h_k(x_k)\), define
\[
\delta_k(U):=\sup_{x\in U}|f(x)-(g_k(x)-h_k(x))|,
\qquad r_k:=\|u_k-v_k\|.
\]
The pair \((\delta_k(U),r_k)\) certifies representation error and approximate criticality: \(\delta_k(U)=0\) gives an exact DC representation on \(U\), while \(r_k=0\) gives \(\partial g_k(x_k)\cap\partial h_k(x_k)\ne\varnothing\). Vanishing residuals require both \(\delta_k(U)\to0\) and \(r_k\to0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The certificate separately measures error in the approximate DC representation and failure of the two convex subdifferentials to share a vector.
assumptions_latex: \(g_k,h_k\) are proper convex and finite on \(U\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\delta_k(U)=r_k=0\) certifies an exact local representation and DC criticality at \(x_k\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The certificate content kind fits the leaf, but no source or standard-field rationale is supplied. Moreover, r_k depends on arbitrary selected subgradients and therefore does not generally measure the distance between the two subdifferentials or their failure to intersect; only r_k=0 has the stated certification meaning. A source is needed to establish the intended residual convention.

children.title: Subsequential Convergence for Quasi-DC Descent
children.top_down_role: The legacy landmark is expanded by exactness, approximation, and constraint regimes.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Exact DC Fixed-Point Criticality
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equivalent criticality formulation for a fixed unconstrained DC decomposition.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For proper closed convex \(g,h\), a point \(\bar x\) satisfies \(\partial g(\bar x)\cap\partial h(\bar x)\ne\varnothing\) if and only if some \(\bar v\in\partial h(\bar x)\) makes \(\bar x\in\operatorname*{argmin}_y\{g(y)-\langle\bar v,y\rangle\}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Fixed-representation DC-criticality is equivalent to solving the point's own exact convex-linearized subproblem.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \partial g(\bar x)\cap\partial h(\bar x)\ne\varnothing\iff\exists\bar v\in\partial h(\bar x):\ \bar x\in\arg\min_y\{g(y)-\langle\bar v,y\rangle\}.
knowledge_statements.title: Exact DC Fixed-Point Criticality

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Exact DC-Criticality Need Not Imply Minimality
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary on the exact cluster-point theorem's conclusion.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(g(x)=0\) and \(h(x)=x^2\), the function \(g-h=-x^2\) satisfies \(\partial g(0)\cap\partial h(0)=\{0\}\), although \(0\) is a strict local maximum.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A shared component subgradient can certify a strict local maximum rather than a minimum.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: 0\text{ is DC-critical but not locally minimizing for }g-h.
knowledge_statements.title: Exact DC-Criticality Need Not Imply Minimality

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Square-Summability of Exact Quasi-DC Steps
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Quantitative consequence of sufficient decrease and lower boundedness.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(f(x^{k+1})\le f(x^k)-c\|x^{k+1}-x^k\|^2\) for \(c>0\) and \(\inf_k f(x^k)>-\infty\), then \(\sum_{k=0}^{\infty}\|x^{k+1}-x^k\|^2\le (f(x^0)-\inf_k f(x^k))/c<\infty\), and hence \(\|x^{k+1}-x^k\|\to0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Sufficient decrease makes the squared steps summable and the steps asymptotically vanish.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \sum_k\|x^{k+1}-x^k\|^2<\infty,\qquad\|x^{k+1}-x^k\|\to0.
knowledge_statements.title: Square-Summability of Exact Quasi-DC Steps
Exact Quasi-DC Cluster-Point Convergence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Subsequential convergence for exact unconstrained DC descent with a fixed representation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(f=g-h\) on \(\mathbb R^n\), where \(g,h\) are proper closed convex functions. Generate \(v^k\in\partial h(x^k)\) and
\[
x^{k+1}\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{x}\{g(x)-\langle v^k,x\rangle\}.
\]
Assume the iterates are bounded, \(f(x^{k+1})\le f(x^k)-c\|x^{k+1}-x^k\|^2\) for some \(c>0\), and the selected \(v^k\) are bounded. If \(f\) is bounded below along the iterates, then every cluster point \(\bar x\) is DC-critical:
\[
\partial g(\bar x)\cap\partial h(\bar x)\ne\varnothing.
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under exact subproblem solution, sufficient decrease, and boundedness, every cluster point shares a subgradient of the two convex components.
assumptions_latex: The iterates and selected subgradients are bounded.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\partial g(\bar x)\cap\partial h(\bar x)\ne\varnothing\) for every cluster point \(\bar x\).

notation.meaning: selected subgradient of the concave component h
cluster point of the iterate sequence

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The theorem content kind and exact fixed-representation setting fit the leaf. The cluster-point argument is plausible under the displayed boundedness and sufficient-decrease assumptions, but no cited source supports this precise theorem, including its subproblem-existence and closed-subdifferential-graph requirements.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Vanishing Subproblem Error Without Representation Consistency
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of limiting criticality when approximate representations are unrelated to the claimed limit.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For every \(k\), let \(g_k=h_k\equiv0\), take \(x^k=0\), and select \(u^{k+1}=v^k=0\). Then the subproblem residual and step are zero. If the claimed limiting representation is instead \(g(x)=x\), \(h(x)=0\), then \(\partial g(0)=\{1\}\) and \(\partial h(0)=\{0\}\), so their intersection is empty.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Exact solutions of unrelated approximate representations can converge to a point noncritical for the claimed limiting representation.
assumptions_latex: No epi-, graphical-, or subdifferential consistency relates \((g_k,h_k)\) to \((g,h)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Vanishing residuals and steps alone do not imply \(\partial g(\bar x)\cap\partial h(\bar x)\ne\varnothing\).
knowledge_statements.title: Vanishing Subproblem Error Without Representation Consistency
Approximate Quasi-DC Cluster-Point Convergence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Cluster-point criticality when representation and convex-subproblem residuals vanish.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For each \(k\), let \(f_k=g_k-h_k\), with \(g_k,h_k\) proper closed convex, and choose \(u^{k+1}\in\partial g_k(x^{k+1})\), \(v^k\in\partial h_k(x^k)\) satisfying \(\|u^{k+1}-v^k\|\le\varepsilon_k\). Assume \(x^{k+1}-x^k\to0\), \(\varepsilon_k\to0\), and that along every subsequence \(x^{k_j}\to\bar x\), bounded selections from \(\partial g_{k_j}\) and \(\partial h_{k_j}\) have graph limits in \(\partial g\) and \(\partial h\), respectively. Then every cluster point satisfies
\[
\partial g(\bar x)\cap\partial h(\bar x)\ne\varnothing.
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Vanishing subproblem error and consistent limiting representations make every cluster point critical for the limiting DC representation.
assumptions_latex: The iterates and relevant subgradient selections are bounded.
The convex subdifferential graphs are outer-consistent with \(g\) and \(h\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\partial g(\bar x)\cap\partial h(\bar x)\ne\varnothing\) for every cluster point \(\bar x\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The theorem content kind fits the approximate cluster-point leaf, but the mathematical version is not source-stable. Boundedness of the relevant subgradient selections appears only in assumptions_latex and not in statement_latex, while the stated graph-limit condition and the limiting functions g,h require more explicit domains and convergence hypotheses. No source is supplied for the exact formulation.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Constrained DC-Criticality and Convex-Subproblem Fixed Points
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Fixed-representation criticality over a closed convex feasible set, under the required convex sum rule.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C\subset\mathbb R^n\) be nonempty, closed, and convex, let \(g,h\) be proper closed convex functions, and suppose \(\partial(g+\delta_C)(\bar x)=\partial g(\bar x)+N_C(\bar x)\). Then \(\partial h(\bar x)\cap(\partial g(\bar x)+N_C(\bar x))\ne\varnothing\) if and only if some \(\bar v\in\partial h(\bar x)\) satisfies \(\bar x\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{y\in C}\{g(y)-\langle\bar v,y\rangle\}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under the convex subdifferential sum rule, constrained DC-criticality is equivalent to solving the point's own exact convex-linearized subproblem.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \partial h(\bar x)\cap(\partial g(\bar x)+N_C(\bar x))\ne\varnothing\iff\exists\bar v\in\partial h(\bar x):\ \bar x\in\arg\min_{y\in C}\{g(y)-\langle\bar v,y\rangle\}.

notation.meaning: convex normal cone to C at the candidate point

knowledge_statements.title: Constrained DC-Criticality and Convex-Subproblem Fixed Points

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Constrained DC-Criticality Is Not Sufficient for Minimality
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Limitation of the constrained cluster-point certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C=[-1,1]\), \(g(x)=0\), and \(h(x)=x^2\). At \(\bar x=0\), \(\partial g(0)=\partial h(0)=\{0\}\) and \(N_C(0)=\{0\}\), so \(0\) is constrained DC-critical. Nevertheless, \(g(x)-h(x)=-x^2<0=(g-h)(0)\) for every nonzero \(x\in C\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Constrained DC-criticality may hold at a strict local maximum.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: 0\text{ is constrained DC-critical but is not a local minimizer of }g-h.
knowledge_statements.title: Constrained DC-Criticality Is Not Sufficient for Minimality
Constrained Quasi-DC Cluster-Point Convergence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Cluster-point criticality for exact DC descent over a closed convex feasible set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(C\subset\mathbb R^n\) be nonempty, closed, and convex, and let \(f=g-h\) on \(C\), where \(g,h\) are proper closed convex. Generate \(v^k\in\partial h(x^k)\) and
\[
x^{k+1}\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in C}\{g(x)-\langle v^k,x\rangle\}.
\]
Assume bounded iterates and subgradient selections, sufficient decrease \(f(x^{k+1})\le f(x^k)-c\|x^{k+1}-x^k\|^2\), and a lower bound for \(f(x^k)\). Then every cluster point \(\bar x\in C\) satisfies
\[
\partial h(\bar x)\cap\bigl(\partial g(\bar x)+N_C(\bar x)\bigr)\ne\varnothing.
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every cluster point of constrained exact DC descent satisfies the decomposition-dependent criticality condition including the feasible-set normal cone.
assumptions_latex: \(C\) is nonempty, closed, and convex; \(g,h\) are proper closed convex.
The iterates and selected subgradients are bounded.
Sufficient decrease holds and the objective values are bounded below.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\partial h(\bar x)\cap(\partial g(\bar x)+N_C(\bar x))\ne\varnothing\).

notation.meaning: convex-analytic normal cone to C at x

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The theorem content kind and constrained criticality condition fit the leaf, and the normal-cone sign is consistent with the displayed convex subproblem. No source is supplied for the precise cluster-point theorem or the regularity needed to pass the subproblem optimality inclusions to the limit.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Objective Consistency Does Not Imply Representation Consistency
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure boundary for iteration-dependent DC decompositions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f_k=f=0\) on \(\mathbb R\), set \(g_k(x)=h_k(x)=(-1)^k x\), and declare the limiting representation \(g=h=0\). Then \(f_k=g_k-h_k=f\), but at \(x_k=0\) the component subgradients equal \((-1)^k\). Along the even subsequence they converge to \(1\notin\partial g(0)=\partial h(0)=\{0\}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Identical objectives can have oscillating DC components incompatible with a chosen limiting representation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: f_k\equiv f\quad\text{while component graphical outer consistency fails}.
knowledge_statements.title: Objective Consistency Does Not Imply Representation Consistency

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Local Uniform Convex-Component Convergence Ensures Outer Subgradient Consistency
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A sufficient regime for graphical outer consistency of varying convex components.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(U\subset\mathbb R^n\) be open and let finite convex functions \(g_k,g:U\to\mathbb R\) satisfy \(g_k\to g\) locally uniformly on \(U\). If \(x_k\to x\in U\), \(u_k\in\partial g_k(x_k)\), and \(u_k\to u\), then \(u\in\partial g(x)\). Applying this independently to \(h_k\to h\) gives componentwise outer consistency.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Local uniform convergence of finite convex components preserves limits of convergent component subgradients.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: u\in\partial g(x).

notation.meaning: open neighborhood containing the relevant points

knowledge_statements.title: Local Uniform Convex-Component Convergence Ensures Outer Subgradient Consistency
Representation-Consistency Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A graphical consistency condition for iteration-dependent convex representations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(f_k=g_k-h_k\) approximate \(f=g-h\) on \(\mathbb R^n\). The representations are subdifferentially consistent on a set \(K\) if, whenever \(k_j\to\infty\), \(x_j\in K\), \(x_j\to x\), and bounded vectors satisfy \(u_j\in\partial g_{k_j}(x_j)\), \(v_j\in\partial h_{k_j}(x_j)\), every limit \((u,v)\) obeys
\[
u\in\partial g(x),\qquad v\in\partial h(x).
\]
A sufficient consistency regime is local uniform convergence of finite convex \(g_k,h_k\) to \(g,h\) on an open neighborhood of \(K\), together with local boundedness of the relevant subgradient selections.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Representation consistency requires limits of approximate component subgradients to remain subgradients of the limiting convex components.
assumptions_latex: \(K\subset\mathbb R^n\) and \(g_k,h_k,g,h\) are proper convex on a neighborhood of \(K\).
Only bounded subgradient selections are considered.
