knowledge_statements.title: Sparse Optimization Interface
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional capped-ℓ1 DC surrogate for cardinality.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(x\in\mathbb{R}^n\) and \(\theta>0\), define \(P_\theta(x):=\sum_{i=1}^n\min\{1,|x_i|/\theta\}\). It has the DC representation
\[
P_\theta(x)=\theta^{-1}\lVert x\rVert_1-\sum_{i=1}^n\max\{|x_i|/\theta-1,0\},
\]
because both terms on the right are finite convex functions. If \(x=0\), then \(P_\theta(x)=\lVert x\rVert_0=0\) for every \(\theta>0\). If \(x\neq0\), then \(P_\theta(x)=\lVert x\rVert_0\) whenever \(0<\theta\leq\min\{|x_i|:x_i\neq0\}\). Consequently, for every fixed \(x\in\mathbb{R}^n\), \(P_\theta(x)\to\lVert x\rVert_0\) as \(\theta\downarrow0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Capped ℓ1 is a DC function. It equals cardinality for every cap at the zero vector and, for a nonzero fixed vector, whenever the cap is no larger than its smallest nonzero component magnitude.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(P_\theta\) is DC and, for every fixed \(x\in\mathbb{R}^n\), \(P_\theta(x)\to\lVert x\rVert_0\) as \(\theta\downarrow0\).

notation.meaning: number of nonzero components of x

source_refs.locator: Chapter 3. Structured Learning via Statistics and Optimization p. 111

source_witnesses.locator: Chapter 3. Structured Learning via Statistics and Optimization p. 111

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Exact DC Equation for a Cardinality Upper Bound
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact DC-compatible equation and residual test for finite-dimensional k-sparsity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(x\in\mathbb R^n\) and \(k\in\{0,\ldots,n\}\), let \(\lVert x\rVert_{(k)}:=\sum_{i=1}^k |x|_{[i]}\), where \(|x|_{[1]}\geq\cdots\geq|x|_{[n]}\), and set \(\lVert x\rVert_{(0)}:=0\). The function \(\lVert\cdot\rVert_{(k)}\) is convex, and \[\lVert x\rVert_0\leq k\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad \lVert x\rVert_1-\lVert x\rVert_{(k)}=0.\] Since this difference is always nonnegative, the equality is equivalently \(\lVert x\rVert_1-\lVert x\rVert_{(k)}\leq0\). This represents the sparsity constraint exactly without representing cardinality itself as a finite continuous DC objective.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A vector is k-sparse exactly when its l1 norm equals the sum of its k largest component magnitudes, giving an exact DC equation and feasibility residual.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\lVert x\rVert_0\leq k\iff \lVert x\rVert_1-\lVert x\rVert_{(k)}=0\iff \lVert x\rVert_1-\lVert x\rVert_{(k)}\leq0\).

notation.meaning: sum of the k largest component magnitudes

children.title: Low-Rank Optimization Interface
children.top_down_role: Boundary topics connecting DC optimization to rank-constrained or rank-penalized models.

knowledge_statements.title: Low-Rank Optimization Interface
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Spectral capped-nuclear DC surrogate for matrix rank.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(X\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}\), let \(q:=\min\{m,n\}\), and for \(\theta>0\) define \(R_\theta(X):=\sum_{i=1}^q\min\{1,\sigma_i(X)/\theta\}\). Then
\[
R_\theta(X)=\theta^{-1}\lVert X\rVert_*-\sum_{i=1}^q\max\{\sigma_i(X)/\theta-1,0\}.
\]
Both spectral terms on the right are convex, so \(R_\theta\) is DC. If \(X=0\), then \(R_\theta(X)=\operatorname{rank}(X)=0\) for every \(\theta>0\). If \(X\neq0\), then \(R_\theta(X)=\operatorname{rank}(X)\) whenever \(0<\theta\leq\min\{\sigma_i(X):\sigma_i(X)>0\}\). Consequently, for every fixed \(X\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}\), \(R_\theta(X)\to\operatorname{rank}(X)\) as \(\theta\downarrow0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A capped singular-value sum is DC. It equals rank for every cap at the zero matrix and, for a nonzero fixed matrix, whenever the cap is no larger than its smallest positive singular value.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(R_\theta\) is DC and, for every fixed \(X\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}\), \(R_\theta(X)\to\operatorname{rank}(X)\) as \(\theta\downarrow0\).

knowledge_statements.title: Integrality Interface
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact DC-compatible constraint for binary vectors inside a box.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(x\in[0,1]^n\), define \(h(x):=\sum_{i=1}^n x_i(1-x_i)\). Every summand is nonnegative on the box, so
\[
x\in\{0,1\}^n\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad x\in[0,1]^n\ \text{ and }\ h(x)\leq0.
\]
Furthermore, \(h(x)=\sum_{i=1}^n x_i-\lVert x\rVert_2^2\), which is a difference of the affine convex function \(x\mapsto\sum_i x_i\) and the convex function \(x\mapsto\lVert x\rVert_2^2\). Thus binary feasibility admits an exact DC inequality representation, although solving the resulting nonconvex problem remains distinct from general integer-optimization theory.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Within the unit box, one concave quadratic inequality exactly enforces binary variables and has an explicit DC decomposition.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x\in\{0,1\}^n\) if and only if \(h(x)\leq0\), with \(h(x)=\sum_i x_i-\lVert x\rVert_2^2\).

notation.meaning: continuous relaxation of the binary cube

knowledge_statements.title: Mixed-Structure Models
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Additive DC construction combining sparse, low-rank, and binary structure.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(z=(x,X,y)\) with \(x\in\mathbb{R}^n\), \(X\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times p}\), and \(y\in[0,1]^r\). For positive weights and cap parameters, set
\[
M(z):=\alpha P_{\theta_x}(x)+\beta R_{\theta_X}(X)+\gamma\sum_{j=1}^r y_j(1-y_j).
\]
Using DC decompositions \(P_{\theta_x}=G_x-H_x\), \(R_{\theta_X}=G_X-H_X\), and \(\sum_jy_j(1-y_j)=G_y-H_y\), one obtains
\[
M=(\alpha G_x+\beta G_X+\gamma G_y)-(\alpha H_x+\beta H_X+\gamma H_y),
\]
whose two aggregate terms are convex. Hence positive weighted combinations of these sparse, low-rank, and binary structural terms remain DC.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Positive weighted sums of DC sparse, low-rank, and binary structural terms remain DC by summing their convex components separately.
assumptions_latex: Each displayed component has the stated finite convex decomposition.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(M\) is a DC function on \(\mathbb{R}^n\times\mathbb{R}^{m\times p}\times[0,1]^r\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Affine Pullback and Overlapping Mixed Structures
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Proposed closure rule for shared or overlapping affine images; deferred because its canonical home is the general block-structured DC-program theory.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let C\subseteq\mathbb R^d be convex. If A_j are affine, f_j=g_j-h_j with finite convex g_j,h_j, and \alpha_j\geq0, then \sum_j\alpha_j f_j(A_jz)=\sum_j\alpha_jg_j(A_jz)-\sum_j\alpha_jh_j(A_jz) is DC on C.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Nonnegative sums of affine pullbacks of DC functions remain DC, including for overlapping coordinate blocks.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\sum_j\alpha_j f_j\circ A_j\) is DC on \(C\).

knowledge_statements.title: Chapter-Ownership Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sharp continuity boundary between classical finite DC functions and exact combinatorial structure.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(U\subseteq\mathbb{R}^d\) is open and \(f=g-h\) on \(U\), where \(g\) and \(h\) are finite convex functions, then \(f\) is continuous on \(U\). Consequently, cardinality cannot have such a representation on an open set containing a vector with a zero coordinate and nearby vectors where that coordinate is nonzero. Likewise, matrix rank cannot have such a representation on an open set containing a rank-deficient matrix and matrices of larger rank. Exact combinatorial models therefore require constraints, extended-valued formulations, or surrogates; only their resulting DC formulations belong to classical DC optimization.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Finite DC functions are continuous, so cardinality and rank cannot be exact finite DC functions across support or rank changes; constraints or surrogates form the interface.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(g-h\) is continuous on \(U\), excluding exact finite DC representations of cardinality or rank across their discontinuity points.
